article_content: A recent study has uncovered a troubling decline in life expectancy for American women under the age of 75, especially in rural counties in the South and West. Researchers observed that nearly half of all U.S. counties have seen an increase in premature female deaths over the past decade. By contrast, men’s life expectancy has remained steady or improved in most areas. Published in Health Affairs, the study by David Kindig and Erika Cheng from the University of Wisconsin analyzed federal death records for almost all 3,141 U.S. counties over a ten-year period. The data reveal that in about 43% of counties, early mortality among women rose from 317 to approximately 333 deaths per 100,000 people, while only around 100 counties showed a similar pattern for men. Experts are still investigating the reasons behind this decline. Theories include higher rates of smoking, obesity, poverty, and lower educational attainment in the hardest-hit regions. Jennifer Karas Montez, a Harvard sociologist focused on this issue, estimates approximately 12% of U.S. women are affected, with the biggest losses among white women without a high school degree. Earlier studies, such as one from Dr. Christopher Murray at the University of Washington, confirm that women in the South are most impacted. Counties with more smokers, less education, and higher poverty have worse outcomes. Some believe that prescription drug abuse is a contributing factor. Bob Anderson of the CDC raises the possibility that healthier women may be leaving rural areas, but this doesn’t seem to affect male death rates. The exact explanations remain the subject of debate among scientists. Historically, women have outlived men on average—with current estimates at 81 years for girls and 76 for boys—but this gap is shrinking. As researchers continue to seek answers, the decline in female life expectancy stands out as a public health concern in many parts of the country.

Los expertos aún buscan las razones detrás de este descenso. Las teorías incluyen mayores tasas de tabaquismo, obesidad, pobreza y un menor nivel educativo en las regiones más afectadas. Chanel’s Autumn/Winter 2015 haute couture show ended memorably as Karl Lagerfeld accompanied a pregnant bride down the runway, ushering in a glamorous take on maternity fashion. The model wore a sophisticated crêpe de Chine dress with a gold brocade cape and a line of buttons along the bodice, her hair styled in a dramatic quiff. Smiling, she walked the runway arm-in-arm with Lagerfeld.

The event’s finale drew loud applause from an audience featuring prominent fashion figures such as Anna Wintour, Kristen Stewart, and Jared Leto. The walk ended with a bow and a kiss on Lagerfeld’s cheek, marking a dramatic close to the show.

Lagerfeld’s vision for the season blended sculptural silhouettes with rich textures, featuring fabrics like brocade, tweed, and heavy silk. Several prints appeared to take inspiration from William Morris and the pre-Raphaelites. Departing from previous seasons’ lighter looks, this collection introduced darker styles, marabou-fringed tweed, and bodices adorned with jewel-like embellishments. 

The runway also featured sequined bell skirts, elaborate lace dresses, and, instead of high heels, models wore black, silver, and white flat sandals tied with grosgrain ribbons—for both style and comfort, especially fitting for mothers-to-be. 

Celebrities in attendance included Jared Leto in tweed jeans, Kristen Stewart in an all-white outfit, and front-row guests Anna Wintour, Grace Coddington, and Baz Luhrmann.

article_content: Skype has taken a major step toward erasing language barriers online with the beta launch of its live translation feature. This new tool lets users converse in different languages during video calls, even if neither party understands the other's tongue. As you speak, Skype instantly translates your words, offering both spoken and written translations. Currently, the preview version—available on Windows 8.1 devices—only supports English and Spanish, but Microsoft is planning to introduce dozens of additional languages. Eventually, over 40 languages (even Klingon from Star Trek) could be included. To try it, users need to sign up on Skype's website. Gurdeep Pall from Microsoft highlighted in a blog post that Skype Translator's mission is to let people communicate freely, regardless of language. To use the feature, select a contact, enable the 'Translation' option, and then speak or type during your call. The system analyzes the audio using millions of pre-recorded samples, removes fillers like 'um' and 'ah,' and then generates the most likely text before translating it. Skype Translator's underlying technology has been significantly enhanced by neural networks, leading to a 30% improvement in speech recognition accuracy compared to earlier attempts. Like other machine learning tools, its effectiveness improves as more people use it and provide feedback. Early reviewers, including Gizmodo, report promising results but note you'll get the best performance by speaking slowly and clearly. Fast or unclear speech can still trip up the system, leading to less accurate translations. The tool is designed to continually refine itself as user participation grows. Skype, which boasts over 300 million users and facilitates more than 2 billion minutes of daily conversation, aims to connect people worldwide—without the high cost of traditional phone bills. The Translator builds on technologies from other Microsoft projects, such as the Cortana voice assistant. While there's no confirmed launch date for the full version yet, Skype Translator marks a significant leap toward making global communication accessible, with ongoing improvements based on technology updates and user feedback.

India's Rohan Bopanna and Australia's Matthew Ebden, seeded third in the Nitto ATP Finals, were eliminated in the semifinals in Turin on Saturday, missing the chance to secure the year-end No.1 doubles ranking. Fifth seeds Marcel Granollers from Spain and Horacio Zeballos from Argentina played strong tennis to defeat the Indo-Australian pair 5-7, 4-6 in the semifinal. Granollers and Zeballos held a 2-1 head-to-head advantage before this match. They broke Ebden's serve in the 11th game of the first set and again in the third game of the second set, and maintained their lead until the end. Bopanna and Ebden, who had beaten Granollers and Zeballos in their previous meeting in Paris, started well in the first set. However, they needed to reach the final to surpass Ivan Dodig and Austin Krajicek, who currently hold the top ranking. If Granollers and Zeballos win the final on Sunday, they will become the new world No.1 pair.

- World Cup Semifinal: Australia’s Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood dominated South Africa’s batting at Eden Gardens, overcoming a century from David Miller as Australia won by three wickets and advanced to their eighth final. South Africa's semifinal misfortune continued despite a strong effort.
- ODI World Cup Final: Expectations are high for the India vs Australia match at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. India have been strong throughout the tournament, while Australia made a comeback after early struggles. Australia's historical ODI record against India is better, but recent games have been closer.
- Australian High Commissioner Philip Green expressed excitement for the India-Australia final, praising both teams and highlighting standout players Virat Kohli and Glenn Maxwell. He congratulated India for their impressive tournament performance.

article_content: Lanny Smith was pursuing his dream of playing in the NBA when he signed with the Sacramento Kings in 2009. However, just 33 days after signing his contract, a serious knee injury ended his basketball career. This sudden change led Smith to face an identity crisis and depression. Eventually, he decided to shift his focus, combining his passion for sports with entrepreneurship. In 2011, Smith established Active Faith, a faith-based sports apparel brand featuring motivational quotes and Bible verses. Teaming up with former NBA player Anthony Tolliver and Warriors’ point guard Steph Curry, Active Faith quickly grew, serving customers in 73 countries and generating $100,000 in its first year, eventually becoming a $7 million business. Despite this success, Smith faced challenges in securing retail partnerships and investment due to racial bias. He noted that some potential investors withdrew support upon realizing his ethnicity. However, seeing the positive impact of Active Faith on its customers inspired him to continue pushing forward. The cultural significance of Marvel’s Black Panther movie in 2018 and subsequent social justice movements, especially following the murder of George Floyd, motivated Smith to create a new brand—Actively Black. He became determined to build a brand for the Black community, centered on empowerment and authentic representation, rather than relying on mainstream brands’ superficial gestures. Smith launched Actively Black on Black Friday 2020, after assessing the competitive landscape and recognizing a need for a brand that uplifted and united the Black community year-round. He aimed to challenge negative stereotypes and promote self-belief through his products. Unlike many companies, Smith is committed to serving the Black community consistently, rather than only during recognized observances like Black History Month or Juneteenth. Actively Black’s manufacturing takes place in Asia and in Lagos, Nigeria, where the company also outfitted Nigeria’s team for the 2021 Winter Olympics. Smith sees Africa as a promising future manufacturing hub as the market grows. After launching with only two employees, Actively Black saw $100,000 in sales in its first week, selling out three months’ worth of inventory in four weeks. The company achieved $2.3 million in revenue in its first year and approached $6 million by the end of 2022. Despite supply chain challenges, a successful Series A funding round allowed Smith to invest heavily in inventory and meet increasing demand. Strategic partnerships—such as collaborations with Marvel (for an official Black Panther collection), Teleport Watches, Nigerian sports federations, Slam Magazine, and deals with HBCU athletes—have boosted Actively Black’s profile. Smith credits his mentor, Daymond John (of FUBU and Shark Tank), with helping secure key licensing deals, notably with Marvel. Beyond business, Actively Black has donated $500,000 to organizations including the Liberation Fund, Compton Girls Club, Black Girls Smile, Black Girls and Black Boys Code, Ujima, and Black Mamas Matter Alliance. Smith describes Actively Black as more than a clothing brand—it is a movement to unite and empower the diaspora globally. With growing international interest, Smith remains committed to serving communities worldwide and positioning Actively Black as both a business and a vehicle for positive change.

article_content: Researchers at Flinders University have made significant progress in wound care with a novel approach. By using an argon atmospheric plasma jet, they have transformed Spirulina maxima, a blue-green microalga, into ultrathin bioactive coatings. These coatings not only combat bacterial infections but also promote faster wound healing and exhibit strong anti-inflammatory properties. This advancement is especially promising for chronic wounds, which often have prolonged healing times. The approach could reduce the risk of toxic reactions from silver and other nanoparticles, as well as address rising antibiotic resistance linked to conventional wound dressings. The development, published in the nanotechnology journal Small, introduces a newly patented plasma-assisted technology that sustainably processes Spirulina maxima biomass into ultrathin coatings. These coatings can be applied to wound dressings and other medical devices to protect patients from infection, accelerate healing, and regulate inflammation. According to Dr. Vi Khanh Truong from the Flinders University Biomedical Nano-engineering Laboratory, the plasma coating technology can turn various types of biomass, such as Spirulina maxima, into high-quality, sustainable coatings. "With our technology, we can convert biomass into coatings for wound dressings, and this plasma process is the first of its kind," said Dr. Truong. An overview of the argon atmospheric plasma jet (Ar-APJ) system includes: (A) a photograph of the setup for plasma treatment transforming S. maxima into a robust ultrathin coating; (B) an image of the plasma jet itself; (C) OES spectra at a flow rate of 10 LPM and voltage of 10 kV; and (D) an illustration of how Ar-APJ turns S. maxima into a continuous ultrathin coating. (Credit: Small, 2023. DOI: 10.1002/smll.202305469) An extract of S. maxima is often used as a protein supplement and to treat skin disorders such as eczema and psoriasis. The World Health Organization has warned that antimicrobial resistance is among the top public health threats of the 21st century. It was linked to nearly 5 million deaths in 2019 and could cost the global economy more than US$1 trillion by 2050 if not addressed. Genetic changes in bacteria like Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa can lead to resistance to multiple antibiotics, resulting in so-called 'superbugs.' Co-author Professor Krasimir Vasilev, NHMRC Leadership Fellow and Director of the Biomedical Nanoengineering Laboratory, says this technology offers better solutions compared to current commercial products that use metals such as silver, gold, and copper, and plays an important role in fighting antibiotic resistance. "This new plasma-facilitated process can improve extraction and purification of useful compounds from biomass without harmful solvents or high energy consumption," Professor Vasilev said. "We are now exploring commercialization of this unique technology. Currently, there are no commercial wound dressings that simultaneously fight infection, regulate inflammation, and stimulate healing. We believe this innovation will give medical wound dressing manufacturers a market advantage and, by reaching hospitals, make a difference in healthcare and patient outcomes."

article_content: Global news recently highlighted that musician Grimes has initiated a custody case against Elon Musk concerning their three children. However, Insider has found that Musk was the first to file a legal suit related to custody. On September 7, Musk filed in Texas to legally establish his parental relationship and access to his children with Grimes: X (3 years old), Exa (Y), and Tau (both age 1). In his filing, Musk accused Grimes (Claire Boucher) of moving to California to avoid the jurisdiction of Texas courts. He mentioned that Grimes and the children had lived with him from May to July of this year. Musk said he hoped the matter would be resolved without court intervention, but wanted Texas courts involved if not. After being served Musk’s suit on September 13, Grimes filed her own lawsuit on September 29. She is seeking physical custody of the children and has requested a standard restraining order to prevent either parent from taking the children out of California. Out of concerns for privacy, the case was sealed and neither parent’s full name nor the children's names appeared in court documents. A scheduled hearing was canceled after both parties agreed to the seal. Lawyers for both sides have declined to comment, and Musk did not reply to requests for statements. These legal actions come amid an already complex relationship; since 2018, Musk and Grimes have had an on-and-off partnership. Grimes has publicly voiced the need to keep their children out of the public spotlight, while Musk has involved their oldest child, X, in public events including interviews, international meetings, and SpaceX launches. Strife between the two has occasionally been visible on social media. In one instance, Grimes posted—and then deleted—a plea to Musk for access to her son via X (formerly Twitter). The situation has also involved Shivon Zilis, another mother of Musk’s children, and grievances aired online about Musk’s decision-making and family transparency. Grimes only learned about Zilis’ child with Musk via the media. Grimes and Zilis have since clarified on social platforms that they are no longer at odds. Musk has not publicly addressed the recent disputes. This custody matter is the latest development in Musk’s elaborate personal life, which includes ten living children with three different mothers.

Choosing a Caribbean cruise during hurricane season comes with risks, but many travelers go ahead, hoping for smooth sailing while staying aware of possible disruptions. During this period—which runs from June through November—cruise itineraries might change suddenly due to storms, and sometimes passengers are left behind if ships depart early to avoid bad weather.

According to Carolyn Spencer Brown, editor in chief of CruiseCritic.com, summer and early fall cruises are popular because families are on vacation and fares are often lower. Ships also have advanced weather tracking and can typically avoid hurricanes by rerouting, unlike stationary resorts. However, Brown explains that cruise tickets include terms allowing lines to change destinations at any time without being required to offer compensation.

There have been cases where passengers expecting warm destinations found themselves rerouted to unexpected locations, causing frustration—especially when packing for different climates. Besides weather, other factors like political unrest can lead to route changes.

Travelers who miss their cruise due to flight delays or early departures may face challenges getting help. If flights were booked through the cruise, the company often assists with hotels and alternate travel. Independent travelers, however, usually bear the costs themselves. For example, during Hurricane Irene, Royal Caribbean left behind some passengers in Puerto Rico who hadn’t arranged air travel through the company, while those who had received full assistance. Carnival, in a similar situation, reportedly contacted all affected guests and provided support, including covering costs or offering future credits.

Brown recommends buying independent travel insurance with good weather coverage, rather than relying solely on cruise line packages, which can be more expensive and less flexible. It’s rare for a cruise to be canceled entirely, since ships can change routes to avoid storms; the Caribbean has many ports to choose from, as highlighted by Carnival spokeswoman Jennifer de la Cruz.

To avoid problems during hurricane season, book travel insurance, arrive at the departure port a day early, stay alert for schedule changes, and remain close to the ship if severe weather is possible. Travelers planning special events, like weddings at a port stop, should be cautious, since those plans may need to change if the ship can't visit the intended location.

Durante esta temporada—que va de junio a noviembre—los itinerarios pueden modificarse repentinamente por tormentas, y a veces los pasajeros se quedan atrás si los barcos salen antes para evitar el mal tiempo.

Según Carolyn Spencer Brown, editora en jefe de CruiseCritic.com, los cruceros en verano y principios de otoño son populares porque coinciden con las vacaciones familiares y las tarifas suelen ser más bajas. Hay casos de pasajeros que esperaban visitar lugares cálidos y terminaron en destinos inesperados, generando frustración, sobre todo si no empacaron para otro clima. Además del clima, factores como la inestabilidad política pueden forzar cambios en el itinerario.

Quienes pierden el crucero por demoras en vuelos o salidas adelantadas enfrentan complicaciones para recibir ayuda. Si el vuelo se contrató con la naviera, la empresa suele brindar hospedaje y ayuda para alcanzar el barco en el siguiente puerto. Para prevenir contratiempos en esta temporada, contrata un seguro de viaje, llega con un día de anticipación al puerto, mantente informado sobre posibles cambios y permanece cerca del barco si puede haber mal tiempo. Si planeas bodas u otros eventos especiales, sé precavido: podrías tener que ajustar tus planes si el barco no puede llegar al destino previsto.

article_content: UC Inclusive Credit (UCIC), backed by Mohandas Pai's Aarin Capital, has raised $8 million in equity from Singapore-based Insitor Partners as part of its plans to expand financing for startups. The non-banking finance company will also raise another $1 million from its existing investors, bringing the total capital infusion to around Rs 73 crore. “The rapid growth of early-stage companies in India creates a strong need for more debt funding. We are raising this equity to further leverage our balance sheet and enable additional borrowing from both existing and new lenders,” said Abhijit Ray, UCIC co-founder and managing director. Founded in 2019, UCIC has lent approximately Rs 1,700 crore to 225 companies to date, with an outstanding portfolio of Rs 570 crore. Aarin Capital is among its early investors. UCIC is promoted and majority-owned by Unitus Capital, which has arranged over $4 billion in funding for more than 200 impact-focused companies. Former RBL Bank chairman Narayan Ramachandran is also an initial investor and serves as UCIC's chairman. “UCIC is transforming early-stage, small-ticket debt funding for SMEs in India, a sector that banks and other financial institutions have traditionally underserved. Bridging this gap is vital for financial infrastructure,” said Nicholas Lazos, co-founder and chief investment officer at Insitor Partners. Insitor Partners manages two funds, Insitor Impact Asia Fund I and II, with a total fund size of $85 million, plus a $10 million Insitor Seed Fund. While its main focus is early-stage Indian companies, Insitor also has investments in Cambodia, Pakistan, and Myanmar. In India, Insitor has invested in 15 companies, with active investments in eight, including EduBridge, Farmley, iDrishti, Medkart, and WorkIndia. The firm’s total investment exposure in these companies is close to $30 million.

article_content: When people talk about their car being 'totaled,' many imagine a severe accident with obvious, extensive damage. However, a vehicle may be considered totaled even if it still appears drivable, as structural damage such as a bent frame often meets the threshold for total loss. Such accidents lead to higher insurance rates because the costs for replacing these vehicles are significant for insurers. To address repair and insurance expenses, carmakers and insurance companies are collaborating on innovations designed to make repairs less costly. Ford recently opened a $650,000 Paint and Body Technology Center in Inkster, Michigan, near its Dearborn headquarters. This new center combines previous operations and works closely with engineers and insurers to identify and solve potential repair challenges early in the design phase. By gathering repair data earlier in vehicle development and collaborating with repair professionals and insurance companies, carmakers like Ford are creating more repair-friendly designs. This allows for more affordable fixes at both dealerships and independent shops, and enables vehicles to be restored more effectively after accidents. Ford’s collaboration began with the 2009 F-150, where engineers recognized that modern materials improved safety but could increase repair costs. This led to new solutions such as front and rear-frame section kits, which allow repairs to a smaller area of the frame, avoiding full-frame replacements and saving at least $2,000 per repair. This collaborative approach continued with the 2010 Mustang, where Ford introduced procedures for repairing only the damaged portions of rear-frame rails, again lowering costs and helping prevent insurance total loss declarations. Other manufacturers, such as GM, are also innovating. GM’s Collision Repair Test Center engages with product engineers and insurers early to ensure new vehicles are designed with effective, cost-efficient repairs in mind. The center has helped reduce both parts and labor costs on vehicles like the Pontiac Solstice and Saturn Aura through partial-assembly and section-specific repair strategies. Such solutions can mean savings of up to $1,500 per repair, and also allow owners greater flexibility and affordability if their vehicle suffers collision damage. A current focus for the industry is improving repair options for side-impact collisions, ensuring that even if a side pillar is damaged, the car isn’t automatically a total loss. This includes exploring new welding and fastening techniques to make these repairs feasible. Industry leaders acknowledge that as new automotive technologies emerge, it’s necessary to develop updated repair strategies that maintain both safety and affordability for vehicle owners.

article_content: Stephen Pope, 35, died from asphyxiation after his neck became trapped under a wooden fence panel while fleeing a burglary in Waltham Abbey, Essex, in March of this year. During his attempted escape with stolen items, Mr. Pope became stuck between the fence panel and a concrete gravel board. An inquest at Chelmsford Coroners’ Court ruled his death as accidental. A post-mortem revealed Mr. Pope had a combination of drugs, including cocaine, cannabis, and methadone, in his system when the incident occurred. His accomplice, Albert Brinkley, 27, who had no fixed address, was previously jailed for 12 months after admitting to burglary. The coroner, Eleanor McGann, confirmed evidence indicating Mr. Pope was involved in the burglary. The inquest heard Mr. Pope was found holding a pillowcase containing stolen property. It was also noted that he was found in a face-down, awkward position that could have led to asphyxiation. According to testimony, an elderly passer-by had spoken with Mr. Pope, believing he was a workman, and Mr. Pope claimed he was 'okay.' A second woman later found him unresponsive and called emergency services. Two nurses from a nearby nursing home attempted to assist by lifting the fence panel, but paramedics were unable to revive him. Coroner McGann stated that it was plausible Mr. Pope told the passer-by he was fine in order to avoid being caught with stolen goods. The official cause of death was compression of the neck, associated with postural asphyxiation, and drug intoxication was identified as a contributing factor. Investigating officer Detective Sergeant Darren Ward told the court a thorough investigation found no third-party involvement or suspicious circumstances. Mr. Pope, who was on bail for a separate theft at the time, was remembered by his family as a 'lovable rogue.' His parents expressed disbelief at the accidental death verdict, citing a previous back injury that they felt would have prevented him from lifting a fence panel. They described him as someone who faced many personal challenges. A family tribute described Mr. Pope as a troubled individual who struggled with mental health issues, saying his loss left a permanent void. Floral tributes were left at the scene. Another person arrested in connection with the incident was released with no further action.

article_content: In her latest book, 'Roseannearchy: Dispatches from the Nut Farm,' comedian Roseanne Barr delves into her unique background as someone who grew up both Jewish and Mormon in Salt Lake City. She also opens up about her journey to stardom through the sitcom that brought her global fame, her ex-husbands, and her life managing a macadamia nut farm in Hawaii. The book, which offers a frank look at Barr’s perspectives on the world, showcases her signature unfiltered style. As she told CNN, 'My writing just pours out, then I shape and refine it.' When the conversation turned political, Barr quipped she was running for both president of the United States and prime minister of Israel through her own tongue-in-cheek Solutions Party and Green Tea Party. She joked that President Obama should take her lead and focus on finding solutions as well. A notable surprise for fans is that Barr’s first husband, Bill Pentland—who inspired the character Dan Conner on 'Roseanne'—penned the introduction for her book. Barr shared that their mutual love of writing connected them from the beginning, and their three children inspired the characters Darlene, Becky, and D.J. on the show. Pentland’s foreword reminisces about their life in 1970s Colorado, recalling their days as 'big hippies' living without modern conveniences. Barr looks back on those times fondly. She credits the ongoing popularity and enduring relevance of 'Roseanne' to its dedicated audience, explaining, 'It’s cool that people continue to discover and watch the show.' She keeps in contact with many castmates, proud that the series not only broke new ground but also helped launch successful writing careers for many. Barr was also amused to learn 'Family Guy' once spoofed 'Roseanne,' though she missed seeing the episode herself. She expressed her approval of the animated series nonetheless. Finally, Barr pointed out how 'The Big Bang Theory' has become somewhat of a reunion spot for 'Roseanne' alumni. Johnny Galecki (Leonard), Sara Gilbert (Darlene), and Laurie Metcalf (Jackie) all have roles on the CBS hit. Barr half-jokingly wondered why she hasn’t been invited to guest star, suggesting maybe a fan campaign is needed. Looking ahead, Barr simply hopes to keep writing.

article_content: Star Trek: Lower Decks has been a fan favorite since its first season, with Tawny Newsome’s portrayal of Beckett Mariner playing a key role. Throughout the show's four seasons, Mariner has evolved from a chaotic, self-destructive ensign to a lieutenant junior grade, joining the rest of the Lower Decks crew in their promotion. The past season has brought significant challenges, especially for Mariner, who, along with Boimler (Jack Quaid), briefly traveled back in time to meet the Strange New Worlds crew. Reflecting on season four in an interview with TVInsider, Newsome shared that Mariner may tone down some of her more reckless tendencies moving forward. Referring to the season finale, Newsome remarked that her character ended up 'in a full Wrath of Khan situation without even trying.' While Mariner may stop actively seeking trouble, she will still take risks, as that's part of her nature. However, she’ll no longer do reckless things just to avoid facing her problems. Growth for Mariner included recognizing that Ransom is a capable commanding officer and not just an obstacle. Their competitive dynamic was enjoyable for Newsome, who praised the writers for developing Ransom into an endearing character. By season four, it’s clear that Ransom is a supportive leader who believes in Mariner, and his influence has been a key factor in her development. Going forward, viewers will see Mariner taking on the responsibilities of her new rank and embracing her promotion. Newsome is optimistic about Mariner’s future, noting that even Tendi’s exit at the end of the season did not unsettle her as it would have previously. The actor is excited to see how Mariner will continue to challenge Starfleet, aiming to help it improve, which remains her ultimate goal. Newsome is also enthusiastic about more live-action opportunities for the Lower Decks cast, expressing her wish to see Noël Wells (Tendi) and Eugene Cordero (Rutherford) portray their characters in live-action as well. She called working with them on screen a dream come true. Newsome’s full interview with TVInsider covers more on the Lower Decks and Strange New Worlds crossover. All four seasons of Star Trek: Lower Decks are available to stream on Paramount+. article_content: A former police holding cell may not seem like the obvious place for a relaxing treatment, but it’s where one of London’s top facialists, Katie England, practices. Located in the historic Bow Street Magistrate’s Court and Police Station, NoMad London is now a sophisticated hotel and home to Katie’s ongoing residency, where she offers treatments in a repurposed holding cell on the first floor. Despite original details like the steel door and subway tiles, the room is transformed with modern art, plush velvet chairs, opulent drapes, and warm golden lighting. A luxurious bathroom and the sound of gentle jazz music complete the atmosphere, giving the space a unique, tranquil vibe. At the heart of the experience is a cozy treatment bed where Katie performs her signature Natural Face Lift, which includes a buccal massage (an inside-the-mouth technique to relax jaw tension and stimulate facial muscles), all while clients are wrapped in a soft duvet. With over ten years in wellness, Katie personalizes each session, using techniques such as facial cupping, facial contouring, intraoral massage, microneedling, and chemical peels. Her focus is on crafting individualized ‘skin journeys’ based on clients’ lifestyles and skin goals. NoMad London, which opened in Covent Garden in May 2021 across from the Royal Opera House, marked a new era for London hotels. Designed by Roman and Williams, the hotel features over 1,600 works of art and a rich, inviting aesthetic, including a dramatic sunken restaurant in a glass atrium. Katie offers exclusive treatments at NoMad, including the Byonik Pulse-Triggered Laser Facial, newly available in the UK. In this treatment, a pulse reader tracks the client’s heartbeat to guide a cold laser over the face, helping to repair skin, stimulate collagen and elastin, and hydrate deeply. The technology reduces redness, inflammation, and is suitable for a wide range of skin types. Preparation for the Byonik facial begins with deep cleansing, followed by intentional dehydration and then targeted application of hyaluronic acid to enhance moisture absorption. Clients can also experience the Slimyonik Air Bodystyler—a pneumatic pressure massage device designed to stimulate the lymphatic system, reduce inflammation, increase metabolism, and support detoxification. The experience is compared to a gentle yet powerful multi-handed massage for the legs and abdomen. Katie recommends a series of six sessions over two to three weeks for optimal results, with benefits lasting for up to a year. She notes that Byonik delivers immediate, pain-free improvements for various skin concerns, improving hydration, firmness, and the look of fine lines. The combined protocol with Slimyonik is ideal for travelers needing hydration and detox post-flight. After treatments, guests can relax at the NoMad’s Library Bar, next to the lobby, featuring creative cocktails and a curated book selection, reinforcing the hotel’s commitment to wellness for both body and mind.

Teresa Tambunting, 50, of Scarsdale, New York, a longtime employee and vault manager at Jacmel Jewelry in Long Island City, is accused of stealing up to $12 million in gold and jewelry from her employer over six years, according to Queens District Attorney Richard Brown. At her arraignment on Wednesday, Tambunting did not enter a plea to charges of first-degree grand larceny and first-degree criminal possession of stolen property. She was released on $100,000 bail and is scheduled to return to court on May 19. Her attorney, David Kirby, has not responded to requests for comment.

Tambunting worked at Jacmel Jewelry for 28 years and has returned about $7 million worth of gold; about $4 million remains unaccounted for, according to Brown. Brown stated, "The defendant is accused of establishing a virtual mining operation in Long Island City which siphoned off millions of dollars' worth of the precious metal from her employer." Police say Tambunting, responsible for overseeing the vault where gold and finished jewelry were kept, confessed to concealing gold in hidden pockets in her purse over several months last year. A January inventory revealed up to $12 million in merchandise was missing.

After an investigation, Tambunting returned to the company's offices with a suitcase containing about 66 pounds of gold, estimated at $868,000. In February, about 450 pounds of gold were recovered from her residence. The timeline of the alleged thefts is unclear, as gold prices fluctuate, affecting the returned gold's value. The charges are based on Jacmel's reported loss of $3 to $12 million.

Benjamin Mark, a former jewelry manufacturer in New York, says preventing such theft is difficult without stringent security such as metal detectors. Jacmel Jewelry, among the country's largest jewelry manufacturers and distributors, employs over 1,000 people worldwide, according to president Jack Rahmey, who says he is cooperating with authorities. If convicted, Tambunting faces up to 25 years in prison.

article_content: As India approaches general elections, key financial institutions are turning to the bond market to raise nearly ₹30,000 crore for infrastructure projects. The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NABFID) is planning a bond issue of up to ₹10,000 crore, while the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway targets up to ₹3,000 crore. State-run banks, including Bank of Baroda and Canara Bank, are also preparing infrastructure bond issuances of ₹10,000 crore and ₹5,000 crore, respectively. This surge in bond activity comes as government bond yields ease, with the 10-year benchmark at 7.25%, down from 7.38% in early October. NABFID's bond sale is expected around mid-December, with a proposed 15-year maturity. This follows their earlier ₹10,000 crore, 10-year bond issued in June, reflecting ongoing investor interest in longer-term infrastructure bonds. Major institutional investors, such as insurance companies and pension funds, are anticipated to participate. The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, which will link India's national and financial capitals, has received a 'letter of comfort' from the National Highways Authority of India for its potential ₹3,000 crore bond issue. These bonds may have a 15-year maturity with a base size of ₹1,000 crore and a green shoe option of ₹2,000 crore, and may launch in late November or early December. Bank of Baroda plans to launch its ₹10,000 crore, 10-year bond by the end of November, while Canara Bank’s ₹5,000 crore issuance, also with a 10-year term, is expected to be offered soon. Pricing could be in the 7.65-7.70% range. State-owned banks have ramped up infrastructure bond activity this year, with the State Bank of India already completing significant issuances. High investor demand is evident through strong subscription and narrow spreads vs. government bonds. In corporate news, an increasing number of women are assuming senior leadership roles in Indian companies, gaining more visibility in corporate boardrooms and disputes. Meanwhile, US carmaker Tesla may invest up to $2 billion in India, contingent on receiving a reduced import duty for its initial period in the country. The government is also considering changes to how it allocates resources among states, possibly by giving more importance to human development and sustainable goals in its funding formula.

article_content: In the Russian city of Tula, a woman attempted to prevent her car from being towed by staging an impromptu striptease on the tow truck. The incident, which occurred outside the Railway Workers' House of Culture, was filmed by a bystander and shared online by Anatoliy Aleksandrovich. The woman climbed onto the truck beside her vehicle and began removing her clothes in an effort to stop the traffic police from towing her car. During the episode, she negotiated with the officers while dancing, although police proceeded to tow her car away regardless. It was later pointed out that, under Russian law, police cannot tow a vehicle if the driver is present. Nevertheless, the car was removed. Commenters online suggested that more traditional approaches, such as negotiating or offering a bribe, are often used to avoid having a car towed or to prevent traffic fines in Russia.

A person with an active tuberculosis infection was able to fly on a commercial airplane last week, despite being listed on a federal 'do-not-board' list, officials said on Tuesday. Airline representative Morgan Durrant confirmed the unidentified patient traveled on US Airways Flight 401 from Philadelphia to San Francisco on Saturday.

An investigation is underway involving US Airways, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) regarding how the individual was able to board. The CDC provides the do-not-board list to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHS), which informs the TSA, and then the TSA notifies the airlines, as explained by an anonymous government official.

In this case, airlines were alerted at 10 p.m. on Friday—over 14 hours before the passenger checked in for the flight departing at noon on Saturday. TSA spokeswoman Kristin Lee stated that the TSA followed all necessary protocols and quickly notified airlines.

The CDC advised US Airways that TB transmission risk is low on flights lasting less than eight hours; Flight 401's duration was under six hours, so the airline did not reach out to other passengers. When the person tried to board another international flight in San Francisco, authorities stopped them, said Dr. Martin Cetron, CDC's director for global migration and quarantine. Cetron stressed that nobody with active tuberculosis should fly, though did not specify if this was a drug-resistant case. The individual is receiving treatment.

Dr. Cetron remarked that, while the person’s flight from Philadelphia did occur, the public health system ultimately worked because the passenger was intercepted in San Francisco. He stated it would have been better if the individual had never boarded the first flight. Since the do-not-board list was created in 2007 after an incident involving Atlanta lawyer Andrew Speaker and drug-resistant TB, a handful of similar incidents have occurred. The list has held 88 names, mostly related to TB, with 76 removed so far. Cetron clarified that the do-not-board list and the DHS’s no-fly list are separate, each with its own procedures. The list covers nine infectious diseases, primarily tuberculosis.

Garmin has introduced new diver’s watches, including the Descent G1 Solar – Ocean Edition and several high-end models in the Descent Mk3 series. The Descent G1 Ocean Edition is an entry-level addition, featuring a case made from fiber-reinforced, ocean-bound plastic. It is priced at $650, identical to the standard Descent G1 Solar in the United States, and is rated for dive depths up to 100 meters.

In comparison, the Apple Watch Ultra 2 is recommended only for dives up to 40 meters, the same as the original model.

Divers seeking more advanced features can explore the new Garmin Descent Mk3 family, starting at $1,200. All Descent Mk3 watches are water-rated to 200 meters, but design, material, and pricing vary among models. The standard Descent Mk3 features a 43mm stainless steel bezel.

Upgrading to the Descent Mk3i brings options for 43mm or 51mm watch sizes, plus upgraded materials like a titanium bezel and base. Customers can choose specialty coatings: Bronze PVD (Physical Vapour Deposition) or DLC (Diamond-Like Coating), both offering scratch resistance. DLC is typically more robust, while Bronze PVD is visually striking.

The Mk3i models also support Garmin’s new T2 Transceiver. This device will enable divers in a group to send preset messages and request assistance (features scheduled for future activation). It also allows viewing of other group members’ oxygen levels and depths.

Garmin’s Descent series is highly specialized for divers, unlike its other product lines for activities like golf or trucking. All models include Garmin’s standard sports tracking features in addition to diving functionality.

The Descent G1 Ocean Edition is expected to ship within 2-3 weeks at $650. The Mk3i 51mm model will also be available in 2-3 weeks, starting from $1,600. The standard Mk3 and Mk3i 43mm models are listed with a longer shipping time of 8-12 weeks.

By Catherine Ostler

As a writer and former magazine editor, I'm used to meeting deadlines. Most of us are. But when a task doesn’t have a fixed deadline, it’s a different story—I often end up procrastinating.

Take a recent assignment with no firm deadline. First, I went out for a cappuccino, justifying it as brain fuel. Then I bought wrapping paper for a child’s birthday present that had to be delivered that day. It’s easy to find reasons to delay work, convincing ourselves other things are urgent—but panic soon follows.

Back home, I called the doctor before the surgery closed for lunch and waited on hold before giving up. I then browsed the local estate agent’s website for an hour (we’re not moving; I was just curious) and picked at leftovers from the fridge. I read the newspaper (for research), washed my hair, and texted someone about a long-standing roof problem. Even a free magazine on the hall table tempted me—more 'research.'

I lost two hours and built up a knot of anxiety in my chest. Everything seemed more pressing than my actual work. Despite telling myself I was clearing other distractions, the hours slipped by and I started to panic. And I’m not alone: about a quarter of people say procrastination is a defining part of their personality. Even in ancient times, people put things off—a magazine reported that Egyptian hieroglyphs from 1400BC read: 'Friend, stop putting off work and let’s go home in good time.'

Social media and internet browsing often feel productive, but valuable hours can be lost online. My personal struggle with procrastination has been lifelong; when I was at school, I filled my homework book with lists until the work became overwhelming. At university, I spent more time making colorful revision timetables than actually studying. Studies even suggest that procrastinating students suffer more colds, flu, and gastrointestinal problems.

I’ve grown used to my 'pet demon,' convincing myself I work best under pressure. But lately, indulgence has turned into annoyance. One sleepless night, I worried, 'What if I keep deferring everything until it’s too late?'

After sharing my concerns with a novelist friend, I was advised to contact Fiona Harrold, a personal coach and business mentor. She said, 'People who procrastinate are often high achievers who set high standards for themselves, but perversely never feel good enough. They’re often creative, and their work feels personal, making them anxious and afraid of being judged. Putting off tasks feels easier, but eventually you have to rush, which feels worse.'

She referred to 'second novel syndrome,' where fear of not measuring up makes it hard to write a follow-up book. Author Elizabeth Gilbert, who wrote 'Eat, Pray, Love,' was relieved when her second book failed, as it freed her from expectations.

Perfectionism and poor time perception feed procrastination. Fiona explained that many people feel they need a certain uninterrupted time frame to do something well. If they can't find it, they put things off. 'Drop that idea and you'll get things done faster—sometimes it's better to finish things imperfectly than to never finish at all.'

How can we stop procrastinating? Fiona recommends giving ourselves shorter deadlines, as work expands to fill available time. If a real deadline is lacking, just create one. Start with the task you want to postpone, even if only for 15 minutes—committing to a brief effort makes it less daunting.

She also noted our shrinking attention spans, thanks to the internet, smartphones, and screens everywhere. No one feels like exercising at first, but committing to just 15 minutes can make it manageable—and you might end up doing more.

Accountability helps, too. Research shows people are more likely to succeed with goals if they share them with others and build support networks. Fiona advises against labeling yourself a procrastinator—others' expectations tend to shape our behavior.

For less important tasks, like ironing or organizing a wardrobe, consider delegating, or commit to doing them for just 15 minutes, perhaps with a reward at the end.

Inspired, I told my husband I was done with procrastinating—he looked skeptical but I applied the 15-minute rule. It works: most tasks are bearable for a short while, and once you start, anxiety fades and you get on with it. I tidied the dolls' house with my daughter, cleared papers off my desk, sent overdue emails, and paid bills.

Procrastination may feel like a treat, but as Fiona says, it wears you out. The good news? You can overcome it—so stop putting it off. You can find more helpful advice at howcast.com.

Por Catherine Ostler

Como escritora y exeditora de revistas, estoy acostumbrada a cumplir plazos. La mayoría lo estamos. Pero cuando una tarea no tiene un plazo definido, la cosa cambia: suelo terminar procrastinando.

Tome como ejemplo un trabajo reciente sin fecha límite clara. Primero, fui a comprar un capuchino, diciéndome que era para activar mi cerebro. Luego compré papel de regalo para un cumpleaños que debía entregar ese día. Es tan fácil encontrar razones para postergar el trabajo, convenciéndonos que otras cosas son urgentes, pero el pánico aparece rápido.

Ya en casa, llamé al médico antes de que cerraran para el almuerzo y estuve en espera hasta que me rendí. Después, pasé una hora mirando la web de una inmobiliaria local (no planeamos mudarnos; solo tenía curiosidad) y piqué restos en la nevera. Leí el diario (como supuesta investigación), me lavé el cabello, y le mandé un mensaje a alguien por un viejo problema en el techo. Hasta una revista gratis en la entrada me llamó la atención—más 'investigación.'

Perdí dos horas y sentí una creciente ansiedad. Todo parecía más urgente que mi verdadero trabajo. Aunque me decía que despejaba distracciones, el tiempo se evaporaba y empecé a ponerme nerviosa. Y no estoy sola: una cuarta parte dice que procrastinar es parte clave de su personalidad. Incluso en la antigüedad la gente posponía tareas—una revista informó que jeroglíficos egipcios del 1400 a.C. decían: 'Amigo, deja de posponer el trabajo y vámonos a casa a tiempo.'

Las redes sociales e internet parecen productivas, pero se pueden perder horas valiosas en línea. Mi lucha con la procrastinación es de toda la vida; en la escuela llenaba mi agenda de listas hasta que me abrumaba. En la universidad, invertía más tiempo haciendo horarios coloridos de repaso que estudiando de verdad. Incluso hay estudios que sugieren que estudiantes procrastinadores sufren más resfriados, gripes y problemas estomacales.

Me acostumbré a mi 'demonio personal', diciéndome que rindo mejor bajo presión. Pero últimamente esa indulgencia se transformó en molestia. Una noche, sin poder dormir, pensé: '¿Y si sigo aplazando todo hasta que sea demasiado tarde?'

Tras contarle mi preocupación a una amiga novelista, me recomendaron contactar a Fiona Harrold, coach personal y mentora. Ella dice: 'Quienes procrastinan suelen ser personas que se exigen mucho y nunca sienten que es suficiente. Muchas veces son creativos y su trabajo es personal, lo que genera ansiedad y miedo a ser juzgados. Postergar se siente fácil, pero después hay que hacer todo de golpe y es peor.'

Fiona mencionó el 'síndrome de la segunda novela', cuando el miedo a no cumplir expectativas bloquea a los escritores. La autora Elizabeth Gilbert, de 'Eat, Pray, Love', se sintió aliviada al fallar con su segundo libro, pues eso la liberó de la presión.

El perfeccionismo y la mala percepción del tiempo alimentan la procrastinación. Explicó que muchos creen necesitar un tiempo ininterrumpido para hacer bien algo. Si no lo encuentran, lo posponen. 'Suelta esa idea y terminarás las cosas más rápido—mejor hacerlo imperfecto que no hacerlo.'

¿Cómo dejar de procrastinar? Fiona sugiere fijar plazos cortos porque el trabajo se expande al tiempo que se le da. Si no hay una fecha real, inventa una. Empieza por lo que más evitas, aunque sea 15 minutos—es menos intimidante hacerlo poco tiempo.

También señaló que nuestra atención es más corta por internet y pantallas. Nadie tiene ganas de hacer ejercicio de entrada, pero si te propones 15 minutos, es manejable y puede que hagas más.

La responsabilidad ayuda. Los estudios muestran que quienes comparten sus metas y cuentan con apoyo tienen más éxito. Además, Fiona recomienda no etiquetarte como procrastinador: las expectativas ajenas influyen mucho.

Para tareas menores, como planchar o arreglar el armario, delega si puedes o hazlas solo 15 minutos, quizá prometiéndote un premio.

Inspirada, le dije a mi esposo que dejaría la procrastinación—él fue escéptico, pero usé la regla de los 15 minutos. Funciona: la mayoría de las tareas no cuestan tanto en poco tiempo y, al empezar, la ansiedad desaparece y sigues adelante. Ordené la casa de muñecas con mi hija, tiré papeles viejos, envié emails pendientes y pagué cuentas.

La procrastinación puede sentirse como premio, pero como dice Fiona, te agota. Lo bueno es que puedes superarla—¡deja de posponer! Para más consejos útiles, visita howcast.com.

article_content: Steve McManaman is optimistic that Raheem Sterling and England’s young players can make a significant impact at the 2014 World Cup, while also gaining valuable experience for future tournaments. The former Liverpool and Real Madrid midfielder believes the nation often puts excessive pressure on its players at major tournaments but supports Roy Hodgson’s squad selection for Brazil. McManaman expects that Sterling, Ross Barkley, Luke Shaw, and other promising young stars will benefit from the World Cup experience, making them better prepared for Euro 2016 in France and the World Cup in Russia in 2018. He said, 'I hope someone lights up the World Cup for England, and that player could be Raheem Sterling. Sterling had a fantastic season with Liverpool and has shown great progress. Both he and Adam Lallana can make things happen for England.' With 37 international caps and experience in three major tournaments, McManaman values tournament exposure. He added, 'We have several players with a lot of potential, but I try not to put too much pressure on the younger players because as a nation, we tend to overhype them.' He believes the main objective is for England’s young players to learn from the World Cup, helping them develop for future challenges: 'If six of them light up the World Cup and England win, that would be amazing, but realistically, winning this time may be a step too far. The journey and experience are what matters most, and in two years, they'll perform even better at the Euros in France.' McManaman spoke at the opening of the Lucozade Sport Conditions Zone at Canary Wharf in London, designed to replicate the hot and humid conditions England’s players will encounter against Italy in Manaus on June 14. At the launch, McManaman participated in five-a-side games in 32°C heat and 76% humidity, describing the conditions as ‘very difficult’. He noted that while England is preparing in Miami, nothing fully compares to Manaus’s climate. The Lucozade Sport Conditions Zone, created by England’s official sports drink partner, simulates Manaus’s climate using increased heat and humidity. Teams can play for free, receive scientific analysis, and have their performance metrics tracked by STATSports Technologies.

article_content: During a recent debate at the United Nations Security Council led by China, India underscored the significance of fair, transparent, and sustainable international financing, cautioning that poor lending practices could lock nations into damaging debt cycles. India's UN Counsellor R Madhu Sudan observed that ongoing financial shortfalls make prospects for peace and development challenging. He pointed to India’s advocacy for reforms in International Financial Institutions, particularly during its G20 presidency, as part of steps to tackle these issues. India cited situations like the lack of equal access to vaccines during COVID-19 and rising costs of essential goods as evidence that the needs of developing countries are sometimes overlooked in global frameworks. The country pressed for more proportional representation of the Global South’s interests in global governance, including within the UN Security Council. India also indirectly referenced China’s lending activities, cautioning Indian Ocean countries to be aware of potential pitfalls in taking on infrastructure projects or loans that might prove unsustainable. The case of Sri Lanka’s Hambantota port—financed and later effectively controlled by China due to debt repayment issues—was noted as a cautionary example. The importance of international cooperation and reforming multilateral organizations was another focus, with Madhu Sudan emphasizing that the Security Council should concentrate on its foundational duties rather than extending into areas overseen by other UN bodies. To close, India called on nations to maintain commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals for 2030, warning that losing focus on these benchmarks through selective priorities could derail much-needed progress. These comments were made alongside the 2023 SDG Summit, where global leaders called for more urgent, transformative action.

German Chancellor Olaf Scholz has stated that up to 14,000 Nigerians residing in Germany may face deportation, primarily because of an uptick in asylum applications from Nigerian nationals lacking valid identification. According to Scholz, around 12,500 Nigerians are currently in Germany with temporary 'tolerated' status since Nigeria is reluctant to receive individuals without proper ID documentation. During a meeting in Abuja with President Bola Tinubu, Scholz voiced concerns about the increase in asylum requests in 2023 and reaffirmed Germany's willingness to work closely with Nigeria on migration issues.

Scholz also indicated that Germany is open to repatriating Nigerian citizens who have adhered to rules and demonstrated good conduct. President Tinubu responded by expressing Nigeria’s openness to accept returning citizens if they are identified as Nigerians and have 'behaved well.' Tinubu and Scholz signaled intentions to strengthen cooperation to address deportation matters.

Tinubu further remarked that Nigeria is committed to reintegrating returnees under these conditions but suggested that such returns should be mutually beneficial. He noted that development funding from Germany, totaling 640 million euros, could be reconsidered if constructive progress is not made.

Historically, Nigeria has been among the leading countries of origin for asylum seekers in Germany, though the share of Nigerian applicants has been decreasing recently.

article_content: LANSING, Mich. — Michigan is joining a nationwide effort to curb deceptive uses of artificial intelligence and manipulated media through state-level policies, as Congress and the Federal Elections Commission continue to debate broader regulations ahead of the 2024 elections. Under legislation expected to be signed in the coming days by Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, political campaigns at both the state and federal level will be required to disclose which political advertisements airing in Michigan were created using artificial intelligence. The legislation would also prohibit the use of AI-generated deepfakes within 90 days of an election unless there is a clear disclosure identifying the media as manipulated. Deepfakes are fabricated media that falsely depict someone as doing or saying something they did not. These are made using generative artificial intelligence, a form of AI that can rapidly create convincing images, videos, or audio. Concerns are growing that generative AI could be used in the 2024 presidential race to mislead voters, impersonate candidates, and disrupt elections on a previously unseen scale. Candidates and committees have already experimented with this quickly advancing technology, which is now more accessible to the public. In April, the Republican National Committee released an entirely AI-generated ad portraying a hypothetical future if President Joe Biden is reelected. The ad disclosed in small print that it was made with AI and featured fake but realistic images of boarded-up storefronts, armored military patrols, and large increases in immigration causing panic. In July, Never Back Down, a super PAC supporting Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, used AI voice cloning to mimic former President Donald Trump's voice, making it seem as if he had narrated a social media post he never actually said. Experts warn that these examples are just a preview of what might happen if campaigns or outside actors use AI deepfakes more maliciously. So far, California, Minnesota, Texas, and Washington have passed laws regulating deepfakes in political ads. According to the nonprofit Public Citizen, similar legislation has been proposed in Illinois, New Jersey, and New York. Michigan's proposed law requires anyone distributing a candidate advertisement to clearly disclose if it uses generative AI. For print ads, the disclosure must use the same size font as most of the ad's text. For television ads, the statement must appear for at least four seconds in letters as large as most of the ad's text, according to a Michigan House Fiscal Agency analysis. Deepfakes used within 90 days of an election would require an additional disclaimer to inform viewers that the content was manipulated to show speech or actions that did not happen. For video, this disclaimer would need to be visible throughout the entire video. Campaigns found in violation could face a misdemeanor, punishable by up to 93 days in jail, a fine of up to $1,000, or both for the first offense. The attorney general or a candidate harmed by the media can also seek relief in circuit court. Federal lawmakers from both parties have emphasized the importance of regulating deepfakes in political ads and have held discussions, though no federal law has yet passed. A recent bipartisan Senate bill co-sponsored by Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO) would ban 'materially deceptive' deepfakes about federal candidates, with exceptions for parody and satire. Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson traveled to Washington, D.C. in early November to join a bipartisan discussion on AI and elections, urging senators to pass the Deceptive AI Act and to support similar state-level efforts. Benson emphasized that federal law's capacity to regulate AI at the state and local levels is limited, and that states need federal funding to address AI-related challenges, especially for hiring staff to handle AI and educating voters about deepfakes. In August, the Federal Election Commission began considering whether to regulate AI-generated deepfakes in political ads under its existing policies against fraudulent misrepresentation, following a petition from Public Citizen. The commission collected public comments but has not made a decision. Major social media companies are also adopting policies to slow the spread of harmful deepfakes. Meta, which owns Facebook and Instagram, announced that political ads on its platforms will be required to disclose if they were created using AI. Google introduced a similar labeling rule in September for political ads on YouTube and other platforms. translated_content: LANSING, Michigan — Michigan se suma a un esfuerzo nacional para frenar el uso engañoso de la inteligencia artificial y medios manipulados mediante políticas estatales, mientras el Congreso y la Comisión Federal de Elecciones siguen debatiendo regulaciones más amplias antes de las elecciones de 2024. Según la legislación que la gobernadora demócrata Gretchen Whitmer se espera firme en los próximos días, las campañas políticas en los niveles estatal y federal deberán revelar qué anuncios políticos que se transmiten en Michigan fueron creados usando inteligencia artificial. La legislación también prohibiría el uso de deepfakes generados por IA dentro de los 90 días previos a una elección, salvo que haya una divulgación clara indicando que el material fue manipulado. Los deepfakes son medios fabricados que muestran a alguien haciendo o diciendo algo que no hizo. Se crean mediante inteligencia artificial generativa, que puede generar rápidamente imágenes, videos o audios convincentes. Preocupa cada vez más que la IA generativa pueda usarse en las elecciones presidenciales de 2024 para engañar a electores, suplantar candidatos y afectar las elecciones a una escala nunca antes vista. Los candidatos y comités ya han hecho pruebas con esta tecnología, que ahora está más al alcance del público. En abril, el Comité Nacional Republicano lanzó un anuncio creado completamente con IA que mostraba un futuro hipotético si el presidente Joe Biden es reelegido. Avisando en letra pequeña que era hecho con IA, el anuncio incluía imágenes falsas pero realistas de tiendas cerradas, patrullas militares y un gran aumento en la inmigración generando pánico. En julio, Never Back Down, un súper PAC que apoya al gobernador de Florida Ron DeSantis, utilizó clonación de voz con IA para imitar la voz del expresidente Donald Trump, haciendo creer que él narró una publicación en redes sociales que nunca dijo. Expertos advierten que estos casos son solo una muestra de lo que podría suceder si campañas u otros actores usan deepfakes de IA de forma más maliciosa. Hasta ahora, California, Minnesota, Texas y Washington han aprobado leyes que regulan deepfakes en anuncios políticos. Según la organización sin fines de lucro Public Citizen, legislaciones similares se han planteado en Illinois, Nueva Jersey y Nueva York. La ley propuesta de Michigan exige que cualquier persona o entidad que distribuya anuncios de candidaturas indique claramente si utiliza IA generativa. Para anuncios impresos, la advertencia debe ser en el mismo tamaño de letra que el resto del texto. En televisión, la declaración debe aparecer al menos cuatro segundos, en letras tan grandes como la mayoría del texto, según análisis de la Cámara Fiscal de Michigan. Deepfakes utilizados dentro de los 90 días previos a una elección requerirán un aviso adicional que informe al público que el contenido fue manipulado para mostrar palabras o acciones que no ocurrieron. Si es un video, la advertencia debe estar visible todo el tiempo. Las campañas que incumplan pueden enfrentar un delito menor de hasta 93 días de cárcel, una multa de hasta $1,000 dólares, o ambos, en la primera infracción. El fiscal general o un candidato afectado también pueden recurrir a la corte de circuito. Legisladores federales de ambos partidos han resaltado la importancia de regular deepfakes en anuncios políticos y han tenido debates, pero aún no hay ley federal. Un reciente proyecto bipartidista en el Senado, copatrocinado por la senadora Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) y el senador Josh Hawley (R-MO), prohibiría deepfakes 'materialmente engañosos' sobre candidatos federales, salvo para parodias y sátira. La secretaria de Estado de Michigan, Jocelyn Benson, viajó a Washington D.C. a principios de noviembre para una charla bipartidista sobre IA y elecciones, y pidió a los senadores aprobar la Ley de IA Engañosa y apoyar esfuerzos estatales similares. Benson destacó que las leyes federales no tienen mucha capacidad para regular la IA a nivel estatal y local, y que los estados necesitan fondos federales, en especial para contratar personal para enfrentar la IA y educar a los electores sobre deepfakes. En agosto, la Comisión Federal de Elecciones comenzó a considerar si debe regular los deepfakes creados por IA en anuncios políticos bajo sus reglas contra la representación fraudulenta, tras una petición de Public Citizen. Recibió comentarios públicos, pero no ha tomado una decisión. Redes sociales grandes también suman políticas para frenar la expansión de deepfakes dañinos. Meta, dueña de Facebook e Instagram, dijo que los anuncios políticos deberán declarar si fueron creados con IA. Google presentó una política parecida en septiembre para anuncios políticos en YouTube y otras plataformas. According to leaked plans from Russia’s space agency, Russian cosmonauts could be living on the Moon by 2030. A draft government program outlines a three-phase plan for lunar exploration, ultimately aiming to construct a permanent Earth-monitoring observatory. The document stresses the urgency of securing a lunar presence before other countries, noting that "leading space powers will expand and establish their rights to convenient lunar footholds" within the next 20 to 30 years.

The plans, obtained by the Russian newspaper Izvestia and reported by the Moscow Times, describe an initial robotic mission to the Moon by 2016, a crewed mission by 2028, and the use of local resources to build a Moon base by 2030. Later phases involve constructing space- and Earth-monitoring observatories. While NASA remains focused on Mars despite facing years of budget cuts, Russia appears to prioritize lunar exploration and is taking a leading role in the emerging space race.

This initiative follows the United States’ increased reliance on Russian rockets for International Space Station missions after the U.S. space shuttle program ended in 2011. Just last month, a Soyuz rocket carried two Russian cosmonauts and a U.S. astronaut to the International Space Station, despite ongoing tensions over Ukraine and sanctions.

China, Japan, and India have also announced plans for forthcoming lunar missions. Russia’s space program, which sent the first human into space in 1961, remains at the forefront and is currently the only nation with explicit plans for crewed lunar missions.

Recently, Roscosmos announced the development of “super rockets” capable of lifting up to 120 tons into orbit. The latest report was prepared by the Russian Academy of Sciences, Roscosmos, Moscow State University, and several other research institutes. The proposal considers international cooperation but emphasizes the importance of maintaining independence in the national lunar program, regardless of foreign participation.

The document builds on earlier plans introduced by Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Rogozin, who stated, "We are coming to the Moon forever." In a government newspaper article, Rogozin described the Moon not just as a step in a new space race, but as a self-contained goal. While Mars and asteroid missions are mentioned, Rogozin asserted that establishing a lunar base is a necessary first step for research and experimentation. He reiterated the permanence of Russia’s lunar ambitions: "We are coming to the Moon forever."

Russia has a prominent space history, including the first intercontinental ballistic missile, first satellite and first animal in space (1957), first human in space (1961), first spacewalk (1965), first unmanned Moon landing (1966), and the first space station (1971). The U.S. achieved the first crewed Moon landing in 1969 with Neil Armstrong.

article_content: In mid-September, TIME interviewed Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur. After a political struggle spanning 25 years—including imprisonment and repression—Anwar assumed power following a divisive election last November. Nearly a year into his role, as public excitement fades and Malaysia’s well-known opposition figure becomes a statesman, he faces challenges stabilizing the political landscape, reviving the economy, and addressing the rise of Islamist politics that is polarizing society. The interview took place in the Malaysian Houses of Parliament, shortly before Anwar addressed lawmakers during a contentious session. The Malaysian Islamic Party (PAS), now the largest party in Parliament, staged a walkout after heated debate over allegations of judicial interference involving a political ally. This incident highlighted one of Anwar’s key challenges: managing a 'unity government' formed of various coalitions, while keeping PAS out of government. PAS has continued to gain support, winning more seats in recent state elections, and its growing influence underscores the rise of Malay-Islamist rhetoric dividing the multi-ethnic society. Former Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad—once known for secular leadership and now often seen on PAS platforms—has criticized Anwar, claiming that a multiracial Malaysia is unconstitutional and accusing him of favoring 'outsiders,' a term referring to Chinese and Indian minorities. Racial and religious identity lies at the heart of Malaysian politics. Malaysia’s majority Malays, who are Muslims by law, benefit from quotas in education, employment, and business via longstanding affirmative action policies. Some Malay-Islamist groups stoke fears about losing these privileges. Anwar discussed the resurgence of identity politics, Malaysia’s role in the U.S.-China rivalry, and his efforts to enhance democracy. He once called Malaysia a tragic example of democratic backsliding in Southeast Asia, after being denied power despite winning the historic 2018 election that ended UMNO’s decades-long rule. For Anwar, restoring democracy requires strengthening institutions and accountability. He highlighted reforms, transparency in government contracts, and the formation of parliamentary committees for oversight. He emphasized that the judiciary has operated independently, with no interference in appointments or cases. The interview occurred a day after Anwar returned from China—his second official visit as Prime Minister—and before he departed to New York for the UN General Assembly. Malaysia’s ties with China and the U.S. were discussed, especially given Malaysia’s recent rejection of China’s updated 'standard map' that claims nearly the entire South China Sea, including Malaysian waters off Borneo. Anwar said he raised the issue at an ASEAN summit, and Premier Li Keqiang assured respect for other countries’ claims. Anwar pointed out that while issues with China remain, diplomatic engagement has been effective, as China has shown restraint in disputed waters after Malaysia’s protests. With the U.S., Anwar stressed ongoing cooperation while rejecting intimidation. He cited Malaysia’s decision to allow both Ericsson and Huawei to supply the national 5G network, despite security concerns raised by U.S. and EU envoys. Anwar’s administration reviewed and eventually endorsed a dual-network approach, prioritizing transparency and national interest. To counter PAS’s influence, Anwar prioritizes economic development and social welfare, allocating nearly $2 billion in cash assistance for low-income Malaysians and launching a $5.3 billion fund for renewable energy and green technology. He recently secured investment from Tesla for their regional headquarters. Education is also key to addressing extremism, bigotry, and ignorance, and Anwar stresses the importance of Malaysia’s diversity, arguing there is no reason for religion or race to become sources of hostility. Although PAS previously allied with Anwar during his reformasi movement, their relationship is strained, largely due to differences in leadership and PAS’s increasingly hardline stance. Anwar indicated he is open to cooperation so long as core principles are upheld, asserting, 'Islam is the religion of the Federation, but this is a multireligious country and every citizen should feel they belong.' He stated, 'No one should be discriminated against or marginalized.' When asked about reconciling with PAS, Anwar said there has been neither a clear rejection nor a positive response, and the political climate remains tense. Any potential cooperation would depend on acceptance of key policy conditions.

Citó la decisión de Malasia de permitir que tanto Ericsson como Huawei participen en la red nacional 5G, pese a preocupaciones de seguridad de enviados de EE.UU. y la UE. La educación también es clave contra el extremismo y la intolerancia, y Anwar resalta la importancia de la diversidad, afirmando que no hay razón para que la religión o la raza generen hostilidad. NAIROBI, Kenya — The European Union has pledged €650 million in assistance to Ethiopia, nearly three years after suspending direct aid to the East African country due to atrocities committed during a violent civil war. Jutta Urpilainen, the EU Commissioner for International Partnerships, announced the agreement at a press conference with Ethiopian Finance Minister Ahmed Shide in Addis Ababa on Tuesday.

"It is time to gradually normalize relations and rebuild a mutually reinforcing partnership with your country," Urpilainen said, describing the aid package as "the first concrete step" in this process following the cease-fire that ended the war last November.

The EU aid package was initially valued at €1 billion (about $1.04 billion) and was intended for Ethiopia from 2021 to 2027, but was suspended in late 2020 when fighting erupted in the northern Tigray region. The U.S. also halted assistance and enacted sanctions.

Finance Minister Shide stated that the aid would support Ethiopia’s post-war recovery and enable much-needed economic reforms at a "critical juncture" for the country. "This strategic partnership is now back on track," he added.

However, direct budgetary support for Ethiopia’s government remains suspended and will not resume until "very clear political conditions" are met, according to Urpilainen, who did not specify these conditions. She also noted that an International Monetary Fund (IMF) program would be required first.

Earlier on Tuesday, Urpilainen held meetings with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and Moussa Faki Mahamat, Chairperson of the African Union Commission.

The Tigray war resulted in thousands of deaths and was marked by massacres, mass rape, and reports of forced starvation. The EU has consistently insisted it would not fully normalize relations with Ethiopia without accountability for these crimes. Ethiopia has attempted to block a United Nations investigation into the atrocities and has initiated its own transitional justice process, which human rights experts consider flawed. The UN has stated that all sides committed abuses, some of which may constitute war crimes.

The EU’s renewed aid pledge was announced a day before the deadline for renewing the UN Human Rights Council’s investigation mandate in Geneva. On Tuesday, UN experts warned that more independent investigations into Ethiopia’s "dire human rights situation" are necessary, highlighting the "overwhelming risk of future atrocities."

"There is a very real and imminent risk that the situation will deteriorate further, and it is incumbent upon the international community to ensure that investigations persist so human rights violations can be addressed, and the worst tragedies averted," said Steven Ratner, a UN expert.

A UN panel report last month cited "grave and ongoing" atrocities in Tigray and questioned Ethiopian officials' commitment to ensuring genuine accountability. Last week, Human Rights Watch urged the EU to submit a resolution at the UN Human Rights Council calling for continued investigations into atrocities. "Not doing so would be renouncing its own commitments," the group said.
