Jutta Urpilainen, comisaria de la UE para asociaciones internacionales, anunció el acuerdo en una conferencia de prensa junto con el ministro de Finanzas etíope Ahmed Shide en Addis Abeba el martes.

"Es hora de normalizar gradualmente las relaciones y reconstruir una asociación mutuamente beneficiosa con su país", dijo Urpilainen, describiendo el paquete de ayuda como "el primer paso concreto" en este proceso tras el alto el fuego que puso fin a la guerra el noviembre pasado.

El paquete de ayuda de la UE estaba valorado inicialmente en 1.000 millones de euros (unos 1.040 millones de dólares) y estaba destinado a Etiopía de 2021 a 2027, pero se suspendió a finales de 2020 cuando estallaron los combates en la región norteña de Tigray. El ministro de Finanzas Shide afirmó que la ayuda apoyará la recuperación de Etiopía tras la guerra y permitirá reformas económicas muy necesarias en un "momento crítico" para el país. "Esta asociación estratégica está nuevamente en marcha", añadió.

Sin embargo, la ayuda presupuestaria directa al gobierno etíope sigue suspendida y no se reanudará hasta que se cumplan "condiciones políticas muy claras", según Urpilainen, quien no especificó cuáles. También señaló que primero se requeriría un programa del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI).

Más temprano el martes, Urpilainen mantuvo reuniones con el primer ministro etíope Abiy Ahmed y Moussa Faki Mahamat, presidente de la Comisión de la Unión Africana.

La guerra en Tigray dejó miles de muertos y estuvo marcada por masacres, violaciones masivas y reportes de hambruna forzada. La UE ha insistido continuamente en que no normalizaría completamente sus relaciones con Etiopía sin que haya rendición de cuentas por estos crímenes. Etiopía ha intentado bloquear una investigación de la ONU sobre las atrocidades y ha iniciado su propio proceso de justicia transicional, que expertos en derechos humanos consideran defectuoso. La ONU ha indicado que todas las partes cometieron abusos, algunos de los cuales podrían constituir crímenes de guerra.

El martes, expertos de la ONU advirtieron que se necesitan más investigaciones independientes sobre la "grave situación de derechos humanos" en Etiopía, señalando el "abrumador riesgo de futuras atrocidades".

"Existe un riesgo real e inminente de que la situación empeore aún más, y es responsabilidad de la comunidad internacional asegurar que continúen las investigaciones para que se puedan abordar las violaciones de derechos humanos y se eviten las peores tragedias", dijo Steven Ratner, experto de la ONU.

Un informe de un panel de la ONU del mes pasado citó "atrocidades graves y continuas" en Tigray y cuestionó el compromiso de las autoridades etíopes para garantizar una verdadera rendición de cuentas. La semana pasada, Human Rights Watch instó a la UE a presentar una resolución en el Consejo de Derechos Humanos de la ONU para que sigan las investigaciones sobre las atrocidades. "No hacerlo sería renunciar a sus propios compromisos", indicó la organización.

article_content: Eating out has become a regular part of life for many people, thanks to our packed schedules and fast-paced routines. While visiting restaurants is convenient, the issue isn't eating out itself but rather the kinds of food we order. Most menus are designed to appeal to our taste buds, often overlooking the nutritional value of the dishes. Certain words on a menu can hint at how unhealthy an item might be. Terms like crunchy, battered, crispy, breaded, or tempura usually mean the food is fried, which increases its calorie and fat content. For example, a 4-ounce chicken breast that is grilled, baked, or roasted typically has around 170 calories, but if it's deep-fried, that number jumps to about 370. Plus, some restaurants use oils with trans fats, which can raise bad cholesterol and lower the good kind, increasing the risk for heart problems. Watch for sugary items too. Words such as BBQ, glazed, sticky, teriyaki, or honey-dipped often indicate sauces laden with added sugars. Even seemingly healthy sides like couscous or quinoa are high in carbohydrates, so they should be eaten in moderation, just like pasta, potatoes, or rice. Menu descriptions such as loaded, creamy, cheesy, or smothered can be signs that something is packed with calories, even if it's marketed as a comfort food. These tempting terms might make a dish sound irresistible but usually signal a high-calorie meal. To make healthier choices, look for dishes that are roasted, baked, broiled, poached, steamed, or grilled. Many restaurants now offer more nutritious menu choices, sometimes even customizing meals or using local ingredients. Don't hesitate to ask questions or look up nutritional information so you can enjoy your meal with both flavor and health in mind.

Aunque visitar restaurantes es conveniente, el problema no es salir a comer en sí, sino los tipos de comida que pedimos. La mayoría de los menús están diseñados para atraer a nuestro paladar, muchas veces dejando de lado el valor nutricional de los platos. Ciertas palabras en un menú pueden indicar cuán poco saludable puede ser un platillo. Términos como crujiente, empanizado, apanado, rebozado o tempura generalmente significan que la comida está frita, lo que aumenta su contenido calórico y de grasa. Por ejemplo, una pechuga de pollo de 113 gramos asada, horneada o a la parrilla suele tener unas 170 calorías, pero si está frita esa cifra sube a unas 370. Además, algunos restaurantes utilizan aceites con grasas trans, que pueden subir el colesterol malo y bajar el bueno, incrementando el riesgo de problemas cardiacos. Ten cuidado también con los alimentos azucarados. Palabras como barbacoa, glaseado, pegajoso, teriyaki o bañados en miel suelen indicar salsas con azúcares añadidos. Incluso algunas guarniciones que parecen saludables, como el cuscús o la quinoa, son altas en carbohidratos, así que deben consumirse con moderación, igual que la pasta, las papas o el arroz. Descripciones como relleno, cremoso, con queso o cubierto pueden ser señales de que un platillo está cargado de calorías, aunque se presente como comida reconfortante. Estos términos pueden hacer que un plato suene irresistible, pero normalmente indican que se trata de una comida alta en calorías. Para hacer elecciones más saludables, busca platos asados, al horno, a la parrilla, pochados, al vapor o a la plancha. Muchos restaurantes ahora ofrecen opciones más nutritivas, a veces personalizando los platillos o usando ingredientes locales. No dudes en hacer preguntas o consultar información nutricional para disfrutar de tu comida pensando tanto en el sabor como en la salud.

World champion Valentino Rossi marked an impressive return to the MotoGP circuit by finishing fourth in his first race since suffering a broken leg six weeks ago. Spaniard Dani Pedrosa, riding for Honda, claimed victory at the German Grand Prix in Sachsenring, finishing ahead of Rossi’s Yamaha teammate Jorge Lorenzo. Former world champion Casey Stoner narrowly beat Rossi to third place in a thrilling conclusion, overtaking the Italian on the final corner and denying the crowd of 98,000 the chance to see Rossi claim a podium finish on crutches.

Despite his recent injury, Rossi raced for personal satisfaction, stating to the official MotoGP website, 'It was easier with a broken leg, and very comfortable from a psychological perspective, because I was there to enjoy myself as I'm no longer in contention for the championship.'

Earlier in the event, a three-bike crash involving French rider Randy de Puniet, who sustained a double leg fracture, caused a race stoppage. The restarted 21-lap race gave Pedrosa his second win of the season, reducing Lorenzo’s lead in the championship standings. 'When they stopped, I wasn't sure about the restart. When you stop and restart it's never the same thing, but for me it was good,' said Pedrosa.

Lorenzo settled for the runner-up spot, recognizing Pedrosa’s superior pace. 'Pedrosa got more pace than me, it was impossible to follow him. He's done a splendid race, so I'm happy with second place, it's very positive for the championship.'

Much attention centered on Rossi, who had missed four races after breaking his tibia in a crash at Mugello 42 days prior, which significantly diminished his hopes of defending his world title. His battle with long-time rival Stoner kept fans captivated. 'I did the best I could this afternoon. I thought Valentino was going to get me but I dragged everything I could out of my bike to get past him,' said Stoner.

Lorenzo leads the championship standings with 185 points, holding a 47-point advantage over Pedrosa, with Rossi in sixth place on 74 points.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed fresh guidelines aimed at restricting how loan recovery agents interact with borrowers. Under these draft rules, agents are prohibited from contacting borrowers or guarantors about overdue loans before 8 am or after 7 pm.

RBI’s proposals require all its regulated entities—including banks, NBFCs, regional rural banks, housing finance providers, and cooperative banks—to develop board-approved codes of conduct for their direct sales, marketing, and recovery agents. These agents must be properly trained to ensure sensitive, respectful customer interactions, safeguard privacy, and provide clear and accurate information about products, while strictly avoiding harassment.

The RBI stressed that regulated entities and their agents must not engage in intimidation, abuse, or any actions that could humiliate or violate the privacy of borrowers and their families. Specifically, threatening messages, persistent or anonymous calls, and misleading information are not allowed.

These recommendations come as part of the RBI’s effort to protect borrowers following reports of aggressive recovery practices, including cases allegedly leading to suicides. For example, in September last year, the RBI temporarily barred Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services from outsourcing recovery activities after reports emerged that a pregnant woman in Jharkhand died during a repossession incident. This restriction was reversed in January.

The draft guidelines also state that lenders wanting to outsource services must have a comprehensive, board-approved outsourcing policy. Even when third parties are involved, boards and senior management remain accountable for risk management. Crucial activities—such as credit approvals or monitoring compliance with KYC norms—cannot be outsourced, ensuring lenders themselves make final decisions. The RBI is inviting stakeholder comments on these proposals until November 28, 2023.

Específicamente, se prohíben los mensajes amenazantes, las llamadas persistentes o anónimas y la difusión de información engañosa.

Esta restricción fue revertida en enero.

Las directrices también establecen que los prestamistas que deseen subcontratar servicios deben contar con una política integral de subcontratación aprobada por el consejo directivo. Aun cuando se involucren terceros, el consejo y la alta dirección siguen siendo responsables de la administración de riesgos. Las actividades cruciales, como aprobar créditos o verificar el cumplimiento de normas KYC, no pueden ser subcontratadas; deben ser decididas internamente por la entidad. article_content: The MIA Market in Rome, regarded as a prominent precursor to Mipcom Cannes, is concluding after an eventful week. Delegates from across the globe, including notable U.S. executives, gathered in the Piazza Barberini’s cinema screening rooms to discuss the industry's tumultuous year and explore paths back to normalcy. This occurred against the backdrop of ongoing conflict between Israel and Hamas, whose impact was felt at the event. Throughout the week, optimism prevailed inside the Cinema Barberini’s halls, even as industry leaders reflected on recent crises, such as dual U.S. labor strikes and uncertainties in the streaming sector. American executives like Paramount’s Nicole Clemens, Miramax’s Marc Helwig, and Anonymous Content’s Davids Levine and Davoli addressed the forum. Although last-minute changes in SAG-AFTRA demands created considerable uncertainty, keynote speakers adopted a forward-looking perspective. Helwig predicted a 'new world order' for the industry, emphasizing lower budgets and further market contraction—a theme echoed by various executives. Pulse Head of Scripted Judy Counihan forecasted a significant contraction, referencing an overabundance of content produced during the streaming boom. Severance executive producer Nicholas Weinstock observed that U.S. agencies now resemble portfolio managers due to their sheer number of clients. Despite the challenges, many believed the contraction could offer opportunities, including making space for new talent. Levine (Anonymous Content) emphasized the company's efforts to introduce fresh filmmakers. Nevertheless, financing remains a pressing concern, with numerous panels dedicated to funding strategies, co-productions, and capital raising. European executives were among the most optimistic. Netflix’s Spain and Portugal chief highlighted Spain’s rising stature, boasting about local facilities and attracting global attention. On one panel, leaders from Mediawan, Sony, Studiocanal, and Universal International Studios cited Europe’s advantages—tax incentives, production hubs, supportive broadcasting ecologies, and a deep talent pool. Mediawan’s Elisabeth D’Arvieu said Europe holds a significant competitive edge, and interest in exporting to the U.S. is rising. One major announcement was the establishment of the 'New8': a broad collaboration involving public broadcasters from Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Nordic countries. This group aims to co-produce eight dramas annually, with contributions from each country. Although some at MIA voiced skepticism about the collaboration's complexity, the overall consensus is that public broadcasters remain vital. Norway’s NRK drama financing head emphasized maintaining relevance in a competitive landscape. MIA also expanded its focus on animation and factual TV, featuring sessions devoted to animation’s evolving role. Marge Dean of Skybound Entertainment advocated for recognizing animation beyond children’s and comedy, citing the success of Amazon Prime Video’s 'Invincible.' She noted that while AI poses some threat, it is manageable with proper oversight. The event took place during a somber time globally, following attacks by Hamas in Israel and the ensuing escalation. The conflict impacted attendance, and Oscar-nominated director Ari Folman (scheduled to keynote on animated documentaries) withdrew from the event. The following week’s Mipcom Cannes is expected to further highlight the situation in the Middle East. With a new report on Italian film and TV due soon, the MIA Market broadened its focus and reinforced its reputation as a leading industry forum despite global instability.

article_content: The second stage of the 101st Tour de France started in York on Sunday morning without Mark Cavendish, who withdrew after suffering a shoulder injury from his crash in Harrogate during the opening stage. Cavendish, 29, and a 25-time Tour stage winner, separated his AC joint after colliding with Australia’s Simon Gerrans (Orica-GreenEdge). The stage was won by Marcel Kittel (Giant-Shimano), who claimed the yellow jersey. This marks the first time since 2008—when Cavendish left to prepare for the Beijing Olympics—that he will not complete the Tour. As the race set off, riders passed notable landmarks such as York Minster and Bettys tea rooms, while crowds gathered along the streets to capture photos and cheer on the peloton. Chris Froome of Britain, last year’s champion, prepared to race watched by thousands at York Racecourse. Cavendish’s withdrawal leaves three Brits in the race: Froome, his Sky teammate Geraint Thomas, and Simon Yates of Orica-GreenEdge, as they began the 201km route from York to Sheffield. Stage two featured nine categorized climbs, including the tough category two ascent at Holme Moss, and a steep finish up Jenkin Road in Sheffield, which reaches a gradient of 33 percent. Jens Voigt (Trek Factory), the race’s oldest rider at 42, wore the King of the Mountains’ polka dot jersey after a solo breakaway on stage one. Once again, huge crowds lined the route through Yorkshire, with an estimated two million spectators on the opening day. A group of riders formed an early breakaway: Perrig Quemeneur (Europcar), Matthew Busche (Trek), Cyril Lemoine (Cofidis), David de la Cruz (NetApp), Armindo Fonseca (Bretagne), and Blel Kadri (AG2R), later joined by Bart De Clercq (Lotto-Belisol). Lemoine was first over the initial categorized climb at Blubberhouses. During this time, Kittel took a tumble trying to rejoin the peloton after answering a call of nature but regrouped without major issues. Lemoine and Quemeneur exchanged leads over subsequent climbs, with Lemoine taking the virtual lead in the King of the Mountains. Kadri attacked on the main climb up Holme Moss, ahead of Thomas Voeckler (Europcar), but stayed clear to the top, followed by Nicolas Edet (Cofidis). Team Sky rode together near the front to keep Chris Froome safe, especially as the narrow roads filled with energized fans. Behind, Kittel struggled, falling behind and later stopping due to a puncture.

Cavendish, de 29 años y con 25 victorias de etapa en el Tour, sufrió una separación de la articulación AC tras colisionar con el australiano Simon Gerrans (Orica-GreenEdge). La etapa fue ganada por Marcel Kittel (Giant-Shimano), quien se quedó con el maillot amarillo. Esta es la primera vez desde 2008—cuando Cavendish se retiró para prepararse para los Juegos Olímpicos de Pekín—que no completará el Tour. La segunda etapa contó con nueve ascensos categorizados, destacando la exigente subida de segunda categoría en Holme Moss y un final empinado en Jenkin Road, Sheffield, que alcanza una pendiente del 33 por ciento. El equipo Sky se mantuvo unido al frente del pelotón para proteger a Chris Froome, especialmente mientras las carreteras estrechas estaban llenas de aficionados entusiastas. Más atrás, Kittel tuvo dificultades, descolgándose del pelotón y luego deteniéndose por un pinchazo.

article_content: In County Durham, police have cautioned that children caught throwing snowballs at cars or at people without their consent could face arrest for anti-social behaviour. The Crook Neighbourhood Police Team posted the warning on Facebook, stating that anyone found aiming snowballs at vehicles, roads, homes, or unwilling individuals may be subject to legal action. While such offenses are usually dealt with via fixed penalty notices, the announcement was met with amusement and criticism by locals, who argued that snowball fights are a cherished tradition. Residents like Eddie Philips from Wolsingham and Paul Emmerton from Middlesbrough voiced their objections online, accusing the police of overreaching. Another local, Chris Clynes, recounted a recent snowball mishap in his own home, admitting he would have acted the same as a child. Police clarified that the message was intended to promote safety and prevent potential harm, not to prohibit snowball fights altogether, as risks could include property damage or injury. No arrests had occurred at the time of writing. The police warning was issued during a period of severe winter weather across England, with plummeting nighttime temperatures resulting in treacherous conditions on roads and pavements. Areas of Yorkshire saw lows of -8C, Norfolk experienced school and airport closures, and the AA and RAC reported increased vehicle breakdowns. The Highways Agency prepared 500 salt spreaders and snowploughs. The Met Office issued an amber weather warning for much of England, forecasting ongoing icy weather and the likelihood of further snow into the following week.
translated_content: En el condado de Durham, la policía ha advertido que los niños que sean atrapados lanzando bolas de nieve a coches o personas sin su consentimiento podrían ser arrestados por comportamiento antisocial. El equipo de policía de barrio de Crook publicó la advertencia en Facebook, señalando que cualquier persona que lance bolas de nieve a vehículos, carreteras, casas o a individuos que no quieran participar podría enfrentarse a acciones legales. Aunque normalmente estos delitos se sancionan con multas fijas, el anuncio fue recibido con burla y críticas por parte de los vecinos, quienes sostienen que las guerras de bolas de nieve son una tradición muy valorada. Residentes como Eddie Philips, de Wolsingham, y Paul Emmerton, de Middlesbrough, expresaron su desacuerdo en redes sociales, acusando a la policía de exagerar. Otro vecino, Chris Clynes, compartió un incidente reciente con una bola de nieve dentro de su hogar, admitiendo que él hubiera hecho lo mismo de niño. La policía aclaró que su mensaje era simplemente para promover la seguridad y prevenir daños, no prohibir las guerras de bolas de nieve, ya que los riesgos pueden incluir daños a la propiedad o lesiones. Hasta el momento de la publicación, no se habían producido arrestos. La advertencia policial se produjo durante un periodo de clima invernal severo en Inglaterra, con temperaturas nocturnas muy bajas que provocaron condiciones peligrosas en carreteras y aceras. En Yorkshire, se registraron mínimas de -8°C, en Norfolk cerraron escuelas y el aeropuerto, y la AA y la RAC reportaron un aumento de averías de vehículos. La Agencia de Carreteras preparó 500 esparcidores de sal y quitanieves. La Oficina Meteorológica emitió una alerta ámbar para gran parte de Inglaterra, pronosticando que las condiciones heladas continuarían y que es probable que la nieve persista la próxima semana.

article_content: French President Francois Hollande has called for an end to Western economic sanctions on Russia, stating that President Vladimir Putin has assured him there are no intentions to annex eastern Ukraine. Hollande emphasized that the sanctions 'must stop now' and expressed hope for progress in resolving the Ukraine crisis during international talks scheduled in Kazakhstan in ten days. The crisis in Ukraine has delayed France's delivery of two Mistral-class warships to Russia, leaving the 1.2 billion euro contract in limbo amid accusations of Russian interference in Ukraine's civil conflict. France could face significant fines if it fails to honor the agreement. In a two-hour interview with France Inter radio, Hollande said, 'I think the sanctions must stop now. They must be lifted if there is progress. If there is no progress, the sanctions will remain.' Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko is set to meet President Putin, along with German Chancellor Angela Merkel, at talks in Astana, Kazakhstan. Hollande stated he would only attend the meeting on January 15 if there is fresh progress and noted, 'If it is to meet and talk without making headway, it is not worth it.' Hollande highlighted the importance of maintaining dialogue with Putin but insisted, 'He must know where to stop, and it has been costly for him.' Sanctions from the European Union and the United States, combined with a sharp drop in oil prices, have caused the Russian rouble to fall by approximately 40% against the dollar. These punitive measures were imposed after Russia annexed Crimea and was accused of supporting separatism in eastern Ukraine—a claim Moscow denies. The conflict has resulted in over 4,700 deaths. Hollande pointed out Putin's assertion that Russia seeks influence, not annexation, in Ukraine, and emphasized France's demand that Russia respect Ukraine's territorial integrity and refrain from supporting separatists. France delayed the delivery of the high-tech Mistral-class vessels to Russia in November. Just before Christmas, roughly 400 Russian sailors who had trained on the ships departed France and returned home.

article_content: URUMQI, China (CNN) -- Several hundred people protested in Urumqi on Tuesday, calling for the release of relatives detained after weekend demonstrations by ethnic Uyghur residents in China's far western Xinjiang region. Eyewitnesses reported that a crowd of 200 to 300 people, mostly women and elderly individuals, gathered as local authorities led journalists through a neighborhood that was heavily damaged during recent riots. Riot police moved in to disperse the group as protesters shouted the names of family members they wanted released. This demonstration signals ongoing tension in the Xinjiang capital, where authorities say at least 156 people were killed and more than 1,000 injured during recent violent demonstrations. In southern China, police detained 15 suspects related to an incident that may have contributed to the violence in Urumqi, according to state-run media. Reports suggest Sunday's protest in Urumqi's predominantly Uyghur Bazaar district may have been prompted by ethnic violence in Guangdong province. At the Guangdong toy factory, a large fight broke out between Uyghur and Han workers, resulting in the reported deaths of two Uyghur workers. Authorities stated that order had been restored in Urumqi through the deployment of soldiers and anti-riot police. Curfews remained in place across major districts. By Tuesday morning, at least 1,434 suspects had been detained, according to the Xinhua news agency. Police had begun interrogations, with officials saying those convicted would face severe punishment. Thousands of Uyghurs protested on Sunday, expressing feelings of discrimination and dissatisfaction, which led to a heavy police presence and a city lockdown. State media reported that some protesters attacked passersby, set buses on fire, and blocked traffic, but did not provide detailed numbers or grievances. An eyewitness described the protest growing to over 1,000 people, including men, women, and children, all ethnic Uyghurs. Police tried to contain the crowd with street barriers, but demonstrators pushed them aside and threw rocks at cars and buses. Riot police reportedly used tear gas and fire hoses to disperse the crowd. Armored vehicles, fire trucks, and ambulances were seen, and gunshots were heard. Late Sunday, People's Liberation Army soldiers and riot police were deployed throughout Urumqi. Witnesses observed protesters being chased into alleys and detained. Xinjiang is home to many Uyghurs. Although China's constitution guarantees ethnic minorities certain rights and autonomy, Uyghurs commonly report discrimination by the Han majority. On Tuesday, tension was also high among Han residents, with groups gathering to guard shops until dispersed by police. The World Uyghur Congress, based in Munich, condemned the crackdown on what it called a peaceful protest, blaming authorities for failing to respond to the factory incident and for the harsh suppression of Uyghur demonstrators. They alleged that Chinese forces used tear gas, firearms, and armored vehicles to disperse protesters, resulting in deaths by shooting and beating. Some demonstrators reportedly were crushed by armored vehicles. Xinjiang officials attributed Sunday's violence to 'foreign forces.' Nur Bekri, the region's chairman, described the riots as premeditated crime organized from abroad, and specifically accused the World Uyghur Congress of incitement. The group denied these allegations. The World Uyghur Congress is led by Rebiya Kadeer, a former businesswoman detained in 1999 who moved to the United States in 2005. Chinese officials claim she helped incite unrest online, using the Guangdong factory fight to stoke ethnic tensions. On Tuesday, internet access was limited in Urumqi, with reporters unable to send messages or access the web from their hotels.

Testigos informaron que una multitud de 200 a 300 personas, en su mayoría mujeres y ancianos, se reunió mientras las autoridades locales guiaban a periodistas por un vecindario gravemente dañado durante los disturbios recientes. La policía antidisturbios intervino para dispersar al grupo mientras los manifestantes gritaban los nombres de los familiares que querían que fueran liberados. Esta manifestación señala las continuas tensiones en la capital de Xinjiang, donde las autoridades afirman que al menos 156 personas murieron y más de 1,000 resultaron heridas durante las recientes protestas violentas. En el sur de China, la policía detuvo a 15 sospechosos relacionados con un incidente que podría haber contribuido a la violencia en Urumqi, según los medios estatales. Informes sugieren que la protesta del domingo en el distrito Bazaar, predominantemente uigur, pudo haber sido motivada por la violencia étnica en la provincia de Guangdong. En una fábrica de juguetes de Guangdong, se produjo una gran pelea entre trabajadores uigures y han, que resultó en la muerte, según informes, de dos trabajadores uigures. Las autoridades afirmaron que el orden fue restablecido en Urumqi mediante el despliegue de soldados y policías antidisturbios. Se mantuvieron los toques de queda en los principales distritos. Para la mañana del martes, al menos 1.434 sospechosos habían sido detenidos, según la agencia Xinhua. La policía inició interrogatorios y las autoridades afirmaron que los condenados serían severamente castigados. Miles de uigures protestaron el domingo, expresando sentimientos de discriminación y descontento, lo que llevó a una fuerte presencia policial y al cierre de la ciudad. Los medios estatales informaron que algunos manifestantes atacaron a transeúntes, incendiaron autobuses y bloquearon el tráfico, pero no proporcionaron cifras ni detalles sobre sus quejas. Un testigo relató que la protesta creció a más de 1,000 personas, incluidos hombres, mujeres y niños, todos de etnia uigur. La policía intentó contener a la multitud con barricadas, pero los manifestantes las derribaron y arrojaron piedras a autos y autobuses. Según informes, la policía antidisturbios utilizó gases lacrimógenos y mangueras de agua para dispersar a la multitud. Se observaron vehículos blindados, camiones de bomberos y ambulancias, y se escucharon disparos. Ya entrada la noche del domingo, soldados del Ejército Popular de Liberación y la policía antidisturbios se desplegaron en Urumqi. Testigos vieron cómo los manifestantes eran perseguidos por callejones y detenidos. Xinjiang es hogar de muchos uigures. Aunque la constitución china garantiza ciertos derechos y autonomía a las minorías étnicas, los uigures suelen denunciar discriminación por parte de la mayoría han. El martes, también había tensión entre residentes han, que formaron grupos para proteger sus tiendas hasta ser dispersados por la policía. El Congreso Mundial Uigur, con sede en Múnich, condenó la represión sobre lo que calificó como una protesta pacífica, culpando a las autoridades por no responder al incidente en la fábrica y por la dura represión contra los manifestantes uigures. El grupo denunció que las fuerzas chinas utilizaron gases lacrimógenos, armas de fuego y vehículos blindados para dispersar a los manifestantes, lo que resultó en muertes por disparos y palizas. Según informes, algunos manifestantes fueron aplastados por vehículos blindados. Funcionarios de Xinjiang atribuyeron la violencia del domingo a 'fuerzas extranjeras'. Nur Bekri, jefe de la región, calificó los disturbios como un crimen premeditado organizado en el extranjero, y acusó específicamente al Congreso Mundial Uigur de incitación. El grupo negó estas acusaciones. El Congreso Mundial Uigur está liderado por Rebiya Kadeer, una exempresaria detenida en 1999 que se trasladó a Estados Unidos en 2005. Las autoridades chinas afirman que ayudó a incitar los disturbios en línea, usando la pelea en la fábrica de Guangdong para avivar tensiones étnicas. El martes, el acceso a internet era limitado en Urumqi y los reporteros no podían enviar mensajes ni navegar desde sus hoteles.

article_content: The much-anticipated trailer for 'Sam Bahadur' has been released, featuring Vicky Kaushal as legendary Field Marshal Sam Manekshaw. During the launch event at Delhi's Manekshaw Centre, Kaushal shared that he initially doubted he could portray Manekshaw, feeling he might not resemble him closely enough. Director Meghna Gulzar, who first talked about making the biopic with Kaushal during their work on 'Raazi,' ultimately chose him for this demanding role. The film spans over forty years of Manekshaw's distinguished military service, including his critical leadership during World War II and as Chief of Army Staff in the 1971 Indo-Pakistan war that led to Bangladesh’s founding. Kaushal described the role as the most challenging of his career, focusing not only on Manekshaw’s style and charisma but also his compassion for his soldiers. Kaushal spent several months preparing for the role, including detailed research, watching interviews, and meeting Manekshaw’s family, working closely with director Gulzar throughout the process. Their partnership on this film is built on trust formed during 'Raazi.' The movie also stars Sanya Malhotra as Silloo Manekshaw and Fatima Sana Shaikh as former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. Malhotra remarked on her fortunate year with significant projects, while Shaikh shared her journey of learning about Manekshaw and highlighted the film's value in educating audiences. Malhotra and Shaikh, who both started their film careers with 'Dangal,' expressed mutual pride in each other’s growth and reflected on their perseverance and dedication over the years. 'Sam Bahadur' is produced by RSVP Movies, written by Bhavani Iyer, Shantanu Shrivastava, and Meghna Gulzar, and is scheduled to premiere in theaters on December 1.

article_content: ATLANTA — Lawyer Sidney Powell pleaded guilty on Thursday to reduced charges in connection with efforts to overturn Donald Trump’s 2020 election loss in Georgia. She is now the second defendant in the wide-ranging case to reach an agreement with prosecutors. Powell had been charged, along with Trump and 17 others, under Georgia’s anti-racketeering law. She entered her plea a day before jury selection was set to begin for her trial. Powell pleaded guilty to six misdemeanors related to intentionally interfering with the performance of election duties. As part of the plea deal, Powell will serve six years of probation, pay a $6,000 fine, and write an apology letter to Georgia and its residents. She has also agreed to testify truthfully against her co-defendants in future trials. Powell, 68, was originally charged with racketeering and six other offenses as part of a scheme to keep Republican President Trump in power after his loss to Democrat Joe Biden in the 2020 election. Prosecutors allege Powell was involved in an unauthorized breach of election equipment in a rural Georgia county office. Powell’s plea marks a significant reversal for a lawyer known for promoting unfounded claims about the 2020 election. If called to testify, she may offer insight into a post-election news conference she joined on Trump’s behalf and a White House meeting in December 2020 where various strategies to challenge the election outcome were discussed. She had been scheduled to go on trial Monday with fellow attorney Kenneth Chesebro, after both requested speedy trials. Jury selection was set to begin Friday. With Powell’s plea, Chesebro will now face trial alone, although prosecutors may consider offering him a plea deal as well. Barry Coburn, Powell’s attorney based in Washington, declined to comment. Last month, a co-defendant, bail bondsman Scott Graham Hall, pleaded guilty to five misdemeanor charges, was sentenced to five years of probation, and agreed to testify in future proceedings. Prosecutors allege Powell conspired with Hall and others to access election equipment without authorization and hired computer forensics firm SullivanStrickler to send a team to Coffee County, Georgia, to copy software and data from voting machines and related computers. The indictment says an unnamed individual emailed a senior SullivanStrickler executive, instructing him to send all data copied from Dominion Voting Systems equipment in Coffee County to an unidentified lawyer linked to Powell and the Trump campaign.

article_content: The Extra Terrestrial Vehicle (ETV) is a sci-fi-inspired concept car designed by Michael Vetter, also known as Kit Car Mike. Priced at £75,000—the same as a Porsche 911—the ETV is based on a standard Chevrolet but completely transformed into a futuristic vehicle. The ETV features a windscreen that stands five feet high, gullwing windows that open remotely, and a body style resembling the car Tom Cruise drove in the film Minority Report rather than anything from the movie E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial. Kit Car Mike operates The Car Factory in Florida, USA, and has built just seven ETVs to date. One of these unique cars is currently displayed at the London Motor Museum in Middlesex. Under the hood, the ETV sports a two-litre supercharged engine that delivers 270 bhp to the front wheels via a five-speed gearbox. It also has two cameras inside, designed to help drivers park its unconventional shape. Vetter describes the ETV as the ultimate car for those searching for something truly different, emphasizing its combination of standout looks and reliability. He stated, 'I was unprepared for the initial response I received while driving it—I get five times as many people taking pictures of this car than if I was in a supercar.' According to The Car Factory’s website, the company offers to build custom futuristic or concept cars to high quality, suitable for everyday driving. The ETV, with its dramatic design, often attracts more attention than high-end cars like the Bugatti Veyron and makes the iconic DeLorean from Back to the Future appear outdated by comparison.

Robbie Williams opened up about his struggles with addiction and mental health during an emotional speech to his fans at Sydney’s Allianz Stadium this week. The 49-year-old performer, addressing a crowd of 38,000, spoke candidly about his substance abuse and mental health challenges at the height of his career. Williams’ journey is also depicted in his Netflix documentary and biopic 'Better Man,' filmed in Australia during the pandemic. He credited his Australian fans with helping him through his darkest moments, sharing, “One of the main things that kept me going was knowing that you turned up for me, even when I doubted myself.”

Reflecting on his early years with Take That, Williams described numbing his pain through drugs and alcohol, which ultimately led to addiction. He said, “I drank and took drugs to stop the pain and silence the inner critic. It became a quick path downward, and eventually, I had to stop or I was going to die.” Williams, who has been sober for 24 years, added that sobriety forced him to face mental health issues head-on. “When you stop drinking, you’re left with who you are. For me, that meant dealing with depression and isolation. I didn’t know how to interact or even be a person,” he told the audience. Now a married father of four, Williams expressed gratitude for his fans and credited them with helping him heal, declaring, “I am the happiest I’ve ever been—I love you, Australia.”

Elsewhere, Williams’ wife, Ayda Field, recently shared their parenting philosophy. She revealed that while Williams flies first class, their children travel in economy to teach them the value of money. “My kids fly economy whenever we fly. I turn left and they turn right. People might judge, but they need to learn the value of money,” she told The Sunday Times. The couple are parents to Teddy, 11, Charlie, 9, Coco, 5, and Beau, 3.

article_content: The BBC is set to launch a documentary chronicling King Charles III’s inaugural year on the throne, narrated by Helena Bonham Carter. Named 'Charles III: The Coronation Year,' it will debut next month and offers an exclusive, in-depth look at the experiences of King Charles and Queen Camilla following Queen Elizabeth II’s passing. The program covers behind-the-scenes moments as Buckingham Palace prepared for and celebrated the first coronation in seven decades, held in May, and follows the royal family during the significant months afterward. Viewers will also hear from various members of the Royal Family and key figures within the royal household. Kate Phillips, the BBC’s Director of Unscripted, commented on the remarkable access the film provides to this important chapter in history and emphasized the documentary’s distinctive approach to exploring the king and queen’s roles around the time of the historic coronation event. Produced by Oxford Films, the 90-minute special will air next month. The production team includes executive producer Nicolas Kent, commissioning editor Simon Young for the BBC, director Ashley Gething, producer Faye Hamilton, and Robert Hardman as writer and co-producer. Helena Bonham Carter, the documentary’s narrator, is recognized for her portrayal of Princess Margaret in 'The Crown.'

article_content: Mumbai residents woke up to moderate showers on Sunday after the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a yellow alert over the weekend. Rainfall measured 5.2 mm at the Santacruz observatory and 9 mm at the coastal Colaba observatory. The rain brought a welcome break from the city’s high daytime temperatures and helped improve air quality, with Mumbai's overall Air Quality Index (AQI) dropping to 95 on Sunday afternoon—considered 'satisfactory.' Out of the city’s 27 air quality stations, 15 recorded AQI in double digits, showing notable improvement from Saturday. The cleanest air was measured at Worli (AQI 46), followed by Borivali East (62), Malad West (66), Khindipada in Bhandup (71), Powai (74), and Mulund West (78). Bandra Kurla Complex saw the highest AQI at 187. Experts noted that showers help clean the air by removing particulate matter, leading to improved air quality. Meteorologists told The Indian Express that light showers are likely to continue until Monday. According to Sunil Kamble, director of IMD Mumbai, the upper air cyclonic circulation over the Bay of Bengal is weakening, but wind interactions are causing thunderstorm activity. Rainfall is expected to decrease by Monday. Although a yellow alert was issued for Mumbai until Sunday, no alerts have been issued for Monday. However, weather forecasts predict light to moderate showers and possible thunderstorms in Mumbai, as well as in the neighboring districts of Raigad, Thane, and Palghar. Many areas in Mumbai and its suburbs experienced unseasonal showers starting Saturday night, with the heaviest rain in the early hours of Sunday. At 4:30 am, IMD issued a nowcast warning for Mumbai and nearby areas, predicting thunderstorms, lightning, and moderate rain with gusty winds up to 30–40 km/h. Data from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation show that between 5 am and 6 am, light rain fell on the island city and eastern suburbs. The heaviest rainfall was recorded at the Andheri fire station (15 mm), followed by the K/W ward office (14 mm) and the Malwani fire station (13 mm) in the western suburbs. This marks the second episode of unseasonal showers to affect Mumbai this November.

article_content: Diplomats have suggested that Syrian President Bashar Assad and his British-born wife, Asma, could be offered immunity from prosecution if this would help bring an end to Assad’s regime. Such a move would effectively forgive him for a violent crackdown during a 15-month uprising, a period during which more than 14,000 people are reported to have died. Assad’s forces have recently been accused of massacring hundreds of civilians, including women and children, and Amnesty International has accused him of crimes against humanity. Both US and British diplomats believe offering Assad protection from prosecution by the International Criminal Court could be the only way to stop the ongoing conflict. Last week, the United Nations warned that Syria is sliding into civil war. The immunity proposal would mean Assad could not be tried for war crimes, genocide, or crimes against humanity, and might allow him to flee the country, potentially to Russia or Iran. Officials are discussing the possibility of providing Assad and Asma safe passage to an international conference in Switzerland, possibly held as soon as next week. The meeting would involve government and opposition representatives, the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, and key regional powers such as Turkey and Saudi Arabia. The primary focus would be on UN-Arab League envoy Kofi Annan’s six-point peace plan, which calls for a Syrian-led political process. Discussions would also include modeling Assad’s exit on that of former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh in 2012, potentially leading to Assad stepping down and a new government forming over 18 to 24 months, followed by free elections. The proposal reportedly follows meetings between President Barack Obama, Prime Minister David Cameron, and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the G20 summit in Mexico. US and British officials believe Putin may not be committed to keeping Assad in power indefinitely. The latest violence has intensified international outrage. More than 100 people, half of them children, were killed in Houla recently. UN observers have visited the area, and images from the aftermath have sparked global condemnation. Meanwhile, a Syrian MiG 21 fighter jet landed in Jordan after the pilot reportedly defected, marking the first defection involving an aircraft during the uprising. The humanitarian crisis continues, especially in Homs, Syria’s third-largest city, where rebels control several neighborhoods under continuous attack by government forces. Activists and the International Committee of the Red Cross report worsening conditions, with shortages of electricity, water, and communications, and civilians forced to hide from daily shelling. The Red Cross and the Syrian Arab Red Crescent are working to evacuate civilians and deliver aid. Among those trapped are approximately 90 Christians, including children, in certain neighborhoods of Homs. Attempts to evacuate them have so far failed, and thousands of Christians have fled areas after rebel takeovers. The Christian minority, which makes up about 10% of Syria’s population, fears becoming further victims of the ongoing conflict. Elsewhere, activists report continued violence, including the shelling of the town of Inkhil in Daraa province, where at least nine people have been killed. Residents and observers report casualties remain trapped under rubble. Daraa is the region where the uprising began in March 2011.

article_content: If you're seeking a memorable winter getaway, New Brunswick in Canada—just a short distance from Maine—invites adventurous spirits with a collection of distinctive winter activities. Whether you dream of wandering through enchanting ice caves, gliding high above snowy treetops on a zipline, ice fishing on a tranquil frozen river, or dashing through snowy forests by dog sled, New Brunswick delivers a refreshing twist on classic winter fun. Here are five top picks to consider for your next cold-weather adventure. 1. Lighthouse Glamping at Broadleaf Ranch: Nestled in the Bay of Fundy, Broadleaf Ranch welcomes guests throughout the year. One highlight is their Cape Enrage glamping lighthouse accommodation, inspired by the iconic Cape Enrage lighthouse. Available year-round for $200 CAD per night, this cozy retreat features a lofted double bed, two pullout single sofa beds in the living area, plus a fully equipped kitchenette and bathroom. Guests can enjoy starry nights, sunrise views, and on-site perks like winter horseback riding or even spa services. 2. Dog Sledding with Birch Bark Adventures: Embracing northern tradition, dog sledding is a don't-miss experience in New Brunswick. Birch Bark Adventures in North Tetagouche—about three hours from the capital—offers guided tours year-round with experienced guides and friendly Alaskan Huskies. Options range from a solo afternoon at $129.99 CAD to extensive multi-day expeditions costing $3,899.99 CAD. Participants receive safety instructions and meet the sled dogs before heading out on the trails. 3. Winter Ziplining at Timbertop Zip Tours: For a blend of excitement and wintry beauty, head to Snider Mountain Ranch, roughly an hour from Saint John, where Timbertop Zip Tours offers 13 zip lines soaring over snow-laden woodlands from November through April. After your flight through the forest, warm up with homemade cookies and hot chocolate by a cozy fire. Admission is $69.99 CAD per person. 4. Ice Fishing with Off the Charts Outfitters: Revel in the chill as you try ice fishing with expert guides from Off the Charts Outfitters. Suitable for all skill levels, their guided sessions target a range of fish species across New Brunswick. Outings run January through March, offering full-day ($225 CAD) and half-day ($150 CAD) rates, with a 50% discount for kids under 16. The price includes all equipment, live bait, and a BBQ lunch out on the ice. 5. Hiking to the Midland Ice Caves: From December to February, set off on an easy, picturesque hike to the Midland Ice Caves in southern New Brunswick. This family-friendly, 1.5-hour trek offers a special opportunity to explore natural ice formations and snowy landscapes starting from the Midland Ice Caves trailhead.

article_content: General Motors rolled out several business updates after new labor contracts were ratified in the US and Canada. CEO Mary Barra stated that the company is facing greater labor costs, persistent issues at its Cruise self-driving division, and difficulties scaling up production of electric vehicle batteries. In spite of these challenges, GM reinstated its 2023 earnings guidance, which it had earlier suspended amid labor negotiations, citing a $1.1 billion financial impact from UAW strikes due to production stoppages. GM now projects 2023 net income between $9.1 billion and $9.7 billion, with adjusted EBIT ranging from $11.7 billion to $12.7 billion. Chief Financial Officer Paul Jacobson reported that North American labor expenses are anticipated to increase by roughly $1.5 billion over previous contracts in 2024. Additionally, GM announced a $10 billion accelerated stock buyback program and will boost its quarterly dividend by 33% to 12 cents per share starting in 2024. Of the buyback, $6.8 billion in GM shares will be retired immediately, with the remainder of the program concluding by late 2024. Addressing recurring operational challenges, Barra pointed to lower-than-expected production of Ultium EV batteries in 2023, but noted that process improvements have been made for better results next year. Rather than creating an all-new EV lineup, GM will focus on updating the Chevrolet Bolt EV, a decision projected to save around $5 billion. GM forecasts overall US sales of electric vehicles exceeding one million units this year, making up approximately 7% of the total vehicle market. As for Cruise, GM's autonomous vehicle unit, operations were suspended after several incidents led California regulators to revoke its permit and the recent resignation of Cruise’s CEO. Moving forward, Barra has prioritized safety, accountability, and transparency, aiming to restore trust with authorities and the public. The company will pause Cruise's rapid expansion and reduce its spending on the unit to several hundred million dollars in 2024. Following these announcements, GM stock jumped by nearly 10%. However, Barra and Jacobson acknowledged missteps in company operations this year but indicated corrective action is underway. Further financial updates will be provided at the Barclays Global Automotive and Mobility Tech Conference.

A pesar de estos desafíos, GM restableció su pronóstico de ganancias para 2023, el cual había suspendido durante las negociaciones sindicales, señalando un impacto financiero de 1,100 millones de dólares debido a las huelgas del UAW y la paralización de la producción. Ahora GM proyecta ingresos netos en 2023 entre 9,100 y 9,700 millones de dólares, con un EBIT ajustado de entre 11,700 y 12,700 millones. Además, GM anunció un programa acelerado de recompra de acciones por 10,000 millones de dólares y aumentará su dividendo trimestral en un 33% a 12 centavos por acción a partir de 2024. De esa recompra, 6,800 millones de dólares en acciones serán retiradas de inmediato, y el resto del programa finalizará a finales de 2024. Sobre los desafíos operativos, Barra señaló que la producción de baterías Ultium para vehículos eléctricos fue menor a la esperada en 2023, aunque afirmó que han mejorado los procesos y esperan mejores resultados el próximo año. En vez de lanzar una nueva línea completamente, GM actualizará el Chevrolet Bolt EV, lo que permitirá un ahorro estimado de 5,000 millones de dólares. GM estima que las ventas totales de autos eléctricos en Estados Unidos superarán el millón de unidades este año, lo que representará cerca del 7% del mercado total. Respecto a Cruise, la unidad de vehículos autónomos de GM, las operaciones se detuvieron tras varios incidentes que causaron la revocación de su permiso en California y la reciente renuncia de su CEO. Barra priorizó la seguridad, la transparencia y la rendición de cuentas, buscando restablecer la confianza con autoridades y comunidades. GM hará una pausa en la expansión de Cruise y reducirá su inversión a varios cientos de millones de dólares en 2024. Tras estos anuncios, las acciones de GM subieron alrededor del 10%. Sin embargo, tanto Barra como Jacobson reconocieron fallas en la gestión interna este año, aunque aseguraron estar tomando medidas correctivas. Se brindarán más novedades financieras en la próxima conferencia Barclays Global Automotive and Mobility Tech.

article_content: A report released today by Members of Parliament alleges that accounting firm PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) has facilitated tax avoidance on a massive scale for hundreds of companies. According to the Public Accounts Committee, leaked internal correspondence shows PwC assisted at least 343 firms in implementing schemes that diverted profits to Luxembourg, allowing them to reduce their tax obligations. The committee, chaired by MP Margaret Hodge—a former PwC employee—claims these practices constitute 'mass-market' tax avoidance. Hodge highlighted that clients were not required to show any business operations in Luxembourg to benefit from these schemes. One notable example is Shire Pharmaceuticals, which reportedly paid just 0.016 percent tax on its profits in Luxembourg by channeling an intra-company loan through a local subsidiary with only two employees. PwC is said to have negotiated directly with Luxembourg authorities to ensure the company paid almost no tax there. MPs accuse PwC executives of previously misleading Parliament when, two years ago, they stated they did not market or create tax avoidance products. However, the leaked documents suggest otherwise. Kevin Nicholson, PwC's head of tax, defended the firm's advice to clients during his testimony in 2013. The recent leak, attributed to French whistleblower Antoine Deltour, revealed 28,000 pages of documents exposing deals PwC brokered for major multinational firms—including Apple, Ikea, and Pepsi—to help them minimize their tax bills. MPs have called for a mandatory code of conduct for tax advisers. Hodge also criticized HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) for not taking more effective action and warned of the potential harm to public finances if reforms are not made. In response, an HMRC spokesperson cited the agency's efforts since 2010 to recover £31 billion by challenging large businesses and their advisers. The report further notes that leather goods company Smythson, which employs the Prime Minister’s wife Samantha Cameron, is among the firms based in Luxembourg for tax purposes.

article_content: Many outstanding Australians were nominated for the Australian of the Year awards, yet recognition for their achievements was diminished after Prime Minister Tony Abbott's decision to grant a knighthood to Prince Philip—a choice that diverted attention and sparked political controversy. Nevertheless, four finalists were celebrated for their remarkable service. Lieutenant General David Morrison, as Chief of Army, became a leading voice for change in military culture. In 2013, his forceful address demanding respect for women and denouncing sexism gained broad attention and helped advance significant reforms. Morrison pushed for the recruitment of more women, collaborated with the White Ribbon organization, and represented Australia at a United Nations summit, firmly advocating for equal opportunity based on merit. Dr Gill Hicks transformed her experience as a survivor of the 2005 London terrorist attacks into a lifelong peace mission. She established M.A.D. For Peace to unite people from varied cultures and backgrounds, despite facing resistance for her inclusive message. Her unwavering dedication to promoting tolerance made her a national finalist. Dr Miriam-Rose Ungunmerr-Baumann, recognized as the Northern Territory’s first Indigenous schoolteacher, devoted her life to enriching education through Indigenous perspectives and strengthening her Daly River community. Her leadership contributed to Indigenous management in local schools, promoted visual arts in education, and provided guidance to governmental organizations. Dr Annie Sparrow, a pediatrician, extended critical healthcare to communities in urgent need, working in places like Africa, Afghanistan, and the Syrian border. Her commitment to protecting vulnerable groups and curbing infectious disease outbreaks led to her selection as the Western Australia finalist.

article_content: A would-be thief was quickly apprehended after his plan fell apart in an unexpected way. Nigel Ball, 52, from Wakefield, stole a £50 hexagonal fish tank from the Pets at Home store in Westgate Retail Park just after 5pm on May 29. Wanting some goldfish for his new acquisition, Ball returned to the same store days later, filling out a form with his real name and address when purchasing the fish. Staff grew suspicious when Ball identified the same uniquely shaped tank that had recently gone missing. They alerted police, who later located the stolen item at Ball’s home on Walnut Avenue. Ball confessed to the theft during a hearing at Wakefield Magistrates' Court. Sentencing was postponed while additional reports are prepared.

article_content: Russian President Vladimir Putin recently claimed that the experimental nuclear-powered cruise missile Burevestnik is now operational. However, nuclear weapons experts question whether it truly offers Russia any meaningful advantage beyond its current arsenal. While the missile represents an advancement in technology, its promised capabilities remain unproven. Earlier this month, Putin announced a successful test of the 9M730 Burevestnik, part of a suite of six new strategic weapons Russia unveiled in 2018. He did not provide further details on the test. Reports suggest Russia conducted more than a dozen tests between 2017 and 2019, none of which were fully successful, though one or two showed potential. A fatal nuclear accident reportedly occurred during an effort to recover a test missile from the sea. If Putin's latest claims are accurate, it raises questions about what capabilities the Burevestnik actually possesses. Can this 'low-flying, stealth cruise missile with a nuclear warhead' operate with an 'unlimited range' and 'unpredictable flight path,' as touted in 2018? Does it truly bypass all existing and future missile defense systems? Pavel Podvig, a leading nuclear weapons expert, offered a critical perspective. He argues that even if the Burevestnik works as advertised, it does not provide advantages over Russia's current strategic weapons such as ICBMs and SLBMs. 'It’s just a very long-range cruise missile,' Podvig stated. Nonetheless, the weapon might hold political value for Moscow. During ongoing Ukrainian offensives and challenges facing Russian forces, Putin could be using the Burevestnik as a bargaining chip or to boost domestic prestige. While Russia considers the Burevestnik one of its 'super weapons,' others in the same category face questions about their effectiveness. For instance, the 3M22 Zircon missile remains under evaluation, and the Kh-47M2 Kinzhal was reportedly intercepted by US-supplied Patriot systems in Ukraine. The Poseidon underwater torpedo is another experimental entry. US scientists once explored similar nuclear-powered missile technology but abandoned it due to safety and environmental concerns. Advances in technology notwithstanding, Podvig remains skeptical of the weapon's utility. He points out that existing ballistic missiles are already highly effective at evading missile defenses, and the Burevestnik may not significantly alter strategic calculations. Russia’s pursuit of new nuclear systems like the Burevestnik accelerated after the US withdrew from the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty in 2002, a move intended to allow the US to develop its own national missile defenses. This led Russia to bolster its strategic capabilities and develop new systems. The Burevestnik has drawn US attention, making potential launch facilities prominent targets in any US-Russia conflict. If deployed, these large, vulnerable facilities could be among the first attacked, reducing the likelihood that the Burevestnik could deliver a retaliatory strike. Podvig notes that traditional ICBMs may offer better second-strike capabilities. Ultimately, the Burevestnik’s main value may be political, serving as an example of technological prowess and as leverage in negotiations. Podvig suggests it is a 'politics project' meant to satisfy leadership demands rather than meet a pressing strategic need. Given current battlefield setbacks, highlighting technological breakthroughs could help bolster domestic support and bargaining power internationally.

article_content: Try a Patch: Can Beauty Patches Solve Common Skin Problems?  By Claire Coleman for the Daily Mail.  Women are increasingly turning to cloth, plaster, and gel 'patches' to address beauty concerns such as lip wrinkles, eye bags, and frown lines. These patches are applied to the face, sometimes overnight, and claim to deliver various skincare benefits. But do they actually work?  Claire Coleman teamed up with skincare expert Jonquille Chantrey, who runs an aesthetic clinic in Cheshire, to test several popular products.  Budget Eyebag Buster: Montagne Jeunesse Anti-Wrinkle Cool Eyes (£1.99 for two pairs, montagnejeunesse.com) Claim: Reduces fine lines, sagging skin, and crow’s feet. The patches are cooled in the fridge before use. Review: The patches feel like jelly and are cooling and moisturizing, making dryness lines disappear temporarily, though the effect doesn't last all day. Expert Opinion: Fine lines and sagging are caused by factors like sun damage and muscle movement. While topical products have limited effect, the cold reduces under-eye puffiness by shrinking blood vessels. Verdict: Provides a temporary boost, especially for a night out. Good value. 3/5  Essence of Snail: Skin Pep Hydro-Gel Decolletage (£14.99 for five, skinpep.com) Claim: Dramatically hydrates, softens, and improves skin elasticity with peptides, botanical extracts, and snail secretion. Review: Helped reduce crepiness on the neck, but not deeper lines. Expert Opinion: The neck often needs targeted care. Snail secretion may contain beneficial proteins for skin rejuvenation. Verdict: Offers a quick neck boost if needed. 3/5  Farewell to Frowns: Frownies Forehead & Between the Eyes (£18.95 for 144 patches, frownies.co.uk) Claim: By keeping facial muscles relaxed overnight, these patches can help reduce frown lines. Review: Easy to apply, and after a few weeks, lines looked less noticeable. Expert Opinion: We often frown during sleep, which can cause lasting lines. These patches may help if they stay in place. Verdict: Inexpensive and somewhat effective, but won’t eliminate wrinkles entirely. 5/5  Luxury Eye Smoothers: Elemis Pro-Collagen Hydra-Gel Eye Masks (£46 for six pairs, timetospa.co.uk) Claim: Clinically proven to instantly reduce fine lines and wrinkles. Review: Larger than budget options, effective for smoothing and tightening, with effects lasting longer than most. Expert Opinion: Contains ingredients with potential anti-inflammatory and hydrating benefits. Verdict: A luxurious occasional treat that delivers hydration and tightening. 3/5  Golden Lips: Jamela Luxurious Gold Crystal Collagen Lip Mask (£46.75 for 16, jamelaskincare.co.uk) Claim: Gold and plant collagen increase cell metabolism and replenish moisture for smoother lips. Review: Softens lips but is difficult to use due to fit. No noticeable plumping effect. Expert Opinion: The thin skin on the lips benefits from hydration, but gold is likely just a marketing gimmick. Verdict: Softens, but expensive for limited results. 1/5  Iron Out Smile Lines: Skyn Iceland Hydro Cool Firming Face Gels (£30 for eight, marksandspencer.com) Claim: Smoothes smile lines in ten minutes using peptide-infused patches. Review: Improved skin surface, but deeper lines remained. Expert Opinion: Some instant smoothing and hydration, but substantial results require daily use. Verdict: Some improvement for surface lines, but not a long-term solution. 2/5  Wipe Away the Years: Line Smoothing Complex High Potency Treatment Mask (£46 for six, drlewinns.co.uk) Claim: Anti-ageing mask to hydrate, plump, and smooth skin using advanced formula. Review: Easy to use, leaving skin hydrated and more radiant. Expert Opinion: Contains an ingredient that may soften expression lines, but is not a replacement for treatments like Botox. Verdict: Effective for softening fine lines and post-party skin recovery, comparable in price to other luxury masks. 4/5
translated_content: ¿Funciona un parche? ¿Pueden los parches de belleza solucionar problemas comunes de la piel?  Por Claire Coleman para el Daily Mail.  Cada vez más mujeres recurren a parches de tela, yeso y gel para tratar preocupaciones de belleza como arrugas en los labios, bolsas en los ojos y líneas de expresión. Estos parches se aplican en el rostro, a veces durante la noche, y prometen beneficios para el cuidado de la piel. ¿Pero realmente funcionan?  Claire Coleman se unió a la experta en cuidado de la piel Jonquille Chantrey, quien dirige una clínica estética en Cheshire, para probar varios productos populares.  Económico para las bolsas en los ojos: Montagne Jeunesse Anti-Wrinkle Cool Eyes (£1.99 por dos pares, montagnejeunesse.com) Promesa: Reduce líneas finas, piel flácida y patas de gallo. Los parches se enfrían en la nevera antes de usar. Opinión: Se sienten como gelatina y son refrescantes e hidratantes, haciendo desaparecer temporalmente las líneas por sequedad, aunque el efecto no dura todo el día. Opinión experta: Las líneas finas y la flacidez se deben a daños solares y movimiento muscular. Aunque los productos tópicos tienen efectos limitados, el frío reduce la hinchazón bajo los ojos al encoger los vasos sanguíneos. Veredicto: Ofrece un impulso temporal, especialmente para salir por la noche. Buena relación calidad-precio. 3/5  Esencia de caracol: Skin Pep Hydro-Gel Decolletage (£14.99 por cinco, skinpep.com) Promesa: Hidrata, suaviza y mejora la elasticidad con péptidos, extractos botánicos y secreción de caracol. Opinión: Ayudó a reducir la piel arrugada en el cuello, pero no las líneas más profundas. Opinión experta: El cuello suele necesitar cuidados específicos. La secreción de caracol puede tener proteínas beneficiosas para la piel. Veredicto: Ofrece un refuerzo rápido para el cuello si lo necesitas. 3/5  Adiós a las líneas del ceño: Frownies Forehead & Between the Eyes (£18.95 por 144 parches, frownies.co.uk) Promesa: Manteniendo los músculos faciales relajados de noche, ayudan a reducir líneas de expresión. Opinión: Fáciles de usar, y después de algunas semanas, las líneas se veían menos marcadas. Opinión experta: Solemos fruncir el ceño al dormir, lo que genera líneas permanentes. Veredicto: Baratos y bastante efectivos, aunque no eliminan las arrugas del todo. 5/5  Lujo para los ojos: Elemis Pro-Collagen Hydra-Gel Eye Masks (£46 por seis pares, timetospa.co.uk) Promesa: Clínicamente probado para reducir líneas y arrugas al instante. Opinión: Más grandes que las opciones económicas; eficaces para alisar y tensar, con un efecto más duradero que la mayoría. Opinión experta: Contienen ingredientes con beneficios antiinflamatorios e hidratantes. Veredicto: Una opción lujosa ocasional que hidrata y tensa. 3/5  Labios dorados: Jamela Luxurious Gold Crystal Collagen Lip Mask (£46.75 por 16, jamelaskincare.co.uk) Promesa: El oro y el colágeno vegetal aumentan el metabolismo celular y reponen la humedad para labios más suaves. Opinión: Suaviza los labios pero es difícil de usar por la forma. Sin efecto visible de aumento de volumen. Veredicto: Suaviza pero es costoso para resultados limitados. 1/5  Alisa las líneas de la sonrisa: Skyn Iceland Hydro Cool Firming Face Gels (£30 por ocho, marksandspencer.com) Promesa: Suaviza las líneas de la sonrisa en diez minutos usando parches con péptidos. X, formerly known as Twitter, may soon enable users to set animated GIFs as their profile images. Andrea Conway, a designer at X, launched a poll recently asking users for feedback on the idea. As of Friday, the poll had gathered more than 13,000 responses, with about 73% supporting the option for GIF profile pictures.

Currently, only a small group of users still have animated GIF avatars, a legacy from the platform’s earlier years. Previously, Twitter discouraged animated profile images, only allowing them within certain technical limitations. In 2013, then-CEO Dick Costolo closed these loopholes, but users who already had GIF avatars were permitted to keep them. Over time, as accounts became inactive or images were changed, these unique avatars grew increasingly rare. For those who kept them, their GIF avatars are a unique badge from Twitter’s past, symbolizing a certain exclusivity.

These legacy GIF avatar users form a small, tight-knit community and often receive messages from others asking about their profiles. Many make light of their status, recalling the evolving culture of Twitter and sharing concerns about possible changes. Some believe a wave of new animated avatars could diminish their special status or visually clutter the platform. There is also speculation that the feature could be limited to X Premium subscribers, which might change the meaning of owning a GIF avatar.

As X continues to change, some users express skepticism about the implementation of new features, with concerns about the platform’s direction and changes like hidden headlines and ad labels. Amid curiosity and apprehension, the community awaits to see whether animated GIF avatars will be widely available again and what that could mean for their long-held digital identities.

Emily Eden, an 18-year-old who is terminally ill, has renewed hope of celebrating Christmas at home thanks to the rapid progress of repairs to her flood-damaged house. Emily and her parents have been living in a hotel room since Storm Babet caused severe flooding at their home in Clay Cross, Derbyshire. Initially, the family was told it could take up to six months before they could return. However, workers have pushed hard to complete the repairs sooner.

Richard Eden, Emily's father, shared, "I've been told we'll probably be back in for December 23, which is amazing. To Emily, that would mean everything." He explained, "They've removed the floors, fully dried the house, taken down the plaster and ceilings, and have had up to 15 men working—even on weekends."

Mr. Eden expressed concern for his daughter's wellbeing during their time living in the hotel with the family's two dogs, describing it as a tough situation that has left him sleep-deprived and anxious. "Emily gets us through every day because she's so strong and brave," he said.

The cost of repairs is being covered by insurance, but Mr. Eden also thanked the local community for raising about £11,000 to support Emily.

Jai Bowling, representing Belfor Ltd – the contractors handling the repairs – said the team's efforts have been heartfelt: "It's a battle, but there is a fighting chance of having [the Edens] back in by December 23."

article_content: Just days before President Barack Obama's diplomatic visit to China, the government-run newspaper Global Times released an editorial critical of his presidency. The piece labels Obama as uninspiring and claims Americans have grown frustrated with his alleged lack of substantial progress. The editorial argues that Obama failed to meet the expectations set by his campaign slogan, 'Yes, we can.' It contends that, despite some economic recovery, most Americans have not seen real benefits, especially in terms of closing the income gap. On the international front, the commentary points to issues such as the withdrawal of U.S. troops from Iraq and Afghanistan without achieving lasting peace, and the emergence of ISIS after Osama bin Laden’s death, as indicators of foreign policy shortcomings. It suggests that these failures, alongside a significant loss in the midterm elections, have further weakened Obama’s image domestically as the Republicans took control of Congress. However, the editorial also acknowledges that Obama faced considerable obstacles upon taking office, including an ailing economy and waning American influence globally. It further criticizes the U.S. political system for its resistance to reform. President Obama’s itinerary includes a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and participation in the APEC Leaders Meeting during his Asia trip, which also covers visits to Myanmar and Australia, aiming to bolster economic and diplomatic engagement across the region. In a recent Forbes ranking of global leaders, Obama placed second behind Russian President Vladimir Putin, with China’s Xi Jinping following closely in third.

article_content: President Joe Biden has announced that Uganda, Gabon, Niger, and the Central African Republic (CAR) will soon be removed from a US trade initiative that supports economic ties with Africa. These countries are being excluded from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa), which has allowed qualifying sub-Saharan African nations duty-free access to the US market for over 1,800 products since 2000. Biden stated the decision is due to severe human rights abuses and these countries' lack of progress toward democratic governance. Niger and Gabon, both of which experienced military coups in 2023, failed to uphold political pluralism and the rule of law—two requirements for Agoa eligibility. In the cases of CAR and Uganda, the US pointed to persistent human rights violations by their respective governments. Uganda’s passage of an anti-LGBTQ law, carrying harsh penalties including death for certain offenses, has drawn global criticism and was a significant factor in the US decision. Since May, the US had discussed Uganda’s possible removal from Agoa and potential sanctions over this legislation. President Biden informed Congress that despite consistent diplomatic engagement, the four countries had not met Agoa’s standards for eligibility. The exclusion is expected to affect the economies of these nations, especially their trade with the US—though to varying degrees. CAR's exports to the US totaled only $881,000 in 2022, while it imported $23 million—highlighting a large trade deficit. Uganda exported $174 million to the US, Gabon $220 million, and Niger $73 million last year. Recently, Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni said that some US companies already stopped purchasing Ugandan textiles due to the anti-LGBTQ law, and in August, he banned imports of second-hand clothes—a measure likely affecting US exporters. The US government has also cut most foreign aid to Gabon and is conditioning its return on progress toward democracy; similar steps were taken in Niger after its military coup. Other African nations, including Burkina Faso, Mali, and Guinea, have previously lost Agoa status after experiencing military takeovers. The removal of Uganda, Gabon, Niger, and CAR from Agoa will take effect at the beginning of next year, just before the 20th Agoa forum convenes in South Africa. So far, none of the affected governments have issued official statements in response.

article_content: Hollywood is experiencing a slowdown in new action movie releases for late 2023 and into 2024 because of strike-related work stoppages involving both writers and actors. Since July, only a few productions with special waivers have moved forward. Even though the writers' strike has ended, the actors' strike remains unresolved, meaning movie release dates for the coming year are still uncertain. Major blockbusters could see release dates pushed back. For example, Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part Two may not be ready in time if the strike continues into the end of the year. Many other high-profile projects might be delayed as well. This October 27, three action films are scheduled to premiere: David Fincher's The Killer (receiving a limited theatrical release before heading to Netflix), Boudica: Queen Of War (a historical epic), and Freelance, featuring John Cena and Alison Brie. Given the generally slow box office aside from large draws like Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour, Freelance has a decent chance to stand out, but because of the strike, its lead actors can't promote the film until the industry dispute is settled. Overall, future release calendars for action movies remain up in the air as long as labor negotiations continue.

A tragic accident at a construction site in Wuhan, central China, claimed the lives of 19 workers when an elevator plummeted 30 floors after a cable broke. The lift fell approximately 328 feet (100 meters) down the side of the building. In response, Wuhan authorities suspended all construction activity to conduct comprehensive safety inspections.

The victims, all decorators, were working on a multi-tower complex, according to China Central Television. This incident underscores the ongoing issue of workplace safety in China. Official reports from the State Administration of Work Safety stated that over 75,500 people died in work-related accidents the previous year. Despite government efforts, regulations are often not strictly enforced.

In a separate case, a man in Shangrao, Jiangxi province, survived after a metal bar pierced through his head at a construction site. Firefighters and emergency services cut the bar, which was safely removed in the hospital, and the man is now in recovery.

Recent accidents further highlight these concerns. A bridge collapsed in Heilongjiang province last month, killing three and injuring five. Days later, a bus collision in northern China caused a fire that killed 36 passengers. These incidents have raised fears that the fast pace of development may be undermining safety standards. Road safety remains a significant challenge, with about 70,000 deaths and 300,000 injuries annually, according to Xinhua.

In yet another tragedy, 26 miners died in a coal mine explosion last week, exemplifying persistent dangers in China's mining industry, which is considered among the most hazardous worldwide due to insufficient safety enforcement.
