article_content: In their first debate since the outbreak of the Israel-Hamas war, Republican presidential hopefuls strongly voiced their support for Israel, while engaging in heated exchanges over China and Ukraine. The debate, held in Miami, unfolded as candidates faced increased pressure to close the polling gap with Donald Trump, who remained absent from the stage. Key figures Ron DeSantis and Nikki Haley sparred over policy, with Haley promising to end U.S. trade relations with China in response to fentanyl deaths and criticizing DeSantis for not taking a similar stance. DeSantis countered by accusing Haley of welcoming Chinese investment during her tenure as South Carolina governor. The candidates spent much of the debate on foreign policy, rather than focusing on Trump’s record. As the Iowa caucuses approach, all five candidates are vying to distinguish themselves and present a viable alternative to Trump. However, many Republican voters appear uninterested in replacing him, and Trump continues to enjoy dominant poll numbers nationwide. His absence at the debate marked another strategic move to maintain media focus on himself. Moderators opened by asking each candidate why they believed they could defeat Trump, prompting DeSantis to suggest that Trump had lost momentum since his 2016 White House win. Haley called out Trump for shifting his stance on support for Ukraine, accusing him of wavering. Nonetheless, the debate soon returned to policy issues, leaving little room for personal attacks or direct confrontations. Foreign policy tensions, particularly regarding China, have fueled a months-long battle between the campaigns of DeSantis and Haley, with both sides accusing the other of weakness on Beijing. Haley also challenged DeSantis on environmental issues, labeling him 'liberal' for opposing offshore drilling in Florida, while DeSantis reaffirmed his support for fracking but rejected drilling in the Everglades. Abortion surfaced as a major topic after recent Democratic wins in several state elections. DeSantis defended signing a six-week abortion ban in Florida, noting that even some GOP supporters had voted for abortion rights measures. Haley emphasized a need for consensus, advocating for a ban on late-term abortions and access to contraception, while urging Republicans to acknowledge the political reality in Congress. Other candidates included Tim Scott, who appealed to evangelical voters in Iowa, Chris Christie, who defended U.S. support for Ukraine against Russia, and Vivek Ramaswamy, who attempted to insert himself into the debate and exchanged barbs with Haley over TikTok. All candidates expressed unwavering support for Israel’s offensive in Gaza after Hamas’ October 7 attack, which resulted in more than 1,400 deaths. The growing Palestinian death toll—reported by the Hamas-run health ministry in Gaza to exceed 10,500—was not addressed in humanitarian terms. Some candidates called for stronger action against antisemitism on college campuses. Trump, despite his four criminal indictments and recent testimony in a civil fraud case, retains a wide lead in the GOP primary. He held a simultaneous rally in Hialeah, Florida, attended by several thousand supporters, and shared the stage with figures including Arkansas Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders. Trump dismissed the debate as irrelevant and signaled that, as a former president, he saw no reason to participate in future debates. The RNC chairwoman, Ronna McDaniel, echoed this sentiment, indicating the party will support whoever wins the nomination.

A medida que se acercan los caucus de Iowa, los cinco candidatos buscan diferenciarse y presentarse como una alternativa viable a Trump. Sin embargo, muchos votantes republicanos parecen no estar interesados en reemplazarlo, y Trump sigue disfrutando de números dominantes en las encuestas a nivel nacional. Su ausencia en el debate fue otra movida estratégica para mantener la atención mediática en sí mismo. Los moderadores comenzaron preguntando a cada candidato por qué creían que podían derrotar a Trump, lo que llevó a DeSantis a sugerir que Trump había perdido impulso desde su victoria en 2016. Haley señaló que Trump ha cambiado su postura sobre el apoyo a Ucrania, acusándolo de tener dudas. Sin embargo, el debate rápidamente regresó a los temas de política, dejando poco espacio para ataques personales o enfrentamientos directos. Las tensiones sobre política exterior, especialmente respecto a China, han alimentado una batalla de varios meses entre las campañas de DeSantis y Haley, con ambos lados acusándose de ser débiles ante Pekín. Haley también desafió a DeSantis en temas medioambientales, calificándolo de 'liberal' por oponerse a la extracción de petróleo frente a las costas de Florida, mientras que DeSantis reafirmó su apoyo al fracking pero rechazó la perforación en los Everglades. El aborto fue un tema importante tras las recientes victorias demócratas en varias elecciones estatales. DeSantis defendió su firma de una prohibición del aborto de seis semanas en Florida, señalando que incluso algunos partidarios del Partido Republicano votaron por medidas a favor del derecho al aborto. Haley enfatizó la necesidad de consenso, abogando por prohibir los abortos de término avanzado y por el acceso a anticonceptivos, al tiempo que instó a los republicanos a reconocer la realidad política en el Congreso. Otros candidatos fueron Tim Scott, quien apeló a los votantes evangélicos de Iowa; Chris Christie, quien defendió el apoyo de Estados Unidos a Ucrania contra Rusia; y Vivek Ramaswamy, quien intentó tomar protagonismo en el debate y tuvo intercambios con Haley sobre TikTok. Todos los candidatos expresaron un apoyo inquebrantable a la ofensiva de Israel en Gaza tras el ataque de Hamás del 7 de octubre, que resultó en más de 1,400 muertes. El creciente número de muertes palestinas —reportado por el Ministerio de Salud dirigido por Hamás en Gaza en más de 10,500— no fue abordado en términos humanitarios. Algunos candidatos pidieron acciones más contundentes contra el antisemitismo en los campus universitarios. Trump, a pesar de enfrentar cuatro acusaciones penales y haber testificado recientemente en un caso civil por fraude, mantiene una amplia ventaja en las primarias republicanas. Realizó un mitin paralelo en Hialeah, Florida, al que asistieron varios miles de seguidores, y compartió el escenario con figuras como la gobernadora de Arkansas, Sarah Huckabee Sanders. Trump desestimó el debate como irrelevante y señaló que, como expresidente, no ve razón para participar en futuros debates. La presidenta del RNC, Ronna McDaniel, coincidió con este sentimiento, indicando que el partido apoyará a quien gane la nominación.

article_content: Tom Stuker, an automotive sales consultant, achieved a remarkable milestone by becoming the first United Airlines customer to fly one million miles in a single year. Stuker divides his time between New Jersey and Chicago, spending most of his days in the air. His accomplishment was recognized on December 6, during United Flight 949 from London to Chicago. At 59, Stuker is already known as a super-frequent flier. In July 2011, he was celebrated as the first person to reach 10 million miles flown with United, and had his name painted on a Boeing 747. Inspired by the movie 'Up In The Air,' in which George Clooney’s character obsesses over frequent flyer miles, Stuker has now flown over 13 million miles. He estimates he has taken over 6,000 flights with United, including about 400 trips in just one year—approximately equal to circling the globe 40 times. As a member of United's invitation-only Global Services, Stuker enjoys exclusive perks and usually flies first class. Most of his travel is work-related, especially to Asia and Australia to assist car dealerships, and he has visited every U.S. state. Stuker will also appear on Spike TV's reality show 'Car Lot Rescue,' where he helps struggling dealerships worldwide. His pursuit of the one-million-mile milestone began as a friendly challenge with another frequent flyer, which he continued solo when his friend withdrew for health reasons. Stuker joked that he could not have achieved this flying in coach. Though his record is impressive, Stuker faces friendly competition from Fred Finn, a British businessman in his 70s who claims to have flown over 15 million miles across different airlines. Stuker told the New York Times, health permitting, he intends to surpass Finn’s self-reported record in the coming years. Beyond work, Stuker and his wife, a teacher, love to travel together for quick getaways. Their upcoming plans include trips to Buenos Aires, Hawaii for President’s Day, and a romantic week split between Paris and Prague.

article_content: Helen Hart, 46, from Redruth, Cornwall, was sentenced to four years in prison for embezzling over £300,000 from PDP Green Consulting Ltd, her employer. Hart used the stolen money to fund a lavish lifestyle, including hiring a private jet for £5,990, spending £7,816 on a hotel stay in Devon, purchasing luxury cars such as a Porsche Boxster, a Range Rover, and a £46,500 Mercedes, and paying for other extravagant expenses. Over approximately six and a half years, Hart siphoned company funds to cover her rent, bills, and personal shopping, including £2,000 on a kitchen, £4,985 on 48 bottles of wine, and undisclosed amounts at Marks & Spencer. She also spent £31,368 on home renovations. PDP Green Consulting Ltd, an architectural and engineering firm based in Truro, Cornwall, discovered the missing funds in May 2011 when the company faced an unpaid £271,000 tax bill after its accounts were wiped out. The estimated financial loss from Hart's fraudulent activities totaled £325,000. Judge John Neligan described her conduct as a 'blatant and brazen breach of trust' and emphasized that Hart carried out the fraud while in a senior and trusted role at the company. He noted that about £65,000 was spent on luxury vehicles. Hart claimed she had only taken £190,000, but the court established the total loss was higher. Hart admitted to using company money to pay her living costs and to fund shopping sprees. She also attempted to donate £10,000 to the charity Ella's Memory, but the cheque bounced. Additionally, she allegedly tried to sponsor Truro Rugby Club, falsely claiming to have inherited £10 million. According to company boss Philip Desmonde and his family, Hart tried to imitate his wife Susanne in dress and lifestyle choices. Hart explained her wealth by telling her employer she had received an inheritance from a relative. Roger Green, managing director of PDP Green, expressed disappointment at the four-year sentence, stating that Hart had defrauded the company over a long period and shown no remorse. Detective Constable Nick Stidwill stated that Hart's luxury lifestyle was funded entirely by the company's stolen money.

article_content: A security guard and his girlfriend have been found guilty of stealing football boots from West Bromwich Albion’s training ground. Tanya Cotton, 24, helped her partner, Aaron Hinds, steal Nike boots valued at £200 that belonged to player Graham Dorrans on August 29 last year. Hinds, 25, admitted to taking the kit from Dorrans and trainers from James Morrison, 27. The thefts happened while Hinds worked at the club, and the pair were caught on CCTV, which was installed due to ongoing thefts. Last November, Hinds pleaded guilty to two counts of theft and one of burglary and was given a 12-month community order with 200 hours of unpaid work at Walsall Magistrates Court. Cotton initially denied involvement but was found guilty in the same court. Security footage showed Hinds choosing the boots, passing them to Cotton, who attempted to hide them in her leggings before handing them back to Hinds for concealment. Cotton stated she believed Hinds had permission to borrow the boots, trusting his explanation because of their relationship. However, the court determined she willingly assisted in the crime. Hinds planned to use the kit for Sunday league football as he couldn't afford his own. In addition to community service, he was ordered to pay £85 in costs and a £60 victim surcharge. Cotton is awaiting sentencing.

The only surviving 'Lord Kitchener Wants You' First World War recruiting poster available to the public has been put up for sale with an asking price of £15,000. This exceptionally rare poster, credited with encouraging millions to enlist, became one of the defining images of the conflict.

Despite its impact, the 'Kitchener Wants You' poster was not mass-produced compared to other recruitment posters, with only about 10,000 printed. Today, just three originals are known to exist: two are displayed in museums—the Imperial War Museum in London and the National Gallery of Victoria in Melbourne, Australia—while the third, now for sale, is the only one in private hands and available for purchase.

The iconic image was originally created by renowned artist Alfred Leete as the cover for a 1914 issue of London Opinion magazine. The Parliamentary Recruiting Committee adapted Leete’s artwork for their posters, distributing it across the country. Lord Kitchener, then Secretary of State for War and a respected military leader, features prominently, pointing directly at the viewer—a design intended to personally motivate enlistment. The phrase on the poster was changed from 'needs you' to 'wants you' to enhance its persuasive power.

The poster's influence extended beyond Britain: it inspired the famous American Uncle Sam 'I Want You' recruitment poster. Lord Kitchener lost his life in 1916 when his ship was sunk by a German mine en route to Russia.

The poster now for sale was acquired at auction in 1983 for just £100 and has been part of a private collection ever since. Auction experts predict it will sell for at least £15,000 when it is offered by Dorset-based auction house Onslows. The poster is set to be exhibited to the public at the Chalke Valley History Festival in Wiltshire from June 23 to 29 before being auctioned on July 9.

Patrick Bogue, auctioneer at Onslows, explained that at the outset of World War I, the British Army faced a shortage of soldiers, relying heavily on recruitment campaigns like the one featuring Lord Kitchener. Bogue emphasized that the Kitchener poster is considered the 'holy grail' among historic recruitment posters, with this particular example representing a unique and valuable piece of wartime history.

article_content: Collective memories—shared recollections passed down through generations—are central to many conflicts worldwide. For example, in April 2007, violent clashes erupted in Tallinn, Estonia, as disputes over how to remember World War II and the Soviet era divided ethnic Estonians and Russians. The unrest left one person dead, over a hundred injured, and resulted in more than a thousand arrests. Unlike history—which aims to examine the past from multiple viewpoints—collective memory simplifies complex events into narratives that strengthen group identity. These stories spread through family lore, education, media, and social traditions. Persistent violence in Nigeria between Fulani herders and farming communities has deep roots in these inherited narratives. Farmers often see land disputes as a repeat of historical invasions, while herders trace their land rights to ancestral ties with the Sokoto Caliphate. Such conflicting memories are reinforced by a legacy of colonialism, wars, and competition for resources—making reconciliation difficult. Recent case studies from Benue State indicate that these shared pasts intensify current grievances and perpetuate cycles of violence. Some experts advocate for cognitive reappraisal techniques to help manage conflict. By encouraging people to reassess emotional events from future or distanced perspectives, such as imagining how they would view a situation years later, groups may reduce hostility and foster more peaceful interactions. Though more research is needed to adapt these approaches to various cultural contexts, including Nigeria, incorporating an understanding of collective memory into conflict resolution strategies shows promise for achieving sustainable peace.

Los disturbios causaron una muerte, más de cien heridos y resultaron en más de mil arrestos. Algunos expertos apoyan el uso de técnicas de reevaluación cognitiva para ayudar a gestionar los conflictos. Al incentivar a las personas a reconsiderar situaciones emocionales desde perspectivas futuras o distantes—como imaginar cómo verían una situación años después—los grupos pueden reducir la hostilidad y fomentar interacciones más pacíficas. Aunque se requiere más investigación para adaptar estos métodos a diferentes contextos culturales, incluido Nigeria, incorporar el entendimiento de la memoria colectiva en las estrategias de resolución de conflictos muestra potencial para alcanzar una paz sostenible.

Bristol City Council spent more than £23,000 of taxpayers' money in an unsuccessful attempt to prevent details from emerging about a child protection case, where a four-year-old girl had been placed in foster care with a man suspected of possessing indecent images of children. Despite police raising concerns and confiscating a laptop containing abuse images, social services took almost three weeks to remove the child from the foster home. The foster father later died by suicide.

The council sought a High Court injunction to restrict media coverage, arguing that it was to protect the child's identity. However, the High Court overturned the restrictions, with Mr Justice Baker ruling that the public had a right to know about the case, while continuing to protect the identities of the child and her families. According to a Freedom of Information request, the legal action cost the council at least £23,528, covering legal fees for multiple hearings and representation for the foster family. Staff time was not included, so the real cost is likely higher.

Bristol City Council's handling of the case drew condemnation from the judiciary and criticism from public advocates such as the TaxPayers' Alliance, who said the legal expenses were an inappropriate use of funds in the context of child protection failures.

The girl remained in the foster placement for several weeks after the initial concerns were raised in March 2012. Social services did not act immediately, even after reports that another child in the household had physically hurt the girl. No social services staff have faced disciplinary action, and the findings of an independent review are still pending. The girl has now been relocated to a new foster family.

On this special day, she updated her look by adding flowers to her hair, evoking the style of her Gangubai Kathiawadi character. She received her award from President Droupadi Murmu to much admiration. Fashion designer Gautam Gupta praised Alia’s decision, emphasizing the lasting significance of heirloom saris and the value of reusing them for memorable moments. Shilpi Gupta, from Shilpi Gupta Designs, highlighted that restyling wedding garments invites personal creativity and fosters sustainable fashion choices. The designers proposed ways to modernize traditional attire: combine saris or lehengas with trendy blouses or shirts, tailor saris into gowns or jackets, and pair blouses or dupattas with different outfits to create fresh styles. They affirmed that reviving wedding attire not only recalls special memories but also champions an eco-friendly approach to dressing. Ultimately, the experts encouraged experimenting with various looks to express one’s individuality and to embrace sustainability by giving cherished outfits new life.

article_content: Harry Roberts, convicted of murdering three police officers in 1966, enjoyed a champagne birthday party and outings to a bowling alley and restaurant while on day release from prison. Roberts, who was sentenced to life imprisonment for the killings of Geoffrey Fox, Detective Sergeant Christopher Head, and Detective Constable David Wombwell, was allowed temporary release as part of his reintegration process after serving a minimum term of 30 years. He was released three months ago after spending 48 years behind bars. While on temporary release in 2001, Roberts volunteered at an animal sanctuary in the East Midlands. For his 65th birthday, staff at the sanctuary organized a party with birthday cake and champagne. According to a source, Roberts was in a good mood, enjoyed the party, and raised a toast to freedom. He also received gifts such as aftershave and socks, and participated in activities like bowling for the first time and dining at a restaurant, where he sent back his steak to be cooked to his satisfaction. Roberts's crimes occurred just six months after the abolition of hanging in the UK. He evaded capture for six months before being found hiding in a barn. During his trial, the judge described the murders, which took place near Wormwood Scrubs prison in West London, as 'the most heinous in a generation.' Gillian Wombwell, widow of Detective Constable David Wombwell, spoke of her distress over the privileges Roberts enjoyed while serving his sentence and after his release. Following Roberts's release in November, it was revealed he had a three-year relationship with a woman 27 years his junior, named as Susan. The relationship ended before his release, but they had exchanged letters and discussed living together if Roberts were freed. Susan said she learned of his impending release from the news, describing mixed emotions over the situation.

article_content: Building strong connections in the workplace can make teams more vibrant and productive, and icebreaker games are a fantastic way to encourage that. By engaging in quick, fun activities, team members can relax, communicate openly, and understand each other better. Check out these seven great icebreaker games for the office:  1. Show & Tell: Team members bring an object that represents something important about themselves, such as a favorite pastime or meaningful item. Each person briefly explains their choice, and others can ask questions to learn more.  2. Collaborative Storytelling: Sitting in a circle, participants create a story together, with each person adding up to three sentences based on what the previous person said. This activity promotes creativity and teamwork.  3. Speed Networking: Similar to speed dating, this involves quick, timed chats between colleagues. After each round, everyone rotates to a new partner. Conversation can focus on personal interests, work topics, or answers to questions drawn from a jar.  4. The Human Knot: In this game, everyone stands in a circle and holds hands with two other people, not next to them. The challenge is to untangle the group into a circle without letting go, which builds problem-solving skills and teamwork.  5. Two Truths and a Lie: Suitable for virtual or in-person meetings, each participant says two true things and one false thing about themselves, while others try to guess which statement is the lie. This improves attention and listening.  6. The Name Game: Especially helpful for new teams, this game helps everyone remember names. Players introduce themselves using an adjective that starts with the same letter as their name (like 'Creative Chris'), and the next person repeats previous names before adding their own.  7. Memory Wall: Using sticky notes or a whiteboard, everyone writes down a memorable or funny work experience. Team members then guess who wrote each note. This game helps share good memories and builds camaraderie.  Introducing these games into the workplace can create a friendly environment, encourage teamwork, and strengthen relationships, making daily work both enjoyable and effective.

Muestra y Cuenta: Cada integrante lleva un objeto que represente algo importante de su vida, como un pasatiempo favorito o un artículo significativo. Cada persona explica brevemente su elección y los demás pueden hacer preguntas para conocer más detalles.  2. Historia Colaborativa: Sentados en círculo, los participantes crean juntos una historia; cada uno agrega hasta tres frases continuando lo que dijo la persona anterior. Esta dinámica promueve la creatividad y el trabajo en equipo.  3. Networking Rápido: Similar al speed dating, consiste en conversaciones cortas y cronometradas entre colegas. Luego de cada ronda, todos cambian de pareja. Puede hablarse sobre intereses personales, temas del trabajo o responder preguntas de un frasco.  4. El Nudo Humano: En este juego, todos forman un círculo y toman de las manos a dos personas diferentes (que no sean las de al lado). El objetivo es desenredarse y volver a formar el círculo sin soltarse, lo que favorece la resolución de problemas y el trabajo colaborativo.  5. Dos Verdades y una Mentira: Perfecto para sesiones virtuales o presenciales; cada persona comparte dos verdades y una mentira sobre sí misma, y los demás deben adivinar cuál es la mentira. Esto potencia la escucha activa.  6. El Juego de los Nombres: Útil para equipos nuevos, ayuda a recordar nombres. Cada uno se presenta con un adjetivo que comienza con la misma letra de su nombre (por ejemplo, 'Sonriente Sofía') y el siguiente repite lo anterior antes de añadir el suyo.  7. Muro de Recuerdos: Usando notas adhesivas o una pizarra, cada persona escribe una experiencia positiva o graciosa vivida en el trabajo. Luego, el equipo trata de adivinar quién escribió cada una. Este juego fomenta la memoria y fortalece los vínculos. article_content: Until now, only Garmin's Venu 2 Plus smartwatch featured atrial fibrillation (AFib) detection via an electrocardiogram (ECG). As of this summer, Garmin is expanding ECG support to several of its high-end wearables: the Venu 3, Fenix 7 Pro, Epix Pro (Gen 2), and tactix 7 — AMOLED Edition. The ECG functionality, approved by the FDA for accuracy in AFib detection, relies on Garmin’s new Elevate v5 heart rate sensor, exclusive to these models. Users can record a 30-second heart rhythm session, with results stored in the Garmin Connect app for review and sharing. This ECG upgrade cannot be retroactively brought to older Garmin models lacking the newest sensor. Unless Garmin implements passive AFib detection using existing heart rate data—like Samsung, Apple, and Fitbit already offer—older watches won't gain this feature. Currently, the clinically validated ECG app is only available to customers in the United States. According to Garmin, they plan to introduce the feature in more regions as they receive regulatory approvals. Of the supported models, most are priced at the higher end ($900+), with the Venu 3 presenting a more accessible option at $450. The Venu 3 is also the first to introduce Garmin’s advanced Sleep Coaching, which analyzes naps, heart rate variability (HRV), and sleep stages to provide personalized recommendations. Experts note that the Elevate v5 heart rate sensor could enable future features like skin temperature tracking, though Garmin has not confirmed plans for this. Owners of supported devices can access the ECG app by updating to the latest software. The Garmin Venu 3 stands out for its long battery life, advanced health and sleep sensors, dedicated wheelchair mode, and the classic Garmin functionalities. Currently, it is available on Amazon with a 5% discount.

article_content: Ireland stands out among Western nations for its outspoken criticism of Israel's actions in Gaza and its support for Palestinian rights. Following the October 7 attack by Hamas in Israel, which resulted in approximately 1,200 deaths and 240 people taken captive, Irish Prime Minister Leo Varadkar condemned the violence. Yet, just days later, he emphasized that 'Israel doesn’t have the right to do wrong,' diverging from other European leaders stressing Israel’s right to self-defense during its subsequent bombing campaign of Gaza. In 41 days, over 11,400 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli operations, according to reports. Varadkar stated that Israel’s bombardment constitutes 'collective punishment,' which the Geneva Conventions prohibit. Irish President Michael D. Higgins, in a largely ceremonial role, criticized European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen for expressing unconditional support for Israel without referencing the occupation of Palestinian territories. Ireland was among the first EU countries to call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, highlighting urgent civilian needs. Irish citizens, like teacher and Fianna Fail member Niamh Nichillin, have expressed empathy for Gaza’s residents, describing Israeli air strikes as disproportionate. She noted, 'This can hardly be called a war in the usual sense.' She and others see official statements from Israeli officials as motivated by a desire to destroy Gaza, which she calls unacceptable. On October 18, Ireland announced an additional 13 million euros in humanitarian aid for Palestinians, bringing its 2023 total to 29 million euros. The Irish Foreign Ministry called the crisis in Gaza a 'humanitarian catastrophe of unprecedented magnitude.' Nichillin hopes Ireland can continue to advocate for a ceasefire, an end to the siege, and increased humanitarian access. Historically, Ireland has supported Palestinian statehood, being the first EU country to do so in 1980 and the last to open an Israeli embassy in Dublin. Politician Frances Black's 2018 Occupied Territories Bill, which sought to ban trading goods from areas occupied by Israel, garnered broad support, though it was dropped during 2020 coalition talks. In 2021, Ireland was the first EU member to declare Israel’s actions as a 'de-facto annexation' of Palestinian land. Cathal O’hEanna of Sinn Fein draws parallels between Irish history of colonization and the Palestinian struggle, stating, 'Our centuries-long struggle for the right to self-determination resonates with the Palestinian struggle for statehood and independence.' John Lyndon of the Alliance for Middle East Peace noted early Irish solidarity with both Jews and Palestinians, with sentiments shifting after Israeli settlements expanded post-1967. Pro-Palestinian protests continue across Ireland, and on a recent evening, over 1,000 people protested outside Dublin’s parliament as motions calling to expel Israel’s ambassador and refer Israel to the International Criminal Court were debated but ultimately defeated. Irish writers, including Sally Rooney and Michael Magee, are organizing events under 'Irish Writers for Palestine' to show solidarity. Magee commented on increased marginalization of pro-Palestinian voices. Lyndon, who lost peace advocate Vivian Silver in the Hamas attack, urges expressions of solidarity that promote cooperation and peace. Lyndon suggests Ireland could act as a peace negotiator due to its history with conflict resolution and good relations with the US, noting it lacks the colonial legacy of other EU states. In Northern Ireland, views on the conflict are split, often along sectarian lines, with Palestinian and Israeli flags common in respective communities. Activist Amr Hashad sees similarities between struggles in Ireland and Palestine. He questions why Western nations have not negotiated with Hamas as they did with the IRA during the Troubles. Sinn Fein, unlike many other Western parties, has stated it would not rule out talks with Hamas in pursuit of peace. While Ireland does not officially recognize Palestine, discussions on recognition are ongoing. Foreign Minister Michael Martin acknowledged the government is preparing for possible recognition, though analysts note this could isolate Ireland within the EU and with the US. Some, like translator Stephanie Nic Carthaig and composer Raymond Deane, urge Ireland to further distance itself from broader EU policy and push for an arms embargo on Israel. Sinn Fein's Mary Lou McDonald has said that recognizing Palestinian statehood would be a foreign policy priority if her party leads the government. This debate continues against the backdrop of Ireland’s history, public sympathy for Palestine, and calls for stronger action from its leaders.

article_content: The National Security Agency (NSA) has technology capable of covertly accessing and monitoring iPhones, according to privacy advocate and journalist Jacob Appelbaum. At the Chaos Communications Conference in Hamburg, Germany, Appelbaum presented evidence suggesting the NSA's surveillance tools include methods to extract information from computers and smartphones, even if offline. Appelbaum’s claims—which he described as more alarming than many expected—were backed by internal NSA slides. He detailed technologies such as hidden backdoors, which enable nearly undetectable remote access, and radar devices that extract electronic data. One slide showed how NSA agents could install malware on Apple iPhones, turning them into surveillance devices. In response, Apple told AllThingsD: 'Apple has never worked with the NSA to create a backdoor in any of our products, including iPhone. Additionally, we have been unaware of this alleged NSA program targeting our products.' Another slide described a 'portable continuous wave generator,' which can, in combination with electronic implants, detect keystrokes and screen content on offline computers. The NSA’s NIGHTSTAND device can allegedly tamper with wireless connections from up to eight miles (13 kilometers) away. NSA spokeswoman Vanee Vines said she was not aware of Appelbaum’s presentation and would not comment on 'alleged foreign intelligence activities.' She repeated the NSA's position that their surveillance targets valid foreign intelligence subjects. Documents first published by German magazine Der Spiegel detail the undercover work of the NSA's Tailored Access Operations (TAO) and their use of tools developed by Advanced Network Technology (ANT). The TAO catalog lists technologies such as modified cables, USB devices, and fake GSM base stations capable of intercepting mobile phone signals—for example, a cable allowing screen monitoring for $30, or a GSM base station for $40,000. These surveillance tools have reportedly been used not only against suspected terrorists but also to monitor communications of foreign leaders, like German Chancellor Angela Merkel. Many tools in the catalog were designed for devices current in 2008 or earlier, and some may now be obsolete. NSA devices exploit vulnerabilities in products from companies including Cisco, Dell, Juniper, Hewlett-Packard, and Huawei. While Appelbaum and Der Spiegel have previously reported extensively on Edward Snowden’s disclosures, it remains unclear if all recent documents are linked directly to Snowden.

article_content: Published: December 11, 2013, By Emma Thomas. Prince Harry shared that the Walking With The Wounded adventurers trekking to the South Pole 'can't wait to reach the end' of their challenge. The 29-year-old royal, who is participating in the demanding charity expedition, explained that spirits were high after organizers suspended the competitive element of the trek. Harry was part of a British team racing against teams from the Commonwealth and the United States. All 12 injured service personnel from Britain, America, Canada, and Australia have overcome life-changing injuries and trained extensively for the extreme conditions in Antarctica. The race aspect was halted over the weekend when some participants, including injured servicemen and women, became fatigued due to difficult terrain. Now, the three teams have joined forces. Harry said they are just over three days from their destination. In a voice blog recorded in Antarctica, Harry said: 'We're three and a half days from the South Pole. It feels like the end is coming quickly. We've been here for about three and a half weeks. Everyone's spirits are really high. The race was canceled a few days ago—a very good decision. It's great to see everyone mixing together, not just at night when we camp, but also during the day.' Harry highlighted fellow adventurer Duncan Slater, who lost both legs after an improvised explosive device exploded under his vehicle in Afghanistan in 2009. Harry joked that for Duncan, walking to the South Pole may not be challenging enough, which was why he enjoyed the competition so much. He added: 'Everyone just can’t wait to reach the finish. I think people back home will be impressed that Duncan, who has no legs, is managing to walk 100km (62 miles) in these conditions. It's an incredible achievement.' The group is trekking around 9 to 12 miles (15 to 20 km) each day, pulling 154 lb (70 kg) sleds called pulks toward the southernmost point on Earth. Harry described the current conditions: 'The weather is still holding off, which is really good—it's about minus 35°C (minus 31°F) with 24-hour daylight, which helps keep the tents warm at night.' Harry supported the organizers’ decision to call off the competitive element for safety reasons. The team began the trek in temperatures of -27°C, with wind chill dropping it to -35°C, and those tough conditions have persisted. Organizers said the event, which started the previous Sunday and was shortened by 37 miles due to weather delays, was proving too taxing. By the fifth day, it became apparent the harsh Antarctic reality was becoming overwhelming, even for the determined team members.

Celebrity trainer Jon Denoris believes you don’t need expensive gym memberships or equipment to achieve a fit, healthy body. He’s worked with stars like Rachel Stevens and Natasha Bedingfield, but says his simple, accessible routines are for everyone, not just celebrities. 

In his book, 'The Pop-Up Gym,' Denoris shows how anyone can use everyday items—like water bottles, bags, or even office furniture—for effective workouts at home, in the park, or while traveling. The book, published by Bloomsbury Sport and released at £12.99, brings together his experience adapting workouts for entertainers and professionals in all kinds of locations.

Jon highlights consistency and sustainable routines over chasing fitness fads. His methods focus on adaptable exercises—squats, lunges, high-intensity intervals—anywhere, anytime, making it possible to stay active even with a busy schedule. Celebrity clients such as Perez Hilton and Boris Johnson have benefited from these flexible strategies, fitting exercise into their hotel rooms or offices.

Denoris also addresses the changing fitness landscape, noting that wearable technology and remote coaching are making fitness guidance more accessible than ever. Alongside exercise advice, his book covers motivation, nutrition, and forming healthy habits that stick for life.

article_content: Manish Sisodia, former Deputy Chief Minister of Delhi, was granted a temporary six-hour release from Tihar jail to visit his seriously ill wife during Diwali. This decision by the Delhi High Court, executed through the Rouse Avenue court, enabled Sisodia to meet his wife at AB 17, Mathura Road—the property now assigned to Delhi Minister Atishi but previously his official residence. Security was stringent, with only Sisodia and his wife allowed to meet and heavy police presence throughout the premises. Sisodia remains in jail in connection with the Delhi liquor policy case. Despite multiple attempts, his bail pleas have been denied by the Supreme Court and lower courts, although the High Court recently permitted his visitation for humanitarian reasons. In a separate case, judicial custody was extended for MP Sanjay Singh regarding the Delhi Excise Policy money laundering allegations, now until November 24, 2023. Singh was also authorized by the court to attend a defamation hearing in Amritsar, Punjab after a production warrant was issued. For this, court-ordered travel and security arrangements were made, including transportation by Rajdhani Express. His advocate submitted documents for Singh's signature related to development projects, which the court approved. On the economic front, India’s industrial growth rate dropped to 5.8% in September 2023, down from a recent peak of 10.3%. Contributing factors included an unfavorable base effect and excessive rainfall that hampered output. Business headlines report that Ranjan Pai, Manipal Education and Medical Group chairman, invested Rs 1,400 crore (approximately $168 million) in Aakash Institute, an affiliate of Byju’s. Additionally, manufacturing companies are increasingly recruiting 2024 graduates skilled in technology and digital tools.

Ben Foster was informed by England manager Roy Hodgson last week that he would start against Ecuador on Wednesday, and he has praised Hodgson’s inclusive management style. Hodgson’s approach stands in contrast to the 2010 World Cup under Fabio Capello, when England’s three goalkeepers did not know who would start the opening group game against the United States until shortly before kick-off. On that occasion, Robert Green was selected but made a costly mistake that allowed Clint Dempsey to equalize, which became a lasting image of a disappointing tournament.

Foster, currently the regular back-up to first-choice England goalkeeper Joe Hart at West Bromwich Albion, is preparing for his first England start in nearly four years. 'I knew last week I’d be playing this game, so I could tailor my week to get ready for it,' Foster said. 'Outfield players have a different routine, but for goalkeepers, it’s crucial to know in advance so you can adjust training, gym work, and prepare mentally.'

He continued, 'It’s the same at your club—if you know you’re playing regularly, you can plan everything better. Roy is very good at being open and approachable, often taking time to speak with players and explain things clearly.'

Foster recalled watching on television when Green let Dempsey’s low shot slip through his hands in Rustenburg, South Africa. 'I was gutted for him. He’s a fantastic guy and a really nice man. It’s a real shame. I don’t know if the late decision affected him. The World Cup brings a lot of pressure, but he handled it and has since bounced back, earning promotion with QPR.'

Foster has praised Hodgson’s approach to management compared to other managers.

Kings of Leon have canceled the remainder of their U.S. tour, citing exhaustion and vocal problems affecting lead singer Caleb Followill. This follows an incident in Dallas where Caleb left the stage after complaining about the heat and feeling ill, promising to return but ultimately not coming back. His bandmates addressed the crowd, apologizing for the abrupt ending.

Members of the band later expressed on Twitter how disappointed and embarrassed they were, with some alluding to deeper internal issues within the group beyond Caleb's exhaustion. The band's management has confirmed tickets will be refunded and stated the U.S. shows cannot be rescheduled due to international tour commitments. They aim to resume their performances in Canada on September 28.

Kings of Leon, a family band from Nashville known for hits like the Grammy-winning 'Use Somebody,' have experienced similar troubles before, such as ending a St. Louis concert due to pigeon droppings and getting into a backstage altercation at the 2009 Brit Awards. Caleb, who is married to model Lily Aldridge, has not commented personally, but the band's ongoing challenges and successes suggest their story will continue to evolve.

He further emphasized the necessity of balancing calculated risk-taking with maintaining scoring rates, and the importance of pre-match analysis sessions. article_content: The Bridgegate controversy is escalating for New Jersey Governor Chris Christie, as more politicians share their opinions on the issue. State Senator Ray Lesniak, a Democrat, called Christie ‘Liar-in-Chief’ on the Saturday morning television program, Up with Steve Kornacki. Lesniak said, 'The Liar-in-Chief is Chris Christie, and obstruction of justice may be his biggest problem. I don’t believe he was directly involved in the lane closures, but those closures violate federal law.' Lesniak criticized Christie for creating a 'phony story' about a traffic study to explain the lane closures and argued that Christie's sudden acknowledgment of the situation came only after it was exposed. Not everyone has turned against Christie. On Sunday, former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani defended Christie, saying the governor’s denial of any prior knowledge of the George Washington Bridge lane closures seemed credible. Giuliani noted, 'He says he didn’t know. I think he’s being truthful. He wouldn’t issue such a broad denial unless it was accurate.' Giuliani added that if it turns out Christie did know, he has put his political career at great risk. Giuliani explained that in large administrations, oversights can occur, especially during campaign periods. He compared the situation to other government controversies, suggesting that leaders sometimes miss critical information. Christie, who was considered a potential presidential candidate in 2016, has repeated that he had no previous knowledge of the plan to close the bridge’s lanes, allegedly as payback against a mayor who refused to endorse his re-election. Assemblyman John Wisniewski, leader of the legislative investigation, has said he finds Christie's denials difficult to accept given the number of close aides involved. Wisniewski told NBC he doubted Christie only learned of the scandal the day of his press conference, and described the involvement of Christie's senior staff as too closely tied for the governor to be unaware. Wisniewski argued that using a public resource for political retribution could constitute a crime and, if linked to the governor, would be an impeachable offense. A special legislative session is scheduled to re-authorize subpoena power for the investigation. Prieto, the Assembly speaker-elect, has stated the investigation must continue to answer unresolved questions about public safety and abuse of power. Christie's press secretary did not respond to requests for comment. Despite the scandal, Christie is expected to attend a campaign event for Florida Governor Rick Scott. Public opinion, according to a poll by Rasmussen Reports, shows that 54 percent of likely New Jersey voters believe Christie was aware of the lane closures, and 56 percent said he should resign if it is proven he approved the tactic as retaliation. Only 36 percent believe Christie's claims of ignorance, and 71 percent suspect other political figures were similarly targeted. Forty-seven percent believe involved staff should be prosecuted. Before the scandal, a Quinnipiac University poll found Christie to be one of the most favorably viewed politicians in the country. However, new revelations show some of Christie's aides were aware of safety risks posed by the lane closures, but the closures still continued for four days. Christie has forcefully denied involvement in a lengthy press briefing.

article_content: FIFA has introduced tougher sanctions to combat racism in global soccer, including the possibility of relegation for clubs and lengthy suspensions for individuals engaged in racist conduct. The move, which was disclosed at the FIFA Congress held in Mauritius, responds to the ongoing spotlight on racist incidents in football worldwide. With a two-stage system, initial offenses may result in warnings, fines, or games played behind closed doors. For repeat or severe violations, clubs could face points deductions, expulsion from tournaments, or relegation. Anyone found guilty of racist behavior will face a minimum ban of five matches. These new rules must now be enforced by FIFA’s over 200 member associations, with only one, unnamed, dissenting. During the announcement, FIFA president Sepp Blatter condemned racism and discrimination, citing examples such as Kevin-Prince Boateng's walk-off after abuse during a match for A.C. Milan and the punishment of Giorgos Katidis of AEK Athens for a Nazi-style salute. The anti-racism group Kick It Out praised FIFA’s stronger stance, noting its ongoing push for more severe actions on discrimination in football. Chairman Lord Herman Ouseley expressed hope that the reforms would bring substantial improvements, applauding FIFA’s efforts to align with other sports in tackling unacceptable behavior. Additionally, FIFA revealed that three women will be joining its executive committee, which oversees key decisions including those related to the World Cup.

Esta medida, anunciada en el Congreso de la FIFA en Mauricio, responde a la atención constante sobre incidentes racistas en el deporte. El sistema de dos etapas contempla que los primeros delitos reciban advertencias, multas o partidos jugados a puerta cerrada. Para reincidentes o casos graves, los clubes podrían perder puntos, ser expulsados de torneos o descender de categoría. El presidente, Lord Herman Ouseley, expresó su esperanza de que estas reformas traigan mejoras sustanciales y aplaudió los esfuerzos de la FIFA por equiparar su lucha con la de otros deportes frente a conductas inaceptables. Además, la FIFA anunció que tres mujeres se incorporarán a su comité ejecutivo, encargado de decisiones clave como la elección de sedes para la Copa del Mundo.

With Lent just a few weeks away, chocolate might soon become one of the treats Pope Francis gives up for the religious fasting period. Therefore, he may want to enjoy his recent gift now—a life-sized statue of himself, crafted from 1.5 tons of cocoa sourced from Atitlán, Guatemala. This unique chocolate statue was presented to the Pope at the Vatican by a group of 20 amateur chocolatiers.

The statue was created by students from the Accademia of Maestri Cioccolatieri near Venice, Italy, who spent four weeks constructing it to honor Pope Francis, whose popularity has soared since he was elected Bishop of Rome in March last year. Despite the impressive creation, the Pope’s simple and health-conscious dietary habits—favoring fruit, salads, and skinless chicken—make it unlikely he will indulge in a piece of the chocolate version of himself.

Pope Francis, who hails from Flores, Buenos Aires, is known for his frugal meals, only occasionally enjoying an espresso or a glass of wine. Thus, it's possible the chocolate statue will instead serve a charitable purpose.

In keeping with his charitable spirit, Pope Francis recently auctioned his Harley Davidson motorcycle and biker jacket to raise funds for Caritas Roma, a charity supporting those in need globally. The 1,585cc Harley Davidson went under the hammer at Bonhams' Grand Palais auction with an initial estimate of £10,000. However, keen interest pushed the price up dramatically, with an online buyer ultimately paying €210,000 (£175,000), and after premiums, the final price reached £200,976. His biker jacket was also sold, raising £47,851, bringing the total from these charity sales to nearly £250,000. The success echoes previous instances, such as when Pope Benedict XVI’s Volkswagen Golf fetched £127,000 at auction in 2005, with all proceeds benefiting charitable causes.

article_content: Irish homeowners applying for debt reductions will be required to give up satellite television, foreign holidays, and private school education for their children under a new strict insolvency law aimed at tackling the country's debt crisis. On Thursday, the Insolvency Service of Ireland outlined monthly spending caps for those seeking debt arrangements with creditors, illustrating the ongoing impact of austerity on Irish spending patterns. For example, a single person will have a monthly allowance of €247.04 for food, €57.31 for heating, and €125.97 for ‘social inclusion and participation’—an expenses category covering events such as sports and cinema outings. “A reasonable standard of living does not mean living in luxury,” said Lorcan O’Connor, director of the newly established Insolvency Service of Ireland. “But it also doesn’t mean people should be punished and live merely at a subsistence level.” In most cases, applicants will also have to forgo private health insurance and cars—unless they do not have access to public transportation, in which case they may keep their vehicle. These guidelines are Ireland’s first attempt to set out acceptable living standards for those seeking bankruptcy or insolvency arrangements under the new system. Banks are expected to use the guidelines as they prepare to restructure tens of thousands of home loans in the coming months. Persistent high unemployment and declining wages, a result of a prolonged economic crisis, have driven nearly one in four Irish mortgage holders to the brink. Approximately 120,000 Irish mortgages are more than 90 days in arrears, while a further 100,000 loans have been given temporary adjustments. Unlike many EU countries—including the UK—Dublin’s insolvency regime includes secured mortgage debt, intended to encourage banks to agree to long-term restructuring deals with debtors. In England, insolvency law is less prescriptive; ‘reasonable’ expenses for bankrupts can include holidays, mobile phones, and video rentals, although gym memberships, private health care, gambling, cigarettes, and alcohol are considered unreasonable. English debtors do not face set monthly cash limits. Alan Shatter, Ireland’s minister for justice, warned banks that heavier losses may occur should they refuse to agree to debt arrangements with struggling mortgage holders, who may instead seek bankruptcy. Property prices have halved since Ireland’s market peaked in 2007, leaving around 400,000 mortgage holders in negative equity. In contrast to some US states, Irish mortgage holders cannot eliminate their debts simply by surrendering their property; banks may pursue borrowers for any shortfall after repossession. Last month, Dublin ordered banks to provide long-term solutions for mortgage holders in distress, raising concerns about the risk of ‘moral hazard’. “We will do write-offs. It is part of the necessary give-and-take in restructuring, where both sides make concessions but it is not simply debt forgiveness,” said David Duffy, chief executive of Allied Irish Banks. “Anything done will consider the potential for moral hazard,” he added.
translated_content: Los propietarios irlandeses que soliciten la reducción de deudas deberán renunciar a la televisión por satélite, las vacaciones al extranjero y la educación privada para sus hijos bajo una nueva y estricta ley de insolvencia destinada a abordar la crisis de deuda del país. El jueves, el Servicio de Insolvencia de Irlanda presentó límites mensuales de gasto para quienes busquen acuerdos de deuda con acreedores, mostrando el impacto continuo de la austeridad en los patrones de gasto irlandeses. Por ejemplo, a una persona soltera se le permitirá una asignación mensual de €247.04 para alimentos, €57.31 para calefacción y €125.97 para ‘inclusión y participación social’—una categoría de gastos que cubre actividades como deportes y cine. “Un nivel de vida razonable no significa vivir con lujos”, dijo Lorcan O’Connor, director del recién creado Servicio de Insolvencia de Irlanda. “Pero tampoco significa que las personas deban ser castigadas y vivir únicamente en un nivel de subsistencia”. En la mayoría de los casos, los solicitantes también tendrán que renunciar al seguro médico privado y a los automóviles—a menos que no tengan acceso al transporte público, en cuyo caso podrán conservar su vehículo. Estas directrices son el primer intento de Irlanda para establecer estándares de vida aceptables para aquellos que buscan la bancarrota o arreglos de insolvencia bajo el nuevo sistema. Se espera que los bancos utilicen las directrices mientras se preparan para reestructurar decenas de miles de préstamos hipotecarios en los próximos meses. El desempleo persistentemente alto y la caída de los salarios, como resultado de una prolongada crisis económica, han llevado a casi uno de cada cuatro titulares de hipotecas irlandesas al límite. Aproximadamente 120,000 hipotecas irlandesas tienen más de 90 días en mora, mientras que otras 100,000 han recibido ajustes temporales. A diferencia de muchos países de la UE —incluido el Reino Unido— el régimen de insolvencia de Dublín incluye deuda hipotecaria garantizada, con la intención de fomentar que los bancos acuerden reestructuraciones a largo plazo con los deudores. En Inglaterra, la ley de insolvencia es menos restrictiva; los gastos ‘razonables’ para personas en bancarrota pueden incluir vacaciones, teléfonos móviles y alquiler de videos, aunque membresías a gimnasios, seguro médico privado, juegos de azar, cigarrillos y alcohol se consideran irrazonables. Los deudores ingleses no enfrentan límites mensuales fijos de efectivo. Alan Shatter, ministro de justicia de Irlanda, advirtió a los bancos que podrían enfrentar pérdidas mayores si se niegan a llegar a acuerdos de deuda con titulares de hipotecas con dificultades, quienes podrían optar por la bancarrota. Los precios de las viviendas se han reducido a la mitad desde el pico del mercado irlandés en 2007, dejando a alrededor de 400,000 titulares de hipotecas en patrimonio negativo. A diferencia de algunos estados de EE. UU., los titulares de hipotecas irlandeses no pueden eliminar sus deudas entregando simplemente la propiedad; los bancos pueden perseguir a los prestatarios por cualquier saldo restante después de la ejecución. El mes pasado, Dublín ordenó a los bancos ofrecer soluciones a largo plazo para titulares de hipotecas en dificultades, lo que genera preocupaciones sobre el riesgo de ‘riesgo moral’. “Haremos quitas. Es parte del necesario toma y daca en la reestructuración, donde ambas partes hacen concesiones pero no se trata simplemente de perdón de deudas”, dijo David Duffy, director ejecutivo de Allied Irish Banks. “Cualquier acción considerará el potencial de riesgo moral”, agregó.

article_content: A priest who was severely injured during an attempted robbery at his church managed to administer last rites to his fellow pastor, who died from a gunshot wound after the attack. Father Kenneth Walker, 28, the associate pastor at the Mother of Mercy Mission Catholic Church in Phoenix, Arizona, died at the hospital after being shot on Wednesday night. The church's pastor, Father Joseph Terra, 56, was also badly wounded but is reportedly in stable condition. According to a fellow priest, Father Terra was able to absolve and deliver last rites to Father Walker despite his severe injuries. The attack took place in the living quarters attached to the church, not in the main sanctuary. Father Walker, originally from Maple Hill, Kansas, was ordained two years ago. Reverend Fred Adamson of the Catholic Diocese of Phoenix noted that the church did not have security, but Father Terra was never afraid. The burglary occurred at 9 p.m., according to Phoenix Police Department spokesman Steve Martos. Despite critical injuries, Father Terra managed to call 911 after the attack. Parishioners gathered outside the church in the early hours on Thursday to pray. Phoenix Mayor Greg Stanton described the attacks as 'striking at our core.' No suspects have been identified and police are reviewing surveillance footage from around the church, near the state Capitol. Authorities are hoping to speak with Father Terra for more information. Father Walker died from his injuries at the hospital. Hospital staff were surprised Father Terra was able to communicate after sustaining such serious wounds. Thursday morning mass at Mother of Mercy Mission was canceled and moved to Saint Catherine of Siena Church. Parishioners mourned, and police held a news conference about the shooting. The Catholic Diocese released a statement expressing shock and sadness over the assault, noting that both priests belonged to the Priestly Fraternity of St. Peter. It confirmed Father Walker's death and that Father Terra is in stable but critical condition. The statement called for prayers for the priests, their families, and the parish. A green 2003 Mazda Tribute belonging to one of the priests was stolen from church property and later found unoccupied four blocks from the church. Authorities are continuing their investigation.

Según otro sacerdote, el padre Terra pudo absolver y administrar los últimos ritos al padre Walker a pesar de sus graves heridas. El ataque tuvo lugar en los aposentos conectados a la iglesia, no en el santuario principal. El padre Walker, originario de Maple Hill, Kansas, fue ordenado hace dos años. El reverendo Fred Adamson, de la Diócesis Católica de Phoenix, señaló que la iglesia no tenía seguridad, pero el padre Terra nunca tuvo miedo. El robo ocurrió a las 9 p.m., según el portavoz del Departamento de Policía de Phoenix, Steve Martos. A pesar de sus lesiones críticas, el padre Terra logró llamar al 911 después del ataque. Los feligreses se reunieron fuera de la iglesia en las primeras horas del jueves para orar. El alcalde de Phoenix, Greg Stanton, describió los ataques como 'un golpe a nuestro núcleo'. No se han identificado sospechosos y la policía está revisando grabaciones de seguridad de los alrededores de la iglesia, cercana al Capitolio estatal. Las autoridades esperan poder hablar con el padre Terra para obtener más información. El padre Walker falleció a causa de sus heridas en el hospital. El personal sanitario se sorprendió de que el padre Terra pudiera comunicarse después de sufrir lesiones tan graves. La misa matutina del jueves en la Misión Mother of Mercy fue cancelada y trasladada a la iglesia Saint Catherine of Siena. Los feligreses estaban de luto y la policía ofreció una rueda de prensa sobre el tiroteo. article_content: The public is being invited to become detectives and help uncover missing First World War sites through the 'Britain from Above' project. Led by English Heritage, the initiative encourages people to tag a vast digital archive of aerial photos, many taken during the 20th century by Aerofilms. These detailed images uniquely document how the Great War shaped England’s towns and countryside. With support from a £1.7 million Heritage Lottery Fund grant, the project is cataloguing, conserving, and digitizing nearly 95,000 aerial photographs. Participants can zoom in on the high-resolution images, tag and describe sites, and contribute by uploading modern or historical photos, stories, or family connections relevant to the locations. Sites waiting to be identified include defense installations, listening stations, shipyards, factories, gardens converted to allotments, hospitals, and country houses used during the war. An interactive map on the site allows users to explore and tag images by geographic location. Helen Grant, the Minister for the First World War Centenary, helped launch the project by tagging a photo of the drained lake in St James’s Park, an action taken during WWI to protect Buckingham Palace from air raids. She highlighted the extensive impact of the war and called on the public to get involved in preserving this aspect of national history. Simon Thurley, CEO of English Heritage, also urged people to use their local knowledge and family history to help identify these historic sites. As a bonus, contributors can freely download and keep copies of the photographs they’ve helped document.

article_content: Prominent BBC journalist John Humphrys has acknowledged that the corporation is 'grotesquely over-managed' and has historically exhibited a 'broadly liberal' bias in its reporting, particularly on issues like immigration and the European Union. Humphrys, a presenter on the Today programme, stated that BBC staff are generally university-educated and therefore more likely to have liberal views, which has influenced coverage through the years. He admitted the BBC was not sufficiently sceptical of pro-European and pro-immigration arguments, saying: 'We bought into the European ideal and didn’t examine potential negatives closely enough.' Humphrys said the BBC has now changed its approach, stating: 'I think we're out of that now. I think we have changed.' He also criticized the corporation's management, suggesting it remains overstaffed and needs more reduction in managers, a view he believes is shared by Director General Tony Hall. Previously, Humphrys criticized the BBC for being too large and for focusing excessively on bureaucratic processes. He addressed past reports of tension with fellow Today presenter Mishal Husain, dismissing them as taken out of context and confirming their positive working relationship. BBC Radio 4 colleague Eddie Mair echoed similar criticisms, describing management procedures as overly complex and obstacles to starting new projects. Last year, Lord Hall stated the BBC could have responded more quickly to bias accusations and needed to present a wider range of opinions.

article_content: Kim Jong Un appears to have further tightened his grip on North Korea’s leadership by reportedly removing his uncle, Jang Sung-taek, from power. Jang, who previously served as the Vice Chairman of the National Defense Commission and was regarded as a key power broker, is said to have been ousted for the third time, according to South Korean legislators. Experts are divided over the reasons behind this high-profile removal. While some interpret it as a sign that Kim feels threatened, the prevailing view is that such purges signal the leader’s confidence and dominance within the regime. Since taking control in 2011, Kim has systematically removed officials, including those once considered close allies. Similar to the tactics used by his father and grandfather, Kim appears to be eliminating both real and perceived threats by fostering rivalries among North Korea’s elite. Theories about Jang’s removal vary—from battles for power and influence, to competition among officials for proximity to Kim, and shifts between the authority of the military and the ruling Korean Workers’ Party. Though Jang was sometimes described in foreign media as a potential reformer pulling strings from behind the scenes, there’s little evidence he promoted substantial changes to North Korea’s policies or approach. The country’s leadership has long managed outside perceptions, often leveraging the idea of internal factions to gain leverage in negotiations. Kim, who assumed power after his father’s death, was initially seen by some observers as a possible reformer due to his time abroad. However, his actions over the past years—including the purge of senior figures and aggressive foreign policy stance—have proven otherwise. North Korea remains committed to its nuclear program, even enshrining it in the constitution, and shows no intention of trading its arsenal for economic incentives. Ultimately, the ousting of Jang Sung-taek is unlikely to bring about meaningful policy change. Instead, it signals the continued consolidation of power by the Kim family and the unlikelihood of major reforms or a softer foreign policy approach from Pyongyang. Observers are cautioned to prepare for ongoing strongman rule in North Korea.

article_content: Javier Milei, an anti-establishment politician, recently won the Argentine presidential election and has attracted attention for his radical and provocative policy proposals. Many critics have described his candidacy as a "leap into the void." With just two weeks before he becomes president of Latin America’s third-largest economy, questions remain about how his ideas will fare in practice. Milei has proposed dollarizing the economy and dissolving the Argentine Central Bank to combat hyperinflation. This would involve adopting the US dollar as Argentina’s official currency, replacing the peso, which Milei claims has rapidly lost value. However, implementing such moves would require approval from Congress and possibly a constitutional amendment. Although Milei won the presidency decisively, his Libertad Avanza party is only the third largest in Congress, indicating that significant negotiations lie ahead. Some economists doubt the feasibility of his plans, arguing that these measures could undermine the government’s control over monetary policy and expose Argentina to economic shocks tied to US dollar fluctuations, such as oil price spikes. Additionally, replacing pesos with dollars would require Argentina to obtain an estimated $35–$50 billion—funds the heavily indebted country currently lacks. Milei has acknowledged that his economic programme might take up to two years to reduce inflation, warning against unrealistic expectations. Another controversial point is Milei’s stance on climate change; he has described himself as skeptical of human-caused global warming and has proposed eliminating the environment ministry. This position risks putting Argentina at odds with the global consensus ahead of the COP28 climate summit. During his campaign, Milei vocally criticized Pope Francis, but after his election, he had a cordial conversation with the pontiff and invited him to visit Argentina. He has also signaled a more pragmatic approach in office, noting that certain responsibilities come with the presidency. Previously, Milei suggested he might freeze diplomatic ties with Brazil and China—Argentina’s top trading partners—because of ideological differences, aligning instead with the US, Israel, and other nations he describes as part of the "free world." This drew concern from Beijing and Brasilia. Despite earlier rhetoric, signals following the election suggest a continuation of economic relations. Chinese President Xi Jinping congratulated Milei, and Foreign Minister-designate Diana Mondino dismissed the idea of ending trade with China or Brazil. Milei’s invitation to former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro to his inauguration was seen as controversial, but Milei stated that current President Lula da Silva would be welcome if he chose to attend. Milei and his vice-presidential running mate, Victoria Villarruel, also stirred debate with their views on Argentina's 1976–83 military dictatorship, disputing the official number of those disappeared and arguing that violence during the era was committed by both the state and guerrilla groups. This position has drawn criticism from human rights organizations such as the Plaza de Mayo mothers and grandmothers. Ultimately, Milei and his team have shaken up Argentina’s political status quo, and the coming years will test whether they can implement their agenda.

Hundreds of US Jewish activists peacefully gathered at the base of New York’s Statue of Liberty on Monday, calling for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza and an end to Israel’s military operations there. Organized by Jewish Voice for Peace, the demonstrators wore black T-shirts emblazoned with slogans such as “Jews demand ceasefire now” and “Not in our name.” They unfurled banners with messages including “The whole world is watching” and “Palestinians should be free.”

This demonstration was the latest in a series of pro-Palestinian protests across the United States, which have surged since the onset of the conflict a month ago. Over the past weekend, tens of thousands gathered in Washington, DC, urging an immediate ceasefire and criticizing the US government’s support for Israel. Similar large-scale protests recently took place at Manhattan’s Grand Central Station and on the Brooklyn Bridge, with participation from pro-Palestinian supporters and members of US Jewish organizations.

article_content:
Higher education institutions are increasingly recognizing the value of students developing strong interpersonal communication skills, driven by employer expectations and the political tensions present on many college campuses. Students often hesitate to discuss politics out of concern for peer condemnation and ostracization. This tension has been heightened by increased political polarization and a loss of in-person communication during the COVID-19 pandemic, which today’s young adults experienced in high school and college. Binghamton University (State University of New York), where I was an undergraduate and now serve as a staff member, faces similar challenges.

However, students and the University community are working together to address the negative effects of polarization, which include strained social and family relationships, classroom tensions, self-censorship, restrictions on speech, and heightened anxiety and depression. Initiatives include introducing constructive dialogue training into student programming, creating platforms for respectful political discourse, and fostering partnerships among student political organizations.

Implementing constructive dialogue training
The Civil Dialogue Project at Binghamton University, which I coordinate with alumnus Bill Groner ‘77, has partnered with the Division of Student Affairs to implement a constructive dialogue curriculum in first-year programs. The hybrid curriculum includes the online Perspectives course from the Constructive Dialogue Institute and two one-hour workshops designed by the Civil Dialogue Project. The program uses cognitive behavioral therapy concepts to help students recognize negative thought patterns and improve communication across social divides. This pilot program will be offered to around 600 first-year students in the Emerging Leaders Program and First-Year Experience courses. The Community-Engaged Research Lab at the Institute for Justice and Well-Being will formally assess the pilot to evaluate its impact on students’ communication skills.

Building platforms for respectful political discourse
As an undergraduate, I and my peers founded a student-run magazine, Happy Medium Magazine, to encourage respectful and productive political conversations. We saw the need for a space supporting the expression of diverse viewpoints, particularly in academic settings. Starting as an online publication, Happy Medium received university grants to publish quarterly print issues in fall 2022 and now has an annual budget from the Student Association. The magazine’s editorial process requires authors to cite sources, which are verified by editors for integrity and to ensure drafts remain free of sensationalism or antagonistic language. Happy Medium has grown into a publishing group that collaborates with other campus groups to start new student-run magazines.

One notable initiative is the High School Magazine Development Program, created with the University’s Writing Initiative, Center for Civic Engagement, and Chenango Valley Central School District. This program sends undergraduate editors to a local high school to work with students on launching a student-run publication. Workshops cover journalistic ethics, research, op-ed writing, and editing, and high school students serve as editors to maintain the publication as a club. The 2023 pilot at Chenango Valley High School led to the first Valley Unveiled edition and won the University’s Excellence in Community Engagement Award.

Promoting partnerships among student political organizations
The Summit on Student Political Engagement first met in April 2023, with student leaders from groups such as the College Democrats, College Libertarians, College Republicans, and voter engagement ambassadors forming a coalition for civic engagement. Together, they drafted and ratified bylaws and agreed to meet at the start of each semester to collaborate on programming, voter engagement, and to address concerns diplomatically. In Fall 2023, student leaders organized joint initiatives, including a voter registration fair, a campus radio talk show, and the Great Debate where political club members debate current issues before an audience. Leaders agree their focus is on mobilizing supporters, supporting candidates, and offering educational programming—not on conflict.

Research and the broader civic mission
A February 2023 study from the Constructive Dialogue Institute and the Aspen Institute’s Citizenship and American Identity Program—“Transforming Conflict on College Campuses”—offers strategies to shift campuses from toxic to healthy conflict. The goal is not to limit political activity but to teach respectful, empathetic, and effective engagement across differences by modeling these behaviors and providing structured opportunities for dialogue.

Central to these efforts is a commitment to open inquiry, viewpoint diversity, and freedom of expression in academics. As society increasingly needs strong civic leadership, colleges are re-embracing this mission. Over 970 colleges and universities now participate in the ALL IN Campus Democracy Challenge. Learn more about the initiative and how to support it.
