article_content: For the first time since October 7, some people in Gaza were permitted to leave through Egypt's Rafah border crossing after Hamas attacked Israel and Israeli forces launched retaliatory strikes on Gaza. According to the Hamas-run Gaza Health Ministry, at least 8,700 people have been killed and 22,000 injured in Gaza. Israeli authorities report at least 1,400 deaths and 4,629 injuries in Israel. On Wednesday, 76 injured Gazan residents crossed into Egypt following the reopening of the Rafah crossing, according to Palestinian Rafah Crossing spokesman Wael Abu Omar. Additionally, at least 335 foreign passport holders, including dual nationals, crossed from Gaza into Egypt on the same day. Omar stated that 51 aid trucks entered Gaza on Wednesday, raising the total to 268 trucks so far. Thousands have sought refuge at Rafah as Israeli airstrikes continued in Gaza, worsening the humanitarian crisis, while tons of aid awaited entry from Egypt. Egypt prepared to open the Rafah crossing, but according to Foreign Minister Sameh Hassan Shoukry, the gate was struck at least four times by Israeli airstrikes on October 17. Countries involved in the conflict blame each other for prolonging the closure and preventing aid deliveries. Egypt accuses Israel of 'deliberately' slowing the delivery of aid to Gaza and called for international protection of convoys from Israeli bombardment, said Diaa Rashwan, head of Egypt's State Information Service, on October 31. Rashwan also stated that Egypt is ready to send 'not hundreds, but thousands of trucks daily' into Gaza if Israeli restrictions were lifted, blaming Israeli inspection measures for the delays. He called for international protection for aid convoys, warning that Israel could use the same force seen in Gaza's siege against aid trucks. Israel and the United States blame Egypt and Hamas for stalled negotiations. U.S. officials previously worked to get Egypt to agree to temporarily open the crossing, and on October 30, State Department spokesperson Matt Miller said Hamas was making demands before allowing people to leave Gaza. Hospitals in Egypt's Sinai region and other cities have been put on alert to handle the influx from Gaza, said the Egyptian Health Ministry on October 16, with the health minister visiting the border to inspect emergency measures. Relief supplies from international organizations and countries — including Turkey, Jordan, and the United Arab Emirates — along with more than 100 Egyptian trucks, have accumulated in the Sinai awaiting entry into Gaza. The Rafah crossing has a complex history in Israeli-Arab relations. It is located in the Sinai Peninsula, which was occupied by Israel during the 1967 Six-Day War, along with the West Bank, East Jerusalem, Gaza, and the Golan Heights. Israel withdrew from Sinai in 1982 after the Camp David Accords and negotiations. Control of movement across Rafah shifted from Israel to Egyptian, Palestinian, and EU authorities in 2005 via the Agreement on Movement and Access and Agreed Principles for Rafah Crossing. However, those crossing must be registered and approved by Israel, which monitors goods moving in and out of Gaza. The U.S. State Department’s Bureau of Consular Affairs warned that the situation at Rafah remains 'fluid and unpredictable,' with openings possibly occurring on short notice and only briefly. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and U.S. President Joe Biden discussed protecting civilians and delivering humanitarian aid to Gaza on October 16, according to a statement from Egypt's presidency. Reporting by William Gretsky.
translated_content: Por primera vez desde el 7 de octubre, algunas personas en Gaza recibieron permiso para salir a través del cruce fronterizo de Rafah con Egipto, después de que Hamás atacara a Israel y las fuerzas israelíes lanzaran ataques de represalia contra Gaza. Según el Ministerio de Salud de Gaza, controlado por Hamás, al menos 8,700 personas han muerto y 22,000 han resultado heridas en Gaza. Las autoridades israelíes informan de al menos 1,400 muertes y 4,629 heridos en Israel. El miércoles, 76 residentes gazatíes heridos cruzaron a Egipto tras la reapertura del cruce de Rafah, según el portavoz palestino de Rafah, Wael Abu Omar. Además, al menos 335 titulares de pasaportes extranjeros, incluidos nacionales con doble ciudadanía, cruzaron de Gaza a Egipto ese mismo día. Omar afirmó que 51 camiones de ayuda ingresaron en Gaza el miércoles, elevando el total a 268 camiones hasta ahora. Miles han buscado refugio en Rafah mientras los ataques aéreos israelíes continúan en Gaza, agravando la crisis humanitaria, mientras toneladas de ayuda esperan para entrar desde Egipto. Egipto se preparó para abrir el cruce de Rafah, pero, según el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Sameh Hassan Shoukry, la puerta fue atacada al menos cuatro veces por bombardeos israelíes el 17 de octubre. Los países involucrados en el conflicto se acusan mutuamente de prolongar el cierre y de impedir la entrega de ayuda. Egipto acusa a Israel de 'retrasar deliberadamente' la entrega de ayuda a Gaza y pidió protección internacional para los convoyes ante los bombardeos israelíes, dijo Diaa Rashwan, jefe del Servicio de Información del Estado egipcio, el 31 de octubre. Rashwan también declaró que Egipto está listo para enviar 'no cientos, sino miles de camiones diarios' a Gaza si se levantaran las restricciones israelíes, responsabilizando a las medidas de inspección israelíes por las demoras. Pidió protección internacional para los convoyes de ayuda, advirtiendo que Israel podría emplear la misma fuerza observada en el asedio de Gaza contra los camiones de ayuda. Israel y Estados Unidos culpan a Egipto y a Hamás por el estancamiento de las negociaciones. Funcionarios estadounidenses han trabajado para lograr que Egipto acceda a abrir temporalmente el cruce, y el 30 de octubre, el vocero del Departamento de Estado, Matt Miller, dijo que Hamás estaba haciendo exigencias antes de permitir la salida de personas de Gaza. Hospitales en la región del Sinaí en Egipto y en otras ciudades han sido puestos en alerta para atender a las personas provenientes de Gaza, dijo el Ministerio de Salud egipcio el 16 de octubre, y el ministro de Salud visitó la frontera para inspeccionar medidas de emergencia. Suministros de ayuda de organizaciones internacionales y de países — incluyendo Turquía, Jordania y los Emiratos Árabes Unidos — junto con más de 100 camiones egipcios, se han acumulado en el Sinaí a la espera de ingresar a Gaza. El cruce de Rafah tiene una historia compleja en las relaciones israelo-árabes. Está ubicado en la península del Sinaí, ocupada por Israel durante la Guerra de los Seis Días de 1967, junto con Cisjordania, Jerusalén Este, Gaza y los Altos del Golán. Israel se retiró del Sinaí en 1982 después de los Acuerdos de Camp David y otras negociaciones. El control del movimiento a través de Rafah pasó de Israel a autoridades egipcias, palestinas y de la UE en 2005 mediante el Acuerdo sobre Circulación y Acceso y los Principios Acordados para el Cruce de Rafah. Sin embargo, quienes cruzan deben estar registrados y aprobados previamente por Israel, que monitorea el movimiento de mercancías dentro y fuera de Gaza. La Oficina de Asuntos Consulares del Departamento de Estado de los EE. UU. advirtió que la situación en Rafah se mantiene 'fluida e impredecible', con aperturas que pueden ocurrir con poco aviso y solo por períodos breves. El presidente egipcio Abdel Fattah El-Sisi y el presidente estadounidense Joe Biden discutieron la protección de civiles y la entrega de ayuda humanitaria a Gaza el 16 de octubre, según un comunicado de la presidencia egipcia. Informe de William Gretsky.

article_content: Prince William was left laughing today after his father, Prince Charles, was described as 'quite buff' during an event in Covent Garden. William, who is second in line to the throne, wore a wetsuit to demonstrate his snorkelling skills in a Central London swimming pool. During the event, a reference to a topless photo of Prince Charles from the 1970s prompted BSAC Chairman Eugene Farrell to joke about Charles being 'quite buff' in his diving days, which amused attendees. Prince Charles appeared bemused by the comment, looking to his son for an explanation. William, 32, explained the term to his father, telling him, 'Pa, you should be pleased!' Charles took it in good humor, joking that William would now demonstrate his own 'buff credentials' during his speech. The event at the Oasis Leisure Centre marked the formal handover of the British Sub-Aqua Club (BSAC) presidency from Prince Charles to Prince William after Charles’s 40 years in the role. The Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Philip, had previously held the position, instilling a love of water sports in his son and grandson. Prince Charles shared stories about encouraging William’s interest in diving, saying, 'I threw him in the swimming pool on occasions. Instead of putting him off, it enthused him.' He also recalled feeling terrified during an Arctic dive and encountering a Moray Eel. William expressed hope that his son, George, would follow in their footsteps, joking that while bath time is challenging right now, snorkelling might calm him down. William then joined eight-year-olds in the pool for a snorkelling session, participated in a friendly race, and demonstrated his diving skills with the group. He later used borrowed equipment for a scuba demonstration. Fellow diver Tom Billingham, 17, commented that William appeared to be a natural and enjoyed himself. Charles watched the demonstration, jokingly tossing a plastic crab into the pool. Tony Marshall, BSAC Vice Chairman, highlighted William’s diving experience, including army training at Fort Bovisand and local groups in Anglesey. The Duchess of Cambridge, Kate, is also a BSAC member. Eugene Farrell said it was an honor to welcome William as the third generation of his family to serve as BSAC president. He expressed hope that William would inspire a new generation of young scuba divers and help protect the underwater world. The event celebrated the royal family's passion for aquatic sports and the tradition of passing down the BSAC presidency.

Dan Bilzerian, a multimillionaire poker player based in Los Angeles, has gained notoriety as Instagram's 'playboy king' by sharing an opulent, high-octane lifestyle. article_content: The European Union's handling of the latest Israel-Hamas conflict has triggered criticism and exposed internal disagreements, with some officials calling the bloc’s approach hypocritical. After Hamas attacked Israel last Saturday, key European landmarks—like Berlin’s Brandenburg Gate, Paris’s Eiffel Tower, and Bulgaria’s parliament—were illuminated with the Israeli flag’s colors. EU institutions in Brussels also flew Israeli flags and hosted memorials for victims. These acts of solidarity were intended to oppose terrorism, but not all Europeans felt represented. Some citizens and EU officials argue such displays ignore the complexities of the conflict, and question why similar gestures are not made for Palestinian victims. An EU official anonymously accused the organization of double standards, asking why no Palestinian flags were flown following earlier violence in the region. The European Commission’s initial decision to suspend €691 million in aid to Palestine—announced after Hamas’s attacks—sparked criticism, with several EU nations insisting such decisions require agreement from all foreign ministers. The Commission soon adjusted its stance, stating aid would be reviewed rather than suspended, in order to prevent misuse. Advocates like former EU ambassador to Palestine, Sven Kuhn von Burgsdorff, stressed that EU financial support is closely monitored and directed at the Palestinian Authority, not Hamas. Swedish MEP Evin Incir criticized any attempt to link EU aid to Hamas as inaccurate. EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell argued that discontinuing aid would harm both the EU’s regional interests and possibly fuel extremism. After discussions with member states, the consensus was to continue support for the Palestinian Authority. Despite official support for a two-state solution with Israel and an independent Palestine, there is ongoing debate within the EU about public demonstrations and maintaining neutrality. Many citizens and diplomats feel that too-visible support for one side harms the EU’s credibility. Europeans from various countries expressed discomfort with the symbolic displays, calling for solidarity with both Israelis and Palestinians. Critics also noticed the EU’s rapid support for Israel contrasted with slower reactions to other global crises. Ongoing violence in the region underscores deep divisions within the EU over the Israel-Palestine issue.

article_content: Few American playgrounds lack a jungle gym, but its roots trace to an unlikely source: British mathematician Charles Hinton. In the late 1800s, Hinton's quest to teach the concept of the fourth dimension led him to devise bamboo climbing frames for his children in Japan—an effort to make three-dimensional thinking second nature. The educational side flopped, but the kids loved scrambling on the cubes. Decades later in Illinois, Hinton’s son Sebastian, moved by these childhood games, designed a sturdy, climbable structure he later patented as the jungle gym. In 1920s Winnetka—a progressive education hub inspired by John Dewey’s holistic learning ideas—superintendent Carleton Washburne encouraged Sebastian to bring his invention into schools. Thus, the jungle gym went from memory to mainstay. The very first jungle gym remains preserved at the Winnetka Historical Society, sparking nostalgia among visitors but strictly off-limits for climbing. Unlike fleeting toy fads, the jungle gym’s open design invites generations to swing and climb their own way. Norwegian professor Ellen Sandseter observes that the jungle gym’s combination of risk and creativity supports children’s growth and confidence, providing freedoms many new playground setups fail to match. As for 'monkey bars': the name stems from Hinton’s patent, which compared kids on the apparatus to monkeys in the treetops—even if, as researcher Luke Fannin notes, swinging by arms is more ape-like. Regardless, the label stuck. Sadly, Sebastian Hinton passed away before seeing his patent’s official approval. While safety tweaks have softened modern playgrounds, the jungle gym’s spirit—a canvas for adventurous play—has endured for a century and counting.

Victoria Ayris, a 30-year-old chemistry teacher, has received a lifetime teaching ban after sending a series of inappropriate and sexually suggestive messages to a male student at Castlebrook High School in Greater Manchester. Over nine months in 2012, Ayris exchanged nearly 2,000 messages with a Year 11 student aged 15 or 16 via WhatsApp. Some of these messages were explicit and included personal photographs, though none of the photos were sexual in nature. 

School officials became aware of the situation following rumors among students and staff, prompting Ayris to urge the student in a panicked message to delete their conversations. Despite police determining that no criminal offence had occurred, an independent professional conduct panel found Ayris guilty of serious misconduct. 

After joining Castlebrook High in 2008, Ayris had been recognized for her hard work and positive results but resigned in April 2013 when the school began its investigation. The school's leadership highlighted its commitment to student safety, asserting that established safeguarding practices allowed for a prompt response to the incident. 

Ayris admitted to her actions, offered apologies, and received support from the student’s parents. However, the panel concluded that her conduct was far beneath the standards expected of teachers. Now believed to be in Australia, Ayris will be allowed to seek a reversal of the ban after two years.

Former television presenter Emma Freud was honored with an OBE by Queen Elizabeth II today in recognition of her work as a trustee and co-founder of Comic Relief. Together with her partner Richard Curtis, Freud established the charity in 1985 and has contributed to its live television fundraisers for about eight years. In March, Comic Relief’s Red Nose Day broadcast raised a record £74.3 million in one night—the highest total in the event’s 23-year history—with the annual total reaching £102 million. Freud credited the generosity of the British public for Comic Relief’s success, emphasizing the importance of community support even during economic hardship.

At the investiture ceremony at Buckingham Palace, the Queen also conferred knighthoods on Sir Mervyn King, governor of the Bank of England, and Sir Henry Cecil, an acclaimed racehorse trainer. Both men expressed gratitude: Sir Mervyn King dedicated his award to the staff of the Bank of England, while Sir Henry Cecil reflected humbly on his years in racing, including 25 Classic wins and multiple champion-trainer titles.

Australian Corporal Benjamin Roberts-Smith, recipient of his nation’s highest gallantry medal, the Victoria Cross, also met with the Queen. Roberts-Smith was celebrated for his bravery during an operation in Afghanistan, where he drew enemy fire and assisted his unit under extreme danger.

Freud, also known for her work as script editor on ‘Four Weddings and a Funeral’ and ‘Notting Hill,’ described the OBE as a reflection of the British people’s charitable spirit, attributing the achievement to collective effort rather than personal accomplishment.

Tinder says the new feature allows individuals to share quiz answers on their profiles, giving others a look at their interests and preferences.

According to Tinder’s survey, 71% of Gen Z users in India believe that sharing values is crucial in dating. Furthermore, 73% prioritize trust and openness, 70% value open-mindedness, 57% appreciate humor, and only 46% consider physical appearance as most important.

Mark Van Ryswyk, Tinder’s Chief Product Officer, said these updates address users’ changing needs and make it easier and more enjoyable to showcase what makes each person unique.

Enhanced Reporting gives users more options to report issues. The Rizz-first Redesign updates the app’s interface and includes a refreshed 'It’s a Match!' screen. Dark Mode is now available for those wanting to use the app in low light or discreetly.

OpenAI, the company responsible for ChatGPT, is intensifying its commitment to tackling dangers associated with advanced artificial intelligence. Recently, the company revealed its new 'Preparedness' team, tasked with identifying and defending against threats that might emerge from high-level AI systems—labeled by OpenAI as 'frontier risks.'

OpenAI emphasized that highly capable AI could benefit society greatly, but also brings rising and severe risks. The Preparedness team will track, evaluate, and predict potential catastrophe-level incidents linked to AI, including those relating to chemical, biological, nuclear, and cyber domains. It will also introduce a Risk-Informed Development Policy, detailing preventative strategies and ensuring AI system oversight.

Aleksander Madry, who is currently on leave from MIT, will serve as the team's lead. OpenAI is recruiting for several positions on this team, including a national security threat researcher and a research engineer, with listed salaries ranging from $200,000 to $370,000 annually. OpenAI and Madry did not respond to Insider's request for comment prior to publication.

Issues of AI safety have been a consistent topic among tech industry leaders. Elon Musk, a former OpenAI cofounder, recently called AI 'one of the biggest risks to the future of civilization.' OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, during a conversation on Lex Fridman’s podcast, noted his understanding of public fears about AI, particularly regarding misinformation, economic shocks such as job loss, and overwhelming threats.

In response to such concerns, other companies are also taking action. Earlier this month, Anthropic—the developer of the Claude chatbot—updated its guidelines with feedback from users to reinforce protective measures and avert harmful or biased responses. Still, some experts hold a less alarmist view. Yann LeCun, Meta’s chief AI scientist, has dismissed warnings about superintelligent AI eradicating humanity as exaggerated, claiming these ideas are more science fiction than actuality, arguing that intelligence does not inherently lead to a desire to dominate.

article_content: During the MTV Video Music Awards in Los Angeles, rapper Common led a tribute to Michael Brown, the 18-year-old Missouri teen who was shot and killed by police officer Darren Wilson two weeks prior. The audience, including notable artists such as Snoop Dogg, observed five seconds of silence in honor of Brown. A 15-second video, featuring a black-and-white image of Ferguson's city sign and the chant 'hands up, don't shoot,' was played, echoing the slogan used by protesters in the St. Louis suburb. Common addressed the crowd, stating that Ferguson residents have shown that ‘each and every one of our lives matters.’ MTV President Stephen Friedman confirmed that the network aired the 15-second video as a call to action to confront bias and continue the discussion on racial issues. On the same day in St. Louis, Michael Brown Sr. and civil rights leader Rev. Al Sharpton participated in Peace Fest, calling for peace and remembrance. After weeks of unrest, demonstrations in Ferguson have become more peaceful following the withdrawal of the National Guard. Common emphasized that hip-hop has been a powerful force for truth and social change and led the audience in a moment of silence before announcing the nominees for Best Hip Hop Video. Michael Brown’s funeral was scheduled to take place at a St. Louis church, with his father calling for a day of silence and peace. Brown’s death sparked nationwide discussions about racial injustice and police conduct, as well as protests throughout Ferguson. A mural honoring Michael Brown has been painted on a city wall amid calls for justice and social change. The federal government has launched an investigation into the shooting, and police presence remains in Ferguson. Rev. Al Sharpton urged calm and respect for Michael Brown’s legacy. Trayvon Martin’s parents also addressed the crowd, encouraging peaceful activism and unity, while expressing support for the Brown family. Trayvon Martin, another unarmed black teen, was shot and killed in 2012 by George Zimmerman, who was later acquitted. While initial protests in Ferguson were often met with police in riot gear and tear gas, recent demonstrations have largely remained peaceful. Police reports indicated that Michael Brown was involved in a physical confrontation with officer Darren Wilson, and some witnesses said Brown’s arms were raised in surrender. An autopsy found that Brown was shot at least six times. Ferguson police identified Darren Wilson as the shooter while releasing footage related to an alleged theft by Brown at a convenience store shortly before the shooting. During the awards ceremony, Miley Cyrus won Video of the Year for ‘Wrecking Ball.’

A statue valued at more than $10,000, stolen from the Palm Beach, Florida, estate of Wall Street investment adviser Bernard Madoff, has been recovered, police announced Thursday. Authorities discovered the 4-foot-high statue, which depicts two lifeguards sitting on a bench, on Wednesday morning in bushes a few blocks from Madoff’s estate. Attached to the statue was a note reading, 'Bernie the Swindler, Lesson: Return stolen property to rightful owners.' The message appeared to target Madoff, who is charged with securities fraud related to an alleged $50 billion Ponzi scheme.

The note was signed 'The Educators.' Police said the statue was found undamaged and that the theft remains under investigation. A property manager noticed the statue was missing on December 19, eight days after Madoff was arrested in New York. Madoff remains under house arrest in New York, awaiting court proceedings. His $10 million bail is secured by properties owned by him and his wife, including their Manhattan apartment and Palm Beach estate. CNN’s Christian Chinnici contributed to this report.

Two civilians were killed and ten others—including three Pakistani soldiers—were injured during a suicide attack targeting a security convoy in the Baka Khel area of Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. According to the Pakistani Army on Monday, an Afghan national carried out the attack by ramming his motorcycle into the military convoy on Sunday, in a region near the Afghan border known for instability. The army reported that seven people, including military personnel, were wounded. While the attacker was identified as Afghan, details such as the assailant's name or the method of identification were not provided and there was no comment from Kabul authorities.

Last month, Islamabad announced plans to expel over a million undocumented refugees, most of whom are Afghans, amid ongoing tensions with Kabul over accusations of sheltering anti-Pakistan militants and claims that many recent suicide attacks were carried out by Afghans—a charge Kabul denies. Before expulsion efforts began in October, Pakistan stated that 14 of 24 suicide bombings this year were attributed to Afghan nationals.

Since October 1, nearly 400,000 Afghans have reportedly left Pakistan, according to the UNHCR. In total, Pakistan hosts more than 4 million Afghan migrants and refugees, about 1.7 million of whom are undocumented. Many arrived following the Taliban's return to power in 2021 or after the Soviet invasion in 1979.

The UNHCR has called for Pakistan to pause deportations during the harsh winter and to ensure the voluntary return of Afghans, encouraging authorities to identify and protect vulnerable individuals needing international protection. Pakistan, however, has yet to address appeals from international organizations and refugee advocates. The Supreme Court of Pakistan is slated to consider a petition from human rights activists on December 1 regarding the halt of these deportations.

article_content: Joplin, Missouri has raised the death toll from the powerful tornado that hit last month to 155, according to a statement by city spokeswoman Lynn Onstot. The previous total, reported Friday, was 154. The latest victim identified is Edmon A. Cooper, who died from injuries sustained during the May 22 tornado. Additional details have not been released. The tornado, which tore through a 13-mile stretch of southwest Missouri, is the deadliest single tornado in the U.S. in more than 60 years, based on data from the National Weather Service. The storm caused widespread devastation, stripping bark from trees and demolishing houses beyond recognition.

European television production is closing the quality gap with American programming while operating at much lower costs, according to leading executives from Mediawan and Sony. Speaking at the MIA Market industry event in Rome, Mediawan CEO Elisabeth D’Arvieu emphasized that European studios now have a significant competitive edge, citing generous tax incentives across Spain, Italy, Greece, and Belgium. She highlighted the combination of cost-effective systems and a talented workforce as key drivers of this advantage.

Brendan Fitzgerald, Sony Pictures Television’s SVP of International Co-Productions in Spain, pointed out the success of Sony-backed shows filming in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) and Greece, benefiting from favorable locations, skilled crews, and tax credits. Fitzgerald predicted that soon, European productions could be created for 55% of the cost of American shows while delivering up to 90% – or even 100%, according to D’Arvieu – of their quality. Tesha Crawford, Universal International Studios’ SVP of Global Scripted Series, agreed, noting that European productions have already achieved quality parity with the US. She acknowledged that historic barriers such as technology and language are declining.

Studiocanal’s Françoise Guyonnet, newly promoted to CEO of Copyrights Group and EVP Kids’ Brands, added that European TV no longer needs to prove its production capabilities. While English-language content remains easier to sell, improved dubbing is broadening the appeal of non-English programming. Guyonnet cited Danish director Thomas Vinterberg’s decision to create the upcoming Studiocanal series 'Families Like Ours' in Danish instead of English, managing the associated production budgets accordingly.

Demand for foreign-language scripted formats adapted into English is growing, providing new commercial opportunities – a point emphasized by D’Arvieu, whose company will be presenting series such as 'Zorro' at Mipcom Cannes. Panelists also noted a resurgence of European public broadcasting, highlighted by the recent expansion of the Nordic Twelve co-production group, now described as Europe’s largest drama collaboration. Guyonnet commended local broadcasters in France and across Europe for greater ambition and willingness to share rights with PSBs, streamers, and international partners.

Changing market dynamics have prompted a shift in strategy, with fewer projects being offered exclusively to streamers before approaching broadcasters. Fitzgerald acknowledged that while Sony’s Culver City division is still highly focused on SVOD markets, in Spain the approach is more oriented towards linear broadcasting. D’Arvieu added that rising costs are fueling demand for documentaries and unscripted content, genres where broadcasters excel. The recent contraction in the TV market has led to more rapid responses from content commissioners, allowing producers to tailor their pitches more efficiently. The MIA Market continues throughout the week, featuring talks from industry leaders such as Nicole Clemens (Paramount), Marge Dean (Skybound), and director Ari Folman.

article_content: India has established a high-level committee to address security concerns raised by the United States, according to Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Arindam Bagchi. On November 18, the Indian government formed a panel to investigate all aspects of the matter highlighted by the US. The government stated it would take further action based on the findings. Earlier, the White House announced that it had thwarted a plot to assassinate Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a dual citizen of the US and Canada, and conveyed concerns to New Delhi regarding possible involvement. India’s anti-terror agency has filed a case against Pannun, alleging he used social media videos to warn Air India passengers of risks. The US stressed the seriousness of the alleged plot and raised the issue with the Indian government at senior levels. White House spokesperson Adrienne Watson said Indian officials expressed surprise and concern when informed, and emphasized that such actions are not Indian policy. The Indian government is continuing its investigation and has been asked by the US to hold any responsible parties accountable. This follows Canada’s claim of credible evidence linking Indian agents to the June killing of Sikh separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Vancouver, a claim that India denies. The Financial Times, which first reported the story, said it was unclear whether the US’s protest caused the plot to be abandoned or if it was foiled by the FBI. The protest reportedly happened after Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s June visit to the US. In other news, India’s Nifty stock index surpassed 20,000 points for the first time since September, amid optimism about US interest rates. Additional updates include regulatory concerns involving Byju’s and semiconductor plans by HCL Group in Karnataka.

Previously unseen underwater footage of the Costa Concordia salvage operation has surfaced as the anniversary of the ship’s sinking approaches. The cruise liner remains partially submerged off the coast of Tuscany, serving as a stark reminder of the disaster in which 32 people lost their lives on January 13, 2012. Salvage efforts were projected to take at least a year after the vessel struck a reef and capsized near the island of Giglio when Captain Francesco Schettino allegedly deviated from the scheduled route.

CBS News’ 60 Minutes program used advanced equipment, including drones and cameras mounted on barges, to document scenes from inside the sunken ship. Producer Rich Bonin described the wreck: “This massive ship, as long as three football fields, sits at an angle on an underwater mountain like nothing you’ve seen before.”

The footage reveals submerged features such as the Costa Concordia’s bell and untouched furniture, along with sun decks and the swimming pool partially underwater. Salvage workers now hang their tools on decks where guests once mingled, creating an otherworldly, disorienting environment. Bonin noted the challenges of capturing these images, mentioning their use of stable platforms and drones to get as close as possible to the wreck.

Reflecting on the tragedy, Bonin remarked on the chilling circumstances faced by passengers and crew: “You realize that at 1am in January, people were forced to escape into freezing waters.”

Investigators have concluded their probe into the disaster and plan to seek a trial for Captain Schettino and seven others, including five crew members and three Costa crisis unit staff. Schettino faces charges of manslaughter, causing a shipwreck, and abandoning ship. Prosecutor Francesco Verusio stated that a request for indictment would be filed by the end of January, and Schettino could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. The final decision on whether to proceed to trial will be made by a judge.

Las imágenes muestran detalles sumergidos como la campana del Costa Concordia y muebles intactos, junto con cubiertas para tomar el sol y la piscina parcialmente bajo el agua. article_content: Reality television is now filled with shows that often recycle existing formats rather than develop truly new ideas. NBC’s ‘Fashion Star,’ presented as an innovative fashion competition, premiered with Elle Macpherson as host and mentors including Jessica Simpson, Nicole Richie, and John Varvatos. The show merges aspects of ‘Project Runway’ and ‘Shark Tank,’ featuring designers pitching outfits to major retailers such as Macy’s, Saks, and H&M. Entertainment analysts observe that finding originality in reality TV is increasingly difficult. Steve Carbone of RealitySteve.com says that today’s shows tend to mix elements from other successful series, as brand-new concepts are rare. ‘The Voice’ succeeded by altering classic features—like rotating chairs and team competitions—even though it drew inspiration from shows like ‘American Idol’ and ‘The X Factor.’ Reactions to ‘Fashion Star’ vary. While the use of star mentors and partnerships with retailers might pull in viewers, some critics, such as Mary McNamara from the Los Angeles Times, believe the format quickly feels repetitive. Despite a growing list of fashion-focused shows, ‘Project Runway’ remains prominent thanks to its continued audience appeal. Experts maintain that direct copies of popular shows rarely thrive unless they introduce original elements. Over the years, television has seen many imitation series fail, while those that refine or reinvent prior formulas tend to find more lasting success. In the end, successful reality shows rely not only on originality but also on strong execution and engaging twists. Even programs that borrow from others can attract audiences if they offer something compelling and distinct.

Emma Hayes, who has managed Chelsea FC Women since 2012, will leave her position at the end of the season. During her leadership, Hayes has propelled Chelsea to landmark achievements such as six Women’s Super League titles, five FA Cups, two League Cups, two historic domestic doubles, and a treble, establishing herself as a leading figure in women’s football.

There is considerable speculation about Hayes potentially taking over as head coach for the U.S. Women's National Team, with reports indicating that her contract could break records for women’s coaching salaries and might even equal the earnings of U.S. men’s coach Gregg Berhalter. Despite these rumors, Hayes has refused to comment, affirming her ongoing dedication to Chelsea until her departure.

Hayes attributes her decision to step down to a desire to focus on her family, specifically to spend more time with her young son, after over a decade of commitment and extensive travel for work. She also underlined the value of a smooth leadership transition for Chelsea.

Hayes lamented that confidential talks with club management about her future were leaked to the media. Some news outlets reported Chelsea tried to retain her with a major salary increase, while others suggested contract renewals had not been prioritized. Nonetheless, Hayes reiterated her connection to Chelsea, conveying both sadness about her exit and gratitude for her journey so far, and looks forward to watching future games alongside the supporters.

article_content: A man has been charged in the March killing of 6-month-old Jonylah Watkins in Chicago, police superintendent Garry McCarthy announced. Koman Willis, 33, is charged with first-degree murder and aggravated battery in a case that gained national attention as a tragic example of Chicago's gun violence. Police say Willis, a gang member with at least 38 prior arrests, was allegedly seeking revenge for the reported theft of a video game system by Jonylah's father, Jonathan Watkins, who was also seriously wounded on March 11. Willis surrendered himself with an attorney on Saturday after learning police were searching for him. Although both Willis and Jonathan Watkins have gang associations, police clarified the motive was related to the burglary and not gang violence. Watkins is unlikely to face theft charges. Lead investigator Kevin Duffin stated that new witnesses came forward last week with key information aiding the investigation. Police have not recovered the weapon or a getaway vehicle, and no further charges are currently expected. Jonathan Watkins did not attend the news briefing. Reverend Corey Brooks of the New Beginnings Church of Chicago shared that the family visited Jonylah's grave and are grateful for the arrest, hoping to find closure.

article_content: In the rapidly evolving world of multifamily real estate, effective risk management has never been more important. Property owners and managers face unpredictable rent fluctuations, rising vacancies, increased fraud, and complex legal challenges. To stay ahead, adopting a holistic risk management approach is essential. This requires more than just standard insurance—it means developing comprehensive strategies to identify and address potential risks. Recent data from CBRE indicates the multifamily market is stabilizing, offering some reassurance to buyers, sellers, and property managers nationwide. As of March 2023, 960,000 multifamily units were under construction, according to the Joint Center for Housing Studies of Harvard University. While this increase in available units is promising, the vacancy rate for professionally managed apartments more than doubled—from a record low of 2.5% in 2022 to 5.2% in early 2023. Meanwhile, although rent prices have moderated since the peak in summer 2022, they continue to rise in most metro areas. Fraud presents a growing threat in the industry. Some housing applicants falsify documents to appear more qualified. For example, simply adjusting a figure on a pay stub can make a candidate’s income seem much higher. My company’s internal data shows tenants who submit fraudulent documents are more likely to default on rent or be evicted, resulting in substantial financial setbacks for property managers. Frequent evictions can quickly erode a property manager’s cash flow and reputation. It’s vital for property managers to stay informed and compliant with ongoing changes to rent control and fair housing laws. In 2021 alone, 25,501 complaints of rental discrimination were filed. Even a minor error in the tenant screening process can lead to costly legal disputes. With the national vacancy rate increasing to 5% in the second quarter of 2023, managers are reevaluating leasing strategies. High vacancy rates decrease cash flow, and may limit access to loans—some lenders only work with properties maintaining over 70% occupancy. Economic slowdowns or crises, such as the Covid-19 pandemic, can intensify vacancy challenges, underscoring the need for advance planning. Addressing these and other industry risks begins with thorough, fair, and legally compliant tenant screening—including credit, background, rental history, and income verification checks. Technological solutions can enhance these processes and help combat fraud (my company is one of several providers in this area). Ongoing staff education regarding local, state, and federal property laws is also crucial. For nationwide legal changes, such as eviction moratoriums during the pandemic, consulting legal counsel and ensuring teams are well-versed in implementation is essential. Reducing vacancies is best achieved by prioritizing tenant retention. Satisfied tenants are less likely to leave, so maintaining attractive amenities, holding community events, and staying on top of maintenance can all help foster loyalty. Regular property inspections, responsive pest control, and well-kept landscaping can contribute to a positive tenant experience. Ultimately, managers who prioritize risk management—by increasing tenant retention, strengthening screening, and remaining vigilant regarding legal developments—will be better equipped to thrive in a changing multifamily market.

Esto va más allá de las pólizas de seguro estándar: implica desarrollar estrategias completas para identificar y abordar riesgos potenciales. Las crisis económicas, como la pandemia de Covid-19, pueden agravar los desafíos de desocupación, lo que subraya la necesidad de una planificación anticipada. Abordar estos y otros riesgos de la industria comienza con una selección de inquilinos profunda, justa y legalmente compatible, incluyendo chequeos de crédito, historial, antecedentes y verificación de ingresos. La educación continua del personal sobre las leyes locales, estatales y federales de propiedad también es crucial. Ante cambios legales nacionales, como las moratorias de desalojo durante la pandemia, es fundamental consultar con abogados y garantizar que los equipos estén bien informados sobre su implementación. La mejor manera de reducir la desocupación es priorizar la retención de inquilinos. Los inquilinos satisfechos tienen menos probabilidades de mudarse, por lo que mantener instalaciones atractivas, organizar eventos comunitarios y estar al día con el mantenimiento puede fomentar la lealtad. Las inspecciones regulares, el control de plagas y áreas verdes bien cuidadas también contribuyen a una experiencia positiva. En definitiva, quienes prioricen la gestión de riesgos—aumentando la retención de inquilinos, fortaleciendo los procesos de selección y manteniéndose atentos a los cambios legales—estarán mejor preparados para prosperar en un mercado multifamiliar en constante cambio.

article_content: A woman trapped in a burning second-floor flat in Hounslow, west London, leapt 25 feet to her death early Wednesday as a fire engulfed the building. The blaze, which broke out above a shop, is being treated as suspicious by police. The 30-year-old woman reportedly struck her head on a telephone box after jumping from the window. She was found on the street and pronounced dead at the scene. Her 37-year-old husband jumped shortly afterwards with an 18-year-old man; both survived but sustained multiple injuries and were taken to St Mary’s Hospital. Firefighters found a second person dead inside the building during a search around 2 a.m. The fire prompted the evacuation of about 50 residents from the affected and neighboring flats. Neighbors and witnesses described waking to explosions and panic. Resident Ewa Glowacka recounted fleeing with her daughter after hearing what sounded like a bomb. Another neighbor, Deelip Silwal, witnessed people jumping from windows and residents attempting to cushion escapes with mattresses. The London Fire Brigade deployed around 58 firefighters and eight engines to extinguish the blaze. Emergency services treated the injured and performed life support at the scene. Police say the investigation is ongoing and that arson has not been ruled out. Officers from the Homicide and Serious Crime Command have been informed. Local roads remain closed while the cause of the fire is investigated. The London Ambulance Service confirmed two deaths—one believed to be a 30-year-old woman—and the hospitalization of two men with serious but non-life-threatening injuries.

article_content: A recent study has raised concerns that genetically modified (GM) crops could affect animal health, after researchers found that pigs fed GM feed had inflamed stomachs and heavier uteruses. The study is significant because pigs have digestive systems similar to humans, who consume pork. Some of the UK's largest supermarkets recently lifted a ban on the use of GM crops for animal feed. According to the research, GM-fed female pigs had, on average, a 25 percent heavier uterus than those not fed GM crops, which could indicate health issues. The trial took place at a commercial piggery in the United States and involved 168 newly weaned pigs, given either GM soy and corn or equivalent non-GM diets. The pigs were raised in similar conditions and autopsied by independent veterinarians who did not know which feed the pigs received. There was also a higher incidence of severe stomach inflammation in pigs that ate GM diets. Dr. Judy Carman, an associate professor at Flinders University in Australia, led the research and called the findings 'striking.' She said more research is needed to determine if similar effects occur in humans who consume GM crops. However, some experts have questioned the study’s findings. Professor Tom Sanders of King’s College London stated there were no differences in growth or mortality rates and that the pigs were otherwise healthy. Professor David Spiegelhalter of Cambridge said the study's conclusions did not withstand rigorous statistical analysis. Howard Vlieger, an Iowa farmer who helped coordinate the study, said digestive and reproductive problems have been observed for years among animals exposed to GM feed. In response, the Biotechnology Industry Organisation said the authors of the study are known anti-biotech campaigners and pointed out that hundreds of other studies have found no difference between animals fed GM or non-GM diets. UK Environment Secretary Owen Paterson supports GM crops, dismissing concerns as 'complete nonsense.' He argues that as the world population grows, technologies like GM crops are essential to increase food production and reduce waste.

article_content: OpenAI, the developer behind ChatGPT, is collaborating with G42, Abu Dhabi’s leading artificial intelligence company, to expand its presence in the United Arab Emirates and the wider region. The partnership will focus on deploying OpenAI’s generative AI models across various sectors including financial services, energy, and healthcare. G42 is chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE’s influential national security adviser. “Leveraging G42’s industry expertise, we aim to empower businesses and communities with effective solutions that address the unique needs of the region,” said Sam Altman, co-founder and chief executive officer of California-based OpenAI. G42 CEO Peng Xiao described the partnership as a “convergence of value and vision.” Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. G42 has been at the forefront of the UAE’s artificial intelligence initiatives, including a partnership with Cerebras Systems Inc., which recently constructed the first of nine AI supercomputers as alternatives to Nvidia technology. In addition, G42 launched the multi-billion-dollar 42XFund last year to invest in technology firms throughout emerging markets. Since OpenAI’s tools launched last year, they have fueled a surge in global investment in AI infrastructure, demonstrating the potential of advanced AI powered by extensive data centers. During a visit to Abu Dhabi in June, Sam Altman commended the UAE’s proactive approach, noting the government’s early adoption of artificial intelligence. “There were conversations about AI in Abu Dhabi before it was cool,” Altman told an audience at the emirate’s international financial free zone.

La alianza se centrará en implementar los modelos de inteligencia artificial generativa de OpenAI en diversos sectores, incluidos los servicios financieros, la energía y la salud. G42 está presidida por el influyente asesor de seguridad nacional de los EAU, el jeque Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan. “Aprovechando la experiencia de G42 en la industria, buscamos empoderar a empresas y comunidades con soluciones efectivas que respondan a las necesidades únicas de la región”, dijo Sam Altman, cofundador y director ejecutivo de OpenAI, con sede en California. El CEO de G42, Peng Xiao, calificó la colaboración como una “convergencia de valor y visión”. Los términos financieros del acuerdo no fueron revelados. G42 ha estado a la vanguardia de las iniciativas de inteligencia artificial en los EAU, incluida una asociación con Cerebras Systems Inc., que recientemente construyó la primera de nueve supercomputadoras de IA como alternativa a la tecnología de Nvidia. Además, G42 lanzó el año pasado el fondo 42X, con varios miles de millones de dólares, para invertir en empresas tecnológicas de mercados emergentes. Desde el lanzamiento de las herramientas de OpenAI el año pasado, se ha impulsado una ola de inversión global en infraestructura de IA, demostrando el potencial de las soluciones de inteligencia artificial avanzada respaldadas por grandes centros de datos. Durante una visita a Abu Dabi en junio, Sam Altman elogió el enfoque proactivo de los EAU, destacando la temprana adopción de la inteligencia artificial por parte del gobierno. “En Abu Dabi se hablaba de IA antes de que fuera popular”, señaló Altman ante una audiencia en la zona franca financiera internacional del emirato.

article_content: Stephen Sokoler, founder and CEO of Journey, explores how Gary Chapman's 'five love languages'—originally meant to describe how people give and receive love—can be adapted to the workplace. The five love languages are: words of affirmation, quality time, acts of service, receiving gifts, and physical touch. While effectiveness in romantic relationships is debated, the framework has greatly influenced popular culture. Focusing on workplace well-being, Sokoler suggests that organizations can use these concepts to build a more positive and productive environment. Here’s how each love language can be integrated at work:  1. Engagement and Empowerment: Employees who value engagement feel appreciated when given opportunities to contribute, make decisions, and know their voices matter. Managers can provide autonomy in tasks, invite participation in committees, and ask for input on projects. Fostering a culture of feedback and trust, and offering Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs), further enhances empowerment.  2. Growth: Employees who desire growth feel supported through learning and development opportunities, such as training, challenging assignments, or sponsorship to conferences. Promoting from within and providing management training can also motivate and engage team members.  3. Feedback and Appreciation: Those who value recognition want specific, actionable feedback and acknowledgment of achievements. Regular, constructive feedback, thank-you notes, and public praise in meetings are effective. Training in stress management and coping skills can also support their overall well-being.  4. Work-Life Harmony: Employees who seek work-life balance benefit from flexible work arrangements, paid time off, and a supportive workplace culture. Managers can offer remote work options or accommodate personal needs, and EAPs tailored to work-life integration can help.  5. Recognition and Rewards: Employees motivated by recognition appreciate public acknowledgment, bonuses, promotions, and support for financial well-being. Managers can nominate them for awards and provide resources for financial planning.  Organizations that implement these approaches may experience higher employee engagement, lower turnover, improved morale, increased creativity, better customer service, and a stronger company culture.  Understanding and applying these 'corporate love languages' allows organizations to show appreciation in meaningful ways for each employee, fostering a healthier and more dynamic workplace.
translated_content: Stephen Sokoler, fundador y CEO de Journey, explora cómo los 'cinco lenguajes del amor' de Gary Chapman—originalmente creados para describir cómo las personas dan y reciben amor—pueden adaptarse al entorno laboral. Los cinco lenguajes del amor son: palabras de afirmación, tiempo de calidad, actos de servicio, recibir regalos y contacto físico. Aunque la eficacia de este enfoque en las relaciones románticas es debatida, el marco ha influido enormemente en la cultura popular. Enfocándose en el bienestar laboral, Sokoler sugiere que las organizaciones pueden usar estos conceptos para construir un ambiente más positivo y productivo. Así es como cada lenguaje se puede integrar en el trabajo:  1. Compromiso y Empoderamiento: Los empleados que valoran el compromiso se sienten apreciados cuando se les permite contribuir, tomar decisiones y sentir que sus opiniones importan. Los líderes pueden dar autonomía en las tareas, invitar a participar en comités y solicitar ideas en proyectos. Promover una cultura de retroalimentación y confianza y ofrecer Programas de Asistencia al Empleado (EAP) también fortalece el empoderamiento.  2. Crecimiento: Los empleados que buscan crecer se sienten apoyados con oportunidades de aprendizaje y desarrollo, como capacitaciones, tareas desafiantes o patrocinio para asistir a conferencias. Promover ascensos internos y brindar formación en liderazgo también motiva al equipo.  3. Retroalimentación y Apreciación: Quienes valoran el reconocimiento desean retroalimentación específica y el reconocimiento de sus logros. La retroalimentación regular y constructiva, las notas de agradecimiento y el reconocimiento público en reuniones son efectivos. La formación en manejo del estrés y habilidades de afrontamiento también contribuye a su bienestar.  4. Armonía vida-trabajo: Los empleados que priorizan el equilibrio vida-trabajo se benefician de esquemas flexibles, tiempo libre remunerado y una cultura de apoyo. Los líderes pueden permitir el trabajo remoto o ajustar horarios según necesidades personales, y los EAP enfocados en integrar vida-trabajo pueden ayudar.  5. Reconocimiento y Recompensas: Quienes se motivan por el reconocimiento valoran los elogios públicos, bonos, ascensos y recursos para el bienestar financiero. Los líderes pueden nominarlos para premios y facilitar herramientas para su planificación financiera.  Las organizaciones que aplican estos enfoques pueden ver mayor compromiso, menor rotación, mejor moral, más creatividad, mejor atención al cliente y una cultura empresarial más fuerte.  Comprender y aplicar estos 'lenguajes del amor corporativos' ayuda a que las organizaciones demuestren aprecio en formas significativas para cada persona, promoviendo así un entorno laboral más saludable y dinámico.

article_content: SHENZHEN, China — In one painting, a child sits with her mouth open as a healthcare worker in white medical clothing extends a long cotton swab toward her throat. In another, a masked officer and medical workers stand in front of an apartment cordoned off with ropes and seals marked 'CLOSED,' as residents look on, visibly frustrated. These are some of the portraits painted by Zeng Fanzhi, 85, to mark three years of China's strict 'zero-COVID' controls, which led to nationwide protests a year ago. Zeng, a retired architect in Shenzhen, does not criticize the measures, under which millions were tested, confined to their apartments, or taken to quarantine centers. Much of his life has been dedicated to serving the Chinese state, including designing monuments in Beijing’s Tiananmen Square and coal plants for the Ministry of Coal. As a member of the government-sponsored artists' association in Shenzhen, his artwork has featured on stamps and has won prizes. Unlike younger protesters, Zeng’s outlook is shaped by his early years in wartime and revolutionary China, and later decades witnessing prosperity and growth. He views China’s commitment to 'zero-COVID' controls as necessary, and sees the public’s compliance as heroic. Chinese leader Xi Jinping has said, 'artistic creation must be from The People’s Standpoint.' Zeng explains that his focus on ordinary people reflects this philosophy: 'Art should reflect the reality of people’s lives. My paintings align with this direction.' Growing up, Zeng experienced some of the most turbulent times in modern Chinese history. His parents, both civil servants, fled to Chongqing — China’s wartime capital during World War II — and Zeng moved frequently, escaping both Japanese invasion and civil war. The Communist Party’s 1949 victory brought an end to these conflicts and some stability to China. Zeng aspired to be an artist and took art school entrance exams in 1957, but failed twice before his parents encouraged him to pursue architecture. Shortly afterward, Chairman Mao Zedong launched the Great Leap Forward, a campaign to rapidly industrialize China, which resulted in widespread famine and hardship. In 1962, Zeng graduated from college and was assigned to an architectural team in Beijing, where he helped design Tiananmen Square and the Avenue of Heavenly Peace. Later, Zeng and his architect wife relocated to Pingdingshan, a coal mining region, where they spent 20 years designing facilities for the industry. By the 1980s, after Mao’s death and Deng Xiaoping’s reforms, new opportunities appeared in China’s coastal cities. Zeng and his wife moved to Shenzhen, newly designated as an economic zone next to Hong Kong. Shenzhen’s rapid development offered promise, and Zeng began teaching at Shenzhen University. Over the years, the city prospered, and the couple contributed to the design of numerous buildings as Shenzhen became a hub of Chinese modernization. Zeng and his wife bought an apartment in central Shenzhen and sent their children abroad to study. Today, Shenzhen boasts more skyscrapers than New York or Tokyo. 'We’ve seen many ups and downs,' says his wife, Zhao Sirong. 'Shenzhen was a young city, and we were pioneers.' Zeng retired from architecture at 80 and pursued his passion for painting. Despite having traditional training, he learned new techniques by watching online tutorials. Influenced by socialist realism, a style he encountered during the Mao era, Zeng draws inspiration from Russian realist painter Ilya Repin, especially works that depict the perseverance of ordinary people. This influence is evident in Zeng's own art, like 'Life Is Not Easy,' which portrays a migrant worker braving harsh winter conditions. Zhao often jokes about her husband's intense work ethic, noting that he paints daily and even on weekends, leaving her to tend to her plants. 'I wish he would slow down,' she says with a laugh. However, she still supports his passion, believing that staying active helps prevent mental decline. The couple observes how young people today often pass time on smartphones or playing outdoor mahjong, contrasting this with their own productive routines. 'My life is still very fulfilling,' Zeng says. 'Painting may be tiring, but so is gambling for some people.' As the coronavirus spread, Zeng became deeply interested in how it transformed daily life. He first painted nurses giving swab tests, then children attending online classes. When his residential complex went into lockdown, he depicted scenes of residents confined at home, guards on patrol, and masked delivery drivers tossing food over fences. 'This was an unprecedented event,' Zeng reflects. He and his wife contracted the virus last winter after the sudden lifting of restrictions. While Zhao recovered quickly, Zeng needed weeks to fully recover. Across China, the healthcare system was overwhelmed and medication shortages occurred, and hundreds of thousands lost their lives. 'We were all infected,' Zhao recalls. 'We struggled through three years, and then suddenly everything opened up. We weren’t psychologically prepared.' Zeng notes that despite the historic nature of the pandemic, few artistic depictions exist in China beyond official exhibitions and state television content praising government efforts. Under Xi Jinping, tighter controls on artistic expression have seen some artists move overseas. At a Beijing art expo this fall, one of Zeng’s paintings depicting lockdowns was hidden from public view for being considered negative. Still, Zeng insists his work is commemorative, not critical. He considers the pandemic a 'great historical event' and sees his art as a tribute to the endurance of ordinary people. Zeng and Zhao are grateful for the government benefits they enjoy — including public medical care, subsidized food, free transportation, and a pension of 10,000 yuan (about $1,400 USD) per month — far more than they expected when younger. 'We understand the country's measures,' Zhao says. 'Overall, our policy was correct. If we reopened too early, it could have been like the United States, where the death rate was very high.' Currently, Zeng is working on a series of paintings featuring Xi Jinping, aiming to positively promote the country's achievements. His latest painting shows Xi seated among villagers, tentatively titled 'Chairman Xi Taking Us on the Road to Prosperity.' 'My work can help illustrate the advantages of our socialist system,' Zeng says. 'This is a great era, and I want to capture it in my paintings.'
translated_content: SHENZHEN, China — En una pintura, una niña está sentada con la boca abierta mientras una trabajadora de la salud vestida de blanco le acerca un hisopo largo a la garganta. En otra, un oficial con mascarilla y trabajadores médicos se mantienen frente a un apartamento acordonado con cuerdas y sellos que dicen 'CERRADO', mientras los residentes observan frustrados. Estos son algunos de los retratos pintados por Zeng Fanzhi, de 85 años, para conmemorar los tres años de estrictos controles de 'cero COVID' en China, que llevaron a protestas nacionales hace un año. Zeng, arquitecto jubilado en Shenzhen, no critica las medidas bajo las cuales millones fueron examinados, confinados a sus apartamentos o llevados a centros de cuarentena. Gran parte de su vida la ha dedicado al servicio del Estado chino, incluyendo el diseño de monumentos en la plaza Tiananmen de Pekín y plantas de carbón para el Ministerio de Carbón. Como miembro de la asociación gubernamental de artistas de Shenzhen, su arte ha aparecido en sellos postales y ha recibido premios. A diferencia de los jóvenes manifestantes, la perspectiva de Zeng está moldeada por sus primeros años vividos en la China en guerra y revolucionaria, y décadas posteriores presenciando prosperidad y crecimiento. Él considera que el compromiso de China con los controles de 'cero COVID' fue necesario y ve la obediencia pública como heroica. El líder chino Xi Jinping ha dicho que 'la creación artística debe partir del punto de vista del pueblo'. Zeng explica que su enfoque en la gente común refleja esta filosofía: 'El arte debe reflejar la realidad de la vida de las personas. Mis pinturas siguen esa línea.' Durante su infancia, Zeng vivió épocas turbulentas de la historia moderna de China. Sus padres, ambos funcionarios públicos, huyeron a Chongqing, capital en tiempos de guerra durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial, y Zeng se mudó repetidamente para escapar tanto de la invasión japonesa como de la guerra civil. La victoria del Partido Comunista en 1949 trajo estabilidad al país tras décadas de conflictos. Zeng aspiraba a ser artista e intentó ingresar a la escuela de arte en 1957, pero falló dos veces antes de que sus padres lo animaran a estudiar arquitectura. Poco después, Mao Zedong lanzó el Gran Salto Adelante, una campaña para industrializar rápidamente China, que resultó en hambre y dificultades generalizadas. En 1962, tras graduarse, Zeng fue asignado a un equipo de arquitectura en Pekín, donde ayudó a diseñar la plaza Tiananmen y la Avenida de la Paz Celestial. Más tarde, él y su esposa arquitecta se mudaron a Pingdingshan, una región minera, donde pasaron 20 años diseñando instalaciones para la industria. En los años 80, tras la muerte de Mao y las reformas de Deng Xiaoping, aparecieron nuevas oportunidades en las ciudades costeras. Zeng y su esposa se mudaron a Shenzhen, recién designada como zona económica especial junto a Hong Kong. El rápido crecimiento de Shenzhen prometía mucho, y Zeng comenzó a enseñar en la Universidad de Shenzhen. Con el tiempo, la ciudad prosperó y la pareja contribuyó al diseño de numerosos edificios mientras Shenzhen se convertía en un centro de modernización china. Zeng y su esposa compraron un apartamento en el centro y enviaron a sus hijos a estudiar al extranjero. Hoy, Shenzhen tiene más rascacielos que Nueva York o Tokio. 'Hemos vivido muchos altibajos', dice su esposa Zhao Sirong. 'Shenzhen era una ciudad joven y fuimos pioneros.' Zeng se jubiló de la arquitectura a los 80 años y se dedicó a su pasión por la pintura. A pesar de una formación tradicional, aprendió nuevas técnicas viendo tutoriales en línea. Influenciado por el realismo socialista del maoísmo, Zeng se inspira en el pintor ruso Ilya Repin, especialmente en obras que muestran la perseverancia del pueblo común. Esto se refleja en su arte, como en 'La vida no es fácil', que retrata a una trabajadora migrante enfrentando el invierno. Zhao suele bromear sobre la ética de trabajo intensa de su esposo, señalando que pinta todos los días, incluso los fines de semana, mientras ella cuida de sus plantas. 'Me gustaría que él se tomara las cosas con más calma', dice entre risas. Sin embargo, apoya su pasión, creyendo que mantenerse activo ayuda a prevenir el deterioro mental. La pareja observa que los jóvenes hoy pasan mucho tiempo en sus teléfonos o jugando mahjong, y contrasta esto con sus propias rutinas productivas. 'Mi vida sigue siendo muy satisfactoria', dice Zeng. 'Pintar puede ser cansado, pero también lo es apostar para algunos.' A medida que se propagaba el coronavirus, Zeng se interesó mucho por cómo cambiaba la vida diaria. Primero pintó a enfermeras haciendo pruebas, después a niños en clases en línea. Cuando su complejo entró en confinamiento, retrató escenas de residentes en casa, guardias patrullando y repartidores lanzando comida por encima de las vallas. 'Fue un evento sin precedentes', reflexiona Zeng. Él y su esposa contrajeron el virus el pasado invierno tras el levantamiento repentino de las restricciones. Mientras Zhao se recuperó rápido, Zeng necesitó semanas para estar bien. En toda China, el sistema sanitario colapsó, hubo escasez de medicamentos y cientos de miles murieron. 'Todos estuvimos infectados', recuerda Zhao. 'Sufrimos tres años y de repente todo se abrió. No estábamos preparados mentalmente.' Zeng señala que, a pesar de la importancia histórica de la pandemia, existen pocas representaciones artísticas fuera de exposiciones oficiales y programas estatales que elogian al gobierno. Bajo Xi Jinping, el control sobre la expresión artística ha aumentado, lo que ha llevado a algunos artistas a mudarse al extranjero. En una exposición en Pekín este otoño, una de las pinturas de Zeng sobre el confinamiento fue retirada de la vista por considerarse negativa. Aun así, Zeng insiste en que su trabajo es conmemorativo, no crítico. Considera la pandemia como un 'gran evento histórico' y ve su arte como un tributo a la resistencia de la gente. Zeng y Zhao están agradecidos por los beneficios gubernamentales que disfrutan — atención médica pública, comida subvencionada, transporte gratuito y una pensión mensual de 10,000 yuanes (aproximadamente 1,400 dólares estadounidenses) — mucho más de lo que imaginaban en su juventud. 'Entendemos las medidas tomadas', dice Zhao. 'En general, nuestra política fue correcta. Si hubiéramos abierto antes, habría sido como en Estados Unidos, donde la tasa de mortalidad fue muy alta.' Actualmente, Zeng trabaja en una serie de pinturas dedicadas a Xi Jinping, buscando promover positivamente los logros del país. Su última obra muestra a Xi sentado entre campesinos, titulada provisionalmente 'El presidente Xi llevándonos por el camino de la prosperidad.' 'Mi trabajo puede ayudar a ilustrar las ventajas de nuestro sistema socialista', dice Zeng. 'Vivimos en una gran era y quiero plasmarla en mis pinturas.'
post_content: Zeng Fanzhi, 85, captures China's strict zero-COVID years in powerful paintings. His life from wartime to modern Shenzhen shapes his art, honoring ordinary people’s resilience and government policy. #ChinaArt #ZeroCOVID #EverydayHeroes

article_content: Bata India reported a 38% decline in second-quarter profit on Wednesday, impacted by a one-time charge and ongoing inflationary pressures that reduced customer traffic at its stores. The footwear manufacturer said its consolidated profit dropped to 339.9 million rupees ($4.1 million) for July-September, compared to 548.2 million rupees in the same period last year. This quarter included a 409 million rupee expense related to a voluntary retirement scheme at one of its manufacturing units. Revenue slipped 1.3% during the period. Indian businesses faced lower store traffic in the quarter, as high inflation led consumers to limit discretionary spending, even though retail inflation has recently eased but remains elevated. In contrast, Relaxo Footwear posted a 97.3% surge in profit earlier in November, driven by strong demand. Khadim India and Campus Activewear are expected to announce their results later this month. Bata, which is part of its Netherlands-based parent group, saw its shares close 1.2% higher before the results announcement. (Exchange rate: $1 = 83.2673 INR) Separately, India's packaged consumer goods industry grew 9% by value and 8.6% by volume in the September quarter compared to a year earlier, boosted by higher rural spending on essentials and discretionary items, according to NielsenIQ. Meanwhile, Snap Inc., parent company of Snapchat, doubled its user base in India to 200 million within a year, thanks to new features such as Spotlight, which competes with Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. In government policy, the finance ministry is discussing reducing the pace of capital expenditure increases in the interim budget for FY25 to help meet fiscal deficit targets.

Mientras tanto, Snap Inc., empresa matriz de Snapchat, duplicó su base de usuarios en India a 200 millones en un año, gracias a nuevas funciones como Spotlight, que compite con Instagram Reels y YouTube Shorts. article_content: Joe McGinniss was shocked by Jeffrey MacDonald’s appearance in a North Carolina courtroom last week. Once confident and charismatic, MacDonald, now 68, seemed diminished and frail, contrasting sharply with the man McGinniss interviewed decades earlier for his book 'Fatal Vision.' Their meeting marked their first encounter in more than 35 years. Over the years, McGinniss has been at the center of controversy for his portrayal of MacDonald, a convicted murderer, in 'Fatal Vision.' At a recent federal hearing in Wilmington, North Carolina, McGinniss testified for the prosecution. The hearing could determine whether MacDonald deserves a new trial or another chance at freedom. MacDonald's defense team argues that new DNA evidence—three hairs not matching MacDonald or the victims—and the secondhand confession from a key witness justify reopening the case. Judge John C. Fox is reviewing the arguments. His decision could let the convictions stand, overturn them, or lead to a new trial. A ruling could take weeks or months in this long-standing criminal case. The case began in 1970 at MacDonald’s home at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. Military police found Colette MacDonald, pregnant at the time, and her daughters Kimberly, 5, and Kristen, 2, brutally murdered. MacDonald, then a captain in the Green Berets, claimed that intruders attacked his family, but prosecutors alleged he staged the scene. The Army initially cleared MacDonald in a military hearing, but a grand jury later indicted him in 1975. He was convicted in 1979 and is serving three life sentences. Unless his appeal succeeds, MacDonald will not be eligible for parole until 2071. He has always maintained his innocence. Errol Morris’s new book, 'A Wilderness of Error,' argues that MacDonald was wrongfully convicted and that the evidence was incomplete and mishandled. Morris claims the case involves significant prosecutorial misconduct. McGinniss, however, stands by his belief in MacDonald's guilt, citing his impressions from the trial and the accumulating evidence against MacDonald. He rejected suggestions that he deceived MacDonald for the sake of his book and denies claims that prosecutors threatened witness Helena Stoeckley to change her testimony. Past disputes between MacDonald and McGinniss include a civil case over the book’s portrayal of MacDonald, which ended with a settlement after the jury deadlocked. Journalist Janet Malcolm later criticized McGinniss’s reporting in a widely-read article. Today, McGinniss describes MacDonald as a shadow of his former self, changed by decades behind bars.

La policía militar encontró a Colette MacDonald, embarazada en ese momento, y a sus hijas Kimberly, de 5 años, y Kristen, de 2 años, brutalmente asesinadas. MacDonald, entonces capitán en los Boinas Verdes, afirmó que unos intrusos atacaron a su familia, pero los fiscales alegaron que él mismo preparó la escena. El Ejército inicialmente absolvió a MacDonald en una audiencia militar, pero más tarde un gran jurado lo acusó en 1975. Fue declarado culpable en 1979 y cumple tres cadenas perpetuas. A menos que su apelación prospere, MacDonald no será elegible para libertad condicional hasta 2071. Siempre ha sostenido su inocencia. El nuevo libro de Errol Morris, 'A Wilderness of Error', sostiene que MacDonald fue condenado injustamente y que la evidencia era incompleta y fue mal manejada. Morris afirma que el caso presenta una importante mala conducta procesal. Sin embargo, McGinniss mantiene su convicción sobre la culpabilidad de MacDonald, citando sus impresiones del juicio y la acumulación de pruebas en su contra. Rechazó sugerencias de que engañó a MacDonald para su libro y niega que los fiscales hayan presionado a la testigo Helena Stoeckley para cambiar su testimonio. Disputas pasadas entre MacDonald y McGinniss incluyen una demanda civil por la forma en que el libro retrataba a MacDonald, la cual terminó en un acuerdo amistoso tras la indecisión del jurado. La periodista Janet Malcolm luego criticó el reportaje de McGinniss en un artículo muy leído. Hoy en día, McGinniss describe a MacDonald como una sombra de lo que fue, marcado por décadas en prisión.

article_content: This year on N7 Day—an annual celebration for Mass Effect fans—BioWare offered only a brief glimpse of Mass Effect 4. The teaser showed an N7 agent wearing a trench coat and helmet, walking down a corridor, plus a poster featuring character art and confirmation of the Geth’s return. Despite the excitement, there's growing concern among fans about what’s actually happening with BioWare’s biggest projects: Dragon Age: Dreadwolf and Mass Effect 4. Both games have remained mostly silent for years.  After Anthem’s 2019 release fell short of expectations despite continued updates, BioWare has kept a low profile. Dragon Age: Dreadwolf has undergone several development restarts with different leaders, and updates have been limited to concept art or a near-static cutscene released nearly a year ago. The most recent official news, from October 2022, celebrated reaching the alpha milestone, but nothing substantial has followed. A 2024 release is speculative and still unconfirmed.  In comparison, Mass Effect 4 appears even further away. Industry journalist Jeff Grubb has stated that, if its timeline mirrors Dreadwolf’s, it might not come out until 2029. This is a stark shift from earlier BioWare years, when new Mass Effect and Dragon Age titles launched much closer together. Unlike the more fast-paced output from studios like Respawn, BioWare’s current development is noticeably sluggish.  With so little information and progress shared publicly, the article urges BioWare to communicate more openly and honestly about where these major titles really stand.
