article_content: On Tuesday, Russia and China used their veto powers at the U.N. Security Council to block a resolution calling for an immediate halt to Syria’s crackdown on dissent. This move came despite nine council members, including the United States, supporting the proposal. Russian Ambassador Vitaly Churkin defended the veto, warning that Security Council involvement would amount to unwarranted interference in Syria and might set a dangerous international precedent. In contrast, U.S. Ambassador Susan Rice denounced the council’s failure to respond to a dire humanitarian crisis and threats to regional security. The proposed resolution called for Syrian President Bashar al-Assad’s government to cease its repressive actions against civilians. Reacting to the outcome, Syrian Ambassador Bashar Ja'afari accused some Western nations of prejudice and inflammatory language against Syria. India, Brazil, South Africa, and Lebanon abstained from voting. Human rights groups condemned Russia and China's veto. Philippe Bolopion from Human Rights Watch stated that their decision allows the Syrian regime’s abuses to continue, especially following months of violence, detentions, and torture. Violence in Syria escalated again as new deaths were reported amid the government’s sustained offensive against protestors—a situation drawing widespread condemnation. Army defectors banded together as the Free Syria Army and appealed for international support. Colonel Riad al-Assa'ad, who leads the Free Syria Army, argued that sustained force is the only way to bring down the Assad regime, which he said has ruled through violence for decades. He urged the international community to implement a no-fly zone and provide weapons to the opposition, aiming to secure a base for resistance. U.S. State Department spokesperson Victoria Nuland reinforced American efforts to persuade the Security Council, asserting that the Assad regime’s brutality demands a strong, unified global message. Reports from activist groups and monitors, like the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights and the Local Coordination Committees, described further clashes and casualties, including soldiers, civilians, and children losing their lives in Homs, Idlib, and other regions. Arrests and demonstrations also continued nationwide. The Syrian government blames 'armed terrorist groups' for recent violence and deaths, while activists point to security forces as responsible for widespread bloodshed. Restrictions on international journalists have made it hard to independently verify these competing claims. As violence intensifies, opposition leaders are urgently seeking outside help. Defectors say more soldiers are joining their ranks despite threats of government retaliation against their families. The Free Syria Army has acknowledged some attacks targeting government forces, stating their goal is to protect civilians and undermine the regime's ability to suppress dissent.

India, Brasil, Sudáfrica y Líbano se abstuvieron en la votación. Organizaciones de derechos humanos condenaron el veto de Rusia y China. El coronel Riad al-Assa'ad, líder del Ejército Libre de Siria, sostuvo que la única manera de derrocar al régimen de Assad es mediante fuerza sostenida, recalcando que, según él, el gobierno ha recurrido a la violencia durante décadas. article_content: By Corey Charlton. A Harry Potter-style rotunda, a Willy Wonka glass lift, and London’s striking skyscraper The Shard are among the nominees for architecture’s top prize. The RIBA Stirling Prize, which also includes Liverpool’s Everyman Theatre, the London Aquatics Centre, the London School of Economics, and the Manchester School of Art, is presented annually to the UK’s best new building. Judges praised the innovative design of the Library of Birmingham. With its 'Harry Potter rotunda' and 'Willy Wonka-style glass lift', it was described as a landmark that has 'shaken the traditional perception of a library.' The futuristic library, designed by Francine Houben and officially opened last year, also houses the city’s collection of archives, photography, and rare books. Judges compared The Shard to the 'Gothic spire of a German cathedral,' calling it 'the most significant step forward on the London skyline since St Paul’s.' The building, which is not yet fully occupied, contains a health clinic, offices, restaurants, a hotel, apartments, and a public viewing gallery. Creating such a tower on a compact site was hailed as a 'rare achievement.' The judges noted, 'Understanding that there are many days when the London skyline reads only as a depressing grey silhouette, the architects have left a substantial part at the top open, adding to the lightness even in these conditions, much like the Gothic spire of a German cathedral.' For the Manchester School of Art, the judges said entering the building felt more like stepping into a metropolitan art gallery than a university department, predicting it would influence the design of similar buildings for years to come. The London Aquatics Centre was highly praised—judges remarked that removing the wings, which accommodated Olympic spectators, allowed the building to 'fly free.' Designed by Zaha Hadid and inspired by the 'fluid geometry of water in motion,' the centre was described as both beautiful and 'conceptually flawless.' It was also the venue for swimming events during the London 2012 Olympics. Liverpool’s Everyman Theatre, built on the site of its predecessor, retains its historical character through the use of recycled and exposed brick. According to judges, 'After nine years’ gestation, Liverpool has a brand new purpose-built theatre of outstanding quality. This is a building that will age gracefully, continually enriched by the patina of daily use. It will both reassure and delight its loyal audience and those discovering this gem for the first time.' Also shortlisted is the London School of Economics’ Saw Swee Hock Student Centre, described as a 'startlingly original building,' 'beautifully constructed,' and 'a massive contribution to its townscape.' RIBA president Stephen Hodder called the shortlist 'poetic,' stating, 'They are beautiful, inspiring, and transformative new buildings that their communities can relish and be proud of. They are remarkably crafted buildings and, the closer you look at their detail, both internally and externally, and their materiality, the more impressive they become.' The winner, selected by a team of judges, will be announced on October 16.

Son construcciones extraordinariamente elaboradas y, cuanto más se observa su detalle, tanto interno como externo, y su materialidad, más impresionan.' El ganador, elegido por un equipo de jueces, se anunciará el 16 de octubre.

article_content: American artist David Bowen has created an interactive installation called 'Cloud Piano,' transforming the ever-shifting clouds overhead into live piano performances. A camera records the sky, and specialized software divides the image into 88 segments—one for each piano key. Using Max/MSP, the system interprets details like cloud thickness, movement, and form, then signals a robotic device to play the piano. The robot strikes keys harder when clouds are dense and presses more softly for lighter clouds, producing music that, while dissonant, has a calming effect. Listeners might also hear faint squeaks as the robot operates the keys. This project continues Bowen’s exploration of nature through technology. His previous work, 'Underwater,' translated the motion of a river—tracked with a Microsoft Kinect—onto ropes moved by hundreds of servo motors, simulating watery ripples. Cloud Piano will debut at a gallery in Saint Etienne, France, offering an imaginative intersection of technology, nature, and music.

Utilizando Max/MSP, el sistema interpreta detalles como la densidad, el movimiento y la forma de las nubes, y luego envía instrucciones a un dispositivo robótico que toca el piano. article_content: April J. Sands, a former lawyer with the Federal Election Commission (FEC), came under investigation for engaging in partisan political activity while at work—promoting campaigns for Barack Obama and other Democrats, and even requesting campaign donations, which is prohibited under federal law. After evidence of her actions surfaced—including partisan tweets and an online interview—Sands resigned in April 2014. The investigation into Sands was hindered when the FEC disclosed that her computer hard drive had already been recycled, effectively eliminating possible digital evidence. This echoed a similar controversy involving Lois Lerner, Sands’s former supervisor at the FEC who later became an IRS official. Lerner had also been investigated for lost emails relating to accusations of targeting conservative groups, following the unexplained destruction of her own hard drive. Sands was well-known in the FEC as an outspoken supporter of Obama, frequently posting partisan messages to her social media, including criticisms of Republicans and calls for Democratic donations during office hours. Some of her public commentary included suggesting only 'straight white men' would vote Republican, and supporting candidates against prominent conservative politicians. The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform launched inquiries into the matter, specifically questioning how evidence in a possible criminal case could be accidentally destroyed. Following news of the investigation, Sands restricted public access to her social media accounts. Sands ultimately admitted to violating the Hatch Act—a law banning most federal employees from partisan politicking during work hours—and accepted a two-year suspension from federal employment as part of a settlement. The incident spotlights enduring concerns about political impartiality among federal workers and the adequacy of procedures for preserving evidence in government investigations. Lawmakers, particularly among Republicans, remain interested in the fate of potentially crucial evidence in politically sensitive cases involving top government officials like Sands and Lerner. Overall, the case underscores the ongoing debate surrounding political expression within federal agencies and raises questions about the conduct of official investigations when partisanship is suspected.

article_content: It’s easy to imagine these vividly colored damselflies on a romantic insect date, as they appear to be holding hands. The charming images were captured by photographer Alberto Ghizzi Panizza, 38, from Parma, Italy, as he walked across a flood plain near the River Po in the Po Valley early one morning. The big-eyed insects seemed to enjoy perching together on wildflowers, appearing like best friends cuddling. Panizza spotted the damselflies covered in dew just after dawn. Adult damselflies eat flies, mosquitoes, and other small insects, while some larger tropical species have been known to eat spiders. Unlike dragonflies, which rest with their wings spread apart, damselflies rest with their wings closed together over their bodies. Like all members of the order Odonata, damselflies have a fascinating breeding system. Before mating, males and females spend significant time in physical contact, which scientists believe allows them to assess each other as potential mates. Once a match is found, the male uses special structures at the end of his abdomen to grasp the female’s thorax. The female evaluates how well the male’s structures fit her sockets, deciding whether to accept or look for another partner. Panizza, amused by the damselflies’ poses, took photos of them resting on wildflowers. He said: 'I found these insects’ expressions very funny. The morning was cold and wet, but they seemed comfortable perched on flowers and branches. My favorite photo looks like they’re holding hands and introduces one as the other’s partner. I call this shot ‘Meet Sally,’ inspired by the film When Harry Met Sally.' The damselflies measure about three centimeters in length, with large eyes roughly one millimeter across. Panizza noted it is sweet to imagine them as close friends. He observed that while butterfly numbers in the Po Valley have dropped this year, damselfly numbers have increased. He’s been taking professional photographs for 15 years and also has profile shots showing the insects’ mating process. During mating, one damselfly remains attached to a branch while the other is grabbed by the neck with the tail, forming a heart-like shape. They maintain this position for several minutes and can even move from branch to branch in flight while still attached. Despite their cute appearance, damselflies are carnivorous, similar to dragonflies. Damselflies undergo incomplete metamorphosis, starting as aquatic nymphs with large, external gills resembling three fins at the end of the abdomen. After several molts, the winged adult emerges. As nymphs, they feed on mosquito larvae and small aquatic organisms using extendable jaws—much like dragonfly nymphs. Panizza has also photographed the damselflies in profile, documenting their unique mating behaviors. Adults feed on small insects, and, distinct from dragonflies, rest with their wings closed together.
translated_content: Es fácil imaginar a estas libélulas de colores vivos en una cita romántica de insectos, ya que parecen estar tomadas de la mano. Las encantadoras imágenes fueron capturadas por el fotógrafo Alberto Ghizzi Panizza, de 38 años, de Parma, Italia, mientras caminaba por una llanura inundada cerca del río Po, en el Valle del Po, temprano por la mañana. Los insectos de ojos grandes parecían disfrutar posándose juntos en las flores silvestres, como si fueran mejores amigos abrazándose. Panizza vio a las libélulas cubiertas de rocío poco después del amanecer. Las libélulas damiselas adultas comen moscas, mosquitos y otros insectos pequeños, mientras que algunas especies tropicales más grandes pueden alimentarse de arañas. A diferencia de las libélulas verdaderas, que descansan con las alas extendidas, las libélulas damiselas reposan con las alas plegadas sobre el cuerpo. Como todos los miembros del orden Odonata, las libélulas damiselas tienen un sistema de reproducción fascinante. Antes de aparearse, los machos y las hembras pasan un tiempo significativo en contacto físico, lo que, según los científicos, les permite evaluarse como posibles parejas. Una vez que encuentran pareja, el macho utiliza estructuras especiales al final de su abdomen para sujetar el tórax de la hembra. Ella evalúa qué tan bien encajan estas estructuras en sus receptáculos y decide si acepta o busca otro compañero. Divertido por las poses de las libélulas damiselas, Panizza tomó fotos de ellas descansando en flores silvestres. Dijo: 'Me parecieron muy graciosas las expresiones de estos insectos. La mañana estaba fría y húmeda, pero parecían cómodas posadas en flores y ramas. Mi foto favorita parece que están tomadas de la mano y presenta a una como la pareja de la otra. Llamo a esta toma ‘Conoce a Sally’, inspirada en la película "Cuando Harry conoció a Sally".' Las libélulas damiselas miden aproximadamente tres centímetros de largo, con grandes ojos de cerca de un milímetro de diámetro. Panizza observó que es tierno imaginar que son amigas cercanas. Señaló que, mientras que el número de mariposas ha disminuido este año en el Valle del Po, el número de libélulas damiselas ha aumentado. Lleva 15 años como fotógrafo profesional y también tiene imágenes de perfil que muestran el proceso de apareamiento de los insectos. Durante el apareamiento, una libélula damisela permanece sujeta a una rama mientras la otra es sujetada por el cuello con la cola, formando una especie de figura de corazón. Mantienen esta posición durante varios minutos e incluso pueden moverse de una rama a otra en vuelo mientras siguen unidas. A pesar de su aspecto tierno, las libélulas damiselas son carnívoras, al igual que las libélulas verdaderas. Las libélulas damiselas sufren una metamorfosis incompleta, comenzando como ninfas acuáticas con branquias externas grandes que semejan tres aletas al final del abdomen. Tras varias mudas, emerge el adulto alado. De ninfas, se alimentan de larvas de mosquito y pequeños organismos acuáticos usando mandíbulas extensibles, al igual que las ninfas de las libélulas verdaderas. Panizza también ha fotografiado a las libélulas damiselas de perfil, documentando sus singulares comportamientos de apareamiento. Los adultos se alimentan de pequeños insectos y, a diferencia de las libélulas verdaderas, descansan con las alas plegadas.

article_content: Walking in the annual Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show, watched by millions worldwide, is considered one of the highest honors in lingerie modeling. This year, Candice Swanepoel will not only walk as a Victoria's Secret Angel but will also wear $10 million (£6.2 million) worth of jewelry. The 23-year-old model will showcase the iconic Royal Fantasy Bra and Belt, designed exclusively for Victoria's Secret by renowned jeweler Mouawad. The Royal Fantasy Bra and Belt are adorned with more than 4,200 precious gems from around the world, including rubies, diamonds, and yellow sapphires. Set in 18-carat gold, the bra features a 52-carat, pear-shaped center ruby. Beyond wearing the luxurious lingerie at the December show, Candice, who is from South Africa, will also model the design in the 2013 Victoria's Secret Dreams & Fantasies Catalogue. This is Candice’s first time wearing a Victoria's Secret Fantasy Bra. She follows supermodels such as Miranda Kerr, Tyra Banks, Gisele Bündchen, Heidi Klum, Alessandra Ambrosio, Adriana Lima, and Claudia Schiffer. Candice expressed her excitement on social media: 'So excited to be wearing the fantasy bra this year in the @victoriassecret fashion show!' She also told People magazine, 'They had to make a mold of my body to be able to make [the bra], I was really excited. I tried to imagine after they’d done the mold how they would make it, how it would look. My imagination didn’t do it justice. My favorite part is this beautiful 52-carat pear-shaped ruby. Every part of it is exquisite.' Candice also noted, 'I’ve never worn anything this expensive, and we have to put gloves on when we handle it. It’s kind of a big ordeal. The bra comes with two bodyguards and we have to be very careful!' The first Fantasy Bra was created in 1996 for Claudia Schiffer. The most expensive, the Ruby Fantasy Bra worn by Gisele Bündchen in 2000, cost $15 million (£9.3 million). Other memorable Fantasy Bras include the $2 million (£1.25 million) 'Bombshell' worn by Adriana Lima in 2010 and the $12.5 million (£7.8 million) Christmas Dreams & Fantasies bra modeled by Heidi Klum in 2001.

article_content: Cisco Systems lowered its yearly revenue and profit guidance on Wednesday, pointing to decreased demand for its networking gear. This announcement sparked nearly an 11% drop in Cisco’s shares after regular trading. The company has been struggling with ongoing supply chain issues and a slowdown in hardware demand post-pandemic, pushing it to emphasize software offerings like cybersecurity. To strengthen its position in software and capitalize on the rise of artificial intelligence, Cisco announced a $28 billion purchase of cybersecurity firm Splunk in September. Cisco explained that fewer new orders in the first quarter were primarily because customers are busy deploying products already shipped to them, leaving a backlog spanning one to two quarters. Chief Financial Officer Scott Herren expressed confidence that order growth will return in the latter half of the year as clients finish implementing what they have. For the full year, Cisco expects to bring in between $53.8 billion and $55 billion in revenue, with adjusted earnings per share ranging from $3.87 to $3.93. These are both lower than its previous forecasts of $57-$58.2 billion in revenue and $4.01-$4.08 in earnings per share. Looking ahead, Cisco predicts second-quarter revenue between $12.6 billion and $12.8 billion, which is significantly less than the $14.19 billion anticipated by analysts. Company executives noted that supply chain constraints are now much less of an issue, with delivery times and backlogs mostly back to normal. Despite the revised forecasts, Cisco reported adjusted first-quarter earnings per share of $1.11, exceeding Wall Street’s estimate of $1.03. Revenue for the quarter also topped expectations. By contrast, competitors Juniper Networks and Arista Networks recently reported strong financial performances, helped by continued solid spending from large business customers.

El director financiero, Scott Herren, se mostró confiado en que el crecimiento de órdenes regresará en la segunda mitad del año, una vez que los clientes terminen de instalar lo que ya tienen. De cara al futuro, Cisco pronostica que los ingresos del segundo trimestre oscilarán entre 12.600 y 12.800 millones de dólares, significativamente menos que los 14.190 millones anticipados por los analistas. article_content: Bayer Leverkusen regained second place in the Bundesliga on Sunday with a 4-2 home win over struggling Stuttgart. Stuttgart twice came from behind, but late goals from Stefan Reinartz and Stefan Kiessling secured the victory for coach Jupp Heynckes’ team. The 2007 German champions, Stuttgart, are now joint bottom of the table with Borussia Monchengladbach, who surprised Champions League side Schalke with a 2-1 home win. Peer Kluge gave mid-table Schalke an early lead in the second minute, but Gladbach equalized through Marco Reus before Mohamadou Idrissou scored to secure their first home win of the season. Only five points separate the bottom five Bundesliga teams, with Stuttgart and Monchengladbach level at the bottom on 19 points. Although Leverkusen are now up to second place, they still trail league leaders Borussia Dortmund by ten points. Dortmund extended their lead with a home win over St. Pauli on Saturday. Leverkusen, however, now enjoy a three-point cushion over third-placed Bayern Munich.

article_content: A man in his 20s was found dead on Mount Snowdon, which stands at 3,560 feet, after he apparently fell. The body was discovered by other walkers on a 2,500-foot ridge near Parson's Nose, a scrambling route that requires some rock climbing skills. The man was pronounced dead at the scene by a medic from the Sea King helicopter search and rescue crew based at RAF Valley in Anglesey. Mount Snowdon, located in North Wales, is the highest peak in England and Wales. The helicopter crew, which includes Prince William among its rescue pilots, assisted the Llanberis and Aberglaslyn mountain rescue teams in transferring the body to a hospital in Bangor. This incident marks the second death on Snowdon in the past month. Over the Easter weekend, an ice climber died after falling more than 100 feet down an icy section of Snowdonia during treacherous conditions. The same RAF crew responded yesterday to another emergency, assisting the North East Wales search and rescue team after a paraglider from Mold in Flintshire was injured in a fall near Llantysilio, Denbighshire. The paraglider, who fell about 40 feet, was airlifted to Wrexham Maelor Hospital with a serious back injury. Sergeant Dickie Myers of RAF Valley stated, 'He took quite a heavy fall and suffered a serious back injury. We put him in a full stretcher and transferred him to hospital in Wrexham.' Last month, the Government announced that Britain's search and rescue helicopter service will be operated by US-based Bristow Helicopters starting in 2016. This £1.6 billion contract will end 70 years of search and rescue service by the RAF and Royal Navy squadrons.

article_content: Jean-Claude Juncker, President of the European Commission and former prime minister of Luxembourg, is facing heightened scrutiny over his role in the country's tax policies. Both senior Conservative and Labour figures in the UK have called for a thorough investigation into allegations that Luxembourg, under Juncker’s leadership, facilitated tax avoidance for multinational companies. While Juncker denies any wrongdoing, he has accepted political responsibility, stating he was not aware of the specifics behind corporate tax agreements. He maintains that he did not directly negotiate these deals. Major firms such as Burberry and Dyson are reported to have leveraged Luxembourg-based divisions to provide loans to overseas branches, thereby reducing taxable profits abroad. In some instances, companies allegedly enjoyed tax rates as low as under 1% on profits moved to Luxembourg. UK Cabinet ministers Iain Duncan Smith and Grant Shapps have increased the pressure, urging the European Commission to launch a transparent investigation. Duncan Smith suggested that the EU must demonstrate its ability to investigate its own leadership and operate openly. Grant Shapps further stressed the importance of accountability for European leaders, and called for a proper inquiry into the allegations. It has also emerged that Juncker, while prime minister, highlighted Luxembourg's favorable tax policies to attract companies like AOL and Amazon. Labour's shadow Europe minister, Pat McFadden, commented that if further evidence surfaces, Juncker’s position may come under question. Despite serving as Luxembourg’s prime minister for 18 years—and concurrently as finance minister for most of that time—Juncker insists he was not responsible for devising the tax rulings criticized for enabling tax avoidance. He has denied orchestrating tax evasion and has referred questions to Luxembourg’s current government.

Si bien Juncker niega cualquier irregularidad, ha aceptado la responsabilidad política y afirma que no conocía los detalles de los acuerdos fiscales corporativos. Sostiene que no negoció estas exenciones directamente. Los ministros del gabinete británico Iain Duncan Smith y Grant Shapps han intensificado la presión, instando a la Comisión Europea a realizar una investigación transparente. Duncan Smith sugirió que la UE debe demostrar su capacidad para investigar a sus propios líderes y proceder con transparencia. Grant Shapps también enfatizó la importancia de la rendición de cuentas entre los dirigentes europeos y pidió una investigación adecuada sobre las acusaciones. También se supo que Juncker, mientras era primer ministro, destacó las políticas fiscales favorables de Luxemburgo para atraer a empresas como AOL y Amazon. El ministro portavoz de Europa en la sombra del Partido Laborista, Pat McFadden, comentó que si se presentan más pruebas, la posición de Juncker podría peligrar. A pesar de haber sido primer ministro de Luxemburgo durante 18 años —y en la mayoría de ese tiempo también ministro de Finanzas— Juncker insiste en que no fue responsable de diseñar las controvertidas decisiones fiscales criticadas por fomentar la evasión de impuestos. article_content: Al Ahly's remarkable journey continued on Sunday as the Egyptian football club advanced to the semifinals of the FIFA Club World Cup in Japan. Back home, the nation was embroiled in political demonstrations against President Mohamed Morsy's planned constitutional referendum, but on the pitch, Al Ahly were setting up a much-anticipated clash with South American champions Corinthians. “Al Ahly fans can now dream of reaching the final. We share that dream and will give our all to clinch the title,” coach Hossam El-Badry told the club’s television channel following a hard-fought 2-1 victory over J-League champions Sanfrecce Hiroshima. With the Egyptian domestic league suspended since a deadly incident in Port Said claimed more than 70 lives during an Al Ahly match in February, reaching this stage is viewed as a remarkable achievement for the Cairo-based team. Al Ahly qualified for the Club World Cup by claiming their record-extending seventh African title last month. This occurred on the same day a tragic train accident in Egypt resulted in the deaths of over 50 children. Most of Al Ahly's home games in the African Champions League were played behind closed doors for security reasons, while the first leg of the final took place at a military facility near Alexandria. One fan summed up the impact of Sunday’s win on Twitter: “Al Ahly is the only entity that can unite millions behind one opinion, hope, and dream.” Veteran midfielder Mohamed Aboutrika scored the decisive second-half goal after replacing Al Ahly’s captain and playmaker Hossam Ghaly, who suffered a serious knee injury. Despite snowy, cold conditions, Al Ahly opened the scoring 15 minutes in when Hiroshima’s substitute goalkeeper Takuya Masuda—forced on early after an injury to first-choice Shusaku Nishikawa—was beaten by Elsayed Hamdi. Hiroshima drew level after Ghaly was forced out with a suspected ruptured knee ligament, as J-League top scorer Hisato Sato found the net in the 32nd minute. Aboutrika, making his fourth appearance in the tournament, notched his fourth goal—bringing him level with stars like Lionel Messi and Denilson on the all-time Club World Cup scoring chart. Al Ahly had also reached the semifinals in 2006 but lost to Brazil’s Internacional before securing third place against Mexico’s Club America. “Corinthians are an excellent team. We will do our best to get a positive result and dedicate it to the victims of the Port Said disaster,” said 34-year-old Aboutrika, who was also part of the 2006 squad. “Playing against Brazilian teams is always special for me, especially as I dream of reaching the World Cup in Brazil with the national team.” Mexican club Monterrey also qualified for the semifinals by defeating Asian champions Ulsan Hyundai 3-1, setting up a meeting with European champions Chelsea. Monterrey, last season’s CONCACAF Champions League winners, went ahead through 19-year-old Jesus Corona, with Cesar Delgado scoring twice late in the game. Ulsan Hyundai’s Lee Keunho, the 2012 Asian player of the year, netted a late consolation goal.

Nosotros compartimos ese sueño y daremos todo para lograr el título”, dijo el entrenador Hossam El-Badry al canal de televisión del club tras la ardua victoria por 2-1 sobre los campeones de la J-League, Sanfrecce Hiroshima. A pesar del clima frío y nevado, Al Ahly abrió el marcador a los 15 minutos cuando el portero suplente de Hiroshima, Takuya Masuda—ingresado temprano tras la lesión del titular Shusaku Nishikawa—fue vencido por Elsayed Hamdi. Hiroshima empató después de que Ghaly debiera salir por una posible rotura de ligamentos de rodilla, y el máximo goleador de la J-League, Hisato Sato, marcó en el minuto 32. Aboutrika, en su cuarta participación en el torneo, anotó su cuarto gol, alcanzando a estrellas como Lionel Messi y Denilson en la tabla histórica de goleadores del torneo. Al Ahly también llegó a semifinales en 2006, pero perdió ante el Internacional de Brasil antes de quedarse con el tercer puesto frente al Club América de México. “Corinthians es un gran equipo. Haremos todo lo posible para lograr un resultado positivo y dedicárselo a las víctimas de la tragedia de Port Said”, dijo el veterano Aboutrika, de 34 años, quien también formó parte del equipo en 2006. “Jugar contra equipos brasileños siempre es especial para mí, sobre todo porque sueño con llegar al Mundial de Brasil con la selección nacional.” El club mexicano Monterrey también clasificó a las semifinales al vencer por 3-1 a los campeones asiáticos Ulsan Hyundai, y ahora se enfrentará a los campeones europeos Chelsea. Monterrey, ganador de la Liga de Campeones de la CONCACAF la temporada pasada, se adelantó con el gol del joven Jesús Corona, de 19 años, y César Delgado anotó dos veces al final. Lee Keunho, jugador asiático del año 2012 de Ulsan Hyundai, marcó el gol de consolación cerca del final.

article_content: Archaeologists working in northern Greece have determined that a mysterious tomb, once believed to be undisturbed, was likely looted ages ago. The massive burial site at Amphipolis drew international fascination, with experts hopeful it might house the remains of a significant figure from Alexander the Great’s era. Initial investigations revealed grand features, such as two sphinxes guarding the entrance and intricate marble decorations. However, evidence like forced entry marks and a hole in the inner wall suggests the site was robbed in antiquity. The monument, measuring nearly 590 meters around, is the largest burial mound discovered in Greece. The tomb, dating from between 325 and 300 BC, has sparked widespread speculation. While the possibility of finding treasures or a prominent historical figure remains uncertain, the site’s unique architecture and scale have impressed both archaeologists and the public alike. Excavations, led by Katerina Peristeri, are continuing despite fears that looters removed much of the original contents. A significant discovery at the site includes the remains of a large stone lion, thought to have once stood atop the mound and now believed to be linked with Laomedon of Mytilene, a commander under Alexander the Great. Recent removal of earth around the sphinxes revealed a marble lintel highlighted by frescoes. Although the tomb’s association with Alexander or his family has not been confirmed, its extraordinary size and features indicate that it was constructed for an individual of considerable importance. Prime Minister Antonis Samaras called the find 'extremely important,' reflecting both the national and global interest in the ongoing excavations. Greek cultural tradition holds that the sphinx is a mythical guardian, blending the body of a lion, the wings of a bird, and a human face. At Amphipolis, the decapitated sphinxes and missing wall sections underline the likelihood that the site was accessed and damaged long ago. The ongoing research aims to answer the pressing question of who was buried within the monument. While the hope of discovering untouched treasures has faded, the excavation is still revealing valuable insights into Greek history, architecture, and culture at the time of Alexander the Great.

Las investigaciones iniciales revelaron detalles impresionantes, como dos esfinges que custodiaban la entrada y elaboradas decoraciones de mármol. Sin embargo, pruebas como marcas de entrada forzada y un agujero en la pared interior sugieren que el sitio fue saqueado en la antigüedad. El monumento, de casi 590 metros de circunferencia, es el mayor túmulo funerario descubierto en Grecia. La tumba, que data entre 325 y 300 a.C., ha generado una gran especulación. Aunque la posibilidad de encontrar tesoros o los restos de una figura histórica relevante sigue siendo incierta, la arquitectura y la escala del sitio han impresionado a arqueólogos y al público. Las excavaciones, dirigidas por Katerina Peristeri, continúan a pesar de los temores de que saqueadores hayan extraído gran parte del contenido original. article_content: Immigration enforcement in Arizona has been thrust into the spotlight following the passage of SB 1070. Supporters of the law, such as native Arizonan Sue Schwartz, who has Mexican ancestry, argue that wanting immigrants to abide by legal procedures is not an act of racism—even if they are sometimes labeled as such. Designed to clamp down on undocumented immigration, SB 1070 allows law enforcement to question individuals suspected of lacking legal status and requires them to carry immigration documents. Supporters hope the measure will prompt voluntary departure of undocumented immigrants and make job opportunities more accessible for residents. Schwartz, a retired postal worker, cites her granddaughter's job-hunting difficulties as an example of the challenges citizens face. She and her peers, like Martha Payan, believe undocumented immigration strains public resources and affects their neighborhoods. Public figures, including singer Shakira and Phoenix Mayor Phil Gordon, have publicly criticized the new law. Meanwhile, the Mexican government has warned its citizens about potential risks of traveling to Arizona. Schwartz views the law as empowering authorities who previously felt restricted in addressing immigration issues. She draws on the values taught by her Mexican family, who prioritized obeying laws and education, in her support for equal enforcement. Anna Gaines, a teacher-turned-activist originally from Mexico, argues that the immigrant mindset has changed over time, citing a shift from hard work to dependency on government benefits. She believes SB 1070 brings state enforcement in line with existing federal laws. Payan, with Puerto Rican heritage, claims her support for the measure is about respecting the law, not about targeting ethnicities. She hopes the law will deter unauthorized border crossings and has shared personal stories that reinforce her views. Despite facing accusations from within her community, Payan stands by her opinion and continues to voice concerns about the impact of illegal immigration on her life.

Ella y amistades como Martha Payan consideran que la migración irregular presiona los recursos públicos y transforma los barrios. Figuras como la cantante Shakira y el alcalde de Phoenix, Phil Gordon, se han manifestado abiertamente contra la nueva ley. article_content: European Union leaders are gathering in Granada, Spain, with the migrant crisis as a top priority. Hungary and Poland are opposing an agreement within the bloc to change how irregular immigration is managed during times of increased arrivals. The EU aims to pass these changes into law ahead of the next round of elections. Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban told reporters, "There is no agreement on immigration because previously we decided that migration would be regulated by a unanimous agreement, but that was changed at the last meeting. Poland and Hungary were not satisfied with the proposal, but it was pushed through anyway, leaving Hungary and Poland totally out. After this, there is no chance for any compromise or agreement on migration. Politically, it's impossible." Poland’s government has called the deal a 'diktat' from Brussels and Berlin. The Polish prime minister rejected plans to penalize countries like Poland for refusing entry to illegal immigrants. Meanwhile, Italy is reporting a rise in migrant arrivals.

El primer ministro húngaro, Viktor Orban, dijo a los periodistas: “No hay acuerdo sobre inmigración porque antes decidimos que la migración se regularía por unanimidad, pero eso cambió en la última reunión. Polonia y Hungría no estaban satisfechas con la propuesta, pero aun así se aprobó, dejando completamente fuera a Hungría y Polonia. Después de esto, no hay posibilidad de llegar a algún compromiso o acuerdo sobre migración. Políticamente, es imposible”. article_content: Salt Lake City’s mayoral campaign is in full swing, with incumbent Erin Mendenhall seeking re-election against former mayor Rocky Anderson and activist-business owner Michael Valentine. Although the role is officially nonpartisan, the city generally leans Democratic, contrasting with Utah’s broader Republican tilt. At the October 24 debate, which was hosted by KSL, the Hinckley Institute of Politics, and Better Utah, the contenders discussed major issues facing the city, including water conservation, climate change, crime, homelessness, and housing affordability. Anderson, who was mayor from 2000 to 2008, criticized Mendenhall’s handling of rising housing costs and advocated for city-led construction of mixed-income housing, as opposed to relying on private developers. Mendenhall defended her approach, pointing to a 413% increase in the city’s investment in affordable housing and a total of 4,000 new units during her administration — more than all previous administrations combined. Valentine countered that the new housing isn’t truly affordable for most service workers and accused Mendenhall of favoring developers and corporations. Mendenhall dismissed his claims, characterizing them as unfounded conspiracy theories. This election is Salt Lake City's first use of ranked-choice voting, introduced in 2021. Voters rank their preferred candidates, and if no one earns a majority, the candidate with the fewest votes is dropped and voters’ next choices decide the winner.

article_content: MINNEAPOLIS — Federal customs agents stopped an Iowa woman who tried to bring giraffe feces from Kenya into the United States to make jewelry. She declared a small box of the feces when selected for inspection at Minneapolis-Saint Paul Airport on September 29, according to U.S. Customs and Border Protection. The woman, whose name was not released, told officials she planned to make a necklace with the giraffe feces, similar to previous crafts she had made using moose droppings. According to Minnesota Public Radio, giraffe feces can be imported into the U.S. only with the appropriate permits and inspections. The woman will not face penalties since she declared the feces and surrendered them to Customs officials. Customs agriculture specialists subsequently destroyed the giraffe feces. "There is a real danger with bringing fecal matter into the U.S.," said Chicago field Director LaFonda D. Sutton-Burke in a statement. "If this person had entered the U.S. and not declared these items, there was a high possibility of contracting a disease from this jewelry that could lead to serious health issues." Customs cited risks of diseases present in Kenya, including African swine fever, classical swine fever, Newcastle disease, foot-and-mouth disease, and swine vesicular disease.

article_content: After a period of rapid post-pandemic growth, agencies’ earnings have returned to single-digit, pre-pandemic levels, while investments in artificial intelligence have surged—reaching $92 billion in 2022 and between $50 and $60 billion so far in 2023. The next phase of growth for agencies relies on their ability to adapt their business models to fully harness the potential of AI within their processes, capabilities, and organizational structure. Looking ahead to 2024, agencies will need to transform from a services-based approach to one focused on solutions—integrating creativity and technology-based products. This shift will affect all types of agencies, including creative, media, PR, digital, and in-house teams, as they adapt to the combination of human talent and technological advancement. Balancing Automation With Augmentation Traditionally, artificial intelligence has been associated with automation and potential job displacement. Technologies such as robotic process automation, deep learning, computer vision, and intelligent automation have shown the capacity to automate around 25% of agency roles. However, generative AI is poised to enhance and augment employee skill sets, rather than simply replace jobs. According to Forrester’s forecast for the US, more agency roles will benefit from the influence of generative AI, with only 7.5% of roles expected to be automated by the end of the decade. The integration of people and AI platforms will influence how creative industries achieve greater efficiency and effectiveness, as seen in recent Hollywood contract negotiations between the Writers Guild of America and major studios. Agencies should strive to balance the cost efficiencies marketers seek with the expanded creativity that can be achieved when AI supports human talent. B2C Marketers: Act Now on AI The era of AI in agencies is underway, with the use of generative AI moving from experimentation to practical implementation. In 2024, there will be both opportunities and challenges as marketing executives, agency leaders, procurement professionals, and technology providers work together to embrace and commercialize the transformative potential of AI. article_content:
Following the world premiere of her AMC-distributed concert film, 'Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour', 12-time Grammy Award winning artist Taylor Swift returned to Kansas City to attend the Chiefs’ NFL game against the Denver Broncos. Her presence follows a previous appearance at a Chiefs-Jets game, which attracted 27 million viewers, making it the most-watched Sunday Night Football telecast since the Super Bowl.

On the night of the movie's preview screenings—a last-minute addition before its official Friday release—Swift was seen cheering for Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce. A video of her at the game reached 3.2 million views on X (formerly Twitter).

Ticket sales for the Thursday previews are estimated at under $5 million, according to Deadline. AMC has not confirmed the figure, and the estimate reflects the last-minute nature of the previews, which Swift only announced after the film's premiere. Original plans slated the film’s release for Friday at 6 p.m. local time, aligning with Swift’s favorite number, thirteen.

Some insiders have criticized the last-minute previews as potentially disappointing for dedicated fans aiming to be the first to see the film. Nevertheless, the movie is projected to earn over $100 million domestically from 3,850 theaters and an additional $50 million internationally, totaling a potential $150 million global opening weekend.

Analysts caution that early ticket sales are likely to be front-loaded, a pattern typical for movies appealing to younger, largely female audiences. Furthermore, as many of Swift's fans are not regular moviegoers, forecasting box office performance has been difficult.

Swift’s marketing relies heavily on her vast social media following—over 523 million followers by some estimates—and exposure from the NFL. She is reportedly receiving close to 60% of the theatrical box office revenue for the film, a significantly better deal than standard studio contracts, with AMC spending minimally on marketing.

While Swift’s concerts have already grossed $2.2 billion, the film's international release spans more than 90 countries—more than any major studio has previously attempted in a single rollout. Key markets include the US, UK, Mexico, and the Philippines, among others. Early reports suggest strong pre-sales, with about $20 million of the $100 million global pre-sale revenue coming from overseas markets.

Uncertainty remains around international box office tracking and final performance, but Swift’s crossover appeal continues to drive both audience engagement and industry interest.

Tras el estreno mundial de su película-concierto distribuida por AMC, 'Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour', la artista ganadora de 12 premios Grammy regresó a Kansas City para asistir al partido de la NFL entre los Chiefs y los Denver Broncos. Esto se produce después de su reciente aparición en el juego Chiefs-Jets, que atrajo a 27 millones de espectadores, convirtiéndose en la emisión de Sunday Night Football más vista desde el Super Bowl.

La misma noche de las funciones de preestreno de la película—una decisión de último minuto antes del estreno oficial del viernes—Swift fue vista animando al ala cerrada de los Chiefs, Travis Kelce. Un video de ella en el juego superó los 3.2 millones de visualizaciones en X (antes Twitter).

Se estima que la venta de boletos para las funciones de preestreno del jueves fue menor a 5 millones de dólares, según Deadline. AMC no ha confirmado esta cifra, que refleja la naturaleza de último minuto de los preestrenos, los cuales Swift anunció sólo después del estreno. El plan original era estrenar la película el viernes a las 6 p.m., en concordancia con el número favorito de Swift: el trece.

Algunos expertos han criticado los preestrenos de último minuto, diciendo que podrían haber decepcionado a los fanáticos más devotos que buscaban ser los primeros en ver la película. No obstante, se proyecta que el filme recaude más de 100 millones de dólares en Estados Unidos, en 3,850 salas, y 50 millones adicionales a nivel internacional, sumando un posible fin de semana global de 150 millones de dólares.

Analistas anticipan que la venta de boletos será más intensa al inicio, una tendencia habitual en películas dirigidas al público joven y femenino. Además, como muchos fanáticos de Swift no acuden regularmente al cine, prever el desempeño en taquilla ha resultado complicado.

La estrategia de marketing de Swift recae fuertemente en sus más de 523 millones de seguidores en redes sociales y en la exposición mediática que le ha dado la NFL. Se informa que recibirá cerca del 60% de los ingresos de taquilla, un acuerdo mucho más beneficioso que los estándares de la industria, y que AMC invirtió poco en publicidad.

Aunque la gira de Swift ya recaudó 2.2 mil millones de dólares, el estreno internacional de la cinta abarca más de 90 países—más que cualquier otro estudio en un solo lanzamiento. Los mercados clave incluyen EE. UU., Reino Unido, México y Filipinas, entre otros. Reportes iniciales muestran fuertes preventas, con unos 20 millones de los 100 millones en ingresos globales provenientes del extranjero.

Aún existe incertidumbre sobre el seguimiento internacional de taquilla y el resultado final, pero el alcance y atractivo de Swift continúan impulsando el interés del público y la industria.

Finland is introducing new controls at its eastern border. On Friday at midnight, four crossings into Russia—Vaalimaa, Nuijamaa, Niirala, and Imatra—will close, according to Prime Minister Petteri Orpo. This step is being taken in response to a noticeable rise in unauthorized entries, mainly involving migrants from Syria, Yemen, and Iraq. However, Salla and Vartius, two crossings further north, will stay open for those seeking asylum.

Finnish border authorities recorded 75 asylum applications on Wednesday. Officials explain that these migrants typically enter Russia lawfully before making their way toward the Finnish border, where they then request asylum. Prime Minister Orpo has openly accused Russian authorities of orchestrating these crossings by assisting and even escorting migrants to the border.

Similar strategies were seen in 2021 when large numbers of migrants traveled through Belarus, an ally of Russia, before entering EU countries. At that time, the EU accused Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko of trying to create instability by facilitating migrant flows. Notably, Finland's border with Russia is the longest in the European Union, stretching about 1,340 kilometers (833 miles).

A serious accident took place in a chemistry class at Beacon School, a well-known public high school in Manhattan’s Upper West Side. On Thursday just after 9 a.m., chemistry teacher Anna Poole, 31, was performing an experiment for her 10th-grade class when a fireball unexpectedly erupted from the demonstration. With about 30 students in the room, the sudden blast caused panic. Sixteen-year-old Alonzo Yanes was unfortunately caught in the flames, sustaining burns to his face, neck, and chest.

According to witnesses, the fire quickly spread, and student Jeremy Reynoso, 15, recalled the severity of Yanes’ injuries. Another student—a girl whose name was not released—suffered burns to her hands. Emergency responders transported both to Weill Cornell Medical Center. Officials described the injuries as non-life threatening; Yanes received second-degree burns and potential airway damage, while the girl was treated for first-degree burns on her hands.

Teacher Michael Shum responded by using a blanket to extinguish the flames engulfing Yanes. 

Authorities, including the Fire Department and Department of Education, are investigating what led to the accident. It is not yet clear whether safety goggles were being worn. The incident occurred on the first day back from the holiday break.

article_content: A Delhi court has granted bail to Harvinder Singh, accused of participating in an illegal visa racket, stating that his continued custody was unnecessary. Singh, arrested on October 12, allegedly charged large sums to help individuals obtain visas for various countries. Investigators reported recovering 46 Bangladeshi passports, a Nepalese passport, 40 stamps from various banks, and 19 blank Bangladeshi stamp papers—along with other documents—from Singh's home. Authorities are also investigating 'Bangladeshi agents' named by Singh. On November 9, Metropolitan Magistrate Devanshu Sajlan granted bail, citing the recovery of crucial evidence, Singh's lack of prior criminal record, and the low risk of him influencing witnesses. The court also noted that statements from alleged victims had not been taken, despite a month passing since the investigation began. Additionally, other co-accused in similar circumstances have not been arrested. Singh's counsel emphasized his clean criminal history and that he is the sole provider for his family, including his autistic daughter.

Las autoridades también investigan a 'agentes bangladesíes' mencionados por Singh. El 9 de noviembre, el Magistrado Metropolitano Devanshu Sajlan le concedió la fianza, señalando la recuperación de pruebas clave, la ausencia de antecedentes penales de Singh y el bajo riesgo de que influya en los testigos. article_content: Roland Griffiths was a pioneering scientist whose research revealed the potential of psychedelics—specifically psilocybin—to ease depression and anxiety in people facing terminal illness. On the interviewer’s desk sits a small, personal collection: six smooth stones gathered from beach trips, reminders that life’s challenges are fleeting, and change is constant. Atop them rests a gold-plated medallion, inscribed with 'Meditation' and the quote: 'The true method of knowledge is experiment,' by William Blake. On the reverse, mushrooms are engraved alongside a blessing: 'May you remain aware of awareness.' The medallion was a gift from Griffiths, whose insights left a lasting impression. In April, the interviewer spoke with Griffiths, who had spent the last phase of his distinguished career at Johns Hopkins University researching how psychedelics like psilocybin could help patients struggling with depression, addiction, and even terminal cancer. Two years prior, Griffiths himself had been diagnosed with stage 4 colon cancer. The scientist became the patient, confronting his own mortality. Their conversation profoundly affected the interviewer—not only inspiring a deeper commitment to meditation, a practice Griffiths credited with helping him approach the end of life peacefully, but also in recognizing how Griffiths accepted his prognosis without fear. In September, the interviewer reached out to share the personal benefits meditation had provided. Griffiths encouraged them to keep practicing, emphasizing how thoughts and feelings can pass if allowed, rather than define one’s identity. Roland Griffiths died on October 16 at age 77. The medallion atop the stones is a reminder: impermanence defines existence. While we cannot control when or how we depart, we choose how to live until then. Earlier this year, Griffiths explained psilocybin in layman's terms: it is a classic psychedelic from certain mushrooms, used by indigenous cultures over centuries for ceremonies and healing. Its effects emerge quickly and last shorter than LSD or mescaline. Griffiths avoided the term 'trips' because of its connotations, focusing instead on psilocybin’s therapeutic use. Their first clinical trial at Johns Hopkins specifically looked at cancer patient volunteers. Results were remarkable: after a single dose of psilocybin under controlled conditions, participants with depression and anxiety showed immediate, substantial, and enduring improvement—lasting at least six months. Patients described losing fear and finding acceptance. Griffiths shared the story of one man who, after his experience, found a profound sense of reassurance and acceptance regarding his condition, which comforted both him and his loved ones. Discussing the language around such spiritual or existential experiences, Griffiths emphasized that people often use words like 'God' to express ineffable feelings because science cannot yet fully explain consciousness or awareness. After facing his own diagnosis, Griffiths called the experience a 'call to celebration,' sharing that he and his wife aimed to live with openness, even amidst treatments and uncertainty. Initially hesitant to try psychedelics after his diagnosis out of concern for his mental clarity, Griffiths eventually tried LSD. During the experience, he imagined speaking to his cancer, expressing gratitude for insights gained, and asking for more time. While he did not receive a direct answer, the experience affirmed his path and encouraged him to share his journey more publicly. Griffiths’ parting message: celebrate the miracle of life and embrace each moment fully—no terminal diagnosis required.

En el escritorio de la entrevistadora hay una pequeña colección personal: seis piedras lisas recogidas en viajes a la playa, recordatorios de que los desafíos de la vida son pasajeros y el cambio es constante. En abril, la entrevistadora conversó con Griffiths, quien dedicó la última etapa de su distinguida carrera en la Universidad Johns Hopkins a investigar cómo los psicodélicos como la psilocibina podían ayudar a pacientes con depresión, adicción e incluso cáncer terminal. Dos años antes, Griffiths fue diagnosticado con cáncer de colon en etapa 4. El científico se convirtió en paciente, enfrentando su propia mortalidad. La conversación impactó profundamente a la entrevistadora—no solo inspirando un compromiso más profundo con la meditación, práctica que Griffiths atribuía a su paz al aproximarse al final de la vida, sino también al observar cómo él aceptaba su pronóstico sin miedo. Su primer ensayo clínico en Johns Hopkins se centró en voluntarios con cáncer. Los pacientes describieron perder el miedo y encontrar aceptación. Griffiths compartió la historia de un hombre que, tras su experiencia, halló un profundo sentido de tranquilidad y aceptación respecto a su condición, lo que reconfortó tanto a él como a sus seres queridos. Al hablar sobre el lenguaje que rodea estas experiencias espirituales o existenciales, Griffiths enfatizó que las personas suelen usar palabras como 'Dios' para expresar sentimientos inexplicables, ya que la ciencia aún no puede explicar totalmente la consciencia o la percepción. Enfrentando su propio diagnóstico, Griffiths lo llamó una 'invitación a la celebración,' compartiendo que él y su esposa intentaron vivir con apertura, incluso durante los tratamientos y la incertidumbre. Inicialmente dudoso de usar psicodélicos después de su diagnóstico por temor a alterar su claridad mental, Griffiths finalmente probó LSD. Durante la experiencia, imaginó dialogar con su cáncer, expresando gratitud por lo aprendido y pidiendo más tiempo. Aunque no recibió una respuesta directa, la vivencia confirmó su camino y lo motivó a compartir públicamente su experiencia. El mensaje final de Griffiths: celebra el milagro de la vida y disfruta cada momento a plenitud—no hace falta un diagnóstico terminal para hacerlo.

article_content: Fernando Alonso is reportedly being sought by McLaren for a potential return to the team, despite a well-documented fallout with chairman Ron Dennis in 2007. According to sources close to the discussions, recent meetings have taken place regarding Alonso's future. Although tension lingered from their previous collaboration, it appears McLaren is interested in acquiring a high-profile driver, and their forthcoming partnership with Honda (beginning next year) could make the team an attractive option for Alonso, especially as he continues to struggle at Ferrari. The arrival of Eric Boullier as the team's new de facto principal, someone uninvolved with past controversies, further supports the prospect of Alonso joining. Speculation was fueled this week by comments from Alonso, who remarked on the contrast between praise from outsiders and criticism from those close to him, stating: 'It is sometimes strange to see good comments and compliments from people outside the team, and the opposite from people who are supposed to be close to you. It's motivating for me and funny when you see the opposite from your closest friends.' Ferrari president Luca di Montezemolo responded by publicly affirming Alonso’s value, calling him 'the best driver in the world, who always gives 200 percent in the races.' While Alonso may still stay with Ferrari, a move to McLaren remains likely. Meanwhile, McLaren drivers Jenson Button and Kevin Magnussen have faced a tough 2014 season. Off the track, there's a growing movement in Europe to ban all alcohol advertising in sports, echoing previous bans on tobacco sponsorship. France has already introduced such legislation, leading to renaming of sporting events and teams (for example, the Heineken Cup is known as the H Cup in France). Experts anticipate other countries will follow, possibly culminating in a European Union-wide ban. The Labour Party has included a potential ban in their draft manifesto for the upcoming general election. This development threatens lucrative sponsorship deals in British sports—including Williams’ partnership with Martini, Force India’s with Smirnoff, and McLaren’s with Johnnie Walker. Collectively, alcohol advertising brings approximately £300 million into British sport, impacting entities such as the FA Cup (Budweiser), the Grand National (Crabbie’s), and Everton FC (Chang Beer). Dr. Kerry O'Brien, head of behavioral studies at Monash University, argues the ban is warranted due to links between alcohol sponsorship and increased risk of problem drinking, particularly among youth. He notes that Formula 1, while a leader in safety, sends mixed messages by promoting alcohol brands, given alcohol's role in road fatalities. Despite such arguments, the author questions the effectiveness and fairness of a ban, suggesting people should have the freedom to make their own purchasing choices and warning of the slippery slope of expanding legislation. On the competitive front, Lewis Hamilton currently leads Nico Rosberg by three points in the drivers’ championship. Hamilton stated this week that he feels 'hungrier' for success because, unlike Rosberg, he did not grow up privileged. The author reflects that Hamilton’s resilient 'us against the world' mentality, shaped by his family's modest beginnings, has contributed to his success. Lastly, after returning to the Monaco track, the author describes the impact of Formula One’s new, quieter engine noise: while the dramatic sound is reduced, spectators are no longer deafened, leading to mixed feelings among fans and participants alike.

article_content: Jungle gyms, a classic feature of American playgrounds since the 1970s, have a surprisingly mathematical origin. The story begins with Charles Hinton, a British mathematician from the late 1800s who was fascinated by the fourth dimension and eager to make advanced concepts accessible to children. While known for science fiction stories and inventive gadgets like a gunpowder-powered pitching machine, Hinton also tried to teach his children spatial reasoning. Hinton believed that if children had more experience moving through three-dimensional space, they would better understand complex concepts like the fourth dimension. In pursuit of this, he built stacked bamboo cubes marked with X, Y, and Z coordinates, encouraging his children to locate specific points as a game. While the math games didn’t capture their interest, the climbing did. Years later, Hinton’s son Sebastian remembered the fun of climbing and swinging on the cubes and sought to recreate that experience. Living in Winnetka, Illinois, and working as a patent lawyer in the early 1920s, Sebastian described his idea at a dinner party attended by local educators associated with John Dewey’s philosophy of holistic education. The educators quickly saw its value and suggested building it in schools. Sebastian Hinton went on to patent his climbing structure, calling it a 'jungle gym.' Sadly, Sebastian died in April 1923, six months before the U.S. Patent Office approved his invention. The first real model is preserved today at the Winnetka Historical Society, though climbing on it is no longer allowed. The structure’s lasting popularity is attributed to its ability to foster risk-taking, creativity, and physical development among children. Experts like Ellen Sandseter emphasize that the jungle gym’s minimal design allows children to play in various ways, helping develop motor skills, self-confidence, and imagination—qualities that many modern toys lack due to their prescriptive nature. The term 'monkey bars' appears in Hinton’s patent, comparing children’s play to monkeys swinging through the treetops, though technically the motion resembles ape behavior. Despite changing materials and safety standards over the last century—which have made playgrounds safer with softer surfaces and rounded edges—the essential, open-ended nature of the jungle gym remains beloved by generations, inviting kids to dream, explore, and perhaps even ponder new dimensions.

Además de escribir relatos de ciencia ficción y crear artefactos como una máquina lanzapelotas de béisbol a pólvora, Hinton intentó enseñar razonamiento espacial a sus hijos. Hinton creía que los niños podrían entender mejor conceptos complejos como la cuarta dimensión si experimentaban más el espacio tridimensional. Por eso, construyó cubos de bambú apilados y marcados con coordenadas X, Y y Z, animando a sus hijos a encontrar puntos concretos como parte de un juego. Aunque los juegos de matemática no les resultaron tan divertidos, trepar sí. article_content: At Lebanon’s border with Israel, residents of the Christian village of Rmeich hope that war can be avoided, even as they prepare for the possibility of increasing hostilities between the Lebanese Shia group Hezbollah and Israel. Situated just a couple of kilometers from the frontier, Rmeich has already suffered the effects of three weeks of clashes between Israel and Hezbollah, which is supported by Iran and is the dominant force in southern Lebanon. Along with the rest of Lebanon, the village is feeling the impact of the conflict taking place around 200km (124 miles) away between Israel and the Palestinian group Hamas, an ally of Hezbollah. Those remaining in Rmeich seem reluctant to discuss the political crisis that has brought conflict so close, and try to maintain normal life in the village, where an 18th-century church still holds mass three times a day. 'I won’t say we’re feeling safe, but the situation is stable,' said village priest Toni Elias, 40, as a military drone buzzed overhead. 'If we don’t hear the drone, we think something odd is going on. We’re used to it every day, 24/7,' Elias added.

Ubicada a solo un par de kilómetros de la frontera, Rmeich ya ha sufrido los efectos de tres semanas de enfrentamientos entre Israel y Hezbolá, que cuenta con el apoyo de Irán y es la fuerza dominante en el sur de Líbano. 'No diré que nos sentimos seguros, pero la situación es estable', dijo el sacerdote del pueblo, Toni Elias, de 40 años, mientras un dron militar zumbaba sobre sus cabezas. 'Si no escuchamos el dron, pensamos que algo extraño está pasando. Ya estamos acostumbrados a eso todos los días, las 24 horas', añadió Elias.

article_content: The foreign ministers of South Korea, Japan, and China are set to hold their first trilateral meeting since 2019 this weekend in Busan, according to South Korea's foreign ministry on Friday. The meeting, scheduled for Sunday in the southern port city, will bring together Park Jin, Yoko Kamikawa, and Wang Yi amid concerns from Beijing about Tokyo and Seoul's strengthening security ties with the United States. This announcement comes shortly after North Korea successfully launched its first military spy satellite into orbit, an event that led to the suspension of a five-year-old military agreement between the two Koreas aimed at reducing tensions on the Korean Peninsula. Earlier this month, US Secretary of State Antony Blinken warned that military ties between North Korea and Russia were 'growing and dangerous', urging China—North Korea's main ally—to restrain the nuclear-armed North. The upcoming talks will see the foreign ministers exchange views on the future of trilateral cooperation as well as regional and international issues, according to a statement from Seoul's foreign ministry. The top diplomats also intend to lay the groundwork for a future trilateral summit involving the leaders of South Korea, Japan, and China.

La reunión, prevista para el domingo en la ciudad portuaria del sur, reunirá a Park Jin, Yoko Kamikawa y Wang Yi en medio de preocupaciones de Pekín por el fortalecimiento de los lazos de seguridad de Tokio y Seúl con Estados Unidos. Este anuncio llega poco después de que Corea del Norte lanzara con éxito su primer satélite espía militar en órbita, un hecho que llevó a la suspensión de un acuerdo militar de cinco años entre las dos Coreas destinado a reducir tensiones en la península coreana. A principios de este mes, el secretario de Estado de EE.UU., Antony Blinken, advirtió que los lazos militares entre Corea del Norte y Rusia estaban 'creciendo y siendo peligrosos', e instó a China—principal aliado de Corea del Norte—a contener al Norte, que posee armas nucleares. Según un comunicado del ministerio surcoreano, en las próximas conversaciones, los ministros de Asuntos Exteriores intercambiarán opiniones sobre el futuro de la cooperación trilateral, así como sobre asuntos regionales e internacionales. Los principales diplomáticos también tienen la intención de sentar las bases para una futura cumbre trilateral entre los líderes de Corea del Sur, Japón y China.

article_content: Ukrainian energy workers are inspecting new power lines in Kyiv, replacing those destroyed months ago. Officials reported that Russia has attacked Ukraine's energy infrastructure about 60 times in the past several weeks as winter approaches and energy consumption increases. Ukraine fears that Russia may be launching another concerted campaign against its power grid this winter, similar to last year when drone and missile attacks caused widespread blackouts. Energy Minister German Galushchenko, currently visiting the United States, said the government is discussing with partners how to get through the critical cold months. Western countries have increased supplies of air defenses to help counter the threats. The energy ministry noted that energy infrastructure facilities were attacked 60 times recently with various types of weapons, and each attack increases the need for new energy equipment, making international aid crucial. Although Ukraine has improved air defenses this winter, its energy system remains vulnerable due to lasting damage from previous attacks. Ukraine’s military intelligence says Russia has stockpiled hundreds of missiles for a winter air campaign. A recent government statement said that a thermal power station in eastern Ukraine was shelled on Tuesday evening. Electricity distribution networks in the Donetsk, Kharkiv, and Kherson regions were also damaged by Russian shelling. The energy ministry also reported damage to natural gas distribution networks in the Dnipropetrovsk region. While these attacks have not caused nationwide blackouts so far, government officials are concerned the situation could worsen as winter sets in. Ukrenergo reported that power consumption is rising as temperatures drop, with a 2.5°C decrease leading to a 1.5% increase in consumption. Ukraine has experienced unseasonably warm weather this autumn, with temperatures around 10°C. However, Ukrenergo said 431 settlements currently lack electricity because of ongoing combat. article_content: Islamic clerics have condemned the recent conflict among a group of Imams in Inisa town, Odo-Otin Local Government Area of Osun State, which reportedly led to the death of two of the five contenders for the community’s Central Mosque Imam position. In a live Facebook video on Tuesday, the Grand Mufti of Yorubaland, Sheik Dawood Molaasan, described how the Imam selection crisis started in 2020, leading to the mosque’s closure. Sheik Molaasan stated that the dispute split the community’s Islamic groups, with tensions escalating due to the involvement of the king, Olunisa of Inisa, Oba Joseph Oladunjoye Oyedele (JP) Fasikun II, who allegedly favored a candidate for the Imam position, despite being a Christian. Islamic philanthropists and the Aare Musulumi (Muslim leader) of Inisa agreed to select a candidate with strong Islamic knowledge, but the king reportedly supported another contender, who was not as experienced and had a pending court case. The league of Inisa’s Islamic clerics chose a candidate with Arabic education in Saudi Arabia and over 20 years’ experience as an Imam in Canada and Osogbo. Though he did not seek the post, the clerics invited him to oversee the mosque. Molaasan emphasized that the king’s favored candidate was less qualified for the Imam position, and called for a competence examination between the contenders instead of voting or external selection, following traditions attributed to Prophet Mohammad (SAW). He also urged the Osun State Government to appoint a temporary prayer leader while the community selects a new Imam. Reacting in a video shared on X (formerly Twitter), Sheikh Hamad Labeeb from Ilorin criticized the mosque’s closure, stating the conflict should have been resolved diplomatically. He called for unity and pledged to lead Friday prayers in defiance of threats. The President of the League of Imams and Alfas in Yorubaland, Edo, and Delta states, Sheikh Jamiu Bello (represented by Sheikh Iskeel Lawal), clarified that the courtroom ordered the mosque’s closure, not Muslim elders. He called on the state governor, Ademola Adeleke, to resolve the crisis so communal worship could resume. The Osun State Government had previously shut the mosque in 2021 following violence and a loss of life. According to a statement from then Deputy Chief of Staff, Mr. Abdullahi Binuyo, the government later reopened the mosque after a peaceful settlement. The government expressed hope that the community would maintain peace and unity following the mosque’s reopening.

Over the past few weeks, UNest—a startup that helps individuals save for significant life expenses such as college, weddings, and home down payments—has experienced considerable internal upheaval. As previously reported by Insider, founder and CEO Ksenia Yudina resigned last month, warning that the company was 'insolvent.' She also accused certain board members of orchestrating a hostile takeover of the struggling business, which she described—per Insider’s reporting—as 'illegal and unethical.'

This marks a dramatic fall for what was once a highly regarded fintech startup that raised nearly $40 million from prominent investors, including Artemis Fund, Anthos Capital, Franklin Templeton, and Northwestern Mutual. UNest also enlisted celebrities such as NBA All-Star Baron Davis and actress Laura Dern as brand ambassadors.

Beyond the potential investor losses, UNest’s challenges have raised concerns among its customers, who have trusted the company with their savings. Here’s what clients should know.

Is my money safe?
Yes. 'The financial health of UNest does not impact the security and status of any client funds,' Michael Doniger, the company’s Chief Operating Officer, told Insider. 'All client deposits and investments remain secure and continue to be invested in the existing portfolio options, which include investments in Vanguard and Blackrock ETFs.'

Where is my money being held?
According to UNest’s terms and conditions, client accounts are not held directly by the company. Instead, they are managed by Apex Clearing Corporation, which also provides backend trading and clearing for platforms like Robinhood and SoFi.

Why is UNest in trouble?
The exact causes of UNest’s struggles are unclear. However, many financial technology startups have been affected over the past two years by declining venture funding and rising interest rates. More broadly, some venture capitalists warn of a 'mass extinction event' for startups as funding becomes scarce and companies find it more difficult to be acquired or go public. According to Crunchbase, over 500 startups have shut down this year alone.

What’s next for UNest?
No official announcements have been made, but Doniger says UNest has signed a term sheet with a new investor to continue operations. 'The board, remaining management, and investors are closely collaborating to secure additional funding for the company,' he stated. 'The new partner brings an experienced team of entrepreneurs and fintech leaders who will help UNest move forward.'

If you have more information about UNest or other struggling startups, contact reporter Ben Bergman at bbergman@insider.com.

article_content: In a major development, Egypt announced a new arrangement enabling 200 trucks of humanitarian aid, 130,000 litres of diesel, and four gas trucks to enter Gaza daily during a brief ceasefire beginning at 7 a.m. local time on Friday, according to The Times of Israel. This widely anticipated deal involves the phased release of 50 Israeli hostages—mostly women and children—by Hamas over four days, in exchange for Israel releasing 150 Palestinian prisoners. Egypt and Qatar facilitated the negotiation after Hamas and other groups abducted 240 individuals in an October 7 assault in southern Israel, which resulted in around 1,200 civilian deaths. Under the agreement, each day of the four-day truce will see groups of hostages released. The first group, scheduled for release on Friday afternoon, will include 13 women and children, The Times of Israel reported. Majed Al-Ansari, spokesperson for Qatar’s foreign ministry, confirmed the release plan, withholding details about the hostages and their exit for security. According to CNN, it is expected that the first 50 hostages will be released through Egypt. On Thursday, the Palestine Red Crescent Society reported that 80 trucks carrying food, water, medical aid, and other necessities reached Gaza from Egypt via the Rafah crossing. An even larger convoy is positioned to enter as soon as the truce takes effect, a source shared with CNN. Fuel began entering Gaza again after Israel’s war cabinet approved regular fuel shipments on November 18, mainly to keep southern desalination plants operational, with United States and Egyptian oversight. Previously, Israel’s policy allowed two daily fuel tankers to support Gaza’s water and sewage systems, after discussions with Israeli military and security authorities, and measures were taken to prevent use by Hamas. Officials explained the policy as a means to prevent public health crises during the ongoing humanitarian emergency in Gaza. Yet, as of Thursday, only 80 humanitarian aid trucks entered Gaza at Rafah, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs—well under the pre-conflict daily average of 500, and often below the UN’s 100-truck target since October 21. Although the US and other mediators advocate over 100 trucks daily to address dire needs, Israel has now agreed to 200 daily aid trucks during the truce. However, US sources told The Times of Israel the current delivery framework is not yet meeting this goal. Alongside the aid shipments, 75,000 litres of fuel entered Gaza from Egypt on Thursday, consistent with Israel’s commitment to regular deliveries. The fuel will help power food distribution, hospitals, water, and sanitation services, as noted by UNOCHA. Fuel issues have been a focal point in recent talks, with US Secretary of State Antony Blinken in discussions in Tel Aviv this month. Israel’s approval for increased fuel came after substantial US pressure, according to CNN.
