Este esperado acuerdo prevé la liberación gradual de 50 rehenes israelíes—en su mayoría mujeres y niños—por parte de Hamás en el transcurso de cuatro días, a cambio de que Israel libere a 150 prisioneros palestinos. Según el acuerdo, cada día de la tregua de cuatro días se liberarán grupos de rehenes. El primer grupo, previsto para su liberación la tarde del viernes, incluirá a 13 mujeres y niños, informó The Times of Israel. Majed Al-Ansari, portavoz del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Catar, confirmó el plan de liberación, pero reservó los detalles sobre los rehenes y su salida por razones de seguridad. Según CNN, se espera que los primeros 50 rehenes sean liberados a través de Egipto. El jueves, la Sociedad de la Media Luna Roja Palestina reportó que 80 camiones con alimentos, agua, insumos médicos y otras necesidades ingresaron a Gaza desde Egipto a través del cruce de Rafah. Una caravana aún más grande está lista para entrar en cuanto comience la tregua, compartió una fuente con CNN. El ingreso de combustible a Gaza se reanudó después de que el gabinete de guerra de Israel aprobara envíos regulares de combustible el 18 de noviembre, principalmente para mantener en funcionamiento las plantas desalinizadoras del sur, con supervisión de Estados Unidos y Egipto. Anteriormente, la política de Israel permitía diariamente dos camiones cisterna de combustible para respaldar los sistemas de agua y saneamiento de Gaza, tras diálogos con autoridades militares y de seguridad israelíes, y se implementaron medidas para evitar que Hamás desviase el combustible. Funcionarios explicaron que esta política busca prevenir crisis de salud pública durante la emergencia humanitaria en Gaza. Sin embargo, hasta el jueves, solo 80 camiones de ayuda humanitaria ingresaron a Gaza por Rafah, según la Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios—muy por debajo del promedio diario de 500 antes del conflicto y frecuentemente bajo el objetivo de 100 camiones diarios establecido por la ONU desde el 21 de octubre. Aunque Estados Unidos y otros mediadores piden más de 100 camiones diarios para cubrir necesidades urgentes, Israel ahora aceptó permitir 200 camiones diarios de ayuda durante la tregua. Sin embargo, fuentes estadounidenses dijeron a The Times of Israel que el marco actual de entregas aún no cumple con esa meta. Junto con los envíos de ayuda, el jueves ingresaron a Gaza desde Egipto 75,000 litros de combustible, en línea con el compromiso de Israel de entregas regulares. Según UNOCHA, este combustible contribuirá a la distribución de alimentos, hospitales, agua y servicios de saneamiento. El tema del combustible ha sido central en discusiones recientes, con el Secretario de Estado de EE.UU., Antony Blinken, participando en conversaciones en Tel Aviv este mes. La aprobación de Israel para aumentar el ingreso de combustible vino tras fuertes presiones estadounidenses, según CNN.

article_content: In 2006, a powerful tornado struck Hendersonville, North Carolina. Amy Hawkins bravely shielded her two sons, Jair and Cole, in their basement as debris fell around them—saving both boys, but suffering devastating spinal injuries herself that left her paralyzed from the waist down. Her husband Jerrod, a firefighter, was at work during the storm and could only witness the destruction from his station. Amy has lived in a wheelchair ever since, often managing pain and tingling in her lower body. With help from ABC's Extreme Makeover: Home Edition, her home was updated for better accessibility. Now, after a delay due to pneumonia, Amy is in California for surgery aimed at restoring her ability to walk. She remains hopeful, drawing strength from her determination to one day walk again and her commitment to her family.

Su esposo Jerrod, bombero, estaba de servicio durante la tormenta y solo pudo observar la destrucción desde la estación de bomberos. Desde entonces, Amy ha requerido una silla de ruedas y a menudo enfrenta dolor y hormigueo en la parte baja de su cuerpo. Gracias al programa Extreme Makeover: Home Edition de ABC, su hogar fue renovado para ser más accesible. Ahora, tras retrasar su cirugía por neumonía, Amy está en California para una operación que busca darle la posibilidad de volver a caminar. Ella sigue esperanzada, motivada por el sueño de caminar de nuevo y su compromiso con su familia.

article_content: Apple is reportedly finalizing the design for a new super-thin smartphone, informally called the 'iPhone Air,' which may launch later this year, according to various leaks and concept renders by independent designers. Concept images and unverified schematics have surfaced online, including visuals by a French tech site working with a 3D artist, showing the potential appearance of the device. The rumored iPhone is expected to feature larger screen options, with speculation about 4-inch, 4.7-inch, and possibly 5.5 or 5.7-inch models. Designers Martin Hajek, Enrico Penello, and Ran Avni have produced concept images that highlight features such as a curved glass screen, illuminated Touch ID sensor, and a thin body with rounded edges. Japanese magazine MacFan and tech outlets like MacRumours have published alleged schematics showing possible 4.7-inch and 5.7-inch models, featuring a bezel-free design and rectangular volume controls similar to the iPhone 5c. Apple has not made any official statements regarding these rumors or the device's specifications. Speculation also suggests the iPhone 6 could feature improved camera technology, potentially upgrading to a 10-megapixel sensor with a new lens and a resin filter possibly supplied by Japanese company JSR. Other rumors suggest the device may be offered in colors such as white and gold. Some design concepts propose removing the physical home button in favor of touchscreen controls to create a slimmer profile, while other concepts retain the home button by varying the phone's thickness. Apple's previous releases, like the iPad Air, have emphasized thinner and lighter devices. Among current smartphones, the Huawei Ascend P6 (6.18mm) and Vivo X3 (5.75mm) are among the thinnest, while Apple's iPhone 5S measures 7.6mm in thickness. Chinese analyst Sun Changxu has suggested that Apple could release new models shortly after their announcement, possibly at Apple's annual developer conference. Industry experts have noted that Apple may increase screen sizes to compete with larger-screen phones from companies like Samsung and HTC. It is important to note that these details are based on unconfirmed rumors and concept images, and no official information has been released by Apple.

article_content: The Occupy Wall Street movement, which began in New York in September, has expanded to major cities worldwide as a protest against wealth inequality. Here's a summary of some recent developments: NEW YORK: Zuccotti Park was mostly empty early Wednesday, following police in riot gear clearing protesters and a state supreme court ruling allowing demonstrators to return, but not to camp overnight. A few people lingered in the park, observed by the New York Police Department, which maintained an overnight presence. The park is open 24 hours, with people permitted to walk through or sit, but not sleep there. For nearly two months, this Lower Manhattan site had been a home base for protesters, and New York's movement inspired similar demonstrations globally. DALLAS: City attorneys met with Occupy Dallas representatives Wednesday after a federal judge denied their request to prevent eviction from City Hall property. U.S. District Judge Jane Boyle’s decision enables the city to remove the camp, although Mayor Mike Rawlings said action would not happen before Wednesday. Early that day, about 200 protesters remained, with participant Raymond Sanford citing the First Amendment as justification for staying. SEATTLE: Police used pepper spray and arrested at least six people Tuesday night following clashes with demonstrators who stayed in city streets after being asked to leave. Protesters marched from Seattle Central Community College to downtown Belltown and blocked traffic. A 17-year-old reportedly swung a stick at an officer and was arrested after officers, hindered by the crowd, used pepper spray to disperse people and make the arrest. Protesters later staged a sit-in at another intersection, which led to another use of pepper spray. According to Occupy Seattle, those affected included an 84-year-old woman, a priest, and a pregnant woman. SAN FRANCISCO: Thousands of students and protesters gathered Tuesday at UC Berkeley for a general strike featuring teach-ins, marches, and an assembly where Occupy Cal protesters set up tents in Sproul Plaza. Last week, police removed tents and arrested 40 people. The university's chancellor indicated on Tuesday that some tents might be allowed as political expression. TORONTO: Protesters in Toronto obtained a court injunction Tuesday against a city eviction notice, allowing them to stay at St. James Park for now. Judge David Brown said more information was needed before making a final ruling. In Calgary, protesters faced a Wednesday deadline to vacate Olympic Plaza after receiving eviction notices. The City of Victoria has also sought an injunction to remove tents from Centennial Square, but the hearing was postponed until Thursday, giving demonstrators more time to respond. LONDON: On Wednesday, London authorities ordered protesters to clear their tents and belongings from beside St. Paul’s Cathedral within 24 hours or face High Court proceedings. The City of London Corporation, which runs the area, paused legal action earlier to negotiate with activists, but after talks broke down, it resumed proceedings. Policy chairman Stuart Fraser said legal action is necessary for roadway safety and business needs. St. Paul’s Cathedral had suspended its own legal case but recognized the authorities' right to act and stated staff would continue meeting with protesters.

SAN FRANCISCO: Miles de estudiantes y manifestantes se reunieron el martes en UC Berkeley para una huelga general con talleres, marchas y una asamblea en la que Occupy Cal volvió a instalar tiendas de campaña en Sproul Plaza. La semana pasada, la policía retiró tiendas y arrestó a 40 personas. El rector de la universidad indicó el martes que algunas tiendas podrían permitirse como expresión política. TORONTO: Manifestantes en Toronto obtuvieron una orden judicial el martes que les permite permanecer temporalmente en St. James Park tras una notificación de desalojo por parte de la ciudad. El juez David Brown pidió más información antes de tomar una decisión final. En Calgary, los manifestantes debían abandonar Olympic Plaza antes del miércoles tras recibir avisos de desalojo. La ciudad de Victoria también buscó una orden para quitar tiendas de Centennial Square, pero la audiencia se pospuso hasta el jueves para dar más tiempo a los manifestantes. LONDRES: El miércoles, autoridades de Londres ordenaron a los manifestantes retirar sus tiendas y pertenencias alrededor de la Catedral de St. Paul en un plazo de 24 horas o se enfrentarán a acciones legales. La City of London Corporation, que administra la zona, había pausado un proceso judicial para negociar, pero al no llegar a acuerdos reanudó los procedimientos. El presidente de políticas, Stuart Fraser, indicó que la acción legal se debe a motivos de seguridad y necesidades comerciales. La Catedral suspendió su propio litigio, pero reconoció el derecho de las autoridades a actuar y afirmó que el personal seguirá reuniéndose con los manifestantes.

article_content: Women hoping to conceive may want to add Brussels sprouts to their regular diet, according to an expert. While many people recall Brussels sprouts as a bitter and overcooked school meal, recent discussions suggest these vegetables could benefit couples trying to have a baby. Studies indicate that nine percent of all conceptions happen during December, making it the most fertile month of the year—a trend attributed partly to seasonal celebrations. Neema Savvides, a nutritional therapist at the Harley Street Fertility Clinic, believes the increased consumption of Brussels sprouts during the festive season could play a role. Savvides describes Brussels sprouts as a 'baby-making superfood' because they are rich in folic acid, which is important for fertility in both men and women. This vitamin can help boost sperm count and provide essential nutrients to help prepare the womb, potentially increasing the chance of successful conception. Additionally, adequate folic acid intake may reduce the risk of miscarriages and birth defects. Brussels sprouts contain a phytonutrient called di-indolylmethane, which helps the body maintain balanced estrogen levels by binding to environmental estrogens—such as those found in pesticides and certain animal products—and assisting in their removal. This, in turn, may support fertility. The nutritious vegetable may also help lower cholesterol and has anti-inflammatory effects. While these benefits are supported by some scientific research on nutrients found in Brussels sprouts, direct links to nationwide conception rates remain the subject of ongoing discussion.

India’s government anticipates surpassing its tax revenue targets in the current fiscal year, affording Prime Minister Narendra Modi additional fiscal space as national elections approach in 2024. According to Bloomberg Economics, the government’s receipts may exceed projections by approximately 1.9 trillion rupees (about $22.8 billion) by March 2024, amounting to roughly 0.6% of GDP. Similarly, Standard Chartered Bank expects a surplus of 0.2% to 0.3% of GDP.

This revenue boost enables the Modi government to expand or launch voter-oriented welfare initiatives. Modi recently announced that a widely-used free food distribution program—delivering monthly grain rations to 800 million citizens—would be extended another five years. Additional measures include higher subsidies for cooking gas and fertilizers and potential support for low-income groups, such as more direct payments to small farmers and some mortgage subsidies.

The increase in government funds is attributed to strong tax collections and larger profit transfers from the central bank. Between April and early October, direct tax revenue rose 18% year-on-year, as per the Finance Ministry.

Bloomberg Economics’ Abhishek Gupta expects most of the surplus to go toward rural support, with the latest spending commitments totaling about 900 billion rupees and around 1 trillion rupees remaining for other uses. Government sources emphasize these maneuverings won’t push the country’s fiscal deficit beyond the 5.9% of GDP target. Nomura suggests short-term economic effects from welfare expansions should be modest, but points to possible longer-term risks. According to Standard Chartered economists, more targeted subsidies have kept fiscal pressures manageable.

In corporate developments, Tata Group sealed a $750 million deal to acquire Wistron’s manufacturing facility, making it the first Indian company to assemble iPhones. In higher education, India has become the most represented nation in the QS Asia University Rankings for 2024, overtaking China. On the corporate front, Religare Enterprises’ independent directors have raised allegations of fraud in response to a takeover bid by the Burman family, bringing the issue to financial regulators.

article_content: Governments in the region that have formed closer ties with Israel are under pressure amid the ongoing war in Gaza. Bahrain confirmed it recalled its ambassador from Israel, as the intensifying conflict in Gaza challenges the policies of states seeking stronger relations with Israel. After a statement from Bahrain’s lower house of parliament, the government announced on Thursday that its ambassador was returning and that Israel’s ambassador in Manama had left 'some time ago.' The advisory parliamentary body, which does not have foreign policy powers, stated earlier that economic ties with Israel had been severed. However, Israel says its relationship with Bahrain remains 'stable.' The Bahraini government’s statement did not mention ending economic relations but confirmed flights between the two countries have been temporarily suspended. This decision comes after weeks of protests across the Middle East, where Israel’s military actions in Gaza have put stress on relations with countries like Bahrain. Earlier this week, Jordan also recalled its ambassador to Israel. In recent years, Bahrain, Sudan, Morocco, and the United Arab Emirates have moved to normalize relations and expand economic and military cooperation with Israel under agreements known as the Abraham Accords. The United States has strongly promoted these accords, presenting them as building blocks for peace in the Middle East. Critics argue these agreements allow Israel greater benefits without addressing the long-standing occupation of Palestinian territories and disregard public opinion by making deals with autocratic governments. Following Morocco’s agreement with Israel, the US recognized Morocco’s autonomy over Western Sahara, a territory long in dispute. Washington also removed Sudan from its list of state sponsors of terrorism after Sudan normalized ties with Israel, providing economic relief to Sudan’s military government during a period of protests and inflation. The tension between public opinion and government policy has grown, as protests supporting Palestinians have swept the Middle East. In Bahrain, where demonstrations are rarely permitted, protestors marched to the Israeli embassy and activists called for reversing normalization. The Gaza war has also slowed progress towards possible normalization between Israel and Saudi Arabia. 'I think this dynamic of normalization will likely slow down or come to a halt,' Steven Cook, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, told the Associated Press.

El órgano parlamentario consultivo, que no tiene competencias en política exterior, afirmó anteriormente que los lazos económicos con Israel habían sido cortados. Sin embargo, Israel afirma que mantiene una relación 'estable' con Baréin. La declaración del gobierno bareiní no mencionó el fin de las relaciones económicas, pero sí confirmó que los vuelos entre ambos países se han suspendido temporalmente. Esta decisión se produce después de semanas de protestas en Medio Oriente, donde las acciones militares de Israel en Gaza han puesto en tensión las relaciones con países como Baréin. A principios de esta semana, Jordania también retiró a su embajador en Israel. En los últimos años, Baréin, Sudán, Marruecos y Emiratos Árabes Unidos han avanzado en la normalización de relaciones y la expansión de la cooperación económica y militar con Israel bajo los Acuerdos de Abraham. Estados Unidos ha promovido fuertemente estos acuerdos, presentándolos como base para la paz en Medio Oriente. Los críticos argumentan que estos acuerdos permiten a Israel mayores beneficios sin abordar la ocupación de los territorios palestinos y desoyen la opinión pública al firmar acuerdos con gobiernos autoritarios. Tras el acuerdo entre Marruecos e Israel, Estados Unidos reconoció la autonomía de Marruecos sobre el Sahara Occidental, un territorio en disputa. Washington también sacó a Sudán de su lista de patrocinadores estatales del terrorismo tras la normalización, proporcionando alivio económico al gobierno militar sudanés en un periodo de protestas e inflación. La tensión entre la opinión pública y la política gubernamental ha aumentado mientras protestas en apoyo a los palestinos se extienden por Medio Oriente. U.S. President Barack Obama and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi have developed a notably friendly relationship, described by officials from both countries as strong 'chemistry.' Their warm interactions during Obama's visit to India included impromptu strolls on the National Mall and a walk together through a rose garden in New Delhi. In anticipation of the visit, Indian weavers prepared traditional saris as gifts for First Lady Michelle Obama, and authorities took measures to clean the city, even removing stray monkeys from areas the president might visit.

The visit garnered significant attention from local television, including speculation about moments such as the two leaders taking a selfie.

Obama's arrival in India set the tone for the trip, as Prime Minister Modi broke protocol by personally greeting Obama on the tarmac and embracing him in a widely publicized 'bear hug.' Their camaraderie continued with another hug following a joint press conference, fueling further discussion about their personal bond.

This visit follows Modi's September trip to the White House, where President Obama extended his schedule to accompany Modi on a walk at the Martin Luther King memorial. In New Delhi, Obama and Modi continued their bilateral talks with a stroll through Hyderabad House's gardens, followed by tea. Modi's team promptly shared highlights of the meeting on social media.

At a prior White House dinner, Modi was fasting for religious reasons and only drank warm water, but during this visit, both leaders shared a meal that included vegetarian and non-vegetarian options. Chef Saransh Goila noted that the menu could have offered more variety.

A grand dinner at the presidential palace featured Indian music and dance, a receiving line, and heartfelt toasts. Modi spoke about the natural kinship between the two nations, while Obama referenced Walt Whitman's 'Passage to India' to highlight global connection and partnership.

Throughout the day, the leaders exchanged light-hearted banter. Obama joked about Modi being welcomed in New York like a Bollywood star and compared their sleeping habits, noting that Modi currently sleeps less. The visit, considered historic, continues with more events scheduled, including a parade for the second day of Obama's trip.

article_content: This week in the Middle East, Gaza is experiencing a severe communications blackout as power outages have disabled telecom services, making it increasingly difficult to share information about those trapped inside. On Wednesday, Israeli forces entered al-Shifa Hospital—the largest in Gaza—where hundreds of patients and thousands of displaced individuals had sought shelter. The hospital, like others, is suffering from fuel and medical shortages, causing the deaths of premature babies and putting cancer patients, dialysis patients, and newborns in incubators in grave danger. Israel justifies attacks on hospitals by claiming they are used by Hamas fighters, but international law generally protects such facilities except under exceptional conditions—circumstances that many legal experts argue do not exist at al-Shifa. Amid growing international concern over strikes targeting civilians and health infrastructure, praise has gone to Indonesian medical volunteers who remain working with their Palestinian colleagues under dire conditions. The devastation in Gaza has been contextualized by mapping its scale against global cities. Among many personal tragedies: a toddler who had just learned to walk was found alive beneath rubble after an airstrike killed her family, leaving her injured and orphaned. At al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, a veteran worker reports the number and severity of casualties is unprecedented, and a local teacher anxiously checks daily to see if her students are among the victims. Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah faces regional and domestic pressures as his group weighs its response to escalating violence along the Lebanese border. Observers question how long the group can remain restrained. Israel maintains its primary objective is to destroy underground Hamas tunnels. However, most military action remains above ground, resulting in significant civilian casualties. Analysts believe Israel is wary of a full-scale tunnel operation because of its complexity and danger, and outline possible military steps required for such an incursion. Meanwhile, Syrian president Bashar al-Assad and his ally Russia have intensified attacks on opposition-held regions, seizing on the broader turmoil in the region. Assad’s vocal condemnation of Israeli actions at a recent summit has drawn criticism from Syrians suffering from his own military’s bombings. Additionally, the US has become more deeply involved as its troops face attacks in Syria and Iraq. According to Dr. Ayman Harb, chief of orthopaedics at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, doctors are now encountering medical cases never before seen.

El miércoles, fuerzas israelíes ingresaron al Hospital al-Shifa, el más grande de Gaza, donde cientos de pacientes y miles de desplazados buscaban refugio. Este hospital, al igual que otros, sufre una grave escasez de combustible y suministros médicos, causando la muerte de bebés prematuros y poniendo en grave riesgo a pacientes oncológicos, personas que requieren diálisis y recién nacidos en incubadoras. Israel justifica los ataques a hospitales alegando que son usados por combatientes de Hamas, pero la ley internacional usualmente protege estos centros salvo en circunstancias excepcionales, condiciones que muchos expertos señalan que no se cumplen en al-Shifa. Ante el aumento de la preocupación internacional por los ataques a civiles e infraestructuras de salud, se reconoce el trabajo de los voluntarios médicos indonesios que permanecen colaborando con sus colegas palestinos bajo condiciones extremas. La magnitud de la devastación en Gaza se ha comparado con ciudades globales para contextualizar su impacto. Entre tantas tragedias personales: una niña que recién aprendía a caminar fue rescatada con vida bajo escombros tras un bombardeo que mató a toda su familia, quedando herida y huérfana. En el Hospital Mártires de Al-Aqsa, un trabajador con años de experiencia describe la gravedad y cantidad de víctimas como nunca antes vistas, y una maestra local revisa a diario, con angustia, si alguno de sus alumnos se encuentra entre los afectados. El líder de Hezbolá, Hassan Nasrallah, atraviesa presiones internas y regionales mientras el grupo evalúa su postura ante el aumento de la violencia en la frontera libanesa. Analistas debaten cuánto tiempo más el grupo mantendrá su contención. Israel sostiene que su prioridad es destruir los túneles de Hamas bajo Gaza, aunque la mayoría de las operaciones siguen centrándose en superficie, provocando importantes víctimas civiles. Los observadores creen que Israel es precavido con una operación subterránea dada su dificultad y peligrosidad, y exponen posibles estrategias para ello. Al mismo tiempo, el presidente sirio Bashar al-Assad y Rusia han aumentado los ataques en zonas opositoras, en medio de la inestabilidad regional. La reciente condena de Assad a las acciones de Israel en una cumbre fue recibida con críticas por parte de sirios víctimas de los bombardeos de su propio gobierno. Además, EE. UU. ha incrementado su involucramiento tras sufrir ataques a sus fuerzas en Siria e Irak. Según el Dr. Ayman Harb, jefe de ortopedia del Hospital Mártires de Al-Aqsa, actualmente enfrentan casos médicos jamás vistos antes.

article_content: Goran Hadzic, the last remaining fugitive indicted by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY), was captured in Serbia on Wednesday, according to the tribunal. Hadzic, a former Croatian Serb rebel leader and ex-president of the self-proclaimed Republic of Serbian Krajina, had been wanted for seven years. He was charged with crimes against humanity and war crimes connected to the conflicts following Yugoslavia’s breakup in the early 1990s. He is accused of attempting to remove Croats and other non-Serbs from parts of Croatia, as well as the murder of hundreds of civilians, as detailed by the ICTY. With his arrest, all 161 individuals indicted by the tribunal have now been accounted for. Serbian President Boris Tadic also announced the arrest, which comes less than two months after the capture of Ratko Mladic, another high-profile war crimes suspect. Plans were in place to transfer Hadzic to the tribunal's custody following legal procedures in Serbia, aiming to bring him soon to The Hague, Netherlands, where the court operates. Tribunal Prosecutor Serge Brammertz said, 'Hadzic's transfer into the Tribunal's custody is a long-awaited development for the victims... and is a significant milestone in the Tribunal’s history.' The European Union and NATO welcomed the capture, with the EU stating it helps pave the way for Serbia’s future EU membership. EU leaders said in a statement, 'This arrest sends a positive signal to the European Union and Serbia's neighbors, especially regarding the rule of law in Serbia. Serbia is confronting its past and turning toward a better European future.' British Foreign Secretary William Hague called the arrest 'an historic moment for international justice and victims of war crimes during the Balkan wars of the 1990s.' Ratko Mladic was arrested on May 26, after over 15 years in hiding, and sent to the Netherlands to face trial. Mladic’s trial has seen delays, and he has often been uncooperative. During the wars, Mladic's superiors included Radovan Karadzic, now on trial, and Slobodan Milosevic, who died during his trial in The Hague. Prosecutor Brammertz stated that apprehending both Hadzic and Mladic marks significant progress in Serbia’s cooperation with the tribunal and reflects a genuine commitment. Brammertz emphasized ongoing challenges in prosecuting war crimes across the Balkan region and the importance of continued support from the international community. Hadzic’s 2004 indictment relates to crimes allegedly committed in eastern Slavonia, including the murder, imprisonment, and forced displacement of Croats and other non-Serbs, as well as the destruction of property and cultural sites. The tribunal alleges that Hadzic was a co-perpetrator in a joint criminal enterprise to forcibly remove Croats and other non-Serbs from large areas of Croatia to form a Serb-dominated state. Specific accusations include extermination, murder, forced labor, detention under inhumane conditions, torture, and destruction of property. CNN reporters Claudia Rebaza and Richard Allen Greene contributed to this report.

Hadzic, exlíder rebelde serbocroata y expresidente de la autoproclamada República Serbia de Krajina, había estado prófugo durante siete años. Fue acusado de crímenes de lesa humanidad y crímenes de guerra vinculados a los conflictos tras la disolución de Yugoslavia en los años noventa. Se le acusa de intentar expulsar a croatas y otros no serbios de partes de Croacia, así como del asesinato de cientos de civiles, según detalló el TPIY. Con su arresto, ya se ha dado cuenta del paradero de las 161 personas acusadas por el tribunal. El presidente serbio Boris Tadic también anunció la detención, que se produce menos de dos meses después de la captura de Ratko Mladic, otro de los principales sospechosos de crímenes de guerra. Había planes para trasladar a Hadzic bajo custodia del tribunal tras concluir los procedimientos legales en Serbia, con la intención de llevarlo pronto a La Haya, Países Bajos, donde funciona la corte. El fiscal del tribunal, Serge Brammertz, declaró: 'El traslado de Hadzic a la custodia del Tribunal es un desarrollo largamente esperado para las víctimas... y un hito significativo en la historia del Tribunal.' La Unión Europea y la OTAN dieron la bienvenida a la captura, y la UE afirmó que esto ayuda a allanar el camino para la eventual membresía de Serbia en el bloque. Líderes de la UE afirmaron en un comunicado: 'Este arresto envía una señal positiva a la Unión Europea y a los vecinos de Serbia, especialmente en cuanto al estado de derecho en Serbia. Serbia está enfrentando su pasado y avanzando hacia un futuro europeo mejor.' El secretario de Relaciones Exteriores británico, William Hague, calificó la detención como 'un momento histórico para la justicia internacional y las víctimas de crímenes de guerra durante las guerras balcánicas de los años 90.' Ratko Mladic fue arrestado el 26 de mayo, tras más de 15 años prófugo, y enviado a los Países Bajos para enfrentar juicio. El proceso de Mladic ha experimentado retrasos y él ha sido frecuentemente poco cooperativo. Durante las guerras, los superiores de Mladic incluían a Radovan Karadzic, ahora en juicio, y Slobodan Milosevic, quien murió durante su proceso en La Haya. El fiscal Brammertz afirmó que la captura tanto de Hadzic como de Mladic representa un avance importante en la cooperación de Serbia con el tribunal y refleja un compromiso genuino. Brammertz también hizo hincapié en los desafíos persistentes de juzgar crímenes de guerra en la región de los Balcanes y la importancia del apoyo continuo de la comunidad internacional. La acusación de 2004 contra Hadzic se relaciona con delitos supuestamente cometidos en Eslavonia Oriental, incluyendo asesinato, encarcelamiento y desplazamiento forzado de croatas y otros no serbios, así como la destrucción de bienes y sitios culturales. El tribunal sostiene que Hadzic fue coautor en una empresa criminal conjunta para expulsar por la fuerza a croatas y otros no serbios de grandes zonas de Croacia, con el fin de formar un estado dominado por serbios. Las acusaciones específicas incluyen exterminio, asesinato, trabajo forzado, detención en condiciones inhumanas, tortura y destrucción de propiedades. Los periodistas de CNN Claudia Rebaza y Richard Allen Greene contribuyeron a este informe.

article_content: A parliamentary panel has recommended a minimum imprisonment of six months for those selling adulterated food or drinks, along with a minimum fine of Rs 25,000. The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs, chaired by BJP MP Brijlal, stated that given the serious health risks posed by adulterated food, current penalties are inadequate. The committee also suggested that the same minimum punishment be applied to cases involving the sale of noxious food or drinks, but with a minimum fine of Rs 10,000. Currently, food adulteration is punishable by up to six months in jail or a fine up to Rs 1,000, or both. The introduction of community service as a punishment under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) was described as a 'commendable effort' by the panel, which views this as a reformative approach that could reduce prison overcrowding and improve prison management. However, the panel noted that the definition, term, and nature of community service have not been specified in the proposed law. The committee recommended clearly defining community service and assigning someone to supervise offenders carrying out such sentences. Additionally, the panel highlighted typographical and grammatical errors in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita draft and stressed that even minor errors could lead to misinterpretation. They recommended that the Ministry address these issues. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS-2023), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS-2023), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA-2023) bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha on August 11 as replacements for the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, 1898, the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, respectively. The panel's reports were submitted to the Rajya Sabha last Friday.

El comité también sugirió que se aplique el mismo castigo mínimo en los casos relacionados con la venta de alimentos o bebidas nocivos, pero con una multa mínima de Rs 10,000. Actualmente, la adulteración de alimentos se castiga con hasta seis meses de cárcel o una multa de hasta Rs 1,000, o ambas. La introducción del servicio comunitario como castigo en el Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) fue señalada como un 'esfuerzo encomiable' por el panel, que considera esto un enfoque reformador que podría reducir el hacinamiento en las cárceles y mejorar la gestión penitenciaria. Sin embargo, el panel observó que la definición, duración y naturaleza del servicio comunitario no han sido especificadas en la ley propuesta. El comité recomendó definir claramente el servicio comunitario y asignar a alguien para supervisar a las personas que cumplan este tipo de castigo. Además, el panel resaltó errores tipográficos y gramaticales en el borrador del Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita y enfatizó que incluso los errores menores podrían llevar a interpretaciones erróneas. Recomendaron que el Ministerio los corrija. El Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS-2023), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS-2023) y Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA-2023) se presentaron en la Lok Sabha el 11 de agosto como reemplazos del Código de Procedimiento Penal de 1898, el Código Penal de la India de 1860 y la Ley de Pruebas de la India de 1872, respectivamente. Los informes del panel se presentaron al Rajya Sabha el pasado viernes.

article_content: Judge William Blair Sylvester of Arapahoe County has ruled that there is sufficient evidence for James Holmes to proceed to trial regarding the Aurora movie theater shooting, which claimed 12 lives and injured dozens more in July 2012. Holmes, formerly a neuroscience graduate student, faces 166 charges, encompassing first-degree murder, attempted murder, and weapons violations. The judge issued his ruling after three days of evidence, agreeing with prosecutors that Holmes meticulously planned the midnight attack during a showing of 'The Dark Knight Rises.' Prosecutor Karen Pearson argued that Holmes deliberately chose the location and time to maximize casualties, declaring, 'He intended to kill them all.' Holmes is being held without bail, with his upcoming hearing changed to an arraignment. The defense, initially expected to argue for diminished capacity, decided not to present such a defense or any witnesses during the hearing, as explained by attorney Dan King. Legal terminology distinguishes diminished capacity—which refers to reduced ability to make decisions due to mental impairment—from insanity, defined as an inability to distinguish right from wrong because of a severe mental disorder. Some victims' families reject the idea of incapacity, insisting Holmes acted with deliberation and competence. Tom Teves, who lost his son Alex, pointed to the calculated nature of the act as evidence of intent, not madness. Investigators indicated Holmes began building his arsenal months before the shooting, obtaining two Glock handguns, an AR-15 rifle, a shotgun, thousands of rounds of ammunition, and tear gas grenades. Surveillance footage and photos recovered from Holmes’ phone show him frequently scouting the theater ahead of time. In his apartment, Holmes set up elaborate and dangerous traps using bomb-making materials, tripwires, and incendiary chemicals designed to cause extensive damage if triggered. He also arranged for loud music to play automatically, apparently to attract someone into the apartment and set off the explosives. Authorities were able to neutralize these hazards before they could do any harm. On July 20, Holmes entered the theater in disguise, propped open an exit, armed himself, and re-entered, deploying gas canisters and opening fire. His rifle jammed during the attack, which likely prevented additional casualties. When police found him outside, he was dressed in body armor and appeared strikingly calm. Officers described Holmes as emotionally detached and compliant during his arrest. While being held, he behaved oddly, such as playing with objects and trying to insert a staple into an electrical socket. No signs of drug or alcohol influence were reported.

Holmes, exestudiante de posgrado en neurociencias, enfrenta 166 cargos que incluyen asesinato en primer grado, intento de asesinato y delitos con armas. El juez emitió su fallo tras tres días de pruebas, coincidiendo con los fiscales en que Holmes planeó meticulosamente el ataque durante una función de medianoche de 'The Dark Knight Rises'. La fiscal Karen Pearson argumentó que Holmes eligió deliberadamente la ubicación y la hora para causar el mayor número posible de víctimas, afirmando: 'Él tenía la intención de matarlos a todos'. Holmes permanece detenido sin derecho a fianza y la próxima audiencia fue cambiada a una lectura de cargos. La defensa, que originalmente iba a presentar un argumento de capacidad disminuida, decidió no hacerlo ni presentar testigos durante la audiencia, según explicó el abogado Dan King. En términos legales, la capacidad disminuida se refiere a una capacidad reducida para tomar decisiones debido a un deterioro mental, mientras que la locura se define como la incapacidad de distinguir el bien del mal a causa de un trastorno mental grave. Algunas familias de las víctimas rechazan el argumento de incapacidad, insistiendo en que Holmes actuó de manera deliberada y competente. Tom Teves, quien perdió a su hijo Alex, consideró que la naturaleza calculada del acto demuestra intención, no locura. Investigadores señalaron que Holmes comenzó a reunir su arsenal meses antes del tiroteo, adquiriendo dos pistolas Glock, un rifle AR-15, una escopeta, miles de municiones y granadas de gas lacrimógeno. Videos de vigilancia y fotos recuperadas de su teléfono muestran que inspeccionó repetidamente el cine antes del ataque. En su apartamento, Holmes preparó trampas sofisticadas y peligrosas utilizando materiales explosivos, cables trampa y productos químicos incendiarios, diseñados para causar daños considerables si se activaban. También programó música a alto volumen, aparentemente para atraer a alguien al apartamento y detonar los explosivos. Las autoridades pudieron neutralizar estos riesgos antes de que causaran daño. El 20 de julio, Holmes entró al cine disfrazado, dejó trabada una puerta de salida, se armó y regresó, lanzando granadas de gas y disparando al público. Su rifle se trabó durante el ataque, lo que probablemente evitó más víctimas fatales. La policía lo encontró fuera del lugar, vestido con chaleco antibalas y luciendo sumamente calmado. Los oficiales describieron a Holmes como emocionalmente distante y cooperador durante su detención. Ya arrestado, mostró comportamientos extraños, como jugar con objetos e intentar meter una grapa en un enchufe. No se hallaron indicios de influencia de drogas o alcohol.

article_content: Ukraine’s former Prime Minister and opposition leader, Yulia Tymoshenko, ended her 12-day hunger strike, according to her Batkivschyna party. Her daughter, Eugenia Tymoshenko, visited her at the Kharkov prison and reported that Yulia is very weak after undergoing her third hunger strike in a short span. Eugenia noted that Yulia ended her protest following appeals from demonstrators gathered at Kiev’s Independence Square, as well as requests from international and European leaders. The protesters urged Yulia to look after her well-being so that she could continue supporting their cause. The hunger strike came amid widespread protests in Kiev, which started when President Viktor Yanukovich suspended talks on an association agreement with the European Union. Many Ukrainians were angered, believing that EU integration would bring modernization and increased trade. By Friday morning, around 7,000 protesters were present in Kiev, mainly in Independence (Maidan) Square and also near government buildings. The crowds tend to grow in the evenings, with plans for even larger protests during the weekend. President Yanukovich’s change of course came under pressure from Russia, which threatened Ukraine with economic retaliation if it moved toward the EU, while offering gas discounts if Ukraine joined the Moscow-led Customs Union. The EU had also pushed for Tymoshenko’s release, as she was Yanukovich’s major political rival. Tymoshenko is serving a seven-year sentence for abuse of authority related to a 2009 gas deal with Russia—a conviction widely seen in the West as politically motivated. During the unrest, Yanukovich met with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss bilateral relations and canceled a planned trip to Malta, citing the need to address the internal political situation. These ongoing demonstrations are the largest since the 2004 Orange Revolution, which significantly changed Ukraine’s political scene. (Kiev reporting by Victoria Butenko. Story by Laura Smith-Spark in London. Contributions from Marie-Louise Gumuchian.)

Muchos ucranianos se indignaron, ya que consideraban que integrar la UE modernizaría el país y abriría oportunidades comerciales. article_content: Rafael Nadal, the reigning Wimbledon champion and top seed, has been given medical clearance to play against American Mardy Fish in the men's singles quarterfinals. Nadal's participation was in doubt after he experienced pain in his left foot during a strenuous victory over Juan Martin del Potro on Monday. After undergoing an MRI scan in a London hospital, it was confirmed that Nadal had not suffered a serious injury. He informed his fans on Facebook, expressing gratitude for their support and confirming that he would resume practicing and compete as scheduled. Nadal's optimism now contrasts with the concern he felt during Monday’s four-hour match, played in difficult heat. At one stage, he nearly considered retiring due to the pain, taking a medical timeout as his foot was treated and questioning whether he could continue. He later said he felt terrible during the first set, especially at 6-5, and feared he might have broken his foot. Nadal has previously battled injuries, most notably a knee problem in 2008 that kept him from defending his Wimbledon crown.

Tras someterse a una resonancia magnética en un hospital de Londres, se confirmó que Nadal no había sufrido una lesión grave. Informó a sus seguidores en Facebook, agradeciéndoles el apoyo y confirmando que volvería a los entrenamientos y competiría como estaba previsto. El optimismo de Nadal ahora contrasta con la preocupación que sintió durante el partido de cuatro horas jugado el lunes bajo condiciones difíciles. En un momento, casi consideró retirarse por el dolor, tomó un descanso médico mientras le atendían el pie y se preguntó si podría seguir jugando. article_content: A tragic explosion struck a mosque in Shiraz, southern Iran, on Saturday evening, resulting in 10 deaths and about 160 injuries. Authorities now attribute the blast to the careless handling of military munitions left over from a recent 'Sacred Defense' exhibition, rather than an intentional bombing as initially believed. The incident occurred around 6 p.m. during evening prayers in the men's section of the mosque, a space also used as a cultural center. The explosion set off a fire while approximately 800 attendees—many of them young people—gathered to hear a cleric criticize Bahai and Wahabi beliefs, both considered controversial by some Shiite groups. While initial reports from the Fars news agency pointed to a homemade bomb, Provincial Police Commander Ali Moaeyri later clarified there was no evidence of sabotage. He suggested live munitions, apparently left behind after the military-themed exhibition, likely caused the disaster. The Basij militia, known for meeting in mosques, were involved in organizing such events. Victims were rushed to a dozen hospitals across Shiraz for treatment. The city, famous for its poets, scholars, and traditional crafts, rarely sees attacks of this nature. However, Iran has experienced occasional acts of violence in recent years, including a significant bombing in February 2007 targeting members of the Islamic Revolutionary Corps. Shiraz, home to more than a million residents and located roughly 400 miles south of Tehran, remains a significant cultural and historical center in Iran.

Afghanistan will begin their first World Cup qualifying campaign since the Taliban's return to power on Thursday, with head coach Abdullah Al-Mutairi urging his players to focus on football and set politics aside as they prepare to face Mongolia. While Afghanistan has never come close to securing a World Cup spot, the team hopes to advance to the second round of Asia's qualifiers for the 2026 tournament. However, Al-Mutairi and his squad face several challenges. Because of the security situation in Afghanistan, they cannot play in front of home fans and are instead hosting their 'home' leg in neighboring Tajikistan before the return match in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, on Tuesday.

“Everyone thinks we are monsters, but that isn't true,” said Al-Mutairi, the Kuwaiti coach, in an interview with Reuters about perceptions of his team since the Taliban's return two years ago. “You cannot judge everyone because of the actions of a few or due to the political situation. We are only a football team. It’s difficult, but we do our best.”

This match is one of ten preliminary ties across Asia involving the continent’s lowest-ranked nations. Winners will advance to the second round, which features teams such as Japan and Australia. Should Afghanistan triumph over Mongolia, they will move into a group with 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar, as well as India and the coach’s native Kuwait. The top two teams from that group will progress further in World Cup qualifying, while the third and fourth-placed teams will compete for a spot at the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia.

“Our goal is to qualify for the 2027 Asian Cup,” said Al-Mutairi. “We’ll give our best effort now.”

Despite the many obstacles since taking over as coach in April, Al-Mutairi says he has successfully formed a cohesive team from players both inside and outside Afghanistan. “We try to show everyone that we all share the same pain,” he said. “We are human beings. Background, culture, place of residence, or birthplace don’t matter. What matters is that we share the same Afghan blood. That can’t be changed—even if you were born abroad, hold another passport, or have never been to Afghanistan. What’s important is playing for the country. Previously this was difficult, but we have overcome that now.”

Lo importante es jugar por el país. Antes era un gran problema, pero ya lo superamos".

Indian stock markets closed higher on Wednesday, with energy sector stocks leading gains as oil prices dropped globally. However, the overall market rise was tempered by declines in financial and IT stocks. The NSE Nifty 50 index increased by 0.19% to settle at 19,443.50, while the S&P BSE Sensex rose just 0.05% to 64,975.61.

Energy and oil & gas companies outperformed, advancing 0.42% and 0.78% respectively, thanks to continued weakness in oil prices driven by reduced demand from China and the US. Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd climbed 3.06% and was the best performer on the Nifty 50, while Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd jumped 7.48% after reporting favorable quarterly results.

Conversely, financial and IT sectors both slipped more than 0.2% after recent gains. Market experts highlighted India’s steady macroeconomic fundamentals, strong company profits, inflows from retail investors, and higher domestic participation as supporting the stock market's resilience. Santosh Pandey from Nuvama underscored these positive trends.

Small- and mid-cap stocks remained the standout performers this year, gaining 37% and 28% so far in 2023, compared to a 7.4% rise in the Nifty. VK Vijayakumar from Geojit Financial Services noted that selling by foreign investors had mostly affected large-cap stocks while the broader market remained strong.

On Wednesday, small-cap stocks gained 0.70% to reach new highs, and mid-caps added 0.99%. The pharmaceutical sector rose 1.48%, led by strong post-earnings moves from Alkem Laboratories and Lupin following their US FDA drug approvals. Real estate stocks advanced 1.52%, powered by Prestige Estate Projects' 5.28% rise after its earnings report.

article_content: For thousands of years, seventeen giant stone slabs formed a bridge across the River Barle in Exmoor, known as the Tarr Steps. According to local legend, the devil built the bridge so he could sunbathe, but this did not prevent the structure from being swept away by floods last year. Today, engineers began the careful process of rebuilding the 180-foot-long crossing. Some believe Tarr Steps dates back to 1000 BC, but experts suggest it is more likely from the Middle Ages, with its first recorded mention in the 14th century. The bridge, located in Somerset, collapsed after being hit by a ten-foot wall of floodwater on December 22. Construction crews have already removed some of the two-tonne, eight-foot-long slabs from the river using heavy machinery. Each slab had previously been numbered to help with restoration in case of damage, allowing teams to methodically reassemble the structure. Tarr Steps links the Somerset villages of Withypool and Dulverton. The bridge was also destroyed by floods in 1952 and required rebuilding by the Army. After further damage in 1982, two thick cables were installed as protection, but these snapped during the most recent floods. Martin Hesp, a local resident, remarked, 'I have lived in the area for over 50 years and I have never seen anything like this before. It must have been some mighty trees that were carried downstream and smashed through them.' Contractors working for Somerset County Council are managing the repair. Rob Wilson-North, conservation manager for the Exmoor National Park Authority, witnessed the damage. He said, 'It was the speed of the water—it was absolutely terrifying. I've worked on Exmoor for 20 years and I've never seen it like that. For me, it was absolutely shocking.' Tarr Steps is one of Britain's best-preserved examples of a clapper bridge (from the Latin 'claperius', meaning 'pile of stones'). It consists of massive stone slabs supported by stone piers, which rise about three feet above the river when water is at normal levels. The name 'Tarr' may come from the Celtic word 'tochar', meaning causeway. Despite local legends attributing supernatural origins and stories of mythical tests—such as a cat reportedly being vaporised by the devil—the bridge's documented history begins in the 14th century. Its current restoration continues the long history of resilience and significance in the area.

article_content: MANCHESTER, England: Manchester United manager Erik Ten Hag defended his position on Friday as his struggling team prepares for a Premier League match against Fulham. The Dutch coach has faced significant pressure after United suffered eight defeats in 15 matches across all competitions—marking their worst start to a season since 1962. The squad’s underperformance and Ten Hag’s tactics have drawn criticism, and some suggest that another loss at Craven Cottage could jeopardize his job. Despite this, Ten Hag remains determined, stating that the team’s mood is focused on improvement after consecutive 3-0 home losses to Manchester City and Newcastle United. 'They're positive and want to put this right. We know the standards here and must meet them every day,' Ten Hag told reporters at United's training ground. 'We had two big setbacks, but this squad, the staff, and I are strong enough to fix things.' United, currently eighth in the table, have lost half of their Premier League games and five of their first ten home matches in all competitions. 'I'm convinced by the players in the dressing room,' said Ten Hag, who has spent £400 million in the transfer market since joining in summer 2022. 'Last year we saw they could do much better.' 'It's up to me to help them play better, and I take responsibility for that. I'll do everything possible to make improvements. As players return from injury, I'm confident our performances will improve.' Ten Hag was also asked about criticism after the City defeat, where he appeared to suggest his team could not play the passing style of his former Ajax side. Responding with energy, Ten Hag said: 'My comments were misinterpreted. I came here to implement my philosophy based on possession football, but I also have to adapt to the club’s DNA and the players’ strengths. Last season, we played good football. This season, our philosophy hasn’t changed. I do not want to play long balls—I bought Andre Onana to help build from the back. We aim to press and be direct with players like Rasmus Hojlund, Marcus Rashford, Anthony, and Bruno Fernandes.' He admitted that injuries and frequent lineup changes have made it difficult to execute his game plan. 'We barely have the same lineup for more than two or three games, and constantly adjusting doesn’t help our routines. But I'm not making excuses—we need to win and be more pragmatic.' United will be without midfielder Casemiro against Fulham due to a hamstring injury that will keep him out for several weeks. However, defender Raphael Varane may be available after recovering from illness.

article_content: Kindness at work creates significant positive effects. In a time of turmoil and division, increasing kindness is especially valuable. World Kindness Day offers an opportunity to honor, celebrate, and inspire acts of kindness. Many people build kindness into their routines—whether paying for the order behind them at a drive-through or running errands for an elderly neighbor. Bringing kindness into the workplace is powerful as well. Since we spend much of our lives at work, the experiences we have there ripple outward, impacting other areas of our lives. The workplace is a valuable setting for kindness, compassion, empathy, and generosity. Each person has the power to influence kindness at work. People learn by observing others, so your actions and attitude significantly affect those around you. World Kindness Day, celebrated internationally on November 13, was established in 1998 to highlight positive actions and community bonds. Some people extend the celebration into Kindness Week, starting on November 13. The day aims to bridge differences and foster unity and empathy. Why is a kind work environment important? Research shows that kindness has major benefits for work and life. For example, a meta-analysis in the Psychological Bulletin, covering almost 200,000 people, found kindness supports physical, cognitive, and emotional well-being. An Ohio State University study found that kindness reduces depression and anxiety. A kind workplace allows people to feel respected and valued, which supports innovation, collaboration, and contribution. When people feel cared for, they are more willing to take risks and aim for accomplishments. Five ways to celebrate World Kindness Day at work: 1. Be Attentive: Celebrate by focusing on others and showing empathy. When life's busy, kindness means putting others first. Happiness is linked to attentiveness, empathy, and imagining others’ perspectives. Empathetic leaders and workplaces report higher engagement, innovation, satisfaction, retention, inclusivity, and cooperation. Kindness and empathy have similar positive effects. 2. Be Inclusive: Extend kindness to all—regardless of role or status. Smile at someone new or express compassion for a close colleague. Be caring across departments, regions, and hierarchies. Offer help or encouragement to those facing challenges. Companies can host kindness fairs, inviting community organizations and encouraging volunteering or charitable giving. Even small acts have a big impact. 3. Be Intentional: Take deliberate action to demonstrate kindness, whether by asking about a coworker’s needs, lending a listening ear, or advocating for colleagues. Express appreciation for colleagues’ work and recognize their efforts publicly. Employers may coordinate group acts of kindness, such as delivering food to a sick coworker or volunteering together. These efforts create a kinder culture. 4. Be Consistent: Small, everyday actions also matter—like bringing coffee for a coworker or catching someone up on a missed meeting. Some companies serve special treats during Kindness Week to express gratitude. According to The Harris Poll, 67% of people report being more compassionate and checking in on those they care about. 5. Make Kindness a Habit: Go beyond a single day or week. Practice ongoing kindness by empathizing, giving people the benefit of the doubt, and establishing routines—such as supporting customers, mentoring new employees, or assisting the elderly. Build a routine of kind actions, at work and beyond. Kindness benefits people, businesses, and society. We all want to work and live where respect and care prevail. Your actions influence others, so choose kindness on World Kindness Day—and every day—for yourself and those around you.

In contrast, countries such as Russia, China, Turkey, the African Union, and the United Arab Emirates urged a de-escalation of violence and emphasized the need to quickly resume diplomatic efforts. article_content: Twelve-year-old Jack Herrera’s return from a Texas summer camp turned tragic when he became one of six Americans who died this year after contracting a rare brain amoeba. His father, Ray Herrera, recounted the heartbreak as Jack, once full of life, quickly declined and died following exposure to Naegleria fowleri in Lake LBJ. The amoeba, which lives in warm freshwater like lakes and rivers, enters the body through the nose and attacks the brain. Symptoms, often mistaken for the flu, appear within 1 to 14 days but can rapidly lead to coma and death. According to the CDC, well-maintained swimming pools do not pose this risk. Health officials, including Dr. Kevin Sherin, stress that early recognition of the infection is crucial, though it remains challenging due to its rarity and initial symptoms. While nearly always fatal, prompt treatment with the right drug combination can provide a chance at survival. Experts cite the hot summer and low water levels as possible reasons for this year’s spike in cases. All recent victims were males aged 10 to 22, possibly because young men often participate in water activities that raise exposure risk. Prevention options are limited—health officials recommend using nose plugs in warm freshwater or avoiding such areas during hot weather. Routine testing of water isn’t practical as it doesn’t offer timely information, according to Dr. Michael Beach of the CDC. While these infections are exceedingly rare but deadly, authorities typically post warnings at affected areas rather than closing them. Despite such efforts, many people continue to swim, with some downplaying the risk when compared to other natural hazards.

Su padre, Ray Herrera, relató el dolor de ver cómo Jack, un niño lleno de vida, empeoró rápidamente y murió tras exponerse a Naegleria fowleri en el lago LBJ. La ameba, que vive en aguas dulces y cálidas como lagos y ríos, ingresa al cuerpo por la nariz y ataca el cerebro. Según los CDC, las piscinas bien mantenidas no presentan este riesgo. Los funcionarios de salud, como el Dr. Kevin Sherin, insisten en que la detección temprana es clave, aunque sigue siendo complicada por lo poco común de la infección y sus síntomas iniciales. Aunque suele ser mortal, un tratamiento rápido con la combinación adecuada de medicamentos puede ofrecer una oportunidad de sobrevivir. Expertos señalan que el verano caluroso y los bajos niveles de agua podrían explicar el aumento de casos este año. Todas las víctimas recientes fueron varones de entre 10 y 22 años, posiblemente porque los jóvenes participan más en actividades acuáticas que incrementan el riesgo de exposición. Las opciones de prevención son limitadas; las autoridades sanitarias recomiendan usar pinzas nasales en aguas dulces y cálidas o evitar estas áreas durante el calor. El análisis rutinario del agua no es práctico porque la información llega tarde, según el Dr. Michael Beach de los CDC. In 1829, English engineer George Stephenson introduced the first steam-powered locomotive, named Rocket, marking the birth of train travel. Nearly two centuries later, while modern life is often focused on speed—like flying from Miami to Seoul in under 15 hours—luxury train journeys are all about enjoying the experience.

Today’s travelers can choose from a variety of immersive train adventures. Some are epic, such as a four-week journey in Africa visiting the pyramids and Victoria Falls, or a two-week Trans-Siberian crossing in Russia spanning eight time zones. Others are shorter but equally memorable, like a day trip through Peru’s lush landscape to Machu Picchu or a scenic ride through the Scottish Highlands while sipping whisky.

As T. S. Eliot said, "The journey, not the arrival, matters." Train travel invites passengers to savor each moment along the route.

World-class luxury train trips include:

Al Andalus, Andalucía, Spain: An 800-mile rail adventure through southern Spain, stopping at historic cities such as Seville, Córdoba, Granada, Ronda, and Cádiz in restored 1929 carriages. The route showcases Spain’s blend of Moorish and Catholic heritage. Price: $3,220, meals included (luxurytrainclub.com).

Eastern & Oriental Express, Singapore to Bangkok: This opulent train features an observation car and live piano music. The seven-day trip runs through the Cameron Highlands and past Malaysia’s Bukit Merah, with stops to taste local teas and strawberries, and crosses the River Kwai via the Tham Kasae viaduct. Price: $9,200, meals included (orient-express.com).

Golden Eagle Trans-Siberian Express, Russia: Guests travel 6,000 miles from Moscow to Vladivostok over two weeks, crossing eight time zones with views of the Ural Mountains and Lake Baikal. Luxuries include a Champagne reception and personal butlers. Price: $21,020, meals included (luxurytrainclub.com).

Hiram Bingham, Peru: A three-and-a-half-hour journey from Cuzco to Machu Picchu, featuring brunch, mountain views, and arrival at Aguas Calientes near the ancient Inca city. Meals and tea are served at Machu Picchu Sanctuary Lodge. Price: $350, meals included (orient-express.com).

Pride of Africa, Africa: This 28-day adventure from Cape Town to Cairo features visits to Uganda, Tanzania, Zimbabwe, and Egypt, with stops at landmarks like Victoria Falls and the Sphinx. The trip includes wine tastings and rare departures. Price: from $6,200, meals and excursions included (rovos.com).

Royal Canadian Pacific, Canada: A six-day round trip from Calgary through the Rockies, climbing Yoho National Park’s Spiral Tunnels and taking in Banff National Park and Lake Louise. Price: $8,145, meals included (luxurytrainclub.com).

The Royal Scotsman, Scotland: Starting in Edinburgh, this ride explores the Kingdom of Fife and the scenic Highlands, with whisky tastings, clan history, and a visit to one of Scotland’s oldest distilleries. Price: $4,020, meals included (royalscotsman.com).

Luxury train travel offers stunning views, comfort, and a spirit of adventure. Which journey would you choose?

article_content: Tiffany Sessions, a 20-year-old University of Florida junior majoring in economics, went missing after leaving her off-campus apartment for a run on February 9, 1989. She told her roommate she’d be back soon and took her Walkman with her, but she was never seen again. At the time, tools like cell phones and online resources did not exist for investigating missing person cases. All police had were reports of a young woman matching Tiffany’s description spotted near Gainesville’s main street around dusk. Tiffany's typical running path included Gainesville’s main street and a dirt trail through nearby woods, totaling about three miles round-trip and taking about an hour. Authorities and her family believe she was likely abducted by the wooded path. Despite widespread searches, neither Tiffany nor any of her belongings, including her Walkman and clothes, were ever recovered. Detective Bob Dean of the Alachua County Sheriff's Office has noted that development in the area over the years has complicated search efforts, but the case remains open and active. Recent attempts have used technologies like ground sonar, with search teams working as recently as the past December. Multiple possible suspects have come forward over the years, but police have ruled out all confessions as unreliable. One man, serving time for another crime, wrote a letter claiming responsibility for Tiffany’s disappearance but later denied involvement; handwriting analysis still linked him to the letter. Although law enforcement doubts he is responsible, Tiffany’s father, Patrick Sessions, still suspects him. Patrick Sessions continues to work with investigators and highlights that the suspect in question was a sex offender released a month and a half prior to Tiffany disappearing. The cold case unit at the Alachua County Sheriff's Office is now responsible for the investigation. On the 20th anniversary of Tiffany’s disappearance, her father used the media to renew calls for information. Police and Tiffany’s family urge anyone with relevant information to call the tip line at 352-367-4161. A $25,000 reward remains available. At the time she vanished, Tiffany Sessions was wearing red sweatpants, a white sweatshirt with 'Aspen' printed on it, a gold Rolex watch, and a black Sony Walkman. She was 5 feet 3 inches tall, weighed 125 pounds, and had blonde hair and brown eyes.

New technology is changing how student engagement is monitored in higher education and may soon influence workplace practices. This spring, nine U.S. colleges began participating in a pilot program from CourseSmart, a Silicon Valley-based provider of electronic textbooks. With the shift toward digital textbooks, CourseSmart enables professors to access real-time data on students' use of these materials. As reported by Alexandra Tilsley of Inside Higher Ed, the platform tracks metrics such as page views, time spent reading, notes, highlights, bookmarks, and whether students opened the textbook. CourseSmart says this system allows faculty to identify students who may be at risk based on their level of engagement.

Tracy Hurley, dean of the business school at Texas A&M University-San Antonio, told The New York Times the approach is like 'Big Brother, sort of, but with good intent.' While the program currently aims to support students, there are concerns that similar technology could be used in the workplace, allowing employers to closely monitor how employees perform their jobs. The article notes that the boundaries between work and personal life have already blurred due to tools like email, key cards, and security cameras, raising further questions about privacy and electronic surveillance. These developments spark debate about individual autonomy and how people are evaluated in educational and professional environments.

The views expressed are solely those of Bob Greene.

article_content: A woman narrowly escaped with her life after being caught by powerful waves on Sardinero Beach in Santander, Spain. Video footage shows her skipping along the shoreline, apparently unaware of the threat as storms created dangerous sea conditions. While her two friends retreated to safety as the tide swept in, the woman in a black swimsuit realized the danger only at the last moment. She sprinted towards a concrete ramp, but was overtaken by the water, slammed against a beach wall, and swept away. Onlookers watched in alarm, with one bystander making a futile attempt to help using an umbrella. Fortunately, despite being tossed by the waves, the woman emerged from the water bruised but alive. The incident occurred on January 6 and was shared online at liveleak.com.

article_content: The majority of readers find deliberately misleading or mysterious headlines frustrating. In response, Facebook is taking steps to reduce 'click-bait'—articles designed primarily to lure clicks without delivering substantial content. By monitoring how much time users spend on articles and their level of engagement, Facebook aims to prioritize quality content in users' News Feeds. Research scientist Khalid El-Arini and product specialist Joyce Tang explained in a Facebook blog post that the company has updated its News Feed algorithm. This change lowers the ranking of links with click-bait headlines and helps users see more relevant, meaningful posts. A survey conducted by Facebook revealed that 80% of users prefer headlines that clearly describe the article’s content, helping them judge if it's worth clicking. Stories with vague or sensationalist headlines can overshadow posts from friends and pages that users care about. To counter this, Facebook is measuring how long people read articles and whether they interact (like or comment) with the content. If users quickly return to Facebook after clicking a link or rarely interact with the article, it signals low value. As a result, these posts will appear less frequently in News Feed. The changes are expected to impact publishers who habitually use click-bait tactics, while larger or playful publishers who use them occasionally may not see significant effects. Facebook stated, 'We're making these changes to ensure that click-bait content does not drown out the things that people really want to see on Facebook.'

article_content: Over the last 18 months, approximately 20 cases of a polio-like syndrome have been identified in children in California, according to Dr. Keith Van Haren, a pediatric neurologist at Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford. Dr. Van Haren has written a report detailing five of these initial cases, which will be presented at the American Academy of Neurology's annual meeting. These children developed paralysis in one or more limbs between August 2012 and July 2013, and all had received the poliovirus vaccine. Treatments have not restored motor function in the affected limbs. Laboratory tests detected enterovirus 68—a rare virus linked to severe respiratory illnesses—in two of the five cases. Samples from the other three children were not processed in time for conclusive results, according to Dr. Emmanuelle Waubant of the University of California, San Francisco. Dr. Van Haren stated that about 20 cases have been identified in the U.S. so far, all in California and occurring within the past 18 months. One of the affected children, Sofia Jarvis, initially presented with symptoms resembling asthma and later developed paralysis in her left arm at age two, despite having received the polio vaccination. Her mother, Jessica Tomei, is raising awareness about the condition. Sofia, now four, is doing well but has had to adapt to her permanent paralysis. Dr. Waubant and her colleagues are encouraging health care providers to be alert for similar cases and to send in samples from patients with these symptoms. They stress that although the cases are serious, they are very rare and do not represent a widespread epidemic. Most children have not regained use of the most severely affected limbs, although some have recovered some function in less affected ones. The syndrome often presents as sudden, severe limb weakness. The California Department of Public Health is monitoring these paralysis cases but considers the risk to families to be low. Dr. Carol Glaser, chief of the Encephalitis and Special Investigation Section, indicated that so far, there is no finding that raises public health concerns. Similar phenomena have been observed in other parts of the world. According to the World Health Organization, poliovirus has been eradicated in the United States for more than 30 years. Only Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Nigeria remain polio-endemic. Poliovirus is a part of the Picornaviridae family, which also includes enteroviruses and rhinoviruses (the viruses that cause the common cold). There are more than 100 types of enteroviruses, causing millions of infections each year in the United States, usually with mild symptoms. Though most people infected with enterovirus have mild or no symptoms, certain types, such as enterovirus 71, can cause more severe complications, including paralysis and encephalitis. It is unclear if the latest California patients were tested for enterovirus 71. Enterovirus 68, which was first identified in 1962, remains rare. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is aware of the cases in California but is not currently involved in the investigation. Parents are urged to vaccinate their children against polio and to practice good hygiene, as there is no vaccine available for non-polio enteroviruses.

El Dr. Van Haren escribió un informe sobre cinco de estos casos iniciales, el cual será presentado en la próxima reunión anual de la Academia Americana de Neurología. Estos niños desarrollaron parálisis en una o más extremidades entre agosto de 2012 y julio de 2013, y todos habían recibido la vacuna contra la poliomielitis. Los tratamientos no lograron restaurar la función motora en las extremidades afectadas. En las pruebas de laboratorio se detectó el enterovirus 68—un virus raro vinculado a enfermedades respiratorias graves—en dos de los cinco casos. Las muestras de los otros tres niños no fueron procesadas a tiempo para obtener resultados concluyentes, según la Dra. Emmanuelle Waubant de la Universidad de California, San Francisco. El Dr. Van Haren indicó que se han identificado unos 20 casos en EE. UU., todos en California y ocurridos en los últimos 18 meses. El síndrome suele manifestarse como una debilidad repentina y grave en las extremidades.
