The world’s largest tobacco companies are spending millions on advertising electronic cigarettes, reviving the style of cigarette commercials banned during the 1990s. This year alone, these firms have invested £11.5 million in the UK to promote 'smoking deterrent products'—which include e-cigarettes and nicotine patches—surpassing last year’s record of £13.6 million. Since 2009, total advertising spending has reached £60 million, according to market research company Nielsen.

Celebrity endorsements are a key marketing tool. Actor Stephen Dorff and former Playboy model Jenny McCarthy have both fronted campaigns for BluCigs, promoting e-cigarettes as a fashionable alternative to smoking. The rise in e-cigarette use has been remarkable: about 1.3 million Britons now 'vape' using battery-powered devices that deliver nicotine vapor, up from 700,000 last year. Sales of these products are projected to reach £193 million by year’s end and could grow to £339 million annually.

While strict advertising rules ban tobacco product promotion, there are still few restrictions on e-cigarette advertisements in the UK. British American Tobacco, maker of Lucky Strike and Benson & Hedges, was the first to launch an e-cigarette in Britain in July. Philip Morris International plans to introduce its own brand soon, and Imperial Tobacco’s electronic cigarette is expected next year.

Health experts warn that widespread e-cigarette advertising could make smoking look appealing again, potentially undermining decades of public health campaigns. The devices, typically costing between £7 and £60, are offered in flavors like blueberry and chocolate. Analysts at Canaccord Genuity describe this trend as one of the most significant developments in the organized tobacco industry’s history. Globally, the tobacco market is valued at £450 billion.

In both the US and UK, companies have launched televised e-cigarette ads. Notably, Strictly Come Dancing contestant Mark Benton appeared in a £600,000 campaign for E-Lites, while Gamucci aims to raise £200 million to finance further advertising. BAT promotes its devices through social media and road tours with attractive young ambassadors driving cars branded with 'Vype.' Philippe Zell, sales and marketing director at BAT’s Nicoventures subsidiary, emphasized plans to further increase their advertising presence.

Advertising spending on e-cigarettes and related products soared from £1.7 million in 2010 to £13.1 million last year, according to Kantar Media. Industry analyst Shane MacGuill from Euromonitor suggests TV ads may use subdued, indirect messaging after watershed hours. Tobacco advertising was banned in British cinemas in 1986 and from television in the early 1990s.

Some experts worry that portraying e-cigarette use on TV could undo years of anti-smoking progress. Despite no conclusive evidence that e-cigarettes are harmful, New York City’s mayor Michael Bloomberg advocates for strict regulation and has supported drafts of tobacco-related legislation in the city council. E-cigarette sales are already banned in Norway, Singapore, and Brazil. France is planning to regulate e-cigarettes under the same laws as traditional tobacco products.

For many years, Sir Alex Ferguson's critical remarks served as an unofficial measure of Premier League rivalries. Clubs such as Liverpool and Arsenal were frequent targets of his sharp comments until they stopped posing a significant threat. Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger, with his enigmatic smile, often found himself at odds with Ferguson.

During Ferguson’s tenure, Manchester United enjoyed remarkable success, a legacy the club has struggled to maintain since his 2013 retirement. In the 1990s, United were dominant in Manchester, highlighted by Eric Cantona’s goal against Manchester City in 1996. At the time, City were not yet a major consideration for Ferguson's United.

This changed dramatically after Manchester City’s takeover by Middle Eastern investors, accompanied by significant spending. As City emerged as genuine contenders for trophies, Ferguson famously called them the 'noisy neighbours'—a nod to their rise and growing threat. One incident that stoked tensions was City’s widely publicized poster of ex-United striker Carlos Tevez with the message 'welcome to Manchester.'

In recent years, the Premier League title race has often been contested between City and United. After Ferguson’s departure, managers like David Moyes and Louis van Gaal (United), as well as Roberto Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini (City), featured prominently. United’s Champions League victory in 1999 contrasted with City’s then-low status in England’s third tier.

City's fortunes soon improved. In 2001, while United prospered, City were relegated. The season was also notable for Roy Keane’s infamous tackle on Alf-Inge Haaland. Despite United not always seeing City as a league threat, local derbies were intense, often defined by high emotions—for example, the 2012 match where Rio Ferdinand was struck by a coin during celebrations, and Joe Hart intervened with a pitch invader after Robin van Persie's late winner.

For City fans, the 2007-08 season was significant, marking their first double over United since 1969. The 2009 derby, regarded as one of the league’s best, saw United win 4-3 with Michael Owen’s dramatic late goal. Wayne Rooney's overhead kick settled the 2010-11 derby, reinforcing the rivalry’s significance.

City’s breakthrough came when Yaya Toure knocked United out of the FA Cup en route to City’s first major trophy since 1976. United responded in later derbies, but City’s emphatic 6-1 win at Old Trafford in 2011, including Mario Balotelli’s “Why Always Me?” celebration, became iconic.

Currently, the rivalry is highly competitive. Manchester City, once overshadowed by United, are now a major force in both the city and English football.

article_content: A Meccano toy car kit from 1930, which has remained in its original packaging for over 80 years, is expected to sell for more than the price of a new full-sized car. Unearthed by auctioneers Bonhams, the red Meccano kit, dating back to 1930, will be auctioned later this month. The kit includes its original instructions and comes packaged in a wooden case along with a silver edition of the same kit from 1995. The classic red Meccano set, produced in 1930, is paired with a silver version from 1995. The intricately designed red toy car has never been removed from its box. Marketed for decades as 'the Perfect Miniature Motor Cars,' these ornate miniatures are powered by a wind-up clockwork motor. The bundled sets will be auctioned during Bonhams' two-day 'Gentleman's Library' sale on 28-29 January in Knightsbridge. Both kits—never assembled—are stored in a brass-banded wooden case measuring 56cm by 44cm by 22.5cm. The combined lot has an estimated guide price of between £10,000 and £15,000. The older kit is a Meccano number 2 model constructor clockwork motor car, known for its vivid red body and light blue trim. The 1930 instruction manual illustrates how to assemble the vehicle. The 1995 silver version bears the maker's mark by Garrard and Co Ltd, London. According to Bonhams, the inter-war period saw Meccano produce some of the finest mass-produced metal toys in the UK. After 1920, their range expanded, introducing successful Aeroplane and Motor Car Constructor sets. The motor car models include custom parts for various car designs and are operated by powerful clockwork motors, enabling long, fast runs with a single wind-up.

article_content: Aatish Kapadia and JD Majethia’s film Khichdi 2 had a decent start at the box office during its first two days, but its performance on Sunday was heavily affected by the India versus Australia World Cup Final. The film collected Rs 1.1 crore on Friday and Rs 1.35 crore on Saturday, but only managed around Rs 60 lakhs on Sunday with a reported 14% occupancy, according to Sacnilk estimates. This brings the film’s total collection to Rs 3.05 crore. Khichdi 2 was released just five days after Salman Khan and Katrina Kaif’s Tiger 3, which has already earned over Rs 200 crore at the box office. Tiger 3 also saw significant impact from the World Cup Final, collecting its lowest figure since its release—Rs 10.25 crore on Sunday, November 12. Directed by Aatish Kapadia, Khichdi 2 stars Supriya Pathak, Rajeev Mehta, Anang Desai, Vandana Pathak, Kirti Kulhari, and JD Majethia in prominent roles. The Khichdi franchise began as a stage play and later became a popular sitcom, web series, and film. The sequel, an adventure comedy, arrives 13 years after the first movie.

article_content: A proposal to integrate fraternities and sororities at the University of Alabama was rejected by the student senate, with 27 votes against, 5 in support, and 2 abstentions. This result has led to criticism over the continued segregation in campus Greek life, especially given the progress made since black students were first admitted over fifty years ago. The issue gained attention when the Crimson White, the university's newspaper, reported that while a few black students had been accepted by predominantly white Greek organizations, alumni objections reportedly hampered the broader push for integration. Since 1963, only one black student has officially joined these groups, with another mixed-race student admitted, but only after acceptance. University president Judy Bonner has advocated for greater inclusivity, emphasizing the goal of making the Greek system open and welcoming to all students. Her comments came as students marked 50 years since black students first enrolled at the university with campus protests calling for further change. To encourage more diversity, President Bonner also allowed for increased sorority membership and more flexible admissions policies. However, many see the senate's recent vote as a significant obstacle in the effort to end racial segregation within these organizations. Although the proposed resolution would not have directly changed Greek system policies, it was intended to publicly convey support for integration and improve the university’s image regarding diversity. The motion's sponsors, Katie Smith and Chisholm Allenlundy, expressed disappointment but said the outcome was not unexpected. Smith noted that senators had the choice and decided against the motion, while Allenlundy suggested that some may have misunderstood the resolution’s intentions to support diversity rather than criticize Greek organizations.

article_content: A climber’s helmet camera captured the dramatic moment Mark Roberts fell approximately 100 feet while climbing in Snowdonia, Wales. The incident occurred last month when a block of ice fell from above as Roberts was ascending in the Parsley Fern Gully at Cwm Glas. In the footage, Roberts can be seen raising his arm as the fall begins. Unable to self-arrest due to the steep slope, Roberts lost control and tumbled down the mountain, hitting rocks, flipping over, and losing his climbing axes. His fall lasted about thirty seconds before he halted on a ledge. After catching his breath, a shaken Roberts commented on the severity of the incident. Within thirty minutes, the Llanberis Mountain Rescue Team reached Roberts, and he was airlifted from the scene by the RAF Search and Rescue 22 Squadron from Anglesey, a team where Prince William has served. Roberts escaped with a broken ankle and bruises, and was expected to make a full recovery. Elfyn Jones of the British Mountaineering Council, who participated in the rescue, highlighted that although accidents can happen, Roberts was well equipped, including wearing a helmet that likely saved his life.

article_content: The long-standing feud between Alf-Inge Haaland and Roy Keane has returned to the spotlight thanks to recent remarks by Keane in his new autobiography. Previously, Keane admitted in his first book that he had deliberately injured Haaland during a Manchester derby in 2001, a decision he stated he did not regret. This act was intended as payback for an earlier incident in 1997 when Haaland accused Keane of exaggerating a serious knee injury during a match between Manchester United and Leeds. Recently, Haaland mocked Keane's beard on social media by posting—and soon deleting—a joke that compared Keane's facial hair to that of Saddam Hussein, suggesting humorously that Saddam's family would not appreciate the association. Haaland later told Norwegian TV2 that he doesn’t take Keane’s criticisms seriously and sees no reason to get upset, emphasizing the importance of accepting differing opinions. The origin of their conflict dates to 1997 when Keane suffered a cruciate ligament injury in a confrontation with Haaland. Haaland had implied Keane was faking his injury at the time. Four years later, Keane took revenge with a harsh tackle on Haaland, resulting in his own suspension and financial penalties after admitting the intent in his autobiography. Although Haaland never played a full game after this and began legal proceedings against Keane, he eventually withdrew the lawsuit on realizing his retirement was caused by unrelated knee problems. Haaland has shared that he has not received, nor expects, an apology from Keane. He expressed resignation over the situation but questioned the example Keane sets, particularly for younger fans, by maintaining a vengeful stance.

Ridley Scott's new biopic, 'Napoleon', delves into the life of France's former emperor, focusing not only on his military exploits but also on his tempestuous relationship with his wife Josephine, played by Vanessa Kirby. Their intense and passionate relationship is brought to life through Napoleon’s emotionally charged letters.

Joaquin Phoenix, who stars as Napoleon, told AFP in Paris that he was surprised to discover a more sentimental, vulnerable side of Napoleon, describing him as 'a teenager in love.' Phoenix characterized Napoleon as socially awkward, saying, 'He was a romantic with a mathematician’s brain.' He added that the emperor’s letters seem almost poetic, becoming endearing if not for his historical responsibility for millions of deaths.

Initially expecting Napoleon to be cold and calculating, Phoenix found the leader’s sense of humor and childlike traits unexpected. 'I waited over two decades to work with Ridley Scott again after 'Gladiator'; Scott reached out when he had a story about a 'petulant tyrant', saying, "I've got just the guy,"' Phoenix joked.

Phoenix avoided drawing comparisons between Napoleon’s wars and current world issues, noting, 'People today are experiencing real pain and grief—it wouldn’t be right to equate that with a fictional film.'

Vanessa Kirby reflected on Josephine and Napoleon's relationship, calling it compelling but 'exhausting,' marked by obsession, infatuation, and fluctuating power dynamics. Both actors cited the challenges of researching their roles, given conflicting historical accounts. Phoenix noted how simple facts like whether Napoleon was left-handed required verification, and Kirby considered Josephine as someone who changed roles as a means of survival.

In related news, the Indian government is examining the possibility of transferring unclaimed funds from the Sahara-Sebi Refund Account to the Consolidated Fund of India, ensuring options for claimed refunds. Apple is targeting ₹1 lakh crore in iPhone production in India this fiscal year, already surpassing ₹60,000 crore. In another development, Nawaz Modi, amid her separation from Gautam Singhania, seeks three-quarters of his reported $1.4 billion net worth for herself and their daughters as part of a family settlement.

article_content: John Cantlie, a British photojournalist who was kidnapped by ISIS while working in Syria over a year ago, is featured in the terror group’s latest propaganda video. This video marks the fifth installment of the 'Lend Me Your Ears' series. Appearing composed in an orange jumpsuit, Cantlie describes his experience as a detainee of ISIS for nearly two years, expressing that he feels abandoned by his government. He discusses the treatment of hostages and ISIS’s methods for targeting Western journalists. Cantlie reads what he claims are emails from the relatives of American hostages, underlining their disappointment with the U.S. government’s actions regarding the captives’ release. He contrasts this with outcomes for non-British, non-American hostages, noting that several European countries, such as France, Germany, and Denmark, succeeded in negotiating the freedom of their citizens, unlike the UK and US, who maintained a non-negotiation policy. He recalls that hostages were generally treated decently as long as they did not attempt escape, in which case punishment, including waterboarding, occurred. During their captivity, prisoners read, played games, and offered lectures among themselves. Throughout the video, Cantlie shares alleged correspondence between hostage families and government officials, emphasizing the families’ sense of desperation and helplessness. He claims that while European governments engaged in talks with ISIS, the British and American governments remained unresponsive. Cantlie says hostages initially hoped for rescue but eventually saw no action from their countries. The article references public appeals from Cantlie’s family, including his sister Jessica and his late father Paul, both of whom urged for his release. It's unclear if Cantlie was ever informed about his father's passing. The article also notes the deaths of other Western hostages—including American journalists Steven Sotloff and James Foley and British aid workers David Haines and Alan Henning—at the hands of ISIS. Cantlie questions why British and American officials chose not to negotiate, pointing out that 16 hostages from multiple European countries were freed after such efforts. Referencing various messages, Cantlie reports that American hostage families felt abandoned and expressed significant disappointment with their governments’ lack of response. Concluding this installment, Cantlie mentions an upcoming discussion about a failed rescue attempt and the emotional resilience needed to survive as a hostage.

article_content: Andy Murray of Scotland will face Roger Federer in the final of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday, after both players won their semi-final matches in straight sets on Saturday. World number four Murray defeated Argentina’s Juan Monaco 6-4, 6-1 in 85 minutes at the Qi Zhong center, reaching his second consecutive final at a Masters 1000 event. Murray broke Monaco’s serve early in the first set for a two-game lead. Although Monaco fought back and Murray double-faulted to lose his serve in the ninth game, Murray quickly recovered to take the set 6-4. In the second set, Murray twice broke Monaco’s serve to secure a comfortable win and his place in the final. “In each match I felt better. I feel like I move well on these courts and I can still get my serve through to earn enough free points,” Murray said after the match, according to AFP. Murray, aiming for his second title of the season, will play Roger Federer in the final. Federer advanced by defeating Novak Djokovic 7-5, 6-4 in the other semi-final. Federer produced impressive form to overcome Djokovic, who had beaten him in the U.S. Open semi-final last month. The Swiss star needed just over an hour to secure the first set, saving four break points in the fourth game. Federer finally broke Djokovic’s serve in the 11th game, then served out the first set before taking an early lead in the second set with two breaks of serve. Djokovic managed to recover one break but Federer closed out the win to reach his fourth final of the season. Sunday’s final is a rematch of the Toronto Masters final in August, where Murray won and currently holds a 7-5 career lead over the 16-time Grand Slam champion. Federer’s win moves him up to world number two ahead of Djokovic, with Rafael Nadal of Spain remaining at number one.

article_content: Cristiano Ronaldo, star of Real Madrid, has become the first athlete to reach 100 million followers on Facebook, surpassing the milestone on Tuesday. This achievement puts him nearly 30 million fans ahead of Barcelona’s Lionel Messi, his main rival for the title of world’s top footballer. Ronaldo's commercial influence is also evident—he currently has 30.5 million Twitter followers and recently posted six sponsored messages for Tag Heuer watches over two days. Over the weekend, Ronaldo played for Portugal against France, reinforcing his status as football's king of social media. His Facebook following alone could fill Real Madrid's Bernabeu stadium more than 1,170 times. These Tag Heuer promotional posts received 34.9 million Facebook hits and 2.4 million likes, which the company valued at over £300,000. Earlier this month, Ronaldo’s former Manchester United teammate Wayne Rooney became the first Premier League footballer to reach 10 million Twitter followers. As England’s captain, Rooney thanked his fans after reaching this milestone. He is currently the fifth most-followed footballer and the sixth most-followed athlete worldwide. Unsurprisingly, Ronaldo also tops the list of most-followed athletes on Twitter. His Facebook posts have generated a total of over 231 million likes and nearly 10 million comments. Data shows that 78 percent of Ronaldo's Facebook fans are male, but the most common fan name is Maria.

article_content: Dr. Kent Brantly, a U.S. physician who contracted Ebola while working in Liberia, has announced that his health is steadily improving. In a message released through Samaritan's Purse, Brantly thanked the medical professionals at Emory University Hospital in Atlanta who are caring for him and fellow aid worker Nancy Writebol, both currently in isolation. Brantly described the severe emotional strain he endured as he treated Ebola patients, highlighting the heartbreaking experiences and immense loss he witnessed in Liberia. He explained that his family's move to Liberia was based on a commitment to serve as missionaries through ELWA Hospital, rather than a specific intention to address Ebola. Both Brantly and Writebol received treatments including ZMapp, an experimental drug not previously tested on humans. The drug's effectiveness remains uncertain. According to Writebol's husband, David, her condition is also getting better. Despite the hope brought by these individual recoveries, ZMapp supplies are extremely limited, and the drug’s safety and efficacy have yet to be proven. The World Health Organization continues to report a rapid increase in Ebola cases in West Africa, with over 1,800 infections and close to 1,000 deaths, including many healthcare workers. WHO officials warn that the outbreak is advancing faster than containment efforts, posing a grave threat worldwide.

Explicó que su familia se mudó a Liberia respondiendo a un compromiso misionero en el hospital ELWA, y no con la intención específica de combatir el Ébola. Funcionarios de la OMS advierten que el brote avanza más rápido que los esfuerzos para contenerlo y representa una grave amenaza mundial.

article_content: A 6.8-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Alaska on Friday, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. The agency initially registered the quake at 7.1 magnitude but later downgraded it slightly. The earthquake occurred at a depth of 22 miles, about 120 miles east-southeast of Atka, Alaska, in the sparsely populated Fox Islands region of the Aleutian Islands. The epicenter was located roughly 1,030 miles west-southwest of Anchorage. The quake prompted a short-lived tsunami warning for Alaska's coastal areas, stretching from Unimak Pass to Amchitka Pass, as announced by the West Coast and Alaska Tsunami Warning Center. However, the warning was soon cancelled. No destructive tsunami occurred, and there is no tsunami danger for the coasts of Alaska, Canada, or the U.S. West Coast, according to officials. The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center also stated there was no risk of a Pacific-wide tsunami. There were no immediate reports of damage or injuries. Notably, a 7.2-magnitude earthquake had struck almost the same location in June, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

El terremoto se produjo a una profundidad de 22 millas, a unas 120 millas al este-sureste de Atka, Alaska, en la escasamente poblada región de las Islas Fox de las Islas Aleutianas. El epicentro estaba aproximadamente a 1.030 millas al oeste-suroeste de Anchorage. El sismo provocó una advertencia de tsunami de corta duración para las áreas costeras de Alaska, desde Unimak Pass hasta Amchitka Pass, según informó el Centro de Advertencia de Tsunamis de la Costa Oeste y Alaska. Sin embargo, la advertencia fue cancelada poco después. No se produjo ningún tsunami destructivo, y no existe peligro de tsunami para las costas de Alaska, Canadá ni la costa oeste de EE.UU., según las autoridades. El Centro de Advertencia de Tsunamis del Pacífico también indicó que no había riesgo de un tsunami destructivo a nivel Pacífico. No se reportaron daños ni heridos de forma inmediata. Cabe destacar que un sismo de magnitud 7,2 sacudió casi la misma zona en junio, según el Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos.

article_content:
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has expressed deep concern over the escalating conflict in Myanmar. According to the UN, fighting has displaced two million people. Guterres has called on all sides to protect civilians and to provide access for humanitarian aid. 

An alliance of three ethnic armed groups in Shan State has driven the military and police from large areas near the border with China, encouraging other opposition forces throughout the country. In Kayah State, located south of Shan along the Thai border, ethnic Karenni insurgents are attacking Loikaw, the main town, and have taken control of the university on its outskirts.

Volunteer People's Defence Forces (PDFs)—local militias formed after peaceful protests were suppressed in 2021—are launching attacks to exploit the military's setbacks in Shan State and maintain pressure on the ruling junta. PDFs are less well-armed and experienced than established ethnic armies, but are improving and often ally with seasoned ethnic fighters with decades of experience.

In Sagaing, where village-based PDFs have been fighting the military, they recently captured the town of Kawlin and are now attacking the strategically important town of Tigyaing on the Irrawaddy River. PDFs are also active around Mandalay, Myanmar's second-largest city.

The junta has lost control of much of the Indian border. Ethnic Chin insurgents now dominate their state and recently seized the border town of Rikhawdar. Further south, the Arakan Army, among the best-armed ethnic groups, has ended its ceasefire and begun attacking army and police posts. Another large force, the Karen National Union in southeastern Myanmar, is intensifying operations against military positions along major trade routes to the Thai border. Attacks against the military are also now regular in Tanintharyi, Myanmar's southernmost state.

All these armed groups remain outgunned by the military, which has Russian and Chinese aircraft, helicopters, and heavy weapons, such as multiple rocket launchers. However, the expanding resistance has over-extended Myanmar's military rulers. The air force has about 40 transport helicopters, but not all are operational, limiting the ability to move troops to trouble spots. The army also faces low morale and recruitment problems. Recent battles have seen units surrender or flee, stories which may circulate among the ranks.

The military's failure to counter-attack in Shan State after three weeks suggests limited capacity to regroup forces or potentially an underestimation of the challenge from Nay Pyi Taw, the capital. Although few believe the military regime, which seized power nearly three years ago, will soon collapse, there are still hardened units—such as the notorious Light Infantry Divisions, frequently accused of abuses—that could be more effectively deployed, though these have reportedly weakened since the coup.

If opposition forces sustain their pressure and improve coordination, elements within the junta may eventually see negotiation as necessary—a step coup leader Min Aung Hlaing has so far refused to consider.

Guterres pidió a todas las partes proteger a los civiles y permitir la entrada de ayuda humanitaria.

Una alianza de tres grupos armados étnicos en el Estado Shan ha expulsado a militares y policías de grandes zonas próximas a la frontera con China, animando a otros grupos opositores en todo el país. En el Estado Kayah, al sur de Shan y colindante con Tailandia, insurgentes étnicos karenis están atacando Loikaw, la ciudad principal, y han tomado la universidad en su periferia.

Las Fuerzas de Defensa del Pueblo (PDF), milicias locales formadas tras la represión de protestas pacíficas en 2021, lanzan ataques para aprovechar los reveses del ejército en Shan y mantener la presión sobre la junta gobernante. Las PDF cuentan con menos armas y experiencia que los ejércitos étnicos tradicionales, pero han mejorado y a menudo se alían con combatientes experimentados.

En Sagaing, las PDF locales han capturado recientemente la ciudad de Kawlin y atacan Tigyaing, localidad estratégica sobre el río Irrawaddy. Las PDF también actúan alrededor de Mandalay, la segunda mayor ciudad de Myanmar.

La junta perdió el control de gran parte de la frontera con India. Insurgentes chins dominan su estado y tomaron la ciudad fronteriza de Rikhawdar. Más al sur, el Ejército Arakan, uno de los grupos más armados, rompió el alto el fuego y lanzó ataques a puestos militares y policiales. Otra gran fuerza, la Unión Nacional Karen (en el sureste), refuerza operaciones contra posiciones militares en rutas comerciales clave a la frontera con Tailandia. Los ataques al ejército ya son habituales en Tanintharyi, el estado más austral de Myanmar.

Todos estos grupos armados siguen estando en desventaja frente a un ejército con aviones, helicópteros y armamento pesado ruso y chino. Pero la resistencia creciente ha sobrecargado a los militares. La fuerza aérea tiene unas 40 helicópteros de transporte, aunque varios están fuera de servicio, dificultando el traslado de tropas a zonas clave. El ejército sufre también problemas de moral y de reclutamiento. En combates recientes, unidades se rindieron o huyeron, historias que probablemente circulan en las filas.

La incapacidad de los militares para lanzar un contraataque en Shan tras tres semanas sugiere baja capacidad para reagrupar fuerzas, o subestimación del desafío en Nay Pyi Taw, la capital. Aunque pocos creen que el régimen impuesto hace casi tres años colapse pronto, aún existen divisiones endurecidas, como las temidas Divisiones de Infantería Ligera, acusadas de abusos, que podrían desplegarse con más efecto aunque se han visto debilitadas desde el golpe.

Si la oposición mantiene la presión y mejora su coordinación, parte de la junta podría considerar negociar, algo que el líder del golpe, Min Aung Hlaing, se niega de momento a aceptar.

article_content: H&M Group has teamed up with DBS to launch a groundbreaking green loan program aimed at making apparel supply chains more sustainable. Through this effort, suppliers are able to tap into financial support from DBS and receive guidance from sustainability experts at Guidehouse to upgrade their facilities for better environmental performance. The inaugural transaction took place in India, where a manufacturer used the green loan to invest in equipment and measures that reduce Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions. Unlike traditional banking—which typically encourages green initiatives indirectly—this program provides direct and attractive financing targeted at verified emission reduction activities. Ulrika Leverenz, H&M’s Head of Green Investment, emphasized that investing in sustainability is not just a responsible move, but also crucial for future growth, underscoring the importance of collaborative financing. Tan Su Shan, Group Head of Institutional Banking at DBS, shared that the partnership leverages DBS's Asian network to deliver practical, sustainable finance, directly enabling suppliers to improve energy efficiency and reduce emissions.

La primera transacción se concretó en la India, donde un fabricante utilizó el préstamo verde para invertir en equipos y soluciones que disminuyen las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero de Alcance 3. A diferencia de la banca tradicional, que usualmente incentiva las iniciativas verdes de manera indirecta, este programa otorga financiamiento directo y ventajoso enfocado en actividades verificadas de reducción de emisiones. Ulrika Leverenz, jefa de inversión verde de H&M, resaltó que invertir en sostenibilidad no solo es responsable, sino esencial para el éxito futuro, subrayando la relevancia de la financiación en colaboración. Por su parte, Tan Su Shan, directora de Banca Institucional de DBS, indicó que la alianza permite aprovechar la red de DBS en Asia para ofrecer financiamiento sostenible de forma práctica, permitiendo directamente a los proveedores mejorar la eficiencia energética y reducir emisiones.

article_content: Nearly half a century ago, Iceland witnessed a remarkable demonstration of solidarity when its women went on strike for gender equality. On October 24, 1975, about 90% of the country’s women refused to work, leading to widespread closures of government offices, businesses, and essential services. Households scrambled as men took up tasks traditionally done by women, highlighting women's indispensable role in society. This event, known as 'Women's Day Off' (Kvennafrí), was a powerful demand for change. The strike sparked a series of societal shifts. In 1976, Iceland’s Parliament enacted legislation guaranteeing equal pay. Vigdís Finnbogadóttir became the world’s first democratically elected female president in 1980. Three years later, women in Iceland founded the first all-female political party, successfully boosting gender parity across politics and driving progress on issues like accessible childcare, parental leave, and gender quotas in corporate boardrooms. Today, Iceland continues to be recognized as a global leader in gender equality, topping the World Economic Forum’s Global Gender Gap Index for 14 years straight. However, significant challenges remain. The gender pay gap persists at 21%. Women still bear a disproportionate share of unpaid and underpaid caregiving and domestic work. Additionally, two in five women in Iceland experience violence at some point in their lives. Acknowledging that continued effort is needed, more than 100,000 women, nonbinary people, and male allies participated in another nationwide strike on October 24, 2023. Prime Minister Katrín Jakobsdóttir and her cabinet joined the effort, calling attention to the need to close the wage gap and end gender-based violence. The movement highlights a growing recognition: gender equality is not only a moral imperative but also a practical necessity for building a sustainable, livable world. Iceland’s former president, Vigdís Finnbogadóttir, argues that women—alongside men—are key to addressing the world’s biggest challenges, including climate change and global conflict. Research shows that greater female involvement in peace processes leads to more durable agreements. Countries with more women in leadership take more ambitious action on climate and see improved health outcomes. Despite this, men still hold over 90% of head-of-government roles and nearly 95% of Fortune Global 500 CEO positions worldwide. At the United Nations’ COP27 climate summit, two-thirds of negotiation teams were men, even though climate change disproportionately affects women and girls. Achieving gender equality requires collective action, with leaders of every gender working to remove structural barriers and promote inclusive, people-first policies. Iceland's ongoing activism demonstrates that persistent, united efforts can drive change. For a livable world for future generations, more women, nonbinary people, and allies must be in leadership at every level.
translated_content: Hace casi medio siglo, Islandia fue testigo de una impresionante muestra de solidaridad cuando las mujeres hicieron huelga por la igualdad de género. El 24 de octubre de 1975, cerca del 90% de las mujeres del país se negó a trabajar, causando el cierre de oficinas gubernamentales, negocios y servicios esenciales. Los hogares se vieron alterados mientras los hombres asumían tareas tradicionalmente realizadas por mujeres, lo que destacó el papel fundamental de ellas en la sociedad. Este evento, conocido como 'Día Libre de las Mujeres' (Kvennafrí), marcó una demanda de cambio. La huelga desencadenó varios cambios sociales. En 1976, el Parlamento islandés aprobó una ley que garantizaba la igualdad salarial. Vigdís Finnbogadóttir se convirtió en 1980 en la primera presidenta elegida democráticamente en el mundo. Tres años después, mujeres islandesas fundaron el primer partido político compuesto solo por mujeres, impulsando la paridad de género en la política y avances en temas como cuidado infantil accesible, licencias parentales y cuotas de género en las juntas directivas. Actualmente, Islandia sigue liderando en igualdad de género a nivel global, ocupando el primer lugar en el Índice Global de Brecha de Género del Foro Económico Mundial durante 14 años seguidos. No obstante, persisten desafíos significativos. La brecha salarial es del 21%. Las mujeres siguen soportando la mayor parte del trabajo de cuidado doméstico, muchas veces no remunerado o insuficientemente pagado. Dos de cada cinco mujeres en Islandia sufren violencia en algún momento de sus vidas. Conscientes de que la lucha debe continuar, más de 100,000 mujeres, personas no binarias y aliados hombres participaron en otra huelga nacional el 24 de octubre de 2023. La primera ministra Katrín Jakobsdóttir y su gabinete apoyaron la iniciativa, resaltando la urgencia de cerrar la brecha salarial y poner fin a la violencia de género. Este movimiento demuestra una toma de conciencia creciente: la igualdad de género no es solo un deber moral, sino también una necesidad práctica para un mundo sostenible y habitable. La expresidenta islandesa Vigdís Finnbogadóttir afirma que las mujeres—junto con los hombres—son esenciales para enfrentar los mayores desafíos globales, como el cambio climático y los conflictos armados. Las investigaciones muestran que cuanto más participan las mujeres en procesos de paz, más duraderos son los acuerdos. Los países con mayor representación femenina en liderazgo asumen medidas más ambiciosas frente al clima y logran mejores resultados en salud. Sin embargo, los hombres siguen ocupando más del 90% de los principales puestos gobernativos y casi el 95% de los cargos ejecutivos en empresas Fortune Global 500. En la cumbre climática COP27 de la ONU, dos tercios de los equipos negociadores eran hombres, aunque el cambio climático afecta más a mujeres y niñas. Alcanzar la igualdad requiere acción colectiva, con líderes de todos los géneros eliminando barreras estructurales y promoviendo políticas inclusivas centradas en las personas. La movilización persistente de Islandia demuestra que la acción unida puede generar cambios. Para un mundo habitable en el futuro, se necesitan más mujeres, personas no binarias y aliados en posiciones de liderazgo en todos los ámbitos.

article_content: Doctors are investigating after a seemingly healthy Missouri mother and her teenage son died just days apart due to an unexplained illness. Nineteen-year-old Zack Smith passed away at a St. Peters hospital on Sunday; his mother, 48-year-old Rhona Smith, died the following Thursday morning. Health officials in St. Charles County are consulting with infectious disease specialists to determine the cause of their rapid decline. Family members noted doctors suggested the pair may have contracted a particularly severe strain of the flu, though there is no official confirmation. According to a GoFundMe page set up for the family, Zack sought treatment at St. Joseph's Health Center on Friday with flu-like symptoms and coughing up blood. His condition quickly worsened, and over two days, he was diagnosed with pneumonia and a staph infection, which led to organ failure and cardiac arrest. He passed away on Sunday morning. Doctors reportedly told his family the illness appeared to be caused by a flu strain not covered by the current flu vaccine. Family member Scott Dyer indicated some suspicion it may have originated abroad, but health officials have not confirmed this. Following Zack's death, Rhona posted on Facebook expressing deep grief. She leaves behind three other children, ages 12, 16, and 21. On Wednesday, Rhona developed fever and severe pain, prompting her family to take her to urgent care, where extremely high blood sugar was detected, despite no diabetes diagnosis. Her health declined rapidly, and despite repeated resuscitation attempts, she died less than 12 hours after being admitted. Doctors have advised family members to get tested for the flu and have chest X-rays. The local health department is conducting an autopsy and awaiting lab results to determine the cause of death. CDC data indicates high flu activity in the United States, with over 13,300 hospitalizations and 86 pediatric deaths reported this season. The CDC also notes that this season’s flu began earlier than usual and may last longer than average. The Smith family is seeking support as they cope with this tragedy.

article_content: The business world is entering a pivotal era where handling data as it flows—streaming data—is transforming operations and offering new opportunities. Tech giants have already leveraged this shift, using live data for everything from instant recommendations to real-time fraud prevention and supply chain optimization. Unlike traditional stored data, streaming data is constantly moving, requiring unique methods to capture its value before it's gone. Businesses now gather massive amounts of this data through modern architectures like message buses, data pipelines, and microservices. Stream processing stands apart because it analyzes information in motion, allowing businesses to act instantly without delay. This immediate approach is essential for situations where every millisecond counts. Currently, organizations face two main hurdles. First, there’s no clear leader among numerous event streaming platforms, making technology choices uncertain. Second, most businesses are still rooted in old habits—using traditional databases to collect and process data long after events happen. Integrating these two approaches is difficult since they weren’t designed to work together. Yet, stream processing unlocks powerful real-time applications. For example, tailored marketing offers, fraud detection, and speedy logistics all depend on rapid analysis of live data combined with key bits of historical information. These focused use cases require only specific data, making them more manageable and effective. To harness the benefits, businesses should identify their pressing needs, map out which real-time and historical data can solve them, and ensure actions can be taken instantly to boost revenue or customer satisfaction. Selecting the best stream processing technology involves ensuring compatibility with diverse databases and data flows across the enterprise. The most successful systems will be able to work flexibly with any data, at any time, to empower truly real-time decision making. Ultimately, organizations that integrate inclusive, adaptable stream processing will be best positioned to thrive as business grows ever more real-time.

En definitiva, las organizaciones que integren procesamiento de streams inclusivo y adaptable estarán mejor posicionadas para prosperar a medida que los negocios se vuelvan cada vez más orientados al tiempo real.

article_content: The United States has dismissed as 'absurd' Russian claims that Ukraine and Western countries were behind the recent anti-Israel riot at Makhachkala airport in Dagestan. U.S. officials say these accusations are part of a familiar strategy where Russia seeks to place blame elsewhere. Russian President Vladimir Putin, during a televised Security Council session, asserted that the riot was incited from abroad, accusing Western intelligence services and Ukraine of stirring unrest in Russia. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov and Dagestan's governor, Sergei Melikov, voiced similar allegations. The riot involved hundreds of people—many wielding Palestinian flags and shouting antisemitic slogans—storming the airport just before a flight from Tel Aviv was due to land. The situation reflects tensions in Dagestan, a mostly Muslim region, as the conflict in Gaza continues. According to online videos, rioters rushed through the airport and reportedly checked the documents of passengers, apparently searching for Israeli passports. Authorities eventually restored order, arresting over 60 individuals. The Russian health ministry said 20 people, including police, were injured, with two in critical condition. Russian officials have also accused the 'Morning Dagestan' Telegram channel of involvement, saying it shared flight information to incite the riot. The channel has prior associations with Ilya Ponomarev, a former Russian MP now living in Ukraine. Both the channel and Ponomarev deny any current connection. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the riot and denied any Ukrainian role. U.S. National Security Council spokesperson John Kirby dismissed Russia’s accusations as 'classic Russian rhetoric' designed to deflect domestic issues, comparing the riot to historical antisemitic pogroms. Israel’s government also denounced the attacks, urging Russian officials to protect Jewish and Israeli citizens and to respond firmly against those responsible for the violence.

article_content: On Friday, a series of car bombs struck Shiite pilgrims south of Baghdad, resulting in at least 32 deaths and leaving 154 injured, according to Iraq’s Interior Ministry. Police report that the blasts occurred in quick succession in the city of Karbala, where large crowds had gathered at the Imam Hussein shrine. The pilgrims had come together to mark Arbaeen, which concludes the 40-day mourning period following Ashura, a significant event remembering the death of Imam Hussein—the Prophet Mohammed’s grandson. His killing in Karbala in 680 A.D. is a historical moment that led to a major division between Sunni and Shiite Muslims. Separate from the Karbala attacks, another bombing in Baghdad targeted Shiite pilgrims, killing one person and wounding 15 others.

article_content: A deceased black pit bull terrier was found abandoned on a street in Detroit, her body covered in white graffiti and a rope tied tightly around her neck. The graffiti spelled 'PBS' along her flank and also marked her back and legs. The exact cause of the dog's death remains unknown, with no visible injuries present. The Michigan Humane Society (MHS) has offered a $2,500 reward for information regarding the incident. Authorities have not yet determined the meaning behind the 'PBS' tag or identified those responsible for the graffiti and abandonment. According to MHS spokesman Kevin Hatman, it is not uncommon in Detroit for graffiti taggers to target animal remains, treating them as blank canvases similar to walls or abandoned properties. Hatman described this as a troubling example of random acts of animal cruelty. The MHS is awaiting the results of a necropsy to clarify the cause of death. Daniel Carlisle, founder of the no-kill Detroit Dog Rescue shelter, noted that pit bulls, often referred to as the 'Detroit dog,' comprise roughly 80 percent of his group’s rescues. Hatman added that pit bulls represent about 35 to 40 percent of the dogs taken in by the MHS, highlighting a persistent pattern of exploitation of the breed in the city.

article_content: Reliance Retail is set to take over Sephora’s Indian operations after Arvind Fashions Limited agreed to sell Arvind Beauty Brand Retail Limited, responsible for Sephora in India, for Rs 216 crore in an all-cash deal, which also clears existing loans. In fiscal year 2022-23, ABBRL recorded a revenue of Rs 336.7 crore (7.6% of Arvind Fashions’ total turnover) and a net worth of Rs 10.6 crore (1% of the company’s assets). AFL will use the proceeds to grow its own brands and pay down debt. Sephora currently runs 26 stores across India, offering premium cosmetics, skincare, hair products, and fragrances. Industry leaders view the sector as ripe for expansion, fueled by growing incomes, urban trends, and social media influences. Alia Gogi, Sephora’s Asia President, says the company is eager to introduce new international beauty brands to India, while Reliance Retail’s V Subramaniam highlights the opportunity to reach more young, fashion-conscious consumers. The Indian beauty and personal care industry is estimated at $17 billion and expanding rapidly at 11% CAGR, marking it as a key market for future growth. Reliance Retail manages a vast network of over 18,650 outlets and reported consolidated revenue of Rs 260,364 crore ($31.7 billion) for the financial year ending March 2023. Other updates: Indian telecom firms claim global tech companies using WhatsApp to send business messages are bypassing regulations and causing revenue losses. The government has involved Apple in a probe about alleged iPhone hacking targeting prominent Indian figures. The DGCA reported to the courts that lessors can reclaim Go First aircraft and engines, affecting the bankrupt airline’s prospects.

article_content: The United Kingdom and Ireland have been chosen to host the 2028 UEFA European Football Championship. Italy and Turkey will co-organize the tournament in 2032 after merging their bids during the summer. UEFA announced these decisions at a meeting in Switzerland, with Turkey withdrawing from the 2028 bidding to join Italy for 2032. This move made the joint proposal from England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland the favorite for 2028. For the 2028 championship, six stadiums in England—including Wembley, plus club venues for Aston Villa, Manchester City, Newcastle, Tottenham, and Everton’s soon-to-open stadium in Liverpool—will be involved. National stadiums in Ireland, Scotland, Wales, and a planned new stadium in Belfast’s Casement Park are also part of the hosting plan. UEFA aims for both the 2024 and 2028 Euros to bring in at least €2 billion in revenue, seeking to restore reserves over €500 million after pandemic-related depletion. Turkey will finally host a European Championship after several previous unsuccessful attempts, such as losing by one vote to France for Euro 2016. The combined bid with Italy for 2032 also lessens concerns about Italy finishing major stadium upgrades, as each nation only needs to provide five stadiums. Although UEFA typically allows co-hosting only between neighboring countries, Italy and Turkey—despite their capitals being over 1,400 kilometers apart—have been granted an exception. On the global stage, FIFA has taken multi-country tournaments further: the 2030 World Cup will span six countries on three continents. The initial European bid, which started with Spain and Portugal, expanded to include Morocco, Argentina, Paraguay, and inaugural World Cup host Uruguay. Ukraine was involved earlier but was quietly dropped. This arrangement let FIFA accelerate the opening of bidding for the 2034 World Cup, limited to Asia and Oceania, where Saudi Arabia is considered the leading contender.

La UEFA anunció estas decisiones en una reunión en Suiza, donde Turquía se retiró de la candidatura para 2028 para aliarse con Italia en la de 2032. Esto convirtió a la propuesta conjunta de Inglaterra, Irlanda del Norte, Escocia, Gales y la República de Irlanda en la favorita para 2028. Para el torneo de 2028, se utilizarán seis estadios en Inglaterra, incluidos Wembley y los de los clubes Aston Villa, Manchester City, Newcastle, Tottenham y el nuevo estadio de Everton en Liverpool que está en construcción. También se emplearán los estadios nacionales de Irlanda, Escocia, Gales y un estadio planificado en Casement Park, Belfast. La UEFA busca que tanto la Eurocopa 2024 como la de 2028 generen al menos 2.000 millones de euros cada una, con el objetivo de recuperar reservas de más de 500 millones de euros tras el impacto de la pandemia. Turquía finalmente será anfitriona de una Eurocopa luego de varios intentos fallidos, como la derrota por un voto ante Francia para la edición de 2016. La candidatura conjunta con Italia para 2032 también reduce la preocupación sobre si Italia completaría las mejoras en sus estadios, ya que ahora cada país debe aportar solo cinco. Aunque la UEFA generalmente solo permite coorganización entre países vecinos, Italia y Turquía —cuyas capitales están a más de 1.400 kilómetros de distancia— recibieron una excepción. En un nivel global, la FIFA ha ido más lejos: el Mundial 2030 se jugará en seis países repartidos en tres continentes. La propuesta europea que inició con España y Portugal incluyó luego a Marruecos, Argentina, Paraguay y Uruguay, el país anfitrión del primer Mundial. Ucrania formó parte de la propuesta en un principio, pero fue retirada sin una explicación oficial. Este acuerdo permitió a la FIFA adelantar el proceso de candidaturas para el Mundial 2034, limitado a Asia y Oceanía, donde Arabia Saudita es vista como la favorita para ganar la sede.

article_content: A female western lowland gorilla born last month at the Gladys Porter Zoo in Brownsville, Texas, is heading to Ohio after her mother refused to care for her. Born on January 29, the baby gorilla remains unnamed. Since her birth, staff at the Gladys Porter Zoo have provided her with around-the-clock care, feeding her every two hours. The infant's mother, Kiazi, ignored her and walked away, according to Zoo Director Jerry Stones. 'Every once in a while there’s a female that does that,' he explained. The father is a silverback named Moja. To provide her with the best chance for social development, the gorilla will be moved this week to the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden. Experts hope she will bond with two adult female gorillas who may serve as surrogate mothers. Kiazi was transferred to the Gladys Porter Zoo in 2011 from the Pittsburg Zoo & PPG Aquarium, as part of an Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA) species survival breeding program. She was originally on a breeding loan from the Cincinnati Zoo. Zoo staff, including keeper Cindy Stones, have been deeply involved in hand-feeding and caring for the little gorilla around the clock since her mother’s rejection.

Seventeen years after a cargo ship lost its load, Lego pieces still wash up on Cornwall's beaches, creating a unique treasure hunt for locals and visitors. On February 13, 1997, the Tokio Express was hit by an enormous wave about 20 miles west of Land's End during its journey from Rotterdam to New York. The force of the wave caused 62 containers to fall into the sea, including one filled with nearly five million Lego pieces.

Most of the lost Lego pieces were sea-themed, such as cutlasses, octopuses, scuba tanks, and flippers. The ship's manifest showed that 4,756,940 pieces fell overboard, with more than three million buoyant enough to float. For years, collectors have scoured the Cornish coast for these elusive toys. Now, rare finds like dragons and octopuses are considered prize discoveries.

Tracey Williams, a beachcomber from Newquay, remembers when children would find and sell Lego dragons in the late 1990s. Today, finding an octopus or dragon is viewed as a major achievement among enthusiasts. US oceanographer Curtis Ebbesmeyer, who tracks marine debris, suggests that the Lego could travel to beaches anywhere in the world, though confirmed sightings are mostly from Cornwall.

Environmental campaigners warn the lost Lego highlights the persistent problem of marine litter. Plastic debris from container spills can remain in the ocean for decades, threatening wildlife. Martin Dorey, founder of the 2 Minute Beach Clean initiative, stresses that while insurance may cover financial losses, the environmental damage often remains unresolved. On average, 2,683 shipping containers are lost at sea each year, adding to global marine pollution.

article_content: At a recent United Nations Security Council meeting focused on maintaining international peace through collaborative development, India firmly rejected Pakistan’s repeated references to Kashmir, describing them as unnecessary and routine. The session was held under China’s leadership, and Pakistan’s UN Ambassador, Munir Akram, again raised the Kashmir issue. In reply, R. Madhu Sudan, a representative from India at the UN, stated he would briefly dismiss what he called ‘unwarranted and habitual’ comments against India and declined to further address them. Tensions between the two countries have increased since India revoked Jammu and Kashmir’s special status in August 2019 by abrogating Article 370, leading Pakistan to downgrade diplomatic ties and expel India’s envoy. Since then, Pakistan has consistently brought up the Kashmir issue at the United Nations. India maintains that the changes concerning Jammu and Kashmir are purely internal matters and emphasizes that improved relations with Pakistan depend on an atmosphere without terrorism or hostility.

article_content: Even Britain’s renowned spy agencies, which inspired James Bond, cannot unravel the mystery behind a secret World War II message discovered with the remains of a carrier pigeon in a house chimney. The code’s meaning seems to have been lost nearly 70 years ago, along with the ill-fated pigeon that David Martin found in his chimney in Bletchingley, Surrey, England. Martin recently came across the pigeon’s skeleton, and surprisingly, the encoded message was still intact inside a small red canister attached to the bird’s leg. Now, curators at the Pigeon Museum at Bletchley Park are attempting to trace the origins of two alphanumeric pigeon identifiers recorded in the message, according to the UK intelligence agency GCHQ. "If these identifiers are solved and their wartime roles established, they could help us decode the message," GCHQ explained about the pigeon’s numbers. To a casual observer, the message is impossible to understand. Handwritten on a slip of paper labeled "Pigeon Service," the note consists of 27 groups of five letters. The text begins with "AOAKN" and "HVPKD," but the groups as a whole make no sense. Cracking the message would require both specific codebooks and possibly a 'one-time pad' encryption system. Those materials were typically destroyed after use, GCHQ noted. While there’s a slight chance a codebook survived, the agency says that without the relevant keys and details of any additional encryption, decryption is likely impossible. The one-time pad approach offered extra security: a random key, used for just one message, made the code unbreakable if kept secret, but required both sender and receiver to share the same key ahead of time. Three aspects add to the mystery: the message is undated, 'X02'—the destination—is not identified, and analysts cannot confirm the sender or his military unit. "Unfortunately, much of the crucial information to place the message in context is missing," GCHQ acknowledged. The sender’s closing appears to read "Sjt W Stot," using the term "Sjt" for "serjeant," an older spelling of "sergeant," suggesting an army connection. Identifying both 'Sjt Stot' and recipient 'X02' could help researchers uncover more details. During World War II, around 250,000 pigeons helped deliver messages for all branches of the British military and Special Operations Executive. Traversing dangerous routes from mainland Europe, these pigeons faced enemy birds and enemy fire to deliver their messages. "Even though we haven’t yet unlocked the message brought back by this brave carrier pigeon, it stands as a testament to the wartime code-makers, whose secure methods still hold strong today under scrutiny," said GCHQ.

El significado del código parece haberse perdido hace casi 70 años, junto con la paloma desafortunada que David Martin encontró en su chimenea en Bletchingley, Surrey, Inglaterra. Recientemente, Martin encontró el esqueleto de la paloma y, sorprendentemente, el mensaje codificado seguía intacto dentro de un pequeño cilindro rojo atado a la pata del ave. Ahora, los curadores del Museo de Palomas en Bletchley Park intentan rastrear el origen de dos identificadores alfanuméricos de la paloma presentes en el mensaje, según la agencia de inteligencia británica GCHQ. "Si se resuelven estos identificadores y se establecen sus funciones durante la guerra, podrían ayudarnos a descifrar el mensaje", explicó GCHQ sobre los números de la paloma. Para un observador casual, el mensaje es imposible de entender. Escrito a mano en un papelito marcado como "Pigeon Service", la nota consta de 27 grupos de cinco letras. El texto comienza con "AOAKN" y "HVPKD", pero los grupos, en conjunto, no tienen sentido. Descifrar el mensaje requeriría tanto libros de códigos específicos como posiblemente un sistema de cifrado "one-time pad". GCHQ señaló que estos materiales normalmente se destruían tras su uso. Aunque hay una pequeña posibilidad de que algún libro de códigos haya sobrevivido, la agencia indica que sin las claves relevantes y detalles de cualquier cifrado adicional, es muy poco probable lograr la decodificación. El método one-time pad ofrecía seguridad adicional: una clave aleatoria, utilizada solo para un mensaje, hacía el código irrompible si se mantenía en secreto, aunque exigía que el emisor y el receptor compartieran la clave de antemano. Tres aspectos acrecientan el misterio: el mensaje no tiene fecha, 'X02'—el destino—no está identificado, y los analistas no pueden confirmar al remitente ni a su unidad militar. "Desafortunadamente, mucha de la información crucial para ubicar el mensaje en su contexto está faltando", reconoció GCHQ. El cierre del mensaje parece decir "Sjt W Stot"; 'Sjt' es una forma antigua de escribir "sergeant", lo que sugiere un vínculo con el ejército. Identificar tanto a 'Sjt Stot' como al destinatario 'X02' podría ayudar a los investigadores a obtener más datos. article_content: Jennifer Rosoff, a 35-year-old advertising executive, died after falling from the balcony of her high-rise Manhattan apartment early on August 3, 2013. Law enforcement officials reported that she had been leaning against a railing in need of repair, which gave way, causing her to fall 17 floors. Rosoff, who was on a first date with someone she had met online, stepped out to smoke a cigarette on her apartment balcony at Stonehenge 57 on East 57th Street. When her date warned her the railing wasn't safe, she responded that she 'did it all the time.' Moments later, the railing collapsed after she propped her leg on it to stretch, and she fell, landing on construction scaffolding below. Authorities said that every balcony in the building was considered defective or not up to code. The Department of Buildings stated that the building’s management was six months late submitting a required facade report, facing a $1,500 fine. Emergency crews pronounced Rosoff dead at the scene. Witnesses reported the metal balcony railings were bent and twisted, and photos showed the top two rails were bent down in a V-shape. Sources said Rosoff’s date told police he heard two sharp sounds before the railing gave way. Police cleared him of any wrongdoing. Neighbors described hearing a loud noise similar to a gunshot or heavy punch when Rosoff fell. Her sister, Alexis Treeby, remembered her as a lovely, generous person who did charity work. Rosoff was Director of Sales at Triplelift, a digital advertising company, and formerly worked at Lucky magazine and The New Yorker. Officials collected the broken railing for examination and issued a vacate order for the building’s balconies, citing perilous conditions. The Department of Buildings said inspectors were investigating the safety of all balconies. Triplelift’s CEO Eric Berry expressed that the company was deeply saddened by Rosoff's sudden loss, describing her as highly respected, energetic, and humorous. Rosoff’s colleagues and family were devastated by her death. The building, constructed before World War II, reportedly has corner balconies only on its higher floors. The structure had previously been cited for a construction violation.

article_content: A United Nigeria Airlines domestic flight, set to travel from Lagos to Abuja, unexpectedly landed in Asaba—almost 200 miles away from its intended destination—on Saturday. The airline clarified in a statement that although passengers were told by flight attendants they had arrived in Abuja, the plane had actually landed in Asaba. This mix-up is comparable to booking a flight to New York and landing in Washington, DC instead. Salihu Tanko Yakasai, a local politician and passenger, posted on X (formerly known as Twitter) that after they landed, the cabin crew announced they were in Abuja. Passengers soon realized they were in Asaba, leading to confusion until the pilot informed them that the flight plan provided from Lagos had been incorrect. Many passengers experienced uncertainty about their location until the pilot's announcement clarified the situation. United Nigeria Airlines issued an apology, explaining that adverse weather conditions in Abuja required the flight to divert to Asaba. The airline noted that a mistaken cabin announcement had contributed to the confusion. According to United Nigeria Airlines, the flight later continued on to Abuja as planned. Social media posts documented passenger reactions, but these accounts have not been independently verified. Such incidents have occurred before in aviation: in 2014, a Southwest Airlines plane landed at the wrong airport in Missouri, and in 2019, a British Airways flight intended for Düsseldorf instead landed in Edinburgh due to a flight plan error. Requests for comment from United Nigeria Airlines and Salihu Tanko Yakasai were not immediately returned.

article_content: Michael Schumacher, widely known as the most successful Formula 1 driver, remains in critical condition after suffering a significant head injury in a skiing accident in the French Alps, hospital authorities confirmed. The 44-year-old German, who retired from Formula 1 for the second time in 2012, fell and hit his head on a rock while skiing off-piste at the Meribel resort, according to the resort’s director. Schumacher was transported to the University Hospital Center of Grenoble, arriving in a coma and undergoing emergency brain surgery. Medical sources have not released full details regarding the extent of his injuries or his prognosis. The fall occurred on unmarked slopes between the Georges Bauduis and La Biche pistes. Christophe Gernignon-Lecomte, the resort’s director, specified that Schumacher was wearing a helmet and was with others at the time of the accident. Rescue teams responded quickly, reaching him within minutes and airlifting him to a nearby hospital. Authorities are still investigating the cause of the accident, clarifying that it was not related to an avalanche. Sabine Kehm, Schumacher’s spokesperson, confirmed the incident happened during a private ski trip. She stated he was wearing a helmet, was not alone, and requested privacy regarding regular health updates. A first-aid responder from Meribel, who preferred to remain anonymous, stated Schumacher was initially conscious at the accident scene and that his injuries were not immediately considered life-threatening. He was first treated at the Hospital of Moutiers before being transferred to the trauma center at Grenoble. Former French F1 driver Olivier Panis visited the hospital to show support, sharing his concerns and respect for Schumacher as a friend and accomplished champion. Schumacher, who entered Formula 1 in 1991, holds seven world titles—five with Ferrari—and after returning to the sport with Mercedes in 2010, claimed a third-place finish at the 2012 European Grand Prix in Valencia as his top result during his comeback. Meribel ski resort is renowned for its challenging slopes located mostly above the treeline, which can create disorientation for even skilled skiers, according to former SKI Magazine editor Paul Hochman. British journalist Kevin Garside commented that Schumacher, though known for pushing boundaries both on the racing circuit and the slopes, was careful about safety and highly aware of skiing risks.

George Zimmerman sold his original painting, which celebrates 'liberty and justice,' on eBay today for $100,000. The artwork, an 18-by-24-inch oil on canvas, depicts a U.S. flag in blue tones with the words 'God, One Nation, With Liberty and Justice for All.' It attracted 96 bids from 24 bidders. Zimmerman, formerly a neighborhood watch captain, posted the painting online on Monday, less than a week after domestic abuse charges were dropped against him when his girlfriend, Samantha Scheibe, chose not to pursue them.

Zimmerman's attorney, Jayne Weintraub, confirmed that he created and posted the artwork to earn income, since he has not been able to find regular employment. The auction winner, whose identity is undisclosed, will receive the signed piece via expedited mail from Sanford, Florida, for $40 shipping. 

Listed under the eBay username 'theRealGeorgeZ,' Zimmerman described the painting as his first hand-painted work and offered personal delivery within the continental U.S. In the listing, he wrote that art is a therapeutic outlet for him, saying, 'I found a creative way to express myself, my emotions, and the symbols that represent my experiences.' The auction began with a $50 starting bid but quickly soared past $90,000 following media attention. 

Despite widespread public attention and ongoing controversy surrounding his 2012 acquittal in the shooting death of unarmed 17-year-old Trayvon Martin, Zimmerman maintained a positive tone, joking that making art allows him to stay indoors and reflect. He closed his auction remarks with: 'I hope you enjoy owning this piece as much as I enjoyed creating it. Your friend, George Zimmerman.'

article_content: Amber Vinson, a 29-year-old ICU nurse who contracted Ebola while caring for Thomas Eric Duncan—the first patient to be diagnosed with Ebola in the U.S.—shared that her engagement ring and wedding binder were incinerated during the hazardous materials clean-up of her Dallas home. The ring, given to her by fiancé Derrick Markray, was lost among her personal belongings as hazmat crews destroyed items to prevent the spread of Ebola. Vinson expressed devastation over losing these sentimental items, especially after infectious disease experts suggested that standard decontamination methods like bleach might have sufficed. Despite this personal loss, Vinson found moments of support and hope. She received encouragement from Markray and her family, and was visited by former President George W. Bush at Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital in Dallas, where he thanked medical staff for their efforts during the outbreak. Vinson faced public criticism for flying from Texas to Ohio after treating Duncan. She maintained that she strictly followed instructions from her hospital and the CDC and felt healthy during her travels, checking her temperature multiple times with no sign of illness. She was twice cleared to travel, and only reported a fever upon her return to Dallas. Vinson recalled her days in quarantine as a blur, marked by uncertainty about her survival. She described the training she received for treating Ebola as a 'crash course,' noting inadequate instruction on using protective equipment. Learning that fellow nurse Nina Pham had also contracted Ebola deepened her understanding of the risks involved. While in Ohio, Vinson kept in close contact with her family and friends. She was transferred to Emory University Hospital in Atlanta for specialized care, received blood plasma from Ebola survivor Dr. Kent Brantly, and was declared free of the virus on October 28. A GoFundMe campaign raised $20,000 to support her, and Vinson emphasized her sense of duty, saying she would not hesitate to care for Ebola patients again. Her colleague Nina Pham was also declared virus-free after treatment in Maryland.

article_content: Adam Struck, founding partner of Struck Capital, has stated that portfolio companies should not hire individuals who openly sympathize with one of the world’s most tragic terrorist attacks. He is referring to the October 7 Hamas-led attack on Israel, which resulted in over 1,400 deaths and has been recognized as a terrorist act by the US government. Struck has committed never to hire anyone who supports Hamas, urging more than 75 businesses he has backed to implement similar hiring standards. Struck was joined by two other Jewish American tech executives, Michael Broukhim (co-CEO and co-founder of FabFitFun) and Matt Frischer (co-founder of Protect), in urging companies to make distinctions between supporting Hamas and expressing concern for Palestinian civilians. They emphasized that sympathy for Palestinian rights and opposition to Hamas are not mutually exclusive, though this distinction has at times been lost in the aftermath of the attacks. Other business leaders have adopted similar policies, with some companies rescinding job offers to candidates who blamed Israel for the violence or expressed support for Hamas. Bill Ackman, CEO of Pershing Square, publicly called for the disclosure of Harvard students who signed a letter attributing responsibility for the attacks to Israel, stating this would inform hiring decisions. Multiple law students from Harvard, Columbia, and NYU have lost job offers following statements and organizational affiliations related to the Israel-Hamas conflict. In interviews with Insider, Struck, Broukhim, and Frischer clarified the boundaries they set in hiring. Broukhim stated unequivocally that he would not hire individuals who supported Hamas, calling it a clear decision as a CEO. He did say, however, that he might reconsider if people who signed such statements reversed their position promptly, as some student groups ultimately did. Broukhim differentiates between explicit support for Hamas and participation in general pro-Palestinian protests, stating that only support for Hamas would disqualify a candidate at FabFitFun. Frischer, whose company Protect develops video safety technology, echoed these views, noting that supporting a group designated as a terrorist organization—even setting aside personal views—is a disqualifier. While he does not conflate general pro-Palestinian activism with support for terrorism, he would avoid hiring anyone who could present potential risks to staff or company culture. Frischer added that he would not exclude candidates for participating in pro-Palestinian rallies, even those featuring controversial slogans, unless it was clear the event was organized to support Hamas. Struck maintains a nuanced position, supporting debate and sympathy for Palestinian civilians or criticism of Israeli policy, but unequivocally condemning rhetoric glorifying violence or Hamas. He warns that hiring individuals unable to distinguish between these positions could harm a company’s moral and rational foundations. Ultimately, all three leaders emphasize the importance of maintaining a clear boundary between legitimate advocacy for Palestinian rights and explicit support for organizations promoting violence.

article_content: HomeToGo, a vacation rental marketplace, has released the results of its annual 2023-24 Ski Season Report, assessing the top 48 ski destinations in North America. The evaluation considers factors such as traveler interest, affordability, lift ticket and accommodation prices, chairlift capacity, and average snow depth. The report names Schweitzer Mountain in Idaho as the top overall ski destination for 2023/24 due to its excellent snow conditions, affordability, substantial lift capacity, and extensive ski terrain. Schweitzer Mountain offers 2,900 acres of skiable terrain and is located in the Selkirk Mountains in northern Idaho. Skiers can enjoy views spanning three states, Canada, and Lake Pend Oreille. Taylor Prather, Marketing & PR at Schweitzer Mountain, highlights the resort’s accessibility from Spokane International Airport, the diverse terrain, the appeal of the local mountain community, and ongoing investment, with $50 million spent on improvements over the past five years, including new lodging and enhanced on-mountain experiences. The report ranks Park City (Utah), Whistler Blackcomb (British Columbia), Mount Baker (Washington), and Palisades Tahoe (California) among the top five ski resorts overall. HomeToGo’s report also identifies the most affordable and most expensive ski destinations. Mission Ridge Ski Area in Washington is the most affordable, with a combined price of $178.37 for lift tickets and lodging. It receives about 200 inches of annual snowfall and is known for its dry, powdery snow. Other affordable locations are Mount Bachelor (Oregon), Gore Mountain (New York), Jay Peak (Vermont), and Schweitzer Mountain (Idaho). Aspen Mountain in Colorado is the most expensive, averaging $608 daily for accommodations and lift tickets, followed by Deer Valley (Utah), Beaver Creek (Colorado), and Vail (Colorado). The average daily adult lift ticket among featured destinations is $198. Sunday River (Maine) offers the lowest lift ticket price at $65, while Deer Valley (Utah) has the highest at $279. Kimberly in British Columbia is noted as the 'hidden gem' for having the lowest search popularity and offers 80 slopes. Across all listed destinations, the average chairlift capacity is 29,889 people per hour. Park City, Utah, offers the highest capacity, accommodating over 81,000 skiers hourly.

A federal judge ruled on Monday that Dominic Adesanya, 23, is incompetent to stand trial and ordered him to undergo 45 days of additional psychiatric evaluation and treatment. During the hearing, Adesanya, upon hearing the judge declare him "incompetent," repeated the word aloud and was instructed to remain quiet. The judge read a report stating that Adesanya is currently unfit to understand the charges against him.

At the end of the proceeding, Adesanya stood up, shouted, "Stop, you're not gonna do this to me!" and resisted as U.S. Marshals attempted to escort him from the courtroom. Although he had previously resisted during a court appearance, Adesanya was not restrained with handcuffs or leg irons on this occasion. As he moved away from the defense table, a U.S. Marshal quickly restrained him, and additional court security personnel assisted in removing him through a secure door.

As the door closed, Adesanya could be heard shouting, "Help me! Help me!" accompanied by the sounds of chains and someone telling him, "Relax! Relax!" His last words heard in the hallway were, "Somebody help me, please! It's a scheme!"

Neither of Adesanya's parents attended the proceeding. Judge John Facciola scheduled another court date for December 22.
