article_content: Toddler diarrhoea (TD) is a frequent cause of chronic diarrhoea in children aged one to five. When Emma Maynard's two-year-old son, Tom, began experiencing diarrhoea, she initially assumed it was just a stomach bug. Tom seemed otherwise healthy and ate normally, but the symptoms persisted. After four weeks, Emma consulted their GP and received a diagnosis of toddler diarrhoea—a term she had not previously encountered. Unlike diarrhoea from infections, toddler diarrhoea can last for months or even years, though the child appears healthy and continues to grow well. The condition generally starts around age one and usually resolves by age four. The precise cause is unknown. Dr Michael Thomson, consultant paediatric gastroenterologist at Sheffield Children's Hospital and London's Portland Hospital, explains: 'It's extremely common. After a thorough medical history, TD can often be distinguished because the child is well and thriving, despite frequent diarrhoea. Nutrients are mostly absorbed in the upper part of the gut, ensuring normal growth.' He notes it's important to rule out other causes, like allergies or coeliac disease, through appropriate tests. Blood and mucus in the stool may suggest a food allergy, not TD. Judy More, a paediatric dietitian, advises eliminating fruit juices—especially clear apple juice—as fructose can be poorly absorbed and trigger diarrhoea. She also recommends increasing healthy fats such as full-fat yoghurt, whole milk, cheese, and moderate amounts of cream, butter, and oil, which can slow gut transit and ease symptoms. Moderating fibre intake can also help, though it should not be completely removed. Dr Thomson warns that anti-diarrhoea medicines, like loperamide, should not be given to children with TD. The condition rarely causes distress to the child, but can be stressful for parents due to its social implications and added laundry. Emma Maynard found nursery attendance challenging, as staff initially thought Tom's diarrhoea was infectious, requiring a letter from the GP to clarify. Alison Gordon, from East Sussex, shares a similar story with her children, Jonah and Ben, both diagnosed with TD. Despite trying dietary eliminations due to family allergy history, symptoms persisted, but the children remained healthy and grew well. Alison notes that as Jonah became toilet-trained, managing the condition became easier. Dr Thomson emphasizes: 'Don’t cut out food groups without specialist guidance. Essential nutrients are vital for growth. If dietary adjustments don’t help, the best approach is patience, as most children outgrow the condition as their gut matures.'

During the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in San Francisco, US President Joe Biden and Chinese President Xi Jinping demonstrated an unexpected cordiality as they encouraged foreign investment from attending business leaders and CEOs. Facing the challenge of revitalizing China’s once-vibrant economy amid an outflow of foreign companies and supply chains, President Xi committed to dismantling barriers for international investors. He promised to introduce measures to foster a market-oriented, law-based, and world-class business environment in China, and to provide equal and high-quality services to foreign investors.

Xi emphasized his government's commitment to facilitating the flow of innovation, deepening reforms in the digital economy, and promoting the legal and free flow of data. He stated that China will implement more supportive policies for foreign nationals, improve financial and service sector access, bolster protection for foreign investors’ rights, further shorten the negative list for foreign investment sectors, and strengthen intellectual property protections.

These pledges come as China reported its first deficit in foreign investment since records began in 1998. In the third quarter, China saw an $11.8 billion outflow, reflecting a decline in foreign investor confidence. Analysts, including Zhou Xin from the South China Morning Post, interpreted this shift as a result of Western de-risking strategies, which may be diminishing China’s economic position globally.

Meanwhile, President Biden addressed the same group of APEC CEOs, asserting the United States’ ongoing commitment to high standards in trade and enduring partnerships across the Asia-Pacific. He stated that the US is not “decoupling” but is instead working to de-risk and diversify its economic ties with China. Biden credited America’s sustained involvement in the region for enabling decades of peace, security, and transformative growth, mentioning that US companies invested $50 billion in fellow APEC economies in 2023 in sectors such as clean energy, aviation, and cybersecurity. He noted that over 60% of US exports go to APEC partners, highlighting strong economic ties.

The summit and speeches from both leaders underline the ongoing competition and complex interdependence between the US and China in the region, set against evolving global economic and political dynamics.

article_content: Toronto Mayor Rob Ford admitted to drinking after a video surfaced on Monday night showing him rambling incoherently in what appears to be a Jamaican accent. The video, which was quickly uploaded to YouTube and went viral, captures Ford in a fast food restaurant, where he is heard swearing and discussing police surveillance. The undated footage shows the mayor speaking in what seems to be an imitation of Jamaican Patois while gesturing animatedly. Ford previously stated in November that he had stopped drinking following his crack-smoking scandal, telling the media he had experienced a personal turning point and attributing his past behavior to excessive alcohol consumption. After police obtained a video that allegedly showed him smoking crack, Ford admitted last year that he had done so 'in one of my drunken stupors.' The existence of this earlier video was first reported by journalists from the Toronto Star and the U.S. website Gawker. Before Rob Ford confirmed the latest video's timing, his brother and fellow politician Doug Ford defended him, suggesting it could not have been recent because Rob had quit drinking. Doug Ford commented on Rob’s appearance in the footage to support this claim, and avoided commenting on the use of the Jamaican accent, stating he hadn’t seen the video. During the clip, Mayor Ford appeared unaware of being filmed. Earlier this month, Mayor Ford made a public appearance at downtown nightclub Muzik, generating buzz across social media. The club, popular with locals, celebrities, and visitors—including stars like Justin Bieber—saw many attendees post photos of a sweaty Ford mingling on the dance floor. Doug Ford asserted that Rob only had a sugar-free energy drink at the club and stayed for about an hour to meet supporters for his upcoming campaign. Two Texas women, Kelly Scruggs and Holly Snow, say they had affairs with Huntington in 2007 and 2008. Scruggs, of Martin, Texas, said she met Huntington at the Wild West club in Waco, and their relationship lasted over a year. She learned he was still married after his involvement in the Colombia scandal came to light. Holly Snow encountered Huntington about a year later and claims he misrepresented his marital status initially. Both women described feeling deceived by him. In 2011, during President Obama's visit to Ireland, another woman reported Huntington lied about being divorced to pursue a relationship. She told reporters she felt 'used' after learning of his marital status and the prostitution scandal. The Colombian incident involved Huntington spending the night with Dania Suarez, an escort, and paying only $28 of an $800 charge. The resulting dispute at Cartagena's Hotel Caribe led to police involvement and triggered a major Secret Service investigation. Ultimately, nine agents lost their jobs due to related misconduct. The scandal, which coincided with the Summit of the Americas, overshadowed President Obama's visit and cast a negative light on the administration’s security operations.

article_content: Six members of Pakistan’s paramilitary Sindh Rangers are facing charges following the fatal shooting of Sarfraz Shah, an unarmed teenager. The incident was caught on video, widely broadcast in Pakistan, and led to widespread public outrage. A senior Karachi police official, Ahtisham Ali, stated that the accused have been turned over to police and will be tried under the country’s anti-terrorism law in a special court, with a one-month deadline for completion, as ordered by the Supreme Court. Pakistan’s Anti-Terrorism Courts are known for expedited proceedings compared to standard courts. Footage filmed by a local cameraman shows the Rangers shooting Shah after he pleads for his life and asks to be taken to the hospital before dying from his wounds. Shah’s killing is the latest in a string of human rights cases that have shaken public confidence in law enforcement. Human Rights Commission Chairwoman Zohra Yusuf highlighted how the clear video and level of brutality led to unusually widespread public and political anger. Officials claim Shah attempted to rob people in Benazir Bhutto Park, allegedly threatening them with a pistol. Park security handed him to the Rangers; police say he tried to seize the Rangers’ guns before they opened fire. The video, however, only shows him reaching toward their weapons before backing away. In response, the Supreme Court mandated leadership changes for the Sindh Rangers and police. Interior Minister Rehman Malik condemned the shooting as unjust but asserted that Shah was accused of threatening women and attempting robbery. Malik promised a transparent and neutral investigation, stating results would be made public. Shah’s family has insisted he was innocent, with his mother firmly stating he did nothing wrong.

article_content: Taylor Swift has added two extra London shows to her record-breaking Eras tour after the first six nights sold out. The new dates, on 19 and 20 August, mean she will now perform a total of eight nights at Wembley Stadium next summer. This matches a record set by Take That, who played eight dates at the venue during their 2011 Progress tour. Those concerts generated £38 million at the box office. London now hosts the most shows on Swift's Eras tour, surpassing Los Angeles and Singapore. She will also perform in Edinburgh, Cardiff, and Liverpool during the UK leg. US rock band Paramore, who will support Swift at all eight Wembley shows, announced the new dates on social media Tuesday morning. In a post on X, they said a limited number of fans who previously registered for London shows would be selected for access to the sale and would receive notifications via email starting that day. Many fans reported receiving access codes for the 19 August pre-sale on Tuesday morning, just hours before it began at 14:00 GMT. The pre-sale for the 20 August show starts at 14:00 GMT on Wednesday, 15 August. Tickets are only available to those who registered for the first batch of shows this summer. Swift's tour is described as a journey through all her musical eras, featuring her biggest hits such as Love Story, Anti-Hero, All Too Well, and Blank Space. The nearly four-hour show became a phenomenon in the US, where countless fans unable to get tickets gathered in stadium parking lots to listen. A shorter version of the concert was released in cinemas last month and quickly became the highest-grossing concert film of all time, earning $242 million (£197 million) at the global box office. Swift recently began the South American leg of her tour with three shows in Buenos Aires, Argentina. She made headlines on Saturday night when she changed the lyrics of 'Karma' to confirm her romance with American football star Travis Kelce, who plays for the Kansas City Chiefs: 'Karma is the guy on the Chiefs/ Coming straight home to me,' she sang as Kelce watched from the audience. Income from the tour has pushed Swift's net worth to over $1 billion (£813 million). In the UK, ticket prices range from £58 to £194. General admission costs £110, and standing tickets near the stage are priced at £172.25. VIP packages, which include bonus merchandise and perks such as early entry, cost between £196 and £662.

Reflecting on the aftermath of Meredith Kercher’s murder, Amanda Knox described her actions at that time as those of a traumatized, inexperienced young woman. Speaking emotionally in an ABC interview, Knox shared her hope that someday Kercher’s parents might forgive her and allow her to honor Meredith at her gravesite. She emphasized that seeking justice for herself does not contradict the Kercher family’s search for truth.

In 2007, Knox and her then-boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito were convicted of Kercher's murder in Perugia, Italy. Their convictions were later overturned in 2011, enabling Knox to return to Seattle. However, another Italian court later reversed her acquittal, and discussions continue regarding whether the U.S. will extradite her.

The Kercher family has repeatedly stated their desire for full clarity about Meredith’s death. After Knox’s acquittal, they were not ready to engage with Knox, who, in turn, asked to be seen as more than the “Foxy Knoxy” media persona.

Knox’s memoir, “Waiting to be Heard,” begins with her account of the Italian trial and the immediate shock she experienced when sentenced. During her ABC interview, she recounted being with Sollecito—spending the night watching a movie, smoking marijuana, and being together—but explained that her memory was dulled, though not erased, by the marijuana.

The next morning, Knox returned to her apartment to shower, since Sollecito's was not well maintained. She noticed the door was open and saw spots of blood, but attributed them to a faulty latch and her own recent ear piercings. Knox explained she lacked experience with traumatic events and therefore did not realize something serious had occurred.

Knox faced criticism for her behavior after the murder—including affectionate gestures toward Sollecito and comments viewed as insensitive—details prosecutors highlighted to portray her unfavorably. Knox admitted during the interview that she wished she had been more mature, and explained that people respond very differently to trauma.

She was often labeled with dramatic nicknames by Italian tabloids, but she denied these characterizations. Knox insists all information she has has already been shared with authorities and in her memoir, reiterating she was not present during Kercher’s murder.

Opinions of Knox’s memoir are polarized: some praise her depiction of Italy’s legal system and prison conditions, while others, such as journalist Barbie Latza Nadeau, accuse her of omitting important details and failing to reconcile inconsistencies in her and Sollecito’s stories.

Looking back, Knox expressed a wish to comfort her past self, acknowledging how unexpected events can dramatically and suddenly change one’s life.

article_content: CD Projekt Red (CDPR) has announced that major updates to Cyberpunk 2077 will conclude following the release of the Phantom Liberty expansion. Marking this transition is the new Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition, available for Xbox Series X/S, PlayStation 5, and PC. This edition contains the base game, all 2.0 updates and additions, and prior content—integrated onto the physical disc, highlighting CDPR's commitment to finalizing the experience and signaling no further significant updates. Notably, while the Phantom Liberty DLC is included on the Xbox disc, the PlayStation 5 version requires users to redeem a download code due to PlayStation's DLC distribution policies—this is not a deliberate disadvantage imposed by CDPR. The Ultimate Edition debuts on December 5, in time for the holiday season. The author expresses strong enthusiasm for the game's current state, emphasizing the dramatic improvements brought by the 2.0 update and Phantom Liberty expansion. While acknowledging the game's troubled launch, the author remains steadfast in his high regard for the title, considering it a top single-player RPG and his personal Game of the Year. Looking ahead, CDPR has officially greenlit a sequel to Cyberpunk 2077. Meanwhile, the studio is also developing a new Witcher game, aiming to manage multiple major series concurrently. The physical release of the Ultimate Edition serves as a fitting capstone for Cyberpunk 2077, and its strong sales may bode well for the franchise's future.

article_content: As Palestine prepares for upcoming World Cup qualifiers, footballers are facing the dangers of ongoing violence in the region. Reporting on football sometimes involves hyperbole, such as when commentator Alastair Brownlee described Middlesbrough's dramatic comeback in 2006 as “the greatest comeback since Lazarus.” However, in 2008, a real-life story unfolded in Gaza. During Israeli air raids in December that year, Hazem Alrekhawi, then a 19-year-old footballer for Shabab Rafah, boarded a bus with classmates in Gaza City. An Israeli airstrike hit the bus, and Alrekhawi was presumed dead along with the other passengers. He was taken to the morgue, but five hours later, his mother discovered he was still alive. Despite severe injuries, Alrekhawi eventually continued his football career, relocating to the West Bank and playing for eight clubs over ten years. This summer, he returned to Shabab Rafah to play alongside his brother Mohammed, 38, who was preparing to retire. On October 11, during renewed bombardment of Gaza, Mohammed survived a bombing that destroyed his home. Photographs showed him emerging from the rubble. The safety of the brothers is currently unknown, but their names have not appeared on official fatality lists. Palestinian football has experienced cycles of hardship and resilience. The Palestinian Football Association (PFA), originally founded in 1928 and later reorganized as the Israel Football Association in 1948, was re-established in 1998, allowing Palestine to rejoin FIFA. Since then, Palestinian football has persisted through political upheaval, conflict, and repeated wars. As Palestine prepares for the 2026 World Cup qualifiers and the 2024 Asian Cup, the situation is more challenging than ever, with persistent conflict and security threats. Footballers in Gaza have been particularly affected. Mohammed Balah, 30, left Gaza for Jordan six years ago to pursue his professional career, eventually playing for several Middle Eastern clubs. He returned to Gaza this summer after an ACL injury, hoping to rejoin the national team. In one of his last social media messages on October 10, Balah described the devastation in Gaza: “Maybe in a few hours, we will be cut off from the world... We will die in silence, away from the eyes of the world and friends.” Balah’s early football journey was shared with Mahmoud Wadi, who transferred to Pyramids FC in Egypt in 2021 for a record fee. Wadi recounted his fears during past conflicts in Gaza and has struggled to stay in contact with family during the current war. He noted that many football peers have died in the violence. Palestinian sports commentator Khalil Jadallah compiled a team of Palestinian athletes killed as a result of ongoing violence, including basketball player Bassim al-Nabahin, footballers Rashid Dabbour and Ahmad Awad, and others. The sporting community across Gaza and the West Bank has ground to a halt. Markaz Balata midfielder Mohammed Maree Sawafta was killed by Palestinian Authority forces during a protest in Tubas. Many Palestinian footballers have been unable to travel as violence and security concerns have increased, leading to the team’s withdrawal from a tournament in Malaysia in October. The squad eventually left the country with help from Palestinian and Jordanian authorities. The national team, managed by Makram Daboub, will face Lebanon and Australia in World Cup qualifiers, hosting the latter on neutral ground in Kuwait. Palestine has a strong recent record but must cope without home advantage. In recent years, few Gaza-based players have joined the national team, as many seek better opportunities elsewhere. The current conflict has further impacted the team’s talent pool and venues, including the destruction of Gaza’s Yarmouk Stadium. Khalil Jadallah notes that the loss of a home venue and the psychological toll pose significant challenges for the squad. Despite all difficulties, Palestinian footballers remain determined to represent their country and persevere.

Cubrir el fútbol a veces implica hipérboles, como cuando el comentarista Alastair Brownlee describió la dramática remontada del Middlesbrough en 2006 como “el regreso más grande desde Lázaro”. Sin embargo, en 2008, una historia real tuvo lugar en Gaza. Durante los bombardeos israelíes en diciembre de ese año, Hazem Alrekhawi, entonces futbolista de 19 años del Shabab Rafah, subió a un autobús con compañeros de clase en la Ciudad de Gaza. Un ataque aéreo israelí impactó el autobús y se creyó que Alrekhawi había muerto junto con los demás pasajeros. Fue llevado a la morgue, pero cinco horas después, su madre descubrió que seguía con vida. A pesar de las graves heridas, Alrekhawi finalmente continuó su carrera futbolística, trasladándose a Cisjordania y jugando para ocho clubes durante diez años. Este verano, regresó al Shabab Rafah para jugar junto a su hermano Mohammed, de 38 años, que estaba a punto de retirarse. El 11 de octubre, durante un nuevo bombardeo en Gaza, Mohammed sobrevivió a un ataque que destruyó su casa. Las fotografías lo mostraron saliendo de los escombros. La seguridad de los hermanos es actualmente desconocida, pero sus nombres no han aparecido en las listas oficiales de víctimas. El fútbol palestino ha experimentado ciclos de adversidad y resiliencia. La Asociación Palestina de Fútbol (PFA), fundada originalmente en 1928 y luego reorganizada como la Asociación de Fútbol de Israel en 1948, fue restablecida en 1998, permitiendo que Palestina se reincorporara a la FIFA. Desde entonces, el fútbol palestino ha persistido a pesar de los conflictos políticos y las guerras repetidas. Mientras Palestina se prepara para las eliminatorias de la Copa Mundial 2026 y la Copa Asiática 2024, la situación es más desafiante que nunca, debido al conflicto y las amenazas de seguridad. Los futbolistas en Gaza han sido particularmente afectados. Mohammed Balah, de 30 años, salió de Gaza hacia Jordania hace seis años para seguir su carrera profesional, jugando luego para varios clubes de Oriente Medio. Regresó a Gaza este verano después de una lesión de ligamento cruzado anterior, con la esperanza de reincorporarse al equipo nacional. En uno de sus últimos mensajes en redes sociales el 10 de octubre, Balah describió la devastación en Gaza: “Quizá en unas horas estaremos incomunicados... Moriremos en silencio, lejos de los ojos del mundo y de los amigos”. El primer trayecto futbolístico de Balah fue junto a Mahmoud Wadi, quien se trasladó al Pyramids FC en Egipto en 2021 por una tarifa récord. Wadi relató sus temores durante conflictos anteriores en Gaza y ha tenido dificultades para mantenerse en contacto con su familia durante la guerra actual. Señaló que muchos compañeros futbolistas han fallecido por la violencia. El comentarista deportivo palestino Khalil Jadallah compiló un equipo de atletas palestinos fallecidos como resultado de la violencia, entre ellos el jugador de baloncesto Bassim al-Nabahin, los futbolistas Rashid Dabbour y Ahmad Awad, entre otros. La actividad deportiva a lo largo de Gaza y Cisjordania se ha detenido. El mediocampista del Markaz Balata, Mohammed Maree Sawafta, fue asesinado por fuerzas de la Autoridad Palestina durante una protesta en Tubas. Muchos futbolistas palestinos no han podido viajar debido al aumento de la violencia y las preocupaciones de seguridad, lo que llevó al retiro del equipo de un torneo en Malasia en octubre. Finalmente, el equipo pudo salir del país con ayuda de las autoridades palestinas y jordanas. El equipo nacional, dirigido por Makram Daboub, enfrentará a Líbano y Australia en las eliminatorias del Mundial, recibiendo a este último en terreno neutral en Kuwait. Palestina tiene un historial reciente fuerte pero deberá lidiar sin la ventaja de jugar en casa. En los últimos años, pocos jugadores de Gaza se han unido al equipo nacional, ya que muchos buscan mejores oportunidades en otros lugares. El conflicto actual ha afectado aún más el grupo de talentos y sedes del equipo, incluyendo la destrucción del Estadio Yarmouk de Gaza. Khalil Jadallah señala que la pérdida de una sede local y el impacto psicológico representan importantes desafíos para el equipo. A pesar de todas las dificultades, los futbolistas palestinos siguen decididos a representar a su país y perseverar.

article_content: Earlier this week, MailOnline reported the troubling case of 25-year-old Gemma Wood, who faced a significant delay in receiving a bowel cancer diagnosis despite expressing her concerns to her GP. This story deeply affected Rebecca Holden, a 36-year-old personal assistant from West London. Having survived her own misdiagnosed bowel cancer, Rebecca, now cancer-free, lives with her husband Piers and their sons Max and Nico. She, too, experienced repeated dismissal from healthcare professionals regarding her symptoms. Rebecca often found her concerns dismissed, but attributes her survival to her determination. She shares her story to highlight that bowel cancer is not exclusive to older adults and aims to encourage others to listen to their bodies and advocate for their health. Diagnosed at 33, just four weeks after the birth of her first son, Rebecca suffered abdominal pain and bleeding. Multiple visits to Charing Cross A&E resulted in inconclusive tests and she was told her problems were due to constipation. Despite these assurances, she was convinced something was seriously wrong. Her situation changed when GP Dr. Louise Cavanagh recommended that Rebecca leverage her private health insurance for a specialist referral. She contacted Professor Sina Dorudi, a colorectal surgeon, whose tests detected a mass in her colon previously missed by NHS exams. Further investigation confirmed it was almost certainly cancer. Rebecca underwent extensive surgery to remove half her colon and her appendix. The timing was crucial in preventing the cancer from spreading, as the tumor was aggressive (stage T4). She believes her recent pregnancy aggravated the symptoms, and recognizes how fortunate she was to receive timely care. She later underwent intensive chemotherapy, which brought its own challenges. Three years after her diagnosis, Rebecca remains free of cancer but continues regular monitoring. Despite concerns about infertility due to chemotherapy, she and Piers had a second son, Nico. While grateful for her medical outcome, Rebecca feels frustration for others whose diagnoses are missed or delayed by healthcare providers. She is committed to increasing awareness about the risk of bowel cancer in younger people and urges anyone with symptoms—persistent abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or blood in stools—to persist in pursuing proper testing. By sharing her journey, she hopes to inspire others to insist on thorough medical assessments. Bowel cancer is the third most common cancer in England, commonly affecting those over 65, but younger individuals are also at risk. Symptoms include changes in bowel habits, unexplained weight loss, fatigue, and breathlessness. Risk factors include age, poor diet, sedentarism, smoking, alcohol use, and family history. Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust issued an apology for Rebecca's experience, stating that extensive tests and reviews had not pointed to cancer at the time, and reiterated their focus on improving patient care and openness to further discussion. Rebecca hopes that by speaking out—especially during Bowel Cancer Awareness Month—she can empower others not to be ignored. For further information, she recommends the website beatingbowelcancer.org.

article_content: Every month, major streaming platforms such as Netflix, Prime Video, Hulu, and Tubi release high-profile movies—some are highly anticipated new titles, while others are classic films returning to screens. These movies often top streaming charts and maintain popularity throughout the month. For October, there’s a wide range of options, perfect for the spooky season. But beyond these major releases, many lesser-known and underrated films also appear on streaming services. Though these hidden gems don’t get as much attention, they can be just as rewarding for viewers. One example is the 2014 horror film It Follows, streaming on Hulu. The story follows Jay, played by Maika Monroe, who is stalked by a supernatural entity after a sexual encounter. The film, which also stars Keir Gilchrist and Olivia Luccardi, was written and directed by David Robert Mitchell, an acclaimed writer-director. Although It Follows was a sleeper hit and received praise from critics, it remains underappreciated within the horror genre. It’s a memorable, thought-provoking movie—one of Hulu’s best horror offerings. Another underrated film is Bone Tomahawk, a Western horror movie available on Tubi. The cast is led by Kurt Russell, alongside Patrick Wilson, Matthew Fox, and Oscar nominee Richard Jenkins. The story revolves around a small-town sheriff leading a rescue mission to find people abducted by cannibalistic cave-dwellers. Bone Tomahawk blends gory horror and Western action, with strong performances all around, yet remains underrated. It’s a standout watch for October. For those interested in video game adaptations, Werewolves Within provides a rare exception to the typically lackluster genre. Directed by Josh Ruben and starring Sam Richardson, Cheyenne Jackson, and Harvey Guillén, the story is set in a small town trapped by a snowstorm, where residents suspect someone among them is a werewolf. The film balances comedy and horror, earning critical acclaim despite still flying under the radar. Streaming on Hulu, Werewolves Within is a hilarious and spooky choice for October viewing.

article_content: Kevin McCarthy, whose acting career spanned 65 years and included the horror classic 'Invasion of the Body Snatchers,' died on Saturday at the age of 96. The distinguished character actor appeared in hundreds of films and television shows, beginning his career in 1945 according to the Internet Movie Database. McCarthy passed away of natural causes at Cape Cod Hospital in Hyannis, Massachusetts, said hospital spokeswoman Robin Lord. Beyond 'Invasion of the Body Snatchers' (1956), McCarthy was also known for playing Biff in the 1951 film adaptation of Arthur Miller's 'Death of a Salesman.' He received an Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actor and won a Golden Globe for this performance. McCarthy also performed frequently on Broadway, including starring in his one-man show 'Give 'Em Hell, Harry!' as President Harry Truman.

India’s economy is demonstrating steady growth but requires expansion at over 8% annually to generate sufficient jobs for its vast population, according to former Reserve Bank of India governor Raghuram Rajan. Speaking via video at a Beijing event on Friday, Rajan stated: “We should aim for 8%-8.5% growth given the country’s population and employment needs.”

Although India’s current economic growth rate of 6%-6.5% is strong compared to other nations, Rajan believes it remains too slow to fulfill the job demand. “We have many young people needing employment,” he said.

Despite rapid economic expansion that outpaces other major countries, India is still falling short in job creation for new workforce entrants each year. The unemployment rate climbed to 10.05% in October—its highest in over two years—according to the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy. HSBC estimates that 70 million new jobs must be created in the next ten years; yet, at a 7.5% growth rate, only about two-thirds of this demand would be met.

High unemployment is a concern for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, particularly as he seeks a third term next year. His administration has tried to address the issue, distributing appointment letters for government jobs in line with a promise to provide one million public sector jobs by year-end.

Rajan emphasized the need for India to upgrade workforce skills to compete globally, notably with efficient manufacturing countries like China and Vietnam. “India is trying to move up the value chain, and there are early signs of progress,” he noted, referencing India’s production of iPhone parts. Still, he cautioned that significant progress is needed before the country can manufacture entire smartphones domestically.

He also highlighted factors driving India's growth: increased government infrastructure spending, improvements in business balance sheets, and rising consumer demand from the upper middle class. Rajan further pointed out China's advances in semiconductor manufacturing and noted that India currently lags behind. On the global stage, he expressed skepticism about a ‘soft landing’ for the US economy, estimating a greater than 50% likelihood that it could slow down excessively.

En un evento en Pekín el viernes, Rajan afirmó por videollamada: “Deberíamos apuntar a un crecimiento del 8%-8,5% dadas las necesidades de población y empleo del país”.

Aunque la tasa de crecimiento actual de la economía india, entre el 6% y el 6,5%, es fuerte en comparación con otras naciones, Rajan considera que sigue siendo demasiado lenta para cubrir la demanda laboral. “Tenemos muchos jóvenes que necesitan empleo”, puntualizó.

A pesar de que la economía india crece más rápido que la de otros grandes países, aún está por detrás en la creación de suficientes empleos para los nuevos trabajadores cada año. La tasa de desempleo asciende al 10,05% en octubre—su nivel más alto en más de dos años—según el Centro para el Monitoreo de la Economía India. HSBC estima que en los próximos diez años deberán crearse 70 millones de nuevos empleos; sin embargo, con un crecimiento del 7,5%, solo se cubrirían cerca de dos tercios de esa meta.

El alto desempleo preocupa al primer ministro Narendra Modi, sobre todo mientras busca un tercer mandato el próximo año. Su gobierno ha intentado abordar el problema distribuyendo cartas de nombramiento para empleos públicos, cumpliendo así la promesa de ofrecer un millón de trabajos gubernamentales antes de fin de año.

Rajan enfatizó la necesidad de que India fortalezca las capacidades de su fuerza laboral para competir globalmente, especialmente con países fabricantes como China y Vietnam. “India está intentando escalar en la cadena de valor y ya existen señales tempranas de avance”, señaló, mencionando la fabricación de partes de iPhone en India. De igual forma, advirtió que aún queda mucho camino por recorrer antes de que el país pueda fabricar teléfonos inteligentes completos localmente.

También destacó los factores que impulsan el crecimiento de India: mayor inversión gubernamental en infraestructura, mejoras en la salud financiera de las empresas y el aumento del consumo en la clase media alta. Rajan resaltó el avance chino en la fabricación de semiconductores y señaló que India sigue rezagada. A nivel internacional, expresó escepticismo ante la posibilidad de un “aterrizaje suave” de la economía estadounidense, estimando más del 50% de probabilidad de una desaceleración excesiva.

article_content: Two superheroes were filmed racing across water in a high-speed barefoot skiing showdown, reminiscent of scenes fans might see in the 2016 film 'Batman v Superman: Dawn Of Justice.' The playful video actually features members of the GB Barefoot Team, produced by 19-year-old Tom Wadsworth of Bad Wolf Editing. In the YouTube video, Superman demonstrates impressive moves on water, facing off against Batman as both try to outdo each other with their barefoot skiing skills. article_content: NEW DELHI: Although Team India could not bring the World Cup home, their dominant unbeaten streak leading up to the final—including standout performances from many players—was reflected in the ICC’s Team of the Tournament announced on Monday. India won 10 consecutive matches (nine in the league stage and one semi-final), but the final that mattered most was claimed by Australia, who outplayed India at Ahmedabad’s Narendra Modi Stadium on Sunday. Virat Kohli earned the 'Player of the Tournament' award for scoring 765 runs in 11 matches. Mohammed Shami finished as the tournament's top wicket-taker with 24 wickets in seven games. Kohli and Shami are among six Indian players named in the ICC's Team of the Tournament, along with Rohit Sharma (captain), KL Rahul (wicketkeeper-batter), Jasprit Bumrah, and Ravindra Jadeja. Champions Australia, who secured a record-extending sixth ODI World Cup title, are represented by all-rounder Glenn Maxwell and leg-spinner Adam Zampa in the ICC’s best eleven. South Africa opener Quinton de Kock, New Zealand’s Daryl Mitchell, and Sri Lanka’s left-arm pacer Dilshan Madushanka also feature in the lineup, with South African pacer Gerald Coetzee named as the 12th man. In the final, despite half-centuries from Kohli (54) and Rahul (66), India posted 240 runs after being asked to bat first by Australian skipper Pat Cummins, who won the toss. India’s formidable bowling attack, which had excelled in their ten consecutive wins, struggled against Australia opener Travis Head, whose 120-ball 137 led his side to victory with seven overs remaining. Head shared a 192-run partnership with Marnus Labuschagne (58) after Australia stumbled early, losing three wickets for just 47 runs. ICC Team of the Tournament: Rohit Sharma (captain), Quinton de Kock (wicketkeeper), Virat Kohli, Daryl Mitchell, KL Rahul (wicketkeeper), Glenn Maxwell, Ravindra Jadeja, Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Shami, Dilshan Madushanka, Adam Zampa. 12th man: Gerald Coetzee.

article_content: India has aligned with a major international effort to transfer authority over global tax regulation from the OECD, which is largely steered by affluent countries, to a more inclusive platform led by the United Nations. On November 22, the UN General Assembly saw India and 125 other nations vote in favor of launching talks on a UN convention for international tax cooperation. Key OECD members like the United States, United Kingdom, and Japan opposed the measure. The resolution, driven by several African countries and supported by the BRICS bloc (Brazil, Russia, India, and China), calls for the creation of a temporary inter-governmental committee consisting of up to 20 nations, ensuring regional and gender balance. Within the next year, this committee must set its agenda, aiming to draft a framework for equitable global tax collaboration. The committee’s mission is to bring both OECD and non-OECD states together to address pressing tax issues such as avoidance, illicit financial flows, asset recovery, and fair taxation of digital economies. Advocacy groups like the Tax Justice Network warn that global inaction could result in trillions lost to tax havens, while critics contend the OECD’s current system disproportionately benefits wealthy nations. Through this UN initiative, developing countries hope to gain a stronger role in crafting fair, effective international tax rules, so that revenue is more justly allocated to where economic activities actually occur. Elsewhere, India’s stock market activity surged as five initial public offerings attracted record investments. The government also issued guidance to social media companies, pressing them to update platforms so users are warned against uploading prohibited content. Additionally, Indians are increasingly choosing locally grown exotic flowers, contributing to a shift away from imports.

El 22 de noviembre, la Asamblea General de la ONU presenció cómo la India y otros 125 países votaban a favor de iniciar conversaciones sobre una convención de la ONU para la cooperación fiscal internacional. Países clave de la OCDE como Estados Unidos, Reino Unido y Japón se opusieron a la medida. La resolución, promovida por diversos países africanos y respaldada por el bloque BRICS (Brasil, Rusia, India y China), propone crear un comité intergubernamental temporal compuesto por hasta 20 países, garantizando equilibrio regional y de género. Dicho comité deberá establecer su agenda durante el próximo año, con el objetivo de redactar un marco para una colaboración fiscal justa a nivel global. La tarea del comité es reunir a países miembros y no miembros de la OCDE para abordar problemas fiscales urgentes como la evasión, los flujos financieros ilícitos, la recuperación de activos y la tributación justa de las economías digitales. Grupos como Tax Justice Network advierten que la inacción mundial podría provocar la pérdida de billones en paraísos fiscales, mientras que críticos alegan que el sistema actual de la OCDE beneficia sobre todo a países ricos. Con esta iniciativa de la ONU, los países en desarrollo esperan ganar mayor relevancia en la elaboración de reglas fiscales internacionales más justas y efectivas, buscando que los ingresos tributarios se asignen con mayor justicia a los lugares donde realmente se genera la actividad económica. En otras noticias, la bolsa de valores de India vivió un auge al atraer inversiones récord gracias a cinco ofertas públicas iniciales. El gobierno también pidió a empresas de redes sociales que actualicen sus plataformas para advertir a los usuarios sobre la publicación de contenido prohibido. Además, cada vez hay mayor preferencia de los indios por flores exóticas nacionales, disminuyendo así la demanda de importaciones.

article_content: Australia advanced to the semifinals of the ODI World Cup 2023 after defeating Afghanistan in a dramatic match. Glenn Maxwell delivered an extraordinary performance, scoring an unbeaten 201 runs, which is considered one of the finest innings in ODI and World Cup history. The match echoed iconic moments from cricket history, drawing comparisons to Kapil Dev's legendary 1983 World Cup knock. Facing a challenging situation at 91 for 7 while chasing a target of 292 runs, Maxwell partnered with captain Pat Cummins to form a record-setting 202-run unbeaten stand for the eighth wicket. Australia successfully chased down the total, winning by three wickets with 3.1 overs remaining. Afghanistan had earlier set a formidable target, scoring 291 for 5—their highest total in World Cup history. Despite conceding over 60 runs in the last five overs, Australia managed a memorable comeback. Australian bowler Josh Hazlewood praised Maxwell’s innings as the best he has witnessed, noting the difficulty bowlers face against Maxwell’s extensive range of shots. Hazlewood admitted the team felt nervous as the game became more intense but ultimately found Maxwell's achievement remarkable. Additional reports in business news include Tata Group acquiring Wistron's manufacturing facility for $750 million, making Tata the first Indian company to assemble iPhones. India also surpassed China to become the most represented country in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2024. Meanwhile, Religare Enterprises’ independent directors have raised concerns regarding the Burman family's takeover bid, alleging regulatory violations.

Tesco's packaging for its Finest Spaghetti Bolognese aimed to evoke the ambiance of a rustic Italian market, with images of salamis and artisanal treats. However, the company overlooked the true meaning of the Italian text on some of the market signs used for the meal's packaging. Specifically, 'Le Palle De Nonno' translates to 'Grandad's balls', and 'Coglioni di Mulo' means 'donkey’s testicles'. These phrases appeared on the packaging, and Tesco has acknowledged that this product has been sold across the UK for some time with these unintended inclusions.

Tesco explained that the photograph was taken at a genuine Italian market but admitted the signs were not reviewed by a translator. The error was uncovered after an Italian-speaking customer brought it to their attention. While other words on the signage referred to meats such as wild boar, buck, deer, and goose, these two phrases were found to be either cheeky slang or vulgar. In Italy, 'Coglioni di Mulo' is considered a serious insult, and 'Le Palle De Nonno' is slang related to a traditional type of salami. Tesco has apologized for any offence caused to Italian-speaking customers and stated they will update the packaging as soon as possible.

Tesco is not the first major brand to encounter problems with unintended messages on packaging. In 1990, Pepsi released promotional cans where stacking them revealed the word 'SEX.' Skittles produced a 'Berry Explosion' variety where the letter 's' made the word look like 'Berry Sexplosion.' An earlier version of the Starbucks logo, dating to the 1970s, showed the mermaid in what some consider a suggestive pose when viewed from a distance.

article_content: An Iranian delegation met with officials from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in Vienna, Austria, on Monday as diplomatic discussions continue regarding Tehran's nuclear program. This marks the first negotiations between Iran and the IAEA in three months; previous talks took place in Tehran earlier this year. According to Iran's state-run Press TV, the current meeting aims to create a framework for addressing questions about Iran's nuclear energy activities, citing Iranian ambassador to the IAEA, Ali Asghar Soltanieh. In March, the IAEA reported a significant and troubling rise in Iran's uranium enrichment capabilities. Iran maintains that its nuclear program is intended solely for civilian energy purposes and denies allegations of pursuing nuclear weapons. However, Western countries and Israel suspect that Iran is attempting to avoid international inspections and is seeking to develop nuclear weapons. These concerns have led to extensive sanctions targeting Iran's economy, government, and leadership. Key world powers—the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council (the United States, France, Russia, China, and Britain) plus Germany (collectively known as the P5+1)—met with Iran last month to discuss the nuclear issue and announced that the next meeting will take place in late May in Baghdad. CNN's Ben Brumfield and Marilia Brochetto contributed to this report.

Estas son las primeras negociaciones entre Irán y la AIEA en tres meses; las conversaciones previas tuvieron lugar en Teherán a principios de este año. Según la cadena estatal iraní Press TV, la reunión actual tiene como objetivo crear un marco para responder las preguntas sobre las actividades nucleares de Irán, citando al embajador iraní ante la AIEA, Ali Asghar Soltanieh. En marzo, la AIEA informó de un aumento significativo y preocupante en las capacidades de enriquecimiento de uranio de Irán. Irán sostiene que su programa nuclear está destinado exclusivamente a fines energéticos civiles y niega las acusaciones de buscar armas nucleares. Sin embargo, los países occidentales e Israel sospechan que Irán intenta evitar inspecciones internacionales y busca desarrollar armas nucleares. Estas preocupaciones han llevado a la imposición de amplias sanciones que afectan la economía, el gobierno y el liderazgo de Irán. article_content: West Ham United’s upcoming Premier League opener against Tottenham Hotspur has sparked outrage among fans as ticket prices soar up to £77 for adults. The match at Upton Park, scheduled for 3pm on Saturday, is classified as a Category A fixture, with the cheapest tickets priced at £50 for members and £55 for non-members. In comparison, Hull City—who finished just three points below West Ham in the previous Premier League season—are offering all adult tickets for £16 for their first home match against Stoke City. Many supporters are angered by West Ham’s high prices, with plans to join Football Supporters’ Federation (FSF) protests at the Premier League and Football League headquarters, demanding fairer pricing. According to FSF chief executive Kevin Miles, 'Nine out of 10 fans think football is simply too expensive,' highlighting widespread dissatisfaction. On social media, West Ham fans have voiced strong criticism of ticket prices, noting last season’s performance—only seven wins out of 19 home games—hardly justifies the cost. For juniors, tickets in Band 1 cost £41 at West Ham, while Hull under-15s attend Category C matches for just £5. The Tottenham game also includes a £2 booking fee, and many fans feel the quality of football does not warrant premium pricing. Still, West Ham offers some initiatives for young supporters, such as six 'Kids for a Quid' matches and one free game for under 16s each season. Upton Park membership costs £35, with non-members facing higher ticket prices, potentially discouraging new fans. Other major home fixtures against teams like Arsenal, Chelsea, and Manchester United are also designated Category A, with a range of prices for different matches. Ticket prices at other clubs vary: Hull charges £50 for adults, £30 for seniors and young adults, and £20 for juniors for Category A fixtures. QPR’s platinum seats for Category A games are £70 for non-members, Arsenal’s top Category A ticket costs £97, and Chelsea Category A tickets can reach £82, showing high prices across London. West Ham, in their penultimate Upton Park season before moving to the Olympic Stadium in 2016, announced a freeze on season ticket prices, with the most expensive adult ticket at £910 for new buyers and the cheapest at £620—still above some city rivals. Although some junior ticket deals exist, the high prices have left many fans feeling priced out and frustrated.

article_content: A key parliamentary committee has ruled that using Hindi titles for three planned criminal justice laws does not breach the Indian Constitution. The decision responds to objections raised by some political groups, who argued that the Hindi names could be exclusionary. The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs, chaired by BJP MP Brijlal, looked to Article 348 of the Constitution, which mandates English for legal documents and proceedings in the Supreme Court and high courts. The committee stated that since the laws themselves are written in English, assigning Hindi names does not contradict Article 348. The three bills, titled Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS-2023), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS-2023), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA-2023), aim to replace the Indian Penal Code of 1860, the Criminal Procedure Act of 1898, and the Indian Evidence Act of 1872, respectively. They were introduced to the Lok Sabha on August 11. Some opposition leaders, such as Congress's P Chidambaram and the DMK's Dayanidhi Maran, criticized the use of Hindi names for nationally implemented laws, pointing out that India has many languages. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin accused the central government of linguistic dominance, calling it "linguistic imperialism" and suggesting it undermines India's diversity. The Madras Bar Association also objected, passing a resolution against the Hindi titles. On the other side, Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan dismissed the criticism as 'petty politics,' arguing that such disputes weaken national unity more than the government's decision does. Union Home Secretary Ajay Bhalla explained to the committee that the bills conform to the Constitution since, per Article 348, the legal text remains in English. The article also briefly mentions unrelated news, including tax evasion probes targeting social media sellers and a personal dispute involving industrialist Gautam Singhania, but these have no direct connection to the debate over the new criminal bills' names.

article_content: More than a third of migration in sub-Saharan Africa takes place within the continent itself. As a result, many children have parents from different African countries, creating unique experiences and challenges regarding their sense of identity. However, there has been limited research on how these children form their identities, especially within Africa, as most existing studies focus on African migrants' children in the global North and primarily investigate parental perspectives.  To address this gap, a team of sociologists conducted in-depth interviews with 54 adults, focusing on the experiences of 32 participants who had one parent from one African country and another parent from a different African country. These participants, all from middle-class backgrounds in Ghana, Botswana, Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia, and South Africa, discussed how their mixed heritage influenced their sense of belonging and identity.  A core criterion for the study was that participants had lived during their formative years (childhood through the end of secondary school) in at least one of their parents' home countries. The researchers asked questions such as: Who are you? Where are you from? How do others see you? What is your relationship with your parents' countries of birth? How has your identity created opportunities or challenges?  The study found that family closeness during a child's formative years—such as regular communication, visits, and participation in cultural rituals—was crucial to how participants saw their primary identity. Even among siblings, different experiences could lead to different identifications. For example, three sisters with a Botswana mother and Ghanaian father formed different connections: the eldest, raised in rural Botswana by her maternal grandmother, identified more with the Kalanga ethnic group than with Ghana, while her younger sisters grew up in Gaborone, spent more time in Ghana during holidays, and identified strongly as Ghanaian.  The acceptance or rejection by extended family also shaped identity. One woman, Meghan, with a Ghanaian father and Nigerian mother, felt more Nigerian because her maternal relatives accepted her more warmly, despite living in Ghana.  Interestingly, speaking a specific African language was not strongly linked to identity among these individuals. The study showed that participants often used their 'secondary' identity for practical reasons such as accessing education or employment in a parent's country, or for more personal/cultural reasons, such as food choices, names, or clothing.  Identity for binational Africans is highly fluid, with people switching between aspects of their heritage as circumstances require, sometimes even daily. Both societal culture and personal experiences shape how individuals see themselves.  This research highlights the importance of giving voice to the children of African migrants on the continent and points to the complex, dynamic nature of identity in a multicultural African context. translated_content: Más de un tercio de la migración en África subsahariana ocurre dentro del propio continente. Como resultado, muchos niños tienen padres de diferentes países africanos, lo que genera experiencias y desafíos únicos en torno a su sentido de identidad. Sin embargo, se ha investigado poco cómo estos niños forman su identidad, especialmente dentro de África, ya que la mayoría de los estudios existentes se centran en hijos de migrantes africanos en el norte global y, principalmente, en la perspectiva parental.  Para abordar esta brecha, un equipo de sociólogos realizó entrevistas en profundidad con 54 adultos, enfocándose en las experiencias de 32 participantes que tenían un progenitor de un país africano y otro de un país africano distinto. Estos participantes, todos de clase media y provenientes de Ghana, Botswana, Kenia, Nigeria, Etiopía y Sudáfrica, hablaron sobre cómo su herencia mixta influenció su sentido de pertenencia e identidad.  Un criterio central del estudio fue que los participantes hubieran vivido durante sus años formativos (infancia hasta finalizar la secundaria) en al menos uno de los países de origen de sus padres. Los investigadores preguntaron: ¿Quién eres? ¿De dónde eres? ¿Cómo te perciben los demás? ¿Qué relación tienes con los países de origen de tus padres? ¿Cómo ha influido tu identidad en las oportunidades o desafíos que has enfrentado?  El estudio halló que la cercanía familiar durante la infancia —como comunicación regular, visitas y participación en rituales culturales— fue clave para cómo los participantes percibieron su identidad principal. Incluso entre hermanos, las experiencias diferentes podían llevar a identificaciones distintas. Por ejemplo, tres hermanas con madre de Botswana y padre de Ghana se conectaron de maneras diferentes: la mayor, criada en el ámbito rural por su abuela materna, se identificó más con el grupo étnico Kalanga que con Ghana, mientras que sus hermanas menores, que crecieron en Gaborone y pasaron más tiempo en Ghana durante las vacaciones, se identificaban fuertemente como ghanesas.  El grado de aceptación por parte de la familia extendida también influyó en la identidad. Una mujer, Meghan, con padre ghanés y madre nigeriana, expresó sentirse más nigeriana porque sus familiares maternos la aceptaron con más calidez, a pesar de vivir en Ghana.  Curiosamente, hablar una lengua africana específica no estaba tan vinculado a la identidad para estas personas. El estudio demostró que los participantes a menudo utilizaban su 'identidad secundaria' por motivos prácticos, como acceder a educación o trabajo en el país de uno de los padres, o por razones más personales/culturales, como preferencias en comida, nombres o vestimenta.  La identidad para los africanos binacionales resulta altamente fluida, y las personas pueden alternar entre aspectos de su herencia según la situación, a veces incluso diariamente. Tanto la cultura social como las experiencias personales moldean cómo cada individuo se reconoce.  Esta investigación resalta la importancia de escuchar las voces de hijos de migrantes africanos en el propio continente y muestra la naturaleza compleja y dinámica de la identidad en un contexto africano multicultural. article_content:
Few names in cinema evoke nightmares and horror quite like John Carpenter. The legendary filmmaker redefined the horror genre with 1978’s Halloween and went on to direct classics such as The Fog, The Thing, They Live, and In the Mouth of Madness. Since his last theatrical film, The Ward (2010), Carpenter has mostly stayed behind the scenes, composing scores for the recent Halloween reboot trilogy directed by David Gordon Green.

This Halloween, Carpenter returns from semi-retirement with a new anthology series on Peacock, John Carpenter’s Suburban Screams, which blends true crime with slasher-style suspense. Digital Trends interviewed Jordan Roberts, executive producer, showrunner, and director of the standout episode, 'A Killer Comes Home'—considered by some to be the most terrifying 45 minutes of television this year.

Asked how he joined the project, Roberts shared that he had worked with fellow executive producer Tony DiSanto, who approached him about the series. The appeal of working with Carpenter was immediate, and Roberts eagerly agreed to direct and showrun.

Roberts, who studied Carpenter’s films in school and grew up immersing himself in the director’s style, described their collaboration as mutually respectful. Carpenter allowed Roberts creative freedom, while Roberts strove to infuse all episodes with Carpenter’s influence, especially in the one he directed.

Roberts cites The Thing as his favorite Carpenter film, describing it as a masterful exploration of paranoia. He explained that Suburban Screams deliberately blurs fiction and reality, combining documentary techniques with horror to heighten the impact. With his documentary background, Roberts wanted to bring authenticity and a new dimension to the genre.

In directing 'A Killer Comes Home,' Roberts prioritized respect for the victims, avoiding any glamorization of the perpetrator. He aimed to convey the feeling of being pursued by a real-life monster, believing this approach made him the right person to tell the story.

Carpenter’s influence is evident both consciously and unconsciously throughout the series, especially in signature style choices like long takes and Steadicam shots. Roberts notes parallel themes between 'A Killer Comes Home' and Halloween, including elements like the killer returning to their hometown.

Ultimately, Roberts hopes Suburban Screams offers more than scares; he believes horror can provoke profound self-reflection and exploration of fear. John Carpenter’s Suburban Screams is now streaming on Peacock.
